Finally, those forms normally available at 12th level are now available at 18th level. At 20th level, the druid is still able to use wild shape at will.
archetype-druid-wild-rider.nature’s stride (ex): Starting at 2nd level, the wild rider’s animal companion may move through any sort of natural undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at its normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect it. If the wild rider is riding her animal companion, she is also unaffected by any damage or impairment that the animal companion avoids. This replaces woodland stride, and essentially grants it to the wild rider’s animal companion, instead.
archetype-druid-wild-rider.smooth ride (ex): Beginning at 3rd level, the wild rider need not make concentration checks in order to cast spells while riding her animal companion. This affects only concentration checks made as a result of vigorous motion. If the wild rider is damaged, or something besides the movement of her animal companion would cause her to have to make a concentration check, she still has to. This ability replaces trackless step.

archetype-druid-pactsworn-pagan.bind spirit: A pactsworn pagan can seal pacts with spirits. The character’s binder level equals his or her druid level, and the character binds spirits as an occultist of that same level. A pactsworn pagan uses Wisdom in place of Charisma on binding checks and when adjudicating the effectiveness of granted abilities. A pactsworn pagan can never gain a bound spirit’s vestigial companion. Even a multiclass pactsworn pagan retains this restriction.
archetype-druid-pactsworn-pagan.constellation alignment: At 1st level, a pactsworn pagan aligns with one of the following constellations: Beast, Dragon, Scholar, Seer, or Tree. The pactsworn pagan cannot seal pacts with a spirit whose constellation opposes the aligned constellation. Also, the pactsworn pagan is treated as a binder of ½ his or her druid level when making binding checks with, and using the granted abilities of, unaligned spirits. Diminished Spellcasting A pactsworn pagan possesses 1 less spell per day at each accessible spell level. If the pactsworn pagan would receive 0 spells per day, he or she only receives the bonus spells that the pactsworn pagan would have gained for having a high Wisdom. Limited Bond A pactsworn pagan may not select an animal companion using the nature’s bond class feature. Instead, the character selects a cleric domain, an animal domain, or a terrain domain. A pactsworn pagan may select the Occult domain from among the normal domain options. This ability replaces nature’s bond.
archetype-druid-pactsworn-pagan.spiritshape (su): At 4th level a pactsworn pagan can shift his or her body into a form that better pleases the spirits. Specifically, the pactsworn pagan may assume the form of a currently bound spirit’s vestigial companion (or a similar creature,with GM approval) as a polymorph effect. A pactsworn pagan can only assume the form of a vestigial companion if it is one of the following creature types: animal, dragon, elemental, magical beast, plant, undead, or vermin. This ability functions as one of the spells on the list below, based on the vestigial companion’s creature type and the pagan’s level. 4th Level: beast shape I, undead anatomy I, vermin shape I 6th Level: beast shape II, elemental body I, vermin shape II 8th Level: beast shape III, elemental body II, plant shape I, undead anatomy II 10th Level: beast shape IV, elemental body III, form of the dragon I, plant shape II, undead anatomy III 12th Level: elemental body IV, form of the dragon II, plant shape III 14th Level: form of the dragon III, undead anatomy IV This ability has no duration; the character may remain in the form for part or all of the pact’s duration. While in vestigial form, the character benefits from his or her spirit’s minor granted abilities. However, the spirit’s major granted ability counts as expended while in vestigial form and for 5 rounds after the end effect ends. In addition, a pactsworn pagan cannot assume a shapeshifted form while the spirit’s major granted ability is expended. At the GM’s discretion, a pactsworn pagan may shift into a form that reflects the constellation of a bound spirit. For example, a GM might allow any sufficiently-leveled pagan acquire the form described in form of the dragon I while bound to a dragon spirit. This ability is modified by any feat, spell, or effect that specifically works with the wild shape druid class feature. For example, the Planar Wild Shape feat lets the pagan add the celestial or fiendish template to his or her spiritshape. This ability replaces wild shape.

archetype-druid-elementalurgist.element bond (su): Each day when meditating on the mysteries of nature to prepare spells, the elementalurgist may attune herself to one element: Air, Earth, Fire, or Water. Attuning herself to the element grants her that domain. She may choose any subdomain of these, except for the Metal subdomain. Attunement to an element lasts until the elementalurgist re-attunes herself as part of the meditation. You cannot choose to not be attuned to an element. When determining the powers and bonus spells granted by this domain, the elementalurgist’s effective cleric level is equal to her druid level. An elementalurgist also receives additional domain spell slots, just like a cleric. She must prepare the spell from her domain in this slot. As the elementalurgist grows in her worship of the elements, she can attune to more elements. When attuned to multiple elements, she receives the powers and spells of the domains of the elements she’s attuned to, but she does not receive additional spell slots from domains gained after the first. At 6th level, she attunes to two elements. At 11th level, she attunes to three elements. At 16th level, she attunes to all four elements. This ability replaces nature bond.
archetype-druid-elementalurgist.spontaneous casting: An elementalurgist can channel stored spell energy into domain spells that she has not prepared ahead of time. She can “lose” a prepared spell in order to cast any domain spell of the same level or lower. She may only use this ability with spells from attuned domains. This ability replaces the ability to spontaneously cast summon nature’s ally spells.
archetype-druid-elementalurgist.endure elements (su): At 2nd level, the elementalurgist druid is constantly under the effects of endure elements. This ability replaces woodland stride.
archetype-druid-elementalurgist.elemental infusion (su): At 3rd level, the elementalurgist gains the ability to call forth aspects of the elements she is attuned to and infuse her allies with these aspects. As a standard action, the elementalurgist can select a number of allies equal to 1 + her Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) to infuse with an aspect, detailed below. An aspect lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1 + half the elementalurgist’s level. All allies receive the same aspect. Each aspect has a minimum level and an element associated with it. You must be high enough level to infuse the aspect, and you must be attuned to the element that the aspect is associated with. At 7th level, and every 4 levels thereafter, you may infuse your allies with one additional aspect, up to 5 aspects at 19th level. While infused with an element, the appearance of allies changes slightly to reflect which aspect they are infused Elementalurgist [Fire] with. An ally whose attacks are infused with fire might have a faint aura of fire around his weapon, while the skin of an ally infused with adamantine hardness takes on a slightly metallic sheen. In addition, the ally’s attacks deal an extra +1d6 points of elemental damage. For every two additional aspects the ally is infused with, this damage increases by +1d6. If infused with an Air aspect, this extra damage is electricity damage. If infused with an Earth aspect, this extra damage is acid damage. If infused with a Fire aspect, this extra damage is fire damage. If infused with a Water aspect, this extra damage is cold damage. If the elementalurgist infuses an ally with aspects from multiple elements, she must choose from those elements as the damage type. Subsequent uses of this ability negate any previous uses still in effect. The save DC for any ability from an aspect is equal to 10 + half the elementalurgist’s level + their Wisdom modifier. Unless otherwise specified, all aspects that modify weapons only modify non-spell weapons. At 3rd level, the elementalurgist has access to the following aspects: Burn [Fire]: The ally’s weapons burst into flame, and the flame lingers in its previous position for longer than expected, as if hinting at its sticky nature. Creatures the ally successfully hits with a weapon must make a Reflex save or catch fire for 1d4 rounds; dealing 1d6 points of fire damage each round. Charged Air [Air]: The air around the ally cracks as small bursts of electricity suddenly appear and disappear. At the start of ally’s turn, creatures adjacent to the ally take 2d4 points of electricity damage unless they make a Reflex save. A successful saving throw halves the damage Clobbering Strikes [Earth]: Right before impact, the weapons of the ally grow twice as large, clobbering the foe with the earth’s fury. The ally’s weapons deal damage as if one size larger. This is a magical effect that increases size. Earthbound Stability [Earth]: The ally’s feet seem to meld with the earth, providing superior stability all the while not restricting movement. The ally receives a +2 competence bonus to their Combat Maneuver Defense when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground. In addition, the ally gains a +1 insight bonus on attack and damage rolls if both it and its foe are touching the ground. Fiery Haste [Fire]: Small wisps of flame sprout off from the ally as they make their way through the battlefield. The ally receives a +5 feet insight bonus to base speed, and receives an extra +2 fire damage on all weapon damage rolls, including spell weapons. Fluid Motion [Water]: The ally’s movements become supernaturally graceful, allowing them to flow over obstacles that would stop others. The ally may take a 5 foot step into difficult terrain. In addition, the ally can move 5 feet if missed by a melee attack. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunities and the ally must end their movement threatened by the enemy who missed. Icy Steps [Water]: The ally’s steps chill the ground where ever they go. Each round, the ally chooses one square they take up. Ice appears in a straight line from where ever the selected square was at the beginning of the turn to where it is at the end of your turn. This ice counts as difficult terrain for one turn, before it melts away. For a medium creature, the square chosen will be the only square the creature is in, but for larger creatures, they just choose one square that they are in. An ally under the effect of Icy Steps does not treat the ice created by this aspect as difficult terrain. Wind to the Back [Air]: Each step brings the ally a little further than normal as small gusts of winds launch the ally forth. The ally receives a +10 foot insight bonus to speed, and all jumps count as running jumps. Elementalurgist [Water] At 7th level, the elementalurgist has access to the following aspects: Haze [Air]: The ally is encased in a protective haze. The ally is treated as if being affected by the blur spell. Iron To Ice [Water]: The ally’s weapons turn into supernaturally stable ice that coldly saps the strength to fight from the ally’s foes. Half the damage the ally inflicts with a weapon is cold damage. Despite the name, this aspect works with all weapons. Trailblazer [Fire]: A blaze follows the ally as they dance across the earth. This glowing trail of fire appears behind you in a straight line starting where you started your turn and ending where you end your movement. Each square where you step out of starts ablaze for a round, causing 2d4 points of fire damage ( Reflex half) to any creature passing through the flames. Toughened Skin [Earth]: The ally’s skin color becomes a shifting gradient of earthy, yet oddly metallic, brown and green. The ally gains DR 1/ adamantine. For every two druid levels past 2nd level (4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, 16th, 18th, and 20th), the DR increases by 1 point, to a maximum of DR 10/ adamantine at 20th level. At 11th level, the elementalurgist has access to the following aspects: Burrowing [Earth]: The ally is easily able to move through earth, and can exist in earth as if he was above ground. Your ally gains a burrow speed equal to 1/4th their base speed, and can breathe while burrow ing. Elemental Resistance [Air, Earth, Fire, or Water]: Your ally gains a resistance to one of the elements you are attuned to. Choose on element when you imbue this aspect. The ally gains energy resistance 15 to that element. You can apply this aspect multiple times, but with different elements. Flight [Air]: The ally is able to fly perfectly with the help of the wind. Your ally gains a fly speed equal to their base speed, with good maneuverability. The ally gains an enhancement bonus to Fly checks equal to half the elementalurgist’s caster level. Rejuvenating Waters [Water]: The ally is imbued with the rejuvenating properties of spring water. They gain fast healing equal to the druid’s Wisdom modifier. This aspect has no effect out of combat. Sheath of Flame [Fire]: A sheath of flames surrounds the ally, flaring up when enemies get close. Any creature striking you with its body or a hand-held weapon deals normal damage, but at the same time the attacker takes 1d6 points of damage + 1 point per elementalurgist level (to a maximum of +15). Creatures attacking with a reach melee weapon do not take the damage. The ally takes no damage from these flames, but sheds light as a torch. At 15th level, the elementalurgist has access to the following aspects: Fiery Burst of Speed [Fire]: The ally is imbued with the ability to summon forth a great burst of flames to propel them forward. Once every 1d4 rounds, the ally may, as a swift action, move up to their base speed, as if taking a move action. When the ally uses this ability, all enemies adjacent to the ally take 6d6 fire damage, with a Reflex save for half. Fluid Form [Water]: The ally’s form becomes more fluid. The ally is affected by the fluid form spell. Mystical Earth [Earth]: The ally is able to tap into the mystical power of the earth to enhance their own spellcasting. While on solid ground, the ally is treated as possessing the Eschew Materials feat and gains a +2 bonus to caster level checks. While under the effects of this aspect, the spellcaster may spend a full-round action to cast any spell that normally has a standard action or less casting time. When doing so, the DC of the spell increases by 1. Swift Attack [Air]: The ally is infused with the celerity of wind, allowing them to attack faster. When making a full attack action, the ally may make one extra attack with one natural or manufactured weapon. The attack is made using the ally’s full base attack bonus, plus any modifiers appropriate to the situation. This aspect does not stack with effects such as haste. The elementalurgist may use this ability a number of times per day equal to 5 + their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces wild shape.
archetype-druid-elementalurgist.diverse elemental infusions: Prerequisite: elementalurgist 7 Benefit: When using your elemental infusion ability, you may give different allies different aspects. Normal: You must give all allies the same aspects.

archetype-druid-henge-kannushi.shrine bond (su): At 1st level, instead of a nature bond, a henge-kannushi bonds with a yokinto shrine and the kami within. This bond functions identically to nature bond (granting access to either a domain or an animal companion ) except as follows. When within 1 mile/level of the shrine, all spells cast by the henge-kannushi gain +1 DC. Spells cast outside this range suffer a -1 DC. Additionally, when within range of his shrine, once per day, the henge-kannushi can cast any one spell he has access to but has not prepared so long as the spell is 1 level lower than the maximum level he can cast.
archetype-druid-henge-kannushi.spirit empathy (ex): The henge-kannushi adds his druid level to any Diplomacy or Intimidate checks made to influence a creature with the elemental, fey, or kami subtype. A henge-kannushi can attempt to influence the attitude of such creatures even if they would not normally be subject to such skill checks. This ability replaces wild empathy.
archetype-druid-henge-kannushi.shrine guardian (ex): Each yokinto shrine is associated with the terrain type in which it is located (typically forest or mountain). When in the terrain associated with their shrine the henge-kannushi gains a bonus on initiative checks, Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth and Survival checks equal to 1/2 his druid level. Additionally, the henge-kannushi cannot be tracked in this terrain, unless he so chooses. This bonus replace woodland stride.
archetype-druid-henge-kannushi.woodland stride (ex): A henge-kannushi gains this ability at 3rd level. This ability replaces trackless step.
archetype-druid-henge-kannushi.pierce the veil (su): At 9th level, the henge-kannushi gains the ability to benefit from true seeing a number of rounds per day equal to his druid level. This ability can be used at will as a swift action and the rounds do not need to be consecutive. This ability replaces venom immunity.

archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery i: At 4th level, a storm lord gains faerie fire and obscuring mist as spell-like abilities, using his druid level as the caster level for these abilities. Once per day, he may use a spell-like ability, freely choosing which one without preparing it in advance.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery ii: At 6th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability twice per day. He also adds fog cloud and gust of wind to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery iii: At 8th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability three times per day. He also adds call lightning, sleet storm, and wind walk to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery iv: At 10th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability four times per day. He also adds air walk and ice storm to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery v: At 12th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability five times per day. He also adds call lightning storm to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery vi: At 14th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability six times per day. He also adds chain lightning to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery vii: At 16th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability seven times per day. He also adds control weather to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery viii: At 18th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability eight times per day. He also adds whirlwind to his list of spell-like abilities.
archetype-druid-storm-lord.storm mastery ix: At 20th level, the storm lord can use a spell-like ability nine times per day. He also adds storm of vengeance to his list of spell-like abilities.

archetype-druid-air-elemental-companion.air elemental: Starting Statistics: Size Small; Speed fly 100 ft. (perfect); AC +1 natural armor; Attack slam (1d4); Ability Scores Str 10, Dex 16, Con 11, Int 3, Wis 14, Cha 8; Special Qualities air mastery, elemental immunities, darkvision 60 ft. 4th-Level Advancement: Size Medium; Attack slam (1d6); Ability Scores Str +2, Dex +2.

archetype-druid-ironskinned-animal-compa.ironskinned animal companion (ex): A character able to select an animal companion can choose an animal companion with the ironskinned template.

archetype-druid-scorpion-whisperer-druid.inured to extremes (ex): At 1st level, a scorpion whisperer is constantly treated as though under the effects of endure elements. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-druid-scorpion-whisperer-druid.resist toxins (ex): At 2nd level, a scorpion whisperer gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against poison and Resist acid 5. At 4th level, the bonus on poison saving throws increases to +4 and the acid resistance increases to 10. This replaces woodland stride and resist nature’s lure.
archetype-druid-scorpion-whisperer-druid.digestive enzymes (ex): At 15th level, as a standard action, a scorpion whisperer can spew digestive enzymes into an adjacent square. Creatures in the square must make a Fortitude saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your druid level + your Wisdom modifier). A creature takes 3 points of acid damage per druid level on a failed save, or half as much on a successful save. Furthermore, a creature that failed to make its saving throw takes the same amount of acid damage again at the start of the following round. A scorpion whisperer can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 1 + their Constitution modifier (minimum 1). This replaces timeless body.

archetype-druid-sunsoul-druid-archetype.sun magic (sp): At 1st level, a sunsoul can cast the spells from the cleric sun domain once each per day as a spell-like ability as soon as she is capable of casting spells of the designated levels. This replaces wild empathy, trackless step, and timeless body.
archetype-druid-sunsoul-druid-archetype.fiery touch (su): At 4th level, a sunsoul gains Resist fire 5. Additionally, a sunsoul can make a melee touch attack that deals 1d4 points of fire damage per druid level. A sunsoul can make a fiery touch attack a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Wisdom modifier. This replaces resist nature’s lure and a thousand faces.

archetype-druid-wildfire-druid-druid-arc.nature bond (ex): At 1st level, a wildfire druid must select the fire or plains domain as her nature bond. This alters nature bond.
archetype-druid-wildfire-druid-druid-arc.wildfire stride (ex): As a wildfire druid grows in power, her gait reflects more and more qualities of wildfire. At 2nd level, a wildfire druid moves with the speed of a wildfire, gaining a +10 bonus to her base land speed. At 3rd level, she gains a +1 dodge bonus to her AC as long as she is wearing non-metal medium or light armor. This replaces woodland stride and trackless step.
archetype-druid-wildfire-druid-druid-arc.flames of rejuvenation (ex): At 4th level, whenever a wildfire druid is the target of a spell or spell-like ability that deals fire damage, she automatically gains fast healing 1 for 1 minute even if she doesn’t take damage from the flames. This ability takes effect as soon as the wildfire druid is exposed to the magical fire effect, up to a maximum of 3 times per day. At 15th level, the fast healing equals the wildfire druid’s Wisdom bonus instead. This replaces resist nature’s lure and timeless body.

archetype-druid-witchdoctor-druid-archet.protection from spirits (su): The witchdoctor adds hide from undead to his spell list. This ability replaces Wild Empathy.
archetype-druid-witchdoctor-druid-archet.will of the ancestors (su): The witchdoctor adds speak with dead, bestow curse and remove curse to his spell list as 3rd level spells. This ability replaces Resist Nature’s Lure.
archetype-druid-witchdoctor-druid-archet.shamanism (su): The witchdoctor adds one spell from the necromancy school (chosen from the cleric, wizard or witch spell lists) to his spell list for each spell level the witchdoctor is able to cast spells from. This ability replaces Wild Shape.
archetype-druid-witchdoctor-druid-archet.fetish mask (su): By crafting and wearing a horrid mask, the witchdoctor can perform songs, dances or speeches in front of large crowds and affect them as per the enthrall spell, usable at will. This ability replaces A Thousand Faces.

archetype-druid-natural-transmogrifist-d.weapon and armor proficiencies: A natural transmogrifist is not proficient with any armor or shields.
archetype-druid-natural-transmogrifist-d.transmogrify armor (su): When a natural transmogrifist casts summon nature’s ally, he can use transmogrify armor. This ability replaces natural bond, but the transmogrifist can gain a ranger’s animal companion beginning at 4th level in place of resist nature’s lure.
archetype-druid-natural-transmogrifist-d.natural aspect (su): At 3rd level, while using transmogrify armor, a natural transmogrifist gains an aspect of the creature he summoned. This functions as the shifter’s aspect ability. At 7th level, the natural transmogrifist also gains one of his summoned creature’s natural attacks while using transmogrify armor.

archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.class skills: A lunar-touched druid adds Stealth to her list of class skills, and removes Ride. This alters class skills.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.moon magic (ex): As the moon’s phases are constantly changing, so too do a lunar-touched druid’s prepared spells. She has one fewer spell slot of each level than a regular druid. If this reduces her number of spell slots of a particular level to zero, she can cast spells of that level only if her Wisdom allows bonus spells of that level. A number of times per day equal to her Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), a lunar-touched druid can “lose” a prepared spell in order to spontaneously cast any other spell on the druid spell list of the same level or lower. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, a lunar-touched druid can spontaneously cast one additional spell in this manner. This alters the druid’s spells per day and spontaneous casting.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.lunar legacy (ex): At 1st level, a lunar-touched druid’s lunar legacy can take one of two forms. The first is a close tie to night, the time at which the moon can be seen most prominently. A lunar-touched druid selecting this option gains the powers of the darkness domain and additional domain spell slots, just like a cleric. Her bonus domain spells, however, are not taken from the darkness domain spell list. Instead, a lunar-touched druid gains the following list of domain spells: 1st—air bubble; 2nd—stone call; 3rd—deep slumber; 4th—air walk; 5th—tidal surge; 6th—cloak of dreams; 7th—lunar veil; 8th—reverse gravity; 9th—tsunami. The second is to form a close bond with a nocturnal animal companion. This ability functions exactly as a druid’s animal companion except that the creature chosen must be nocturnal (badger/dire, bat/dire, beaver, coyote, crocodile, feline [all], fox, frog/giant, hedgehog, hyena, kangaroo, owl, raccoon, rat/dire, scorpion/giant, skunk/giant, weasel/giant, wolf/dire). Once the lunar-touched druid has selected what form their lunar legacy takes, it cannot be changed. This alters nature bond.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.nocturnal senses (ex): At 1st level, a lunar-touched druid gains low-light vision and a +2 bonus on Perception and Stealth skill checks. At 4th level, a lunar-touched druid gains darkvision 60 feet. (If she already has darkvision, it increases by 30 feet.) This replaces wild empathy, nature sense, and resist nature’s lure.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.lunar stride (ex): A lunar-touched druid can alter gravity. At 2nd level, she gains a +2 bonus on Acrobatics skill checks, and is always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump. Additionally, a lunar-touched druid treats her Strength score as 4 higher when determining her carrying capacity. At 9th level, the druid’s Acrobatics checks to jump are no longer modified by the surface on which she stands. At 15th level, a lunar-touched druid’s bonus on Acrobatics skill checks increases to +4, and she is considered to be constantly under the effects of feather fall. This replaces woodland stride, and timeless body.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.eclipse (ex): At 3rd level, once per day, as a swift action, a lunar-touched druid can increase or decrease the light levels within 100 feet by 1 step (bright to normal, normal to dim, dim to dark) for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 her druid level. These effects stack, and each level lower costs another round of eclipse to use. This replaces trackless step.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.lunar aura (su): A lunar-touched druid can generate auras with opposing effects just as the moon experiences extremes in light and temperature. At 4th level, a lunar-touched druid gains the ability to assume a lunar aura of their choice once per day. The effect lasts for 1 hour per lunar-touched druid level or until she selects another aura. Generating an aura is a standard action which does not provoke an attack of opportunity. A lunar-touched druid can have only one aura active at a time. Any time an aura ability requires a saving throw, the DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 the lunar-touched druid’s level + her Wisdom modifier. A lunar-touched druid can use this ability an additional time per day at 6th level and every four levels thereafter, for a total of five times per day at 18th level. The lunar auras are as follows: Aura of Clarity and Confusion: While under the influence of this aura, a lunar-touched druid gains a +2 insight bonus to attack rolls, caster level checks, concentration checks, and Will saves. This bonus increases by +1 at 6th and 10th level. Additionally, when a lunar-touched druid rolls a natural 20 on a melee attack roll against a target while this aura is active, the target must make a successful Will save or suffer the dazed condition for 1 round. At 16th level, a creature failing its Will save gains the confused condition for a number of rounds equal to the lunar-touched druid’s Wisdom modifier instead. When a creature rolls a natural 1 on its melee attack roll against the lunar-touched druid while this aura is in effect, the creature becomes distracted, losing its Dexterity bonus to AC and gaining the flat-footed condition until the start of its next turn. (There is no save for this effect.) At 12th level, all enemies beginning their turn within 5 feet of a lunar-touched druid under the influence of this aura must make a successful Will save or become hesitant, suffering a -2 circumstance penalty on attack rolls while within the aura and for 1 round after leaving it. A creature that successfully saves against this effect is immune to the same druid’s aura for 24 hours. The effects requiring Will saves from this ability are mind-affecting effects. Aura of Frost and Flame: When assuming this aura, a lunar-touched druid must decide whether it will be a frost or flame aura. The frost or flame component does not change for the duration of the aura. While under the influence of this aura, a lunar-touched druid gains the benefits of endure elements, and inflicts 3 additional points of either cold (frost) or fire (flame) damage on successful melee attacks. This bonus damage automatically bypasses any energy resistance the target might have. It increases by 3 at 6th and 10th level. Additionally, when a lunar-touched druid rolls a natural 20 on a melee attack roll against a target while this aura is active, the target must make a successful Fortitude save or suffer the fatigued condition as though suffering from hypothermia (frost) or heatstroke (flame) for 1 round. At 16th level, the fatigued condition lasts for a number of rounds equal to the lunar-touched druid’s Wisdom modifier instead. Unlike the normal fatigued condition, the fatigue caused by this aura disappears after the duration of the ability’s effect expires. At 12th level, a lunar-touched druid under the influence of this aura is considered to be constantly under the effects of fire shield, with the caveat that a creature striking the lunartouched druid with its body or handheld weapon only suffers 1d6 points of fire or cold damage. Aura of Liveliness and Lethargy: While under the influence of this aura, a lunar-touched druid gains a +5 foot bonus (untyped) to her land speed, a +2 dodge bonus to AC, a +2 morale bonus on Initiative rolls, and a +2 resistance bonus on Reflex saves. The bonus to speed increases by +5 feet and all other bonuses increase by +1 at 6th, 10th, and 12th level. Additionally, when a lunar-touched druid rolls a natural 20 on a melee attack roll against a target while this aura is in effect, the target must make a successful Fortitude save or suffer the staggered condition for 1 round. At 16th level, the staggered condition lasts for a number of rounds equal to the lunar-touched druid’s Wisdom modifier instead. When a creature rolls a natural 1 on its melee attack roll against the lunar-touched druid while this aura is in effect, it becomes sluggish until the start of its next turn, incurring a -2 penalty on Reflex saving throws and a -10 foot penalty to its speed. This ability cannot cause a creature’s speed to drop below 5 feet. (There is no save for this effect.) This replaces wild shape.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.light steps (ex): At 9th level, a lunar-touched druid learns to move while barely touching the surface underneath her. As a full-round action, she can move up to twice her speed, ignoring difficult terrain. While moving in this way, any surface will support her, no matter how much she weighs. This allows her to move across water, lava, or even the thinnest tree branches. She must end her move on a surface that can support her normally. She cannot move across air in this way, nor can she walk up walls or other vertical surfaces. When moving in this way, the druid does not take damage from surfaces or hazards that react to being touched, such as lava or caltrops, nor does she need to make Acrobatics checks to avoid falling on slippery or rough surfaces. Finally, when using light steps, the druid ignores any mechanical traps that use a location-based trigger. This replaces venom immunity.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.gravity bow (sp): At 13th level, as a swift action, a lunar-touched druid gains the effects of gravity bow for a number of rounds per day equal to 1/2 her druid level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. This replaces a thousand faces.
archetype-druid-lunar-touched-druid-drui.blue moon (su): At 20th level, a lunar-touched druid can have two auras active at a time, but she must expend two uses of the lunar aura ability to initiate the second aura, and the duration of the second aura is limited to 1 minute per druid level.

archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order: At 1st level, a nature’s muse selects an order which immediately grants a unique boon. Furthermore, the nature’s muse chooses one of the two spells listed as “novice” spells. This spell can be cast once per day as a spell-like ability with a caster level equal to the muse’s level. This selection is permanent and cannot be changed. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the arachnid: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a +1 bonus on Climb skill checks. Novice: magic fang, web bolt Adept: whip of spiders, web Master: spider climb, communal, web cloud
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the avian: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a pair of feathery wings that are not strong enough for flight, but act to slow a fall, reducing the distance fallen by 20 feet. Novice: commune with birds, winter feathers Adept: eagle eye, wing bounty Master: wing thorns, wooden wing shield
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the currents: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order can hold its breath three times as long as normal. Novice: touch of the sea, wave shield Adept: slipstream, water walk, communal Master: control water, ride the waves
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the dunes: Boon: When making a Fortitude save in conditions of severe and extreme heat to determine the amount of non-lethal damage suffered, a nature’s muse of this order doubles the duration between required saving throws and gains a +2 bonus to those rolls. Novice: cloak of shade, sun metal Adept: fury of the sun, heat metal Master: grove of respite, healing warmth
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the green: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a limited form of photosynthesis such that only 1/2 the typical daily nutritional requirements of food and water are needed to survive. Novice: entangle, goodberry Adept: climbing beanstalk, greensight Master: green caressHA, thorn body
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the infestation: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a +2 bonus on saves against disease. Novice: diagnose disease, remove sickness Adept: pox pustules, sickening strikes Master: fleshworm infestation, touch of slime
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the night: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains the equivalent of a full night’s rest in 1/2 the normal amount of time. Novice: restful sleep, sleep Adept: darkness, dust of twilight Master: darkvision, greater, vigilant rest
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the predator: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a +5 foot enhancement bonus to its land speed. Novice: deadeye’s lore, hunter’s howl Adept: acute senses, aspect of the bear Master: aspect of the wolf, burst of speed
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the scorpion: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a +2 bonus on saves against poison. Novice: delay poison, nauseating dart Adept: accelerate poison, pernicious poison Master: giant vermin, vermin shape ll
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the tempest: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains resist electricity 3. Novice: shock shield, shocking grasp Adept: aggressive thundercloud, gusting sphere Master: aggressive thundercloud, greater, ball lightning
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the volcano: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a +2 bonus to CMD to avoid bull rushes, overrun, and reposition attempts. Furthermore, you count as being one size larger than your actual size for the purposes of these, i.e. if you’re size Medium, you count as size Large, and a Small creature cannot bull rush you. Novice: stone fist, stone shield Adept: groundswell, stone discus Master: obsidian flow, volcanic storm
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.adept (sp): At 2nd level ( druid ), 5th level ( hunter ), or 7th level ( ranger ), a nature’s muse chooses one of the two spells listed as “adept” spells. This spell can be cast once per day as a spell-like ability. Furthermore, the nature’s muse can use his novice spell-like ability one additional time per day. This replaces woodland stride.
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.master (sp): At 15th level (druid) or 17th level (hunter and ranger), a nature’s muse chooses one of the two spells listed as “master” spells. This spell can be cast once per day as a spell-like ability. Furthermore, the nature’s muse can use his adept spell-like ability one additional time per day. This replaces timeless body (druid), one with the wild (hunter) and hide in plain sight (ranger).
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.novice (sp): Bard: This is gained at 5th level and replaces loremaster. Hunter: This is gained at 1st level. Ranger: This is gained at 1st level. Skald: This is gained at 6th level and replaces the rage power gained at that level.
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the fens: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains a +1 bonus on Swim skill checks. Novice: air bubble, mudball Adept: grasping vine, sickening entanglement Master: explosion of rot, slowing mud
archetype-druid-natures-muse-druid-arche.order of the glacier: Boon: A nature’s muse of this order gains resist cold 1. Novice: frostbite, snowball Adept: frigid touch, winter’s grasp Master: creeping ice, ice storm *Special note: progression for a nature’s muse bard archetype follows a slightly different time frame (see the Other Muses sidebar on the previous page for details).

archetype-druid-beastshaper.wild bond (ex): A beastshaper druid may not select a domain and must choose an animal companion. This ability replaces nature bond.
archetype-druid-beastshaper.endless forms most beautiful (su): At 4th level, a beastshaper gains the ability to infuse her animal companion with some of the beneficial qualities of an animal once per day. Her options for new forms include all creatures with the animal type. This ability functions like the infuse fauna I spell, except as noted here. The effect lasts for 1 hour per beastshaper level, or until the beastshaper chooses to end it. This ability can only be used on the beastshaper’s animal companion and has a range of 25 feet + 5 feet for every two beastshaper levels. Using this ability is a standard action that doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity. The form chosen must be that of an animal the beastshaper is familiar with. A druid can use this ability an additional time per day at 6th level and every two levels thereafter, for a total of eight times at 18th level. At 20th level, a beastshaper can use this ability at will. As a beastshaper gains levels, this ability allows them to infuse their companion with the forms of larger and smaller animals. Each form expends one daily usage of this ability, regardless of the form taken. At 6th level, a druid can use this ability to infuse her companion with a Large or Tiny animal, functioning like infuse fauna II. At 8th level, this ability functions as infuse fauna III, allowing the beastshaper to infuse her companion with elements from a Huge or Diminutive animal, or a Small or Medium magical beast. At 12th level, this ability allows the beastshaper to infuse her companion with elements from a Tiny or Large magical beast, functioning as infuse fauna IV. This ability replaces wild shape.

archetype-druid-critter-chitterer.call of the wild (ex): At 1st level, a critter chitterer develops a natural rapport with animals. This doesn’t take the form of a bond with a single animal, as it does with many druids, but rather an instinctual understanding of animal behavior that lets them communicate with almost any receptive animal. As a standard action, the critter chitterer can temporarily teach an indifferent or better animal one of the tricks listed under the Handle Animal skill. Teaching an animal a trick this way does not require a Handle Animal check, although commanding an animal to use a trick still does. Any tricks learned with this ability are forgotten 24 hours after being learned. This ability can affect a number of HD of animals per day equal to the critter chitterer’s class level and can be split between multiple animals. At 5th level, the critter chitterer can teach an animal two tricks per use of this ability. They can teach an additional trick for every additional 5 levels after. This ability replaces nature bond.
archetype-druid-critter-chitterer.tongue of claw and fang (su): At 13th level, a critter chitterer gains the ability to talk to animals at will, as though using speak with animals. This ability replaces a thousand faces.
archetype-druid-critter-chitterer.savage dominance (su): At 15th level, a critter chitterer can spend one use of their call of the wild ability to force their will on nearby animals. This functions as dominate animal with a target of one animal per level within a 15-foot radius spread. If one animal breaks the spell, the spell is not broken for the remaining creatures. This ability replaces timeless body.

archetype-druid-entomancer.chitinous bond (ex): An entomancer may not select a domain and must choose a vermin companion. This ability replaces nature bond.
archetype-druid-entomancer.vermin empathy (su): An entomancer can improve the attitude of vermin as a normal druid can with animals. Wild vermin typically have a starting attitude of unfriendly. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-druid-entomancer.clickspeaking (ex): At 2nd level, an entomancer gains Vermin Heart as a bonus feat. This ability replaces woodland stride.
archetype-druid-entomancer.imperturbable (ex): Starting at 4th level, an entomancer becomes immune to effects that would cause her to be sickened or nauseated. This ability replaces resist nature’s lure.
archetype-druid-entomancer.wild shape (su): At 6th level, an entomancer can use wild shape to turn into a Small or Medium vermin, as though using vermin shape I. At 8th level, the entomancer can take the form of Tiny or Large vermin, as though using vermin shape II. At 12th level, an entomancer can use wild shape to transform into a swarm of vermin, functioning as swarm skin, but not allowing her to split into more than one contiguous swarm. She doesn’t leave her gear behind when she uses this ability, and she can revert to her mundane form normally. The entomancer does not gain the ability to turn into an elemental.

archetype-druid-fist-of-the-forest.diminished spellcasting: A fist of the forests’ number of spells per day for each spell level is one less than normal (for example, a 4th-level fist of the forest can cast three cantrips, two 1st level spells, and one 2nd level spell per day). If this reduces the number of spells for a level to 0, she gains only the bonus spells for that level she would be entitled to based on her Wisdom score.
archetype-druid-fist-of-the-forest.unarmed strike: At 1st level, a fist of the forest gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. A fist of the forest may attack with fists, nails, elbows, teeth, knees, and feet. This means that a fist of the forest may make unarmed strikes with her hands full. A fist of the forest applies her full Strength modifier (not half) on damage rolls for all her unarmed strikes. Usually, a fist of the forest’s unarmed strikes deal lethal damage, but she can choose to deal nonlethal damage instead with no penalty on her attack roll. She has the same choice to deal lethal or nonlethal damage while grappling. A fist of the forest’s unarmed strike is treated as both a manufactured weapon and a natural weapon for the purpose of spells and effects that modify either manufactured weapons or natural weapons. A fist of the forest also deals more damage with her unarmed strikes than others, dealing unarmed damage as a monk of the same level.
archetype-druid-fist-of-the-forest.martial flexibility (ex): Starting at 4th-level, a fist of the forest can take a move action to gain the benefit of a combat feat she doesn’t possess. This effect lasts for 1 minute. The fist of the forest must meet all the feat’s prerequisites. She may use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + 1/2 her fist of the forest level. The fist of the forest can use this ability again before the duration expires in order to replace the previous combat feat with another choice. If a combat feat has a daily use limitation (such as Stunning Fist ), any uses of that combat feat while using this ability count toward that feat’s daily limit. At 6th level, a fist of the forest can use this ability to gain the benefit of two combat feats at the same time. She may select one feat as a swift action or two feats as a move action. She may use one of these feats to meet a prerequisite of the second feat; doing so means that she cannot replace a feat currently fulfilling another’s prerequisite without also replacing those feats that require it. Each individual feat selected counts toward her daily uses of this ability. At 10th level, a fist of the forest can use this ability to gain the benefit of three combat feats at the same time. She may select one feat as a free action, two feats as a swift action, or three feats as a move action. She may use one of the feats to meet a prerequisite of the second and third feats, and use the second feat to meet a prerequisite of the third feat. Each individual feat selected counts towards her daily uses of this ability. At 12th level, a fist of the forest can use this ability to gain the benefit of one combat feat as an immediate action or three combat feats as a swift action. Each individual feat selected counts toward her daily uses of this ability. At 20th level, a fist of the forest can use this ability to gain the benefit of any number of combat feats as a swift action. Each feat selected counts toward her daily uses of this ability. This ability replaces wild shape.

archetype-druid-green-rider.weapon and armor proficiencies: Green riders are skilled with a wider array of weapons than normal druids. In addition to the basic druid weapon proficiencies, green riders are also proficient with lances, shortbows, and javelins.
archetype-druid-green-rider.mount (ex): At 1st level, a green rider must select an animal companion as her nature bond. The creature must be one that she is capable of riding and is suitable as a mount (i.e. at least one size larger than the green rider). A green rider does not take an armor check penalty on Ride checks while riding her mount. The mount is always considered combat trained. This ability changes nature bond.
archetype-druid-green-rider.woodland gallop (ex): Beginning at 2nd level, a green rider may move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) while on foot or while riding her mount at her normal speed and without her or her mount taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect her. This ability replaces woodland stride.
archetype-druid-green-rider.ancient aegis (su): At 13th level, a green rider gains DR 3/ cold iron, increasing to DR 4/ cold iron at 16th level and DR 5/ cold iron at 19th level. This ability replaces a thousand faces.

archetype-druid-henge-guard.weapon and armor proficiencies: Unlike normal druids, henge guards are not proficient with light or medium armor. They are proficient with all shields, but must only use non-metal ones.
archetype-druid-henge-guard.ac bonus (ex): While not wearing any armor and unencumbered, the henge guard adds her Wisdom bonus (if any) to her AC and her CMD. In addition, a henge guard gains a +1 bonus to AC and CMD at 4th level. This bonus increases by 1 for every four henge guard levels thereafter, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks or when the henge guard is flat-footed. She loses these bonuses when she is immobilized or helpless when she wears any armor, or when she carries a medium or heavy load.
archetype-druid-henge-guard.nature bond (ex): A henge guard may not choose an animal companion. A henge guard must choose a druid -legal cleric domain instead.
archetype-druid-henge-guard.green trance (su): A henge guard can call upon her inner reserves of focus and mystical might, granting her additional combat prowess. Starting at 4th level, a henge guard can trance for a number of rounds per day equal to 8 + her Wisdom modifier. At each level after 4th, she can trance for 2 additional rounds. Temporary increases to Wisdom, such as those gained from trance and spells like owl’s wisdom, do not increase the total number of rounds that a henge guard can trance per day. A henge guard can enter a green trance as a free action. The total number of rounds of trance per day is renewed after resting for 8 hours, although these hours do not need to be consecutive. While in trance, a henge guard gains a +4 morale bonus to her Strength and Wisdom. In addition, she takes a -2 penalty on Reflex and Fortitude saves. While in trance, a henge guard cannot use any Charisma -, Dexterity -, or Intelligence -based skills (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride ) or any ability that requires patience. She can cast spells that do not have a casting time of longer than 1 round. At 11th level, the bonuses to Strength and Wisdom while in trance increase to +6. At 20th level, they increase to +8. A henge guard can end her trance as a free action and is fatigued after trance for a number of rounds equal to 2 times the number of rounds spent in the trance. A henge guard cannot enter a new trance while fatigued or exhausted but can otherwise enter trance multiple times during a single encounter or combat. If a henge guard falls unconscious, her trance immediately ends. This ability replaces wild shape.
archetype-druid-henge-guard.trance powers (su): As a henge guard gains levels, she learns to use her trance in new ways. Starting at 6th level, a henge guard gains a trance power. She gains another trance power for every two levels of henge guard attained after 6th level. A henge guard gains the benefits of trance powers only while in a green trance, and some of these powers require the henge guard to take an action first. Unless otherwise noted, a henge guard cannot select an individual power more than once. Any henge guard who meets the powers’ prerequisites can select and use trance powers. A henge guard may also take, in place of a trance power, any supernatural barbarian rage power for which they qualify, using their henge guard level in place of their barbarian level, and changing all references from rage to trance. Dominance (Ex): You can use wild empathy while in trance as a standard action. Normal: You can’t use Charisma -based skills while in trance, and wild empathy usually takes 1 minute. Overgrowth Wave (Su): Once per trance, as a standard action you may cause plants, shrubs, and even dormant seeds to erupt with the sudden growth in a 60-foot cone emanating from you. From the cone origin to 30 feet out becomes heavy undergrowth, while the area beyond the halfway point becomes light undergrowth. This ability doesn’t function in areas that cannot support plant life. Roiling Magic (Su): While in trance, targets affected by your spells must make concentration checks when using spells or spell-like abilities (DC equals the save DC of the roiling spell plus the level of the spell being cast) for 1 round. Targets that avoid the spell’s effects avoid this effect as well. Unearthly Glide (Su): While in trance, you move across the ground as though floating, as if under the effects of a feather step spell. Vibrant Metamagic (Su): While in trance, you gain access to a pool of 1 trance charge. You may use this charge when casting a prepared spell to add the effects of a metamagic feat you possess to it. This costs 1 trance charge per level increase of the metamagic feat being applied. The pool refills when you meditate to recover your daily allotment of spells. Special: You can take this power multiple times. Every time you do, the maximum number of trance charges increases by 1.
archetype-druid-henge-guard.wildvision (su): While in trance, you gain greensight 60 ft. Special: You can take this power a second time, extending the range of greensight during trance to 120 ft. You cannot take this power more than twice.

archetype-druid-ley-weaver.ley pool: As their familiarity with the basic energy of the world grows, ley weavers learn to directly manipulate the energies invoked but not always understood by other druids. At 4th level, a ley weaver gains a pool of ley points, supernatural energy she can use to power her abilities. The number of points in a ley weaver’s pool is equal to two less than her ley weaver level + her Wisdom modifier.
archetype-druid-ley-weaver.ley power: A ley weaver can select a ley power (see below) for which she qualifies in place of the following druid class abilities: wild shape (4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 20th), venom immunity (9th), a thousand faces (13th), timeless body (15th). This replaces the druid class ability the ley weaver gives up for this ley power. Ley powers are abilities that draw on the primal energy of the world. The standard druid has seve ral abilities that count as ley powers, such as wild shape and a thousand faces. A ley weaver can learn additional ley powers, which often replace non-ley abilities such as timeless body. Ley powers are divided into two categories: druid abilities and spells.
archetype-druid-ley-weaver.druid abilities: Some ley powers are standard druid abilities. Even if a ley weaver selects a different ley power in place of a standard druid ability, she can select that druid ability later as one of her ley powers. Wild shape deserves special note, in that its daily limit on a number of uses is now based on the ley pool instead of an extra time every two levels, but still, has a duration of 1 hour per ley weaver level.
archetype-druid-ley-weaver.spells: These ley powers duplicate the effects of a spell, and are spell-like abilities. A ley weaver’s class level is the caster level for these spell-like abilities, and she uses Wisdom to determine her concentration check bonus. Requirements: All ley powers have a minimum ley weaver level requirement to select them. A ley weaver who does not meet this requirement cannot select that ley power. In addition, an ability with a numeral after it requires all lower numbered versions of that ability to already have been selected. Activation: Most ley powers require the ley weaver to spend ley points; the exact amount is listed after the ley power. Ley powers that cost 0 do not require the ley weaver to have any ley points in her pool to use the ability. The saving throw against a ley weaver’s power, if any, is equal to 10 + 1/2 the ley weaver’s level + the ley weaver’s Wisdom bonus. 4th-Level Ley Powers barkskin (1 ley point) vine strike (1 ley point) wild shape I ( beast shape I, 2 ley points) wilderness soldiers (1 ley point) 6th-Level Ley Powers daylight (1 ley point) dispel magic (1 ley point) dominate animal (1 ley point) lily pad stride (1 ley point) water breathing (2 ley points) wild shape II ( beast shape II & elemental body I, 2 ley points) 8th-Level Ley Powers arboreal hammer (1 ley point) command plants (2 ley points) true form (1 ley point) venom immunity (0 ley points) wild shape III ( beast shape III & elemental body II & plant shape I, 2 ley points) 10th-level Ley Powers jungle mind (2 ley points) snake staff (1 ley point) tree stride (1 ley point) wild shape IV ( elemental body III & plant shape II, 2 ley points) wall of thorns (1 ley point) 12th-Level Ley Powers a thousand faces (0 ley points) blazing rainbow (1 ley point) share skin (1 ley point) swarm skin (2 ley points) transport via plants (2 ley points) wild shape V ( elemental body IV & plant shape III, 2 ley points) 14th-Level Ley Powers animate plants (1 ley point) control weather (2 ley points) fairy ring retreat (2 ley points) siege of trees (1 ley point) timeless body (0 ley points) 20th-Level Ley Powers wild shape VI (changes the cost of wild shape to 0 ley points) shapechange (2 ley points) world wave (2 ley points) winds of vengeance (1 ley point)

archetype-druid-mushroom-shepherd.fungal bond (ex): At 1st level, a mushroom shepherd develops a mystical rapport with plant life. This bond can take one of two forms: The first grants the mushroom shepherd one of the following domains or subdomains: Cave, Decay, Plant, Swamp. When determining the powers and bonus spells granted by this domain, the mushroom shepherd’s effective cleric level is equal to her druid level. A mushroom shepherd who selects this option also receives additional domain spell slots, just like a cleric. She must prepare the spell from her domain in this slot, and this spell cannot be used to cast a spell spontaneously. The second option is to form a close bond with a plant companion. A mushroom shepherd may begin to play with any of the plants listed below. This plant is a loyal companion that accompanies the mushroom shepherd on her adventures. Except for the companion being a creature of the plant type, drawn from the list below, this ability otherwise works like that of a standard druid’s animal companion ability. This ability replaces nature bond.
archetype-druid-mushroom-shepherd.plant companions: Each plant companion has different starting sizes, speeds, attacks, ability scores, and special qualities. All plant attacks are made using the creature’s full base attack bonus unless otherwise noted. Plant attacks add the plant’s Strength modifier on the damage roll unless it has only one attack, in which case it adds 1-1/2 times its Strength modifier. Some plant companions have special abilities, such as scent. Plant companions cannot gain armor or weapon proficiency feats, even as they advance in hit dice, and cannot use manufactured weapons at all unless their description says otherwise. As you gain levels, your plant companion grows in power as well. It gains the same bonuses that are gained by animal companions. Each plant companion gains an additional bonus, usually at 4th or 7th level, as listed with each plant choice. Instead of taking the listed benefit at 4th level, you can instead choose to increase the companion’s Strength and Constitution by 2. Hoplite, Agarician Starting Statistics Size Small; Speed 30 ft; AC +4 natural armor; Attack slam (1d6 plus poison ); Ability Scores Str 15, Dex 10, Con 15, Int 2, Wis 11, Cha 4; Special Attacks poison ( frequency: 1 round [6], Effect 1 Str damage, Cure 1 save, Con -based DC); Special Qualities luminescent lamella, powerful leap, low-light vision. Luminescent Lamella (Ex) The underside of a hoplite constantly glows with a soft blue light, equivalent to a candle. This is suppressed whenever a hoplite is laying on the ground or otherwise concealing its underbelly. Powerful Leap (Ex) A hoplite has a powerful set of rear legs, giving it a +8 bonus on Acrobatics checks made to jump. 4th-Level Advancement Size Medium; Attack slam (1d8 plus poison ); Ability Scores Str +4, Dex -2, Con +2 Mould Mutt Starting Statistics Size Small; Speed 40 ft; AC +3 natural armor; Attack bite (1d4 plus poison ); Ability Scores Str 13, Dex 17, Con 15, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 6 Special Attacks poison ( frequency: 1 round [4], Effect 1 damage to a randomly determined ability score, Cure 1 save, Con -based DC); Special Qualities scent. 4th-Level Advancement Size Medium; Attack bite (1d6 + poison ); Ability Scores Str +4, Dex -2, Con +2. Musheep (Mushroom Sheep) Starting Statistics Size Small; Speed 40 ft.; AC +2 natural armor; Attack gore (1d4); Ability Scores Str 10, Dex 17, Con 11, Int 2, Wis 14, Cha 7; Special Qualities low-light vision, scent. 4th-Level Advancement Ability Scores Dex +2, Con +2; Special Attacks spore burst, powerful charge (gore, 1d8) Spore Burst (Ex) As a standard action, a musheep can cause the mushroom on its back to emit a burst of spores into the squares surrounding it. Any creature adjacent to a musheep using this ability must make a DC (10 +1/2 HD + Wis modifier) Will save or be dazed for 1 round. Puffball (Floating Fungus) Starting Statistics Size Small; Speed 20 ft., fly 60 ft. (average); AC +1 natural armor; Attack thorn (1d4 plus poison ); Ability Scores Str 10, Dex 15, Con 12, Int 2, Wis 14, Cha 6; Special Attacks poison ( frequency: 1 round [6], Effect 1 Con damage, Cure 1 save, Con -based DC); Special Qualities low-light vision. 4th-Level Advancement Ability Scores Str +2, Con +2. Green Empathy (Ex) At 1st level, a mushroom shepherd can improve the attitude of a plant creature the way a normal druid can improve the attitude of animals. Wild plant creatures typically have a starting attitude of indifferent. A mushroom shepherd can also use this ability to influence an animal, but she takes a -4 penalty on the check. This ability replaces wild empathy. Toxicologist (Ex) At 9th level, a mushroom shepherd has become so infused with fungal spores that poisons often have no effect on them. They gain a +4 bonus to all saving throws against poisons. In addition, if they deliberately expose themselves to a poison and succeed on their saving throw, they gain a temporary alchemical bonus to the ability scores the poison would have damaged. This bonus is equal to the maximum amount of damage the poison could have done in a single round, and it has a duration based on the duration of the poison itself: if the poison has a duration measured in rounds, the bonuses last for the same duration. If the poison has a duration measured in minutes, hours, or days, it lasts for that many rounds. For example, a mushroom shepherd who deliberately consumed belladonna and succeeded on their save would gain a +2 bonus to strength for 6 rounds. If the mushroom shepherd is immune to poison, the DC of any poisons they expose themselves to is increased by 10. Although there is no risk to their health if the save fails, it is harder for them to activate this ability. This ability replaces venom immunity.

archetype-druid-vate.mystery: A vate gains access to a small range of Oracle mysteries related to the natural world. A vate must pick one mystery upon taking her first level of vate. Once made, this choice cannot be changed. Each vate must choose from among the following mysteries: Nature, Life, Solar, Heavens, Flame, Waves, Stone, Wind, Wood. This ability replaces nature bond.
archetype-druid-vate.spontaneous casting: In addition, to summon nature’s ally spells, a vate can channel stored spell energy into mystery spells she hasn’t prepared ahead of time. She can “lose” a prepared spell in order to cast any spell from her mystery bonus spells list of an equal or lower spell level.
archetype-druid-vate.revelation: At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, a vate uncovers a new secret about her mystery that grants her powers and abilities. The vate must select a revelation from the list of revelations available to her mystery. If a revelation is chosen at a later level, the vate gains all of the abilities and bonuses granted by that revelation based on her current level. Unless otherwise noted, activating the power of a revelation is a standard action. Unless otherwise noted, the DC to save against these revelations is equal to 10 + 1/2 the vate’s level + the vate’s Charisma modifier. This replaces all instances of wild shape.
archetype-druid-vate.final revelation: At 20th level, a vate learns the final revelation about her mystery, granting her amazing powers and abilities. The vate receives the same final revelation as an oracle of her level and mystery.

archetype-druid-oaken-fist.verdant spontaneous casting: An oaken fist does not spontaneously cast summon nature’s ally spells. Instead, an oaken fist can “lose” a prepared spell in order to cast any spell of the same level or lower from her verdant spells. The following spells comprise the oaken fist’s verdant spell list: 1st— goodberry, 2nd— vine strike, 3rd— resinous skin, 4th— explosion of rot, 5th— sturdy tree fort, 6th— transport via plants, 7th— transmute metal to wood, 8th— horrid wilting, 9th— wooden phalanx. This alters spontaneous casting.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.green-bonded: At 1st level, an oaken fist must choose the Plant domain (or any of its subdomains except decay) as her nature bond. This alters nature bond.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.verdant thoughts (ex): At 1st level, an oaken fist gains a +1 bonus on Will saving throws against mind affecting effects. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.natural climber (ex): At 3rd level, an oaken fist does not lose her Dexterity bonus to AC when climbing trees and she automatically succeeds on all Climb skill checks made to climb trees. This replaces trackless step.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.tree scamper (ex): At 4th level, an oaken fist gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against spells or effects that target plants or note a unique effect upon plants in the spell’s description such as entangle, spike growth, explosion of rot, or horrid wilting, for example. This replaces resist nature’s lure.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.wild shape (su): At 4th level, an oaken fist gains a new option for her wild shape. She cannot assume the form of an animal. Instead, she gains the oaken fist wild shape that allows her to assume a hybrid form in which she retains her own type, but her skin becomes bark-like and her arms and fists become longer and harder like tree limbs. In this oaken fist form, an oaken fist gains the following benefits: • A +2 bonus (untyped) to her natural armor class. This bonus increases by +1 at 8th level, and every four levels thereafter, to a maximum of +6 at 20th level. Two natural primary slam attacks made at her full base attack bonus which deal bludgeoning damage equal to the unarmed strike damage of a monk of the same level. An oaken fist adds her full Strength modifier to both attacks. A +2 enhancement bonus to her Strength. This bonus increases to +4 at 6th level and to +6 at 8th level. An increase of +1 to her bonus against mind affecting effects from her verdant thoughts ability. In oaken fist form, an oaken fist retains her ability to speak, cast spells, and hold objects such as torches or shields, but she cannot effectively wield weapons or manipulate fine tools such as thieves’ tools with her hands in this form. This oaken fist hybrid form functions in all other ways as wild shape, and for the purposes of interacting with feats, is considered to be a wild shape form. The one exception is that oaken fist form lasts 1 hour for every two druid levels rather than 1 hour per druid level. An oaken fist never gains the ability to use her wild shape ability to assume animal or plant forms, though her oaken fist form continues to evolve as she gains levels. An oaken fist’s ability to assume elemental forms is unchanged and progresses along the same schedule as a typical druid. This alters wild shape.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.deep roots and long limbs: Beginning at 6th level, the oaken fist wild shape becomes more powerful. An oaken fist gains the following special abilities at the listed levels while she is in the hybrid oaken fist wild shape: • Roots. At 6th level, an oaken fist can use an immediate action to send roots into the ground to gain a +5 circumstance bonus on her CMD against attempts to bull rush, drag, overrun, reposition, or trip her. The roots dissolve immediately after the check is made. Limbs. At 8th level, an oaken fist’s reach increases to 10 feet and she gains the constrict and grab monster special abilities. Dormancy. At 10th level, an oaken fist gains cold resistance 20. Regeneration. At 12th level, an oaken fist gains regeneration 2, but she can only regenerate a number of hit points up to half of her maximum using this ability for each use of oaken fist form. This further alters wild shape.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.flurry of limbs (ex): At 13th level, when an oaken fist is in her hybrid oaken fist wild shape form, she can make a flurry of limbs as a full-attack action. When making a flurry of limbs, the oaken fist can make one additional attack at her highest base attack bonus. This additional attack stacks with the bonus attacks from haste and other similar effects. This replaces a thousand faces.
archetype-druid-oaken-fist.acorn barrage (su): At 15th level, once per day, as a standard action, an oaken fist can exhale a gout of acorns in a 30-foot cone or a 60-foot line. The acorns deal 1d6 points of bludgeoning damage per oaken fist level. A successful Reflex save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your oaken fist level + your Wisdom modifier) halves the damage. This replaces timeless body.

archetype-druid-ancestral-conduit-druid-.sacred council (su): At 1st level, as a move action, an ancestral conduit can call upon their ancestors to provide council. This advice grants the ancestral conduit a +2 bonus on any one d20 roll. This effect lasts for 1 round. An ancestral conduit can use this ability a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom bonus. This replaces wild empathy and trackless step.
archetype-druid-ancestral-conduit-druid-.spirit of the warrior (su): At 12th level, as a swift action, an ancestral conduit can summon the spirit of a great warrior ancestor to allow it to possess them. The ancestral conduit gains a +4 enhancement bonus to their Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution, and a +4 natural armor bonus to AC. While possessed, the ancestral conduit’s base attack bonus equals their ancestral conduit level, and they gain the Improved Critical feat with a weapon of their choice. An ancestral conduit can use this ability for 1 round for every 2 ancestral conduit levels they possess. This duration does not need to be consecutive, but it must be spent in 1-round increments. This replaces the druid’s ability to take the form of a Huge elemental or Huge plant gained at 12th level as well as the one additional use of wild shape gained at that level. (Ancestral conduits never gain the ability to assume the form of a Huge elemental or Huge plant creature, and they gain one less use of wild shape per day than normal.)
archetype-druid-ancestral-conduit-druid-.spirit walk (su): At 13th level, as a standard action, an ancestral conduit can become incorporeal and invisible. While in this form, an ancestral conduit can move in any direction and pass through solid objects. The ancestral conduit can take no action other than to move while in this form. They remain in this form for a number of rounds equal to their ancestral conduit level, but they can end this effect prematurely as a standard action. An ancestral conduit can use this ability once per day. This replaces a thousand faces.
archetype-druid-ancestral-conduit-druid-.spirit strike (ex): At 15th level, any creature an ancestral conduit summons with a summon nature’s ally spell treats all of their natural weapon attacks as though they had the ghost touch special weapon quality. This replaces timeless body.
archetype-druid-ancestral-conduit-druid-.soul scourge (su): At 20th level, as a standard action, an ancestral conduit can summon the spirits of their ancestors to attack in a ghostly barrage, creating physical wounds on creatures in the area. The scourge has a range of 100 feet and is a 20-foot-radius burst. The conduit is never affected by this ability, and they can exclude an additional number of creatures equal to their Wisdom modifier from this effect. All other creatures in the area of effect take 1d10 hit points of damage for every ancestral conduit level. A successful Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 ancestral conduit level + Wisdom modifier) reduces the damage to half. In addition to taking damage, any creature that does not succeed on their Will save gains a number of negative levels equal to the ancestral conduit’s Wisdom modifier. This ability can be used once per day. This replaces the druid’s ability to use wild shape at will. (An ancestral conduit only gains seven total uses of their wild shape ability per day.)

archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.earth’s child (ex): At 1st level, a druid of the earth gains Terran as a bonus language. At 3rd level, she gains Sylvan as a bonus language. At 15th level, whenever a druid of the earth is in contact with the ground (worked or unworked sand, soil, stone, or clay) and she is the recipient of a spell or ability that cures hit point damage, she gains an additional number of hit points equal to her Wisdom modifier.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.flaying fangs (ex): At 1st level, a druid of the fang can extend her canine teeth as a swift action to gain a primary natural bite attack which deals 1d6 + Strength modifier damage and crits on a 20. If a druid of the fang uses her bite attack in conjunction with manufactured weapons, the attack is treated as a secondary natural attack. She can use these fangs for a number of rounds per day equal to 3 + her Wisdom modifier. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. At 15th level, whenever a druid of the fang damages an opponent with her bite attack, she flays the flesh for an additional 1 point of bleed damage.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.flame’s friend (ex): At 1st level, a druid of the flame gains fire resistance 1. At 15th level, the fire resistance increases to 5.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.networking (ex): At 1st level, at the start of every day, a druid of the hive can designate a number of creatures equal to her Wisdom modifier as her hive mates. (She does not include herself when determining this number.) Once per day, when casting a spell with a range of personal (or a target of you), a druid of the hive can select one additional creature designated as a hive mate to receive the benefits of the spell in addition to herself. The hive mate must be within 5 feet of the druid of the hive at the time of casting to benefit from the spell. At 3rd level, a druid of the hive can select two creatures designated as hive mates (rather than just one) to receive the benefits of a personal spell. At 15th level, up to three times per day, when any member of her hive (including herself) rolls a skill check, a druid of the hive can choose one other hive mate to roll the check as well. The better of the two rolls can then be used to determine the outcome of the skill check.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.versatile vine (su): At 1st level, as a standard action, a druid of the leaf can cause a vine (approximately the length of an arm) to grow from their body. The vine can be used to carry an object that weighs 5 pounds or less- it cannot make attacks with the object it carries. With a free action, a druid of the leaf can cause the vine to wither and fall off. Many druids of the leaf use their vine to carry a light source, potion, dagger, or some other useful tool. Retrieving an item carried by the vine doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity and requires a swift action. At 15th level, three times per day, a druid of the leaf can extend the vine up to 20 feet to deliver a touch spell.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.spew maggots (ex): At 1st level, three times per day, as a standard action, a druid of the scourge can expel maggots from her mouth in a 5 foot line. A creature caught in the line gains the sickened condition for a number of rounds equal to the druid of the scourge’s Wisdom modifier. A successful Reflex save (DC = 10 + 1/2 green faith follower level + Wisdom modifier) reduces the duration to 1 round. At 15th level, the line’s range increases to 10 feet, and creatures suffer the nauseated condition instead.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.elemental survivalist (ex): At 1st level, a druid of the storm is always considered to be under the effects of endure elements. At 3rd level, a druid of the storm gains electricity resistance 3. At 15th level, this resistance increases to 5.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.soul of the sea (ex): At 1st level, a druid of the wave gains a +1 insight bonus on Swim skill checks. This bonus increases by 1 for every three druid of the storm levels, to a maximum of +5 at 12th level. At 15th level, a druid of the wave grows gills, gaining the ability to breathe water as easily as air.
archetype-druid-green-faith-follower-dru.spider senses (ex): At 1st level, as a standard action, a druid of the web can attune her eyes to the dark, gaining darkvision with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour. If the druid of the web already has darkvision, the range increases by 30 feet instead. At 3rd level, and every three levels thereafter, a druid of the web can use this ability for 1 additional hour, to a maximum of 5 hours per day at 12th level. These hours do not need to be consecutive, but must be spent in 1 hour increments. At 15th level, a druid of the web gains the monster special ability tremorsensep with a range of 10 feet.
