Additionally, when using Acrobatics, the dragon lancer ignores fall damage equal to the height they successfully jumped. This replaces armor training 1 and armor mastery.
archetype-fighter-dragon-lancer-fighter-.spear specialty (ex): A dragon lancer must select Spears or Polearms with their weapon training.
archetype-fighter-dragon-lancer-fighter-.acrobatic prowess (ex): At 7th level, a dragon lancer’s jumping skills continue to improve. They add their level on all Acrobatics checks, and high jumps are no longer limited by their movement. Additionally, when a dragon lancer willingly falls, they take all falling damage as nonlethal and are never made prone after falling or missing a Branch Pounce attack. This replaces armor training 2.
archetype-fighter-dragon-lancer-fighter-.winged glide (ex): At 11th level, when jumping a dragon lancer can choose not to fall until the end of their next turn instead. This cannot be used in simultaneous turns until 15th level. At that point, they can maintain this ability for an additional simultaneous turn. This replaces armor training 3 and 4.

archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.mettle (ex): At 1st level, a guardian gains a Mettle pool that is refreshed each day. The pool’s maximum is equal to their Constitution modifier, plus any feats and special abilities that increases the pool maximum. Some abilities may restore points to this pool during the day. But the guardian may not have more points of Mettle than the pool’s maximum. The guardian may expend Mettle to gain one of the following benefits. As an immediate action they may gain a bonus equal to their Constitution modifier on the next non- Fortitude saving throw. The bonus must be used before the beginning of their next turn. As part of making a Strength or Dexterity check to gain a bonus equal to their Constitution bonus on that check. The guardian may restore a point of Mettle to your pool in the following ways. If they use the aid another action to assist an ally’s skill check and the ally would have failed the check without their action If the guardian uses the aid another action to improve an ally’s AC and the ally would have been hit without the their action If an ability which expends Mettle allows for the use of an attack of opportunity, the attack of opportunity allowed by that ability may be taken even while using the total defense action.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.valorous deflection (ex): At 1st level, when an opponent makes a melee attack against the guardian or an adjacent ally, they can spend a point of Mettle and a use of an attack of opportunity to attempt to parry the attack. The guardian makes an attack roll as if they were making an attack of opportunity. For each size category the attacking creature is larger, the guardian takes a -2 penalty to this attack. If the attempt is made using a shield attack, the guardian may apply any enhancement or ability bonuses to shield AC to the attack. If the attack result is greater than the attackers, the attack automatically misses. The attempt must be declared before the results of the attack are known. If this attack is made while they are using the Combat Expertise feat, fighting defensively, or taking the total defense action they may also add the bonus from those abilities to the attack roll to block an attack, but loses any used bonuses until the beginning of their next turn. Upon a successful parry, if the guardian has at least one point of Mettle they may make a riposte attack on the creature they parried as an immediate action, provided the target is in their threatened area. If the parry attempt fails, the attack is instead directed at the guardian at its normal result and the guardian is flatfooted and loses their shield bonus to AC if the shield was used in the attempt. This replaces the bonus feat given at 1st level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.behind me (ex): At 2nd level, the guardian may elect to place themselves in the path of danger in order to protect an ally. When rolling initiative, the guardian may select a target as a charge. This selection may not change for the duration of the encounter. Any time that they are within 5 feet of their charge, and the charge is the target of an attack, the guardian may, as an immediate action, enter the square occupied by the charge and receive the attack in their place. The attack automatically hits the guardian. The charge is placed in any empty square adjacent to the guardian of their choice. The guardian may activate this ability after knowing whether their charge will be hit. If the guardian suffers a critical hit as a result of using behind me they restore a point of Mettle. This ability replaces the bravery granted at 2nd level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.ever vigilant (ex): At 6th level, all squares the guardian threatens with a melee weapon, including just a shield, are considered difficult terrain for enemies. This ability applies even to jumping, flying, and incorporeal foes, as well as swarms, so long as the guardian wields a melee weapon or shield capable of affecting them. The guardian must be aware of the enemy to affect them. The guardian also provides cover but not total cover to adjacent allies if their square lies between the ally and the origin of the attack or effect that includes the ally as a target. This replaces the bravery granted at 6th level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.active defense (ex): At 7th level, a guardian may spend a point of Mettle as an immediate action to apply any shield bonus they benefit from to their CMD and touch AC for a number of rounds equal to their Constitution modifier. They may activate this ability even while grappled or otherwise restrained so long as they are still benefiting from a shield bonus. Starting at 11th level, the guardian may apply this bonus to themselves and one adjacent ally. Additionally, this ability now adds their shield bonus to Reflex saves during duration. Starting at 16th level, the guardian’s shield bonus always applies to their own CMD, touch AC and Reflex saving throws. They may now expend a use of Mettle to apply this bonus to up to two adjacent allies. If the guardian has levels in another class that provides this ability, their effective class levels stack. This ability replaces the armor training granted at 7th level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.always ready (ex): At 7th level, whenever the guardian rolls for initiative they gain 2 bonus points of Mettle that exceeds their normal maximum. This Mettle is spent first if the guardian uses any abilities which require Mettle. If they spend no Mettle before the end of combat these bonus points disappear when combat ends. The bonus points of Mettle gained increases to 3 at 13th level and to 4 at 19th level. This ability does not stack with other instances of this ability, however, any class that provides this ability stack with this class to determine the number of bonus Mettle.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.bulwark (ex): At 10th level, the guardian has learned to defend against some kinds of magic. If they are armored or wielding a shield they may expend a point of Mettle and deflect a ray effect that targets them as an immediate action causing it to harmlessly dissipate. If the guardian expends an additional point of Mettle they make a Reflex save against that ray using whatever the save DC vs the effect would normally be, even if it does not allow one. If the guardian succeeds they may redirect the ray to a target of their choice. The target must be within range of the spell as though the guardian was the point of origin. This redirection uses the same attack roll result by the original caster. This ability replaces the bravery gained at 10th level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.brace (ex): At 10th level, if the guardian succeeds on a Reflex save against a spell or effect while wielding a shield they may expend a point of Mettle as an immediate action to prevent that effect from affecting all squares adjacent to them as well as negating the effect fully on themselves. This ability replaces the bonus feat granted at 10th level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.implacable (ex): At 14th level, the guardian is no longer slowed by difficult terrain, whether natural, magical, or magically augmented. Additionally, they are not slowed by effects which reduce their base move speed, and become immune to the dazed and stunned conditions so long as they have at least 1 point of Mettle and remain conscious. This ability replaces the bravery gained at 14th level.
archetype-fighter-guardian-fighter.incredible recovery (ex): At 18th level, the guardian’s ability to recover from injury is truly extraordinary. They gain fast healing 1 when not in combat. This cannot restore hit points lost to starvation, thirst, or suffocation nor does it reattach severed limbs. This replaces the bravery gained at 18th level.

archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.spotter (ex): At 1st level, the sniper reduces the bonus to the DC of Perception checks due to distance by 1/2 their class level (to a minimum of +0 to the DC). Additionally, the penalty to ranged attacks from distance is reduced by the same amount, to a minimum of -0. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.shot from above (ex): Beginning with 3rd level, when making a ranged attack from a higher altitude than their target, the sniper deals +2 damage. These attacks ignore cover unless there is a ceiling or cover above the target. This ability replaces the armor training gained at 3rd level.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.hidden sniper (ex): Starting at 4th level, the sniper reduces the penalty to Stealth checks to remain hidden while sniping by half their class level. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 4th level.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.expert archer (ex): At 5th level, a sniper gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with bows. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 5th. This ability replaces the 5th level weapon training.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.camouflaged armor (ex): At 7th level, a sniper learns techniques to camouflage with their armor. They reduce the armor check penalty to Stealth checks from their armor by 1/4 their level (minimum 0). Additionally, if they take 10 minutes to apply camouflage to their armor, they gain a bonus on Stealth checks equal to 1/2 their class levels on such checks to avoid being spotted. This does not apply to Stealth checks to avoid being heard. Additionally, the camouflage only applies to one terrain taken from the ranger ’s favored terrain. To gain any of the benefits, the sniper must be proficient with the armor. This ability replaces the armor training gained at 7th, 11th, and 15th levels.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.arcing shot (ex): Starting with 9th level, so long as there is 40 feet of vertical clearance between the sniper and their target, they treat their maximum range increments as 15 range increments for projectile weapons and 7 range increments for thrown weapons. This ability replaces the weapon training gained at 9th level.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.camouflage (ex): A sniper of 12th level or higher can use the Stealth skill to hide in the terrain for which they used their camouflaged armor ability, even if the terrain doesn’t grant cover or concealment. This ability replaces the bonus combat feat gained at 12th level.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.horizon shot (ex): Starting with 13th level, as a standard action, the sniper can make a single ranged attack and ignore all ranged penalties on the attack, though it is still restricted by the attack’s maximum range. This attack can be used in conjunction with Vital Strike and other similar feats or abilities. This ability replaces the weapon training gained at 13th level.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.volley (ex): At 17th level, as a full-round action, a sniper can make a single bow attack at their highest base attack bonus against any number of creatures in a 15-foot radius burst, making separate attack and damage rolls for each creature. This ability replaces the weapon training gained at 17th level.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.hide in plain sight (ex): At 19th level, while in the terrain chosen when using the camouflaged armor ability, the sniper can use the Stealth skill even while being observed. This ability replaces armor mastery.
archetype-fighter-sniper-fighter-archety.weapon mastery (ex): A sniper must choose a type of bow for their weapon mastery class feature.

archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.flanker (ex): At 1st level, a strategic soldier may designate any square adjacent to them as the square they are occupying for the purposes of gaining and granting flanking bonuses. The strategic soldier may declare this square as a free action once per round. The next change in the same round is a swift action. This ability replaces the bonus combat feat gained at 1st level.
archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.sidestep (ex): At 2nd level, a strategic soldier gains Sidestep as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. This ability replaces all instances of bravery.
archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.interpose (ex): At 3rd level, a strategic soldier can take the damage dealt by an attack to an ally if they are adjacent to the attacker. The strategic soldier takes the damage and other effects of the attack as if they were the initial target. This ability is usable once per day at 3rd level, and an additional time per day for each 3 levels thereafter. This ability replaces the armor training gained at 3rd level.
archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.defending allies (ex): Starting at 7th level, anytime a strategic soldier uses fighting defensively, full defense, or Combat Expertise, they can provide the AC bonus to up to two adjacent allies. The allies don’t take the penalties to attack, but the strategic soldier does. This ability replaces the armor training gained at 7th level.
archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.reckless strike (ex): Starting with 11th level, a strategic soldier can eschew defense to make more dangerous strikes. They gain a +5 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 round. However, during the round, any attacks that hit them are considered critical threats. This ability replaces the armor training gained at 11th level.
archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.knock off-kilter (ex): Starting at 15th level, a strategic soldier can make a single attack as a full-round action. If the attack hits, the target provokes attacks of opportunity from any ally threatening the target with a weapon capable of performing attacks of opportunity. You can apply Vital Strike and similar feats to this attack. This ability is not usable on creatures more than one size category larger than the strategic soldier. This ability replaces the armor training gained at 15th level.
archetype-fighter-strategic-soldier-figh.punishing strike (ex): Starting with 19th level, a strategic soldier can make an attack of opportunity against a foe that deals damage to an ally. They must be able to hit the attacker and perform attacks of opportunity with their equipped weapon to trigger this ability. This ability replaces armor mastery.

archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.mettle (ex): At 1st level, a valiant commander gains a Mettle pool that is refreshed each day. The pool’s maximum is equal to their Charisma modifier, plus any feats and special abilities that increases the pool maximum. Some abilities may restore points to this pool during the day. But the valiant commander may not have more points of Mettle than the pool’s maximum. The valiant commander may expend Mettle to gain one of the following benefits. As an immediate action they may gain a bonus equal to their Constitution modifier on the next non- Fortitude saving throw. The bonus must be used before the beginning of their next turn. As part of making a Strength or Dexterity check to gain a bonus equal to their Constitution bonus on that check. The valiant commander may restore a point of Mettle to your pool in the following ways. If they use the aid another action to assist an ally’s skill check and the ally would have failed the check without their action If the valiant commander uses the aid another action to improve an ally’s AC and the ally would have been hit without the their action If an ability which expends Mettle allows for the use of an attack of opportunity the attack of opportunity allowed by that ability may be taken even while using the total defense action.
archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.test of valor (ex): At 1st level, the valiant commander expends a point of Mettle to issue a challenge as a free action to any creature that has an Intelligence score of 5 or greater. It must be intelligent enough to have a sense of pride, honor, and/or narcissism. It need not share a language with the valiant commander, as many creatures can understand a challenge and recognize a threat. This creature must be of a CR no less than the valiant commander’s character level – 2. While this challenge lasts, the valiant commander gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls, and damage rolls. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter these bonuses each increase by an additional +1. The test of valor lasts until the valiant commander or the target falls to 0 or fewer hit points or combat ends because either them or the target have surrendered honestly. If a cowardly knave surrenders as a trick, the valiant commander does not need to spend another point of Mettle to regain the bonuses of the effect. The challenge resumes with renewed fervor because the target has attempted to take advantage of your honor or reputation. When this happens the bonuses from the original challenge are doubled. This automatic regaining of your test of valor bonuses can only occur within the first hour after combat ends. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.always ready (ex): At 7th level, whenever the valiant commander rolls for initiative they gain 2 bonus points of Mettle that exceeds their normal maximum. This Mettle is spent first if the valiant commander uses any abilities which require Mettle. If they spend no Mettle before the end of combat these bonus points disappear when combat ends. The bonus points of Mettle gained increases to 3 at 13th level and to 4 at 19th level. This ability does not stack with other instances of this ability, however, any class that provides this ability is added to the effective class level to determine the amount of bonus Mettle.
archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.call to action (ex): At 8th level, the valiant commander gains the ability to rouse the minds and bodies of their allies. By spending a point of Mettle as a move action they can shout a word of encouragement and inspiration to their allies. All allies within 100 feet that can see and hear the valiant commander may immediately make a new saving throw against any mind-affecting ability, ability that impedes their movement, or ability that limits the kinds of actions they can take on their turn (this also grants a new check to escape a grapple, though this isn’t a saving throw). The ally gains a bonus on this new roll equal to the valiant commander’s Charisma bonus. If this new roll is successful the effect is treated as though the ally had succeeded on their original save. The valiant commander regains an amount of Mettle equal to the number of allies who succeeded their check or save, up to their Charisma modifier. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 8th level.
archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.death before dishonor (ex): At 11th level, the valiant commander gains Diehard as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. At any time while the Diehard feat is active, the valiant commander may expend a point of Mettle to suppress the staggered condition for the round. Any strenuous action still causes damage as normal. Additionally, if the valiant commander’s hit points are below their Constitution score, they may expend a point of Mettle each round to continue to act under the Diehard feat until they reach a negative hp total equal to their valiant commander class levels plus their Constitution score. During this time, they may still expend additional Mettle to suppress the staggered condition. If the valiant commander does not expend Mettle while still within this threshold, they are considered dying and stable for one round. If they do not receive healing within the round to bring their hit points back above their Constitution score, they die. This replaces the armor training gained at 11th level.
archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.to arms (ex): At 13th level, the valiant commander has learned to truly lead by example. As a full-round action that costs 2 points of Mettle, the valiant commander may make a single attack against an enemy. If it hits, this attack is treated as the feat Vital Strike, and each ally within 60 feet who can see and hear you is granted an attack of opportunity on a target they threaten or a target within the first range increment of a ranged or thrown weapon they are currently wielding. This ability allows allies with ranged weapons to make an attack of opportunity when they normally could not. This ability benefits from the Improved Vital Strike and better feats. This ability replaces the weapon training at 13th level.
archetype-fighter-valiant-commander-figh.overwhelming presence (ex): At 16th level, as a swift action the valiant commander may spend 2 points of Mettle to project their superior skill and strength of arms to all enemies, weeding out the weak and allowing only the strong to face them. All enemies within 60 feet of the valiant commander must make a Will save (DC equal to 10 + 1/2 their class levels + their Charisma modifier) or become shaken until the end of combat. Any creature that fails its save by 5 or more or has fewer HD than the valiant commander’s character level minus 4 is frightened for 1 minute. Afterwards they become shaken as long as they can see and hear the valiant commander. Regardless of the outcome, this ability can only affect a given creature once every 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect, though it can affect any creature with an Intelligence score regardless of immunity, in such a case the creature can only become shaken. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 16th level.

archetype-fighter-vengeance-bringer-figh.bringer of vengeance (ex): Starting with 2nd level, a vengeance bringer gains a +1 bonus on Intimidate, Perception, and Sense Motive against a target for whom you have been tasked with bringing vengeance. You also gain a +1 bonus on damage and attack rolls against the target. You must be tasked by an organization or other quest-giver to gain these benefits as decided by the GM. These bonuses increase by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-vengeance-bringer-figh.mystic backlash (su): At 4th level, a vengeance bringer punishes a spellcaster that attempts to affect them. Anytime they succeed at a saving throw against a spell that specifically targets them, the vengeance bringer sends a mystic reverberation back to the caster, dealing them 1d6 nonlethal damage. This damage increases by 1d6 every 4 levels beyond 4th. This ability replaces a bonus feat gained at 4th and 12th levels.
archetype-fighter-vengeance-bringer-figh.counterattack (ex): At 10th level, a vengeance bringer can make an attack of opportunity as an immediate action against an opponent who hits them with a melee attack, so long as the attacking creature is within the vengeance bringer’s reach or if the attack was a natural attack. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 10th level.

archetype-fighter-spellmarked-warrior-fi.spellmarked (su): Beginning at 1st level, the spellmarked warrior is inscribed with runes and tattoos that bind them to a spellcaster. They gain a resistance bonus on saving throws against spells and spell-like abilities equal to 1/4 their class level. This bonus doubles against mind-affecting spells. However, the spellmarked warrior automatically fails all saving throws on spells cast by their bonded spellcaster. Additionally, the spellmarked warrior gains a bonus to Intimidate checks equal to 1/2 their class level as long as their markings are visible. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level and all instances of bravery for the fighter.
archetype-fighter-spellmarked-warrior-fi.mystic defender (su): At 2nd level, the spellmarked warrior brings retribution to those that would harm their bonded spellcaster. They gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to 1/2 their class level against any enemy that attacks their bonded spellcaster. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-fighter-spellmarked-warrior-fi.keep fighting (su): At 9th level, as long as their bonded spellcaster is alive and within 30 feet, the spellmarked warrior is treated as having ferocity. Additionally, they can use a swift action to act normally on their turn. This ability replaces the weapon training gained at 9th level for the fighter.
archetype-fighter-spellmarked-warrior-fi.donate life (su): At 11th level, as long as their bonded spellcaster is within 30 feet, the spellmarked warrior can donate their hit points to the bonded spellcaster. As a swift action, the spellmarked warrior can give up to a number of hit points equal to their class level plus their Constitution modifier at once. This ability replaces the armor training gained by the fighter at 11th level.

archetype-fighter-beast-hunter.weapon and armor proficiencies: The beast hunter is not proficient with medium armor, heavy armor, or tower shields. The beast hunter gains proficiency with the bola, lasso, mancatcher, and net.
archetype-fighter-beast-hunter.tight catch (ex): At 2nd level, the DC for Escape Artist or Strength checks made to escape or break out of a beast hunter’s lasso, mancatcher, or net increases by +1. Additionally, the beast hunter gains a +1 bonus to opposed Strength checks she makes when using lassos and nets. These bonuses increase by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-beast-hunter.far catch (ex): At 3rd level, a beast hunter is able to catch creatures at a greater distance. Increase the range increment for bolas, lasso, and net he wields by +10 feet. This increases by another +10 feet at 11th level. The trailing rope on lassos and nets are likewise extended. This ability replaces armor training 1.
archetype-fighter-beast-hunter.effective catch (ex): At 7th level, when a foe entangled within the beast hunter’s net or lasso attempts a concentration check to cast a spell, the DC of the concentration check is increased by +5. Additionally, a creature tripped by a beast hunter’s bola attack must use a full-round action to stand. This ability replaces armor training 2.
archetype-fighter-beast-hunter.big game hunter (ex): At 11th level, the beast hunter is adept at catching unusually sized creatures. She may use lassos, nets, and mancatchers on creatures one size larger than normal without penalty. She may use lassos, nets, and mancatchers on creatures two sizes larger than normal without penalty at 15th level. Additionally, using the mancatcher, the beast hunter is able to pin a creature caught in the weapon. This ability replaces armor training 3 and 4.
archetype-fighter-beast-hunter.bring them down (ex): At 19th level when a creature is entangled or grappled by a beast hunter’s weapon they must make an immediate Fortitude saving throw or gain the dazed condition for 1 round. A creature must make this save again at the beginning of their turn each round they are entangled or grappled, with failure meaning they are dazed for that round. The DC is 10 + ½ the beast hunter’s level + his Dexterity modifier. This ability replaces armor mastery.

archetype-fighter-berserker.weapon and armor proficiencies: Berserkers are not proficient with heavy armor or tower shields.
archetype-fighter-berserker.fast movement (ex): A berserker’s base speed is increased by +5 ft. at 1st level and again at 3rd level. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-berserker.uncanny dodge (ex): At 2nd level a berserker gains the uncanny dodge ability as a rogue of the same level. This ability replaces the fighter’s 2nd-level bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-berserker.improved uncanny dodge (ex): At 6th level a berserker gains improved uncanny dodge. This ability replaces the fighter’s 6th-level bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-berserker.frenzy (ex): A berserker gains rage at 1st level and greater rage at 11th level as the barbarian class features. A berserker also gains rage powers as a barbarian of the same level. For any effects dependent on barbarian levels the berserker’s levels count as barbarian levels. This ability replaces weapon training 1, 2, 3, and 4.

archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.weapon and armor proficiencies: Gun fighters are not proficient with medium armor, heavy armor or tower shields. Gun fighters gain Exotic Weapons Proficiency (firearms) as a bonus feat. A beast hunter’s prey is often as dangerous as she is.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.gunsmith (ex): This functions as the gunslinger class ability of the same name. This ability replaces the 1st level bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.shoot fast (ex): At 2nd level, a gun fighter gains a +1 bonus to initiative. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.gun training (ex): This functions as the gunslinger class ability of the same name, except a gun fighter gains it at 3rd level instead of 5th level, and only once for one type of firearm. This ability replaces armor training 1.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.dead shot (ex): At 7th level, a gun fighter is able to use the gunslinger dead shot deed. They are only able to do so in a surprise round, or anytime a target is denied their Dexterity bonus to AC. This ability replaces armor training 2.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.opening volley (ex): At 11th level, when using the dead shot deed the critical threat range increases to 19-20. This stacks with Improved Critical, but only increases the range to 18-20 when doing so. Additionally, when using dead shot, modifiers to damage are multiplied by the number of successful attack rolls made. This ability replaces armor training 3.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.put them down (ex): At 15th level, when using dead shot, a gun fighter deals 1d4 bleed damage for each successful attack made. This ability replaces armor training 4.
archetype-fighter-gun-fighter.knock them down (ex): At 19th level, when using dead shot, a gun fighter is allowed a ranged trip combat maneuver attempt anytime they use the dead shot ability. They gain a +2 circumstance bonus to this attempt for each successful hit with the attack, and cannot be tripped themselves if they fail the trip attempt. This ability replaces armor mastery.

archetype-fighter-harpooner.harpoon expert (ex): At 2nd level, a harpooner gains a +1 bonus to Strength checks to control the leading rope of a harpoon, and the DC for Escape Artist checks to escape a harpoon he wields increases by +1. The bonus and DC increases by +1 for every four levels after 2nd to a maximum of +5 at level 18. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.sea familiarity (ex): At 3rd level, a harpooner is skilled in attacking aquatic targets from above the waves. Creatures that are swimming, treading water, or wading in water only have partial cover (+2 cover bonus to AC) in relation to the harpooner. Creatures fully submerged in water have only cover (+4 cover bonus to AC, +2 to Reflex saves) against the harpooner. Additionally, harpooners may use weapons in the spear weapon group underwater like projectile ranged attacks, taking the normal penalties for doing so. This ability replaces armor training 1.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.spearman (ex): Starting at 5th level a harpooner gains a +1 bonus to attacks and damage with the Spear weapon group. This bonus increases by +1 every four levels after 5th, to a maximum of +4 at 17th. This ability replaces weapon training 1.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.pierce the waters (ex): Beginning at 7th level a harpooner becomes more effective at attacking creatures underwater. His ranged attacks only suffer a -1 penalty for each 10 feet of water they pass through, in addition to any other penalties due to range. This ability replaces armor training 2.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.tether line (ex): At 9th level, a harpooner is able to tie off the harpoon, allowing him to keep the creature entangled and his hands free to continue to attack. On any turn after he has entangled a creature with a harpoon, he may choose to tie off the leading rope to a solid anchored object he is adjacent to. This special action provokes an attack of opportunity and takes a full-round action. If the creature is tethered to a vehicle (such as a boat or ship) it may make a Strength check opposed to the pilot’s Profession (driver) or Profession (sailor) check to move, pulling the vehicle along with it. The creature entangled by a tethered harpoon can escape through normal means. If the harpooner attempts to entangle the creature with another harpoon he gains a +2 bonus to attack and the Escape Artist check DC increases by +2. This bonus stacks with each harpoon entangling the creature. A creature entangled by multiple harpoons only has to successfully make an Escape Artist roll once to escape all of them, but would have to destroy each leading rope to escape through that method. This ability replaces weapon training 2.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.master of the waves (ex): At 11th level, a harpooner is a master at attacking underwater creatures from land or a vehicle. Partially submerged creatures have no cover bonus against the harpooner. Completely submerged creatures only have partial cover in relation to the harpooner. This ability replaces armor training 3.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.relentless hunter (ex): Starting at 13th level, a harpooner can wear down their targets. For each successful attack with a weapon in the spear weapon group on a creature entangled with a harpoon, that creatures a -1 Strength penalty, to a maximum equal to the harpooner’s level. This penalty can be removed by removing the entangled condition. This ability replaces weapon training 3.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.fluid throw (ex): At 15th level, a harpooner knows how to make thrown attacks through water as easily as he can through air. His thrown weapon attacks do not take any penalties from moving through water. They still take penalties from range. This ability replaces armor training 4.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.bleed ‘em dry (ex): Beginning at 17th level, anytime the harpooner successfully deals damage to a creature he entangled with a harpoon he deals 1 point of bleed damage. This damage stacks with itself and can be stopped by a DC 15 Heal check or through the application of any spell that cures hit point damage. This ability replaces weapon training 4.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.control the beast (ex): At 19th level a harpooner gains a +4 dodge bonus to AC and Reflex saves against creatures he has entangled with his harpoon. This ability replaces armor mastery.
archetype-fighter-harpooner.weapon mastery (ex): The harpooner must choose the harpoon as the weapon for this ability. This ability modifies weapon mastery.

archetype-fighter-highborn-fighter.weapons befitting his station: A highborn fighter is proficient with the dagger, shortsword, longsword, rapier, sword cane, and warhammer and with light armor and shields (except tower shields). This ability replaces the fighter’s normal weapon proficiencies.
archetype-fighter-highborn-fighter.noble training (ex): The highborn fighter gains 4 skill ranks + a number of skill ranks equal to his Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of the normal 2 skill ranks + Intelligence modifier at each level. Furthermore, Diplomacy ( Cha ), Knowledge (geography) ( Int ), Knowledge (nobility) ( Int ), Linguistics ( Int ), and Sense Motive ( Wis ) are all class skills for the tactician. This ability replaces the bonus fighter combat feat gained at 1st level.
archetype-fighter-highborn-fighter.force of personality (ex): At 3rd level, the highborn fighter adds his Charisma modifier, instead of his Dexterity modifier, to his Armor Class, Reflex saving throws, and CMD. Any condition that would cause him to lose his Dexterity modifier to his Armor Class instead causes him to lose his Charisma modifier to his Armor Class. He loses this ability if he wears medium or heavy armor, carries a medium or heavy load, or uses something other than a weapon befitting his station. This ability replaces armor training 1 and 2.
archetype-fighter-highborn-fighter.elegant strikes (ex): When using a weapon befitting his station, the highborn fighter gains a bonus on attack and damage rolls equal to his Charisma bonus. At 4th level, the maximum bonus is +2. This bonus increases by 2 at 8th, 12th, and 16th level. This ability replaces weapon training 1-4.
archetype-fighter-highborn-fighter.medium armor proficiency: At 11th level, the highborn fighter gains proficiency with medium armor. However, the armor must have at least 1,000 gp spent in addition to the normal cost in gilding, inlaid precious materials, jewels, and other adornments. These decorations provide no additional benefit but add greatly to the armor’s visual appeal. This ability replaces armor training 3.

archetype-fighter-holy-warrior.holy smite (su): A paladin is imbued by his deity to fight the enemies of his faith. When he does so he gains an attack and damage bonus vs. such creatures equal to his level divided by four, rounded down (+1 at 4th level, +5 at 20th level.) This ability replaces weapon training 1-5.
archetype-fighter-holy-warrior.holy weapon (su): A paladin is gifted a special weapon blessed by his deity to aid him in his battle against his gods enemies. This weapon counts as a magic weapon but has no other benefits at 1st level. At 4th level the weapon is treated as holy and as a +1 weapon. At 8th level the weapon can be used once per day to banish an outsider and gains +1. At 12th level it can be used once per day to outright destroy an outsider or undead who’s HD are 4 or more less than the paladins. At 16th level any hit from the weapon upon an evil outsider or undead whose HD are 8 or more less than the paladins automatically destroys the creature. At 20th level the paladin can use his weapon to open a gate to the celestial plane once per week and the weapons bonus increases by an additional +1. This ability replaces armor training.
archetype-fighter-holy-warrior.war horse: A paladin is aided by a powerful steed. At 1st level this steed is a heavy war horse with maximum hit points. At 3rd level the steed gains the celestial creature template. This ability replaces weapon training.

archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.skills: The iaidoka master gains Bluff as a class skill.
archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.one movement (ex): The iaidoka master gains the Quick Draw feat. Additionally the iaidoka master may return a drawn weapon to it’s scabbard as a free action. This ability replaces the 1st level bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.improved feint (ex): The iaidoka master gains Improved Feint as a bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.first to strike (ex): At 2nd level, the iaidoka master can always act in a surprise round, even if he failed to make a Perception roll to notice a foe, but is still flat-footed until he acts. Further, the iadoka master gains a bonus to initiative rolls equal to his iaidoka master level. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.strike the unprepared (ex): Starting at 9th level, the iaidoka master can make a strike so fluid and lightning-fast many foes do not even realize they are under attack. The iaidoka master may use the feint action against any creature, even non- humanoids and animals, without penalty. The iaidoka master gains a bonus to Bluff checks to feint in combat equal to his base attack bonus. Further, the iaidoka master may use the feint action as part of If he successfully feints in combat with a weapon he drew in the same round, he gains a bonus to damage equal to adds 1 ½ times his Strength modifier to damage, or double his Strength modifier if the attack is with a two-handed weapon. This ability replaces weapon training 2.
archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.critical first strike (ex): At 13th level, when the iaidoka master attacks for the first time with a weapon he just drew, he can make the attack an automatic critical threat. This ability may be used three times a day. This ability replaces weapon training 3.
archetype-fighter-iaidoka-master.one strike kill (ex): At 17th level, when using the Critical First Strike ability, the iaidoka master’s damage multiplier increases by one. This does not stack with anything that increases a weapon’s damage multiplier, with the exception of the Weapon Mastery ability. This ability replaces weapon training 4.

archetype-fighter-irontide-charger-fight.irontide armor (ex): At 2nd level, an irontide charger constructs a customized suit of abnormally heavy armor. Although the suit is augmented with a steam-powered drivetrain, only the irontide charger—through specialized training with the suit—can effectively use it, they reduce the armor check penalty of irontide armor by 2. An irontide charger’s speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor. The irontide armor is fitted with metal horns or tusks that give the irontide charger a primary gore attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. While anyone wearing irontide armor cannot wield weapons, the ironhide charger can integrate weapons from the close weapon group into the armor’s gauntlets at the weapon’s normal cost. It takes a minute and the proper tools to equip, remove, or replace a weapon integrated into the armor. If an irontide charger loses their irontide armor, they can replace it at half the normal cost by spending a week manufacturing a new suit. They must have the necessary tools and a workshop to do so. By modifying a suit of heavy armor, the irontide charger can reduce the cost of creating the irontide armor by 1/5th of the armor’s cost. This ability replaces the fighter’s bravery ability at 2nd level.
archetype-fighter-irontide-charger-fight.devastating charge (ex): Starting at 5th level, an irontide charger learns to use the momentum provided by his bulky armor to make his charge nearly unstoppable. While wearing heavy armor, the irontide charger can, while making a charge, overrun multiple creatures in the path of his charge. Overrunning a creature is a free action. If the overrun against a creature is unsuccessful, the irontide charger ends his charge in the space directly in front of the creature he was attempting to overrun. At 9th level, the irontide charger gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with weapons in the close weapon group ( gauntlet, heavy shield, light shield, punching dagger, sap, spiked armor, spiked gauntlet, spiked shield, and unarmed strike ) as well as with gore attacks. This bonus increases by +1 at 13th and 17th level. The irontide charger also adds this bonus to bull rush and overrun combat maneuver checks while wearing heavy armor and doubles the bonus while wearing ironhide armor. In addition, at 13th level, the irontide charger can make a trample attack, as per the trample universal monster rule, and is considered to be a Large creature for the purposes of determining which creatures the irontide charger may target. This ability replaces weapon training at 5th level.
archetype-fighter-irontide-charger-fight.charge mastery (ex): At 20th level, while wearing irontide armor, an irontide charger can attempt to overrun a creature of any size. When the irontide charger fails a combat maneuver check, if the target is no more than one size category larger than the irontide charger, it is pushed back 5 feet. As a free action, the irontide charger can make a primary attack against any creature it attempts to bull rush or overrun. This ability does not allow the irontide charger to trample larger creatures with its devastating charge ability. This ability replaces weapon mastery at 20th level.

archetype-fighter-navaja.stick it deep (ex): A navaja applies double his Strength bonus to damage when he attacks with a dagger, kerambit, kukri, punching dagger, starknife, or swordbreaker dagger. This ability replaces armor training 1.
archetype-fighter-navaja.pincushion (ex): When a navaja successfully attacks a creature with a weapon listed in the Stick it Deep class feature, he may opt to leave the blade sunk deep within the body of the enemy. For each blade affecting it, the creature suffers a -1 penalty to attack rolls and concentration checks, to a maximum penalty of -5. A creature may expend a standard action to remove all blades affecting it. Doing so provokes attacks of opportunity but all blades drop to the ground in it’s space and it suffers no additional effects. Alternatively, the creature may expend a swift action to remove all blades affecting it but it suffers 1 point of bleed damage for each weapon removed in this way. If it removes them in this way it does not provoke attacks of opportunity. This ability replaces weapon training 1.

archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.weapon and armor proficiencies: Siege engineers are not proficient with medium armor, heavy armor, shields, or martial weapons. Siege engineers begin with the proficiency with one siege engine of their choice.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.mechanically inclined (ex): Siege engineers gain Disable Device as a class skill. Further, a siege engineer gains a bonus to Disable Device checks when applied to siege engines equal to his siege engineer level.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.fine tuned trajectory (ex): At 2nd level, the range of the siege engines the siege engineer is the crew leader on increases by +10 feet. Every four levels thereafter the range increases by an additional +10 feet. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.siege commander (ex): At 3rd level, the siege engineer can be the crew leader for multiple engines at once. He may command a number of siege engines equal to his Intelligence modifier. When he is the crew leader of multiple engines he may give the command to fire all of them at the same time as a full-round action, making a roll for each engine. He may only be the crew leader in this way on ranged siege engines. He only counts towards the crew of one siege engine, but is considered the crew leader of all the siege engines he commands. For example, if he was commanding four siege engines that each required a crew of 1, he would count as the crew for one of them and three other crew members would work the remaining three engines, taking orders from him as to where to aim, when to reload, and when to fire. The crews on the siege engines he commands must be able to see and hear him. Alternatively, if he is the crew leader for only one siege engine he reduces the aim time by 1 and reload time by 2. If any of these is reduced to 0 it takes the crew a free action to perform the task. At 11th level, the time it takes to do both tasks is again reduced by 1. This ability replaces armor training 1 and 3.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.effective aiming (ex): At 5th level, the siege engineer halves all penalties due to range when using a siege engine. This ability replaces weapon training 1.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.worth two men (ex): At 7th level, a siege engine that the siege engineer is the crew leader on requires 1 less crew member, to a minimum of 1. If the siege engineer is commanding multiple siege engines, this reduces the crew of only one engine. At 11th level, and again at 15th level, the number of crew needed is again reduced by 1. If the siege engineer is commanding multiple engines, he may split up this reduction between multiple engines. This ability replaces armor training 2 and 4.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.best ammunition (ex): Beginning at 9th level, the siege engineer gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage with siege engines. Every four levels after 9th (13th and 17th,) the bonus increases by an additional +1, to a maximum of +3 at 17th level. This ability replaces weapon training 2.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.engineering expert (ex): Starting at 13th level the siege engineer adds his Dexterity modifier to damage when using direct-fire siege engines, and his Intelligence modifier to damage when using indirect-fire siege engines. These bonuses are doubled when damaging structures and objects. This ability replaces weapon training 3.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.find the weakness (ex): At 17th level, the siege engineer can have an attack from a siege engine he is the crew leader on be an automatic critical hit. He is able to do this three times a day. This ability replaces weapon training 4.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.keep them running (ex): At 19th level, when a siege engineer is a crew leader for a siege engineer he adds his Intelligence modifier to its AC, and its hardness and hp are doubled. This ability replaces armor mastery.
archetype-fighter-siege-engineer.siege mastery (ex): At 20th level, the siege engineer chooses one siege engine. He automatically confirms all critical hits with that siege engine, and the damage multiplier increases by 1. Additionally, the times required to aim and load are both lowered by 1. This ability replaces weapon mastery.

archetype-fighter-thrower.eye for distance (ex): At 3rd level, the thrower reduces range penalties he suffers with thrown weapons by 1 for every two thrower levels he possesses (reduces penalty by 1 at 3rd level, 2 at 4th level etc.) At 7th level, the penalty a thrower suffers when throwing weapons not designed to be thrown, is reduced from -4 to -2. This ability replaces armor training 1.
archetype-fighter-thrower.supple wrist (ex): At 7th level, the thrower is able throw weapons further and more accurately. Weapons thrown by the thrower have their ranges increased by 10 feet. At 11th level, the range increases once more by 10 feet. This ability replaces armor training 2.
archetype-fighter-thrower.strong arm (ex): Starting at 11th level, the thrower adds his full Strength modifier to attack and 1 ½ times his Strength modifier to damage with thrown weapons. If the weapon is thrown with both hands he adds double his Strength modifier. This ability replaces armor training 3.
archetype-fighter-thrower.trick throw (ex): At 15th level, the thrower may make some combat maneuvers against opponents within the first range increment of the thrown weapon. He may attempt any of the following maneuvers: Bull Rush, Dirty Trick, Disarm, Grapple, Sunder, or Trip. If the thrower successfully grapples an opponent with this ability he does not gain the grappled condition but he is not able to maintain the grapple in the next round. The grappled creature may attempt to escape on its turn, making either an Escape Artist check or a grapple check to break the grapple as normal. This ability replaces armor training 4.
archetype-fighter-thrower.return to sender (ex): At 19th level, the thrower may catch a thrown weapon and return the attack as an immediate action. The weapon does not need to be aimed that him but the original target must at least be adjacent. The thrower must have at one hand free to do this. This ability replaces armor mastery.

archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.spiked tackle (ex): At 1st level, when a wicked wrecker is successful in performing a bull rush or reposition combat maneuver, he may make an attack with his armor spikes or spiked gauntlet as a swift action against the target of the maneuver before the effects of the combat maneuver happen. This attack is done with the highest attack bonus. Additionally, damage from armor spikes and spiked gauntlets counts as piercing and bludgeoning. This ability replaces the 1st level bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.body toss (ex): At 2nd level, a wicked wrecker becomes skilled in grabbing foes and tossing them around. A wicked wrecker gains a +1 bonus to CMB when performing bull rush, grapple, and reposition combat maneuver attempts. A wicked wrecker also gains a +1 bonus to CMD when attacked with bull rush, grapple, and reposition combat maneuver attempts. These bonuses increase by +1 for every four levels after 2nd (to a maximum of +5 at 18th level). This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.take down (ex): At 2nd level, a wicked wrecker chooses one of the following feats: Improved Bull Rush, Improved Grapple, or Improved Reposition. He gains this feat, even if he does not meet the prerequisites for it. This ability replaces the 2nd level bonus feat.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.maneuver slam (ex): At 5th level, a wicked wrecker is able to use the very environment around him in battle. When a wicked wrecker rolls a natural 20 on a bull rush, grapple, or reposition combat maneuver against an opponent that is adjacent to either a large unattended object (such as a table, wagon, or tree) or a wall, in addition to automatically succeeding on the combat maneuver, he may also roll a second attempt as if confirming a critical hit with a normal attack roll. If this check succeeds he then deals damage to the target and the adjacent object or wall, equal to his normal unarmed damage. Additionally, when a wicked wrecker damages objects directly, he ignores hardness of 5 and less and have a +2 bonus to damage against unattended objects. This ability replaces weapon training 1.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.living weapon (ex): At 9th level, when a wicked wrecker successfully moves an opponent using a bull rush, grapple, or reposition combat maneuver he can use them as weapons against other creatures in one square movement. A wicked wrecker may make an attack as a free action at a -5 penalty, using the moved creature as an improvised weapon against the creature they are slammed into. The attack deals 1d8 points of bludgeoning damage, assuming the moved opponent is sized Small. Larger or smaller creatures used as a bludgeon deal damage based on their size using this base damage. A size Tiny creature deals 1d6 points of damage, a size Medium creature deals 1d10 points of damage, and so on. A wicked wrecker deals damage normally to the attacked creature, with the moved creature taking an equal amount of damage. This ability replaces weapon training 2.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.superior wrecker (ex): At 13th level, a wicked wrecker can use Maneuver Slam if he rolls a 19 or 20 on a bull rush, grapple, or reposition combat maneuver. He deals damage equal to double his unarmed strike when using that ability, and this damage to objects ignores hardness of 5 or less. Additionally, when a wicked wrecker directly attacks objects he ignores hardness of 10 or less and gain a +4 bonus to damage. This ability replaces weapon training 3.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.greater living weapon (ex): At 18th level, a wicked wrecker is a master at tossing foes about. When a wicked wrecker uses another creature as an improvised weapon after moving them with a bull rush, grapple, or reposition the attack has a critical of 19-20 and the creature is considered one size larger when determining how much damage it deals. This ability replaces weapon training 4.
archetype-fighter-wicked-wrecker.adamant wrecker (ex): At 20th level, a wicked wrecker can use Maneuver Slam if he rolls 17-20 on the required maneuver checks. This ability now ignores hardness less than 15. Additionally, when attacking objects he ignores hardness less than 20 and gains a +6 bonus to damage. This ability replaces weapon mastery.

archetype-fighter-creche-defender-fighte.psionic shielding (su): At 2nd level, the creche defender gains a +1 bonus on all saving throws against psionic powers and effects. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd.
archetype-fighter-creche-defender-fighte.psionic armor training (su): At 3rd level, the creche defender can use his inherent psionic ability to reinforce himself against damage. When the creche defender sustains a hit from a physical weapon, he can expend his psionic focus to reduce the damage from that attack by 1 (minimum 1 damage). He must use this ability after the attack has been confirmed to hit but before damage is rolled. Every four levels after 3rd, the damage is reduced by an additional 1 point, to a maximum of 4 at 15th level. Additionally, the creche defender can expend 1 power point when expending his psionic focus to reduce the damage from that same attack by an amount equal to his Charisma modifier. Finally, the creche defender can spend one power point per round to move at his normal speed while wearing medium armor. At 10th level, he can use this ability to move at his normal speed while wearing heavy armor.
archetype-fighter-creche-defender-fighte.psionic weapon training (su): Starting at 5th level, the creche defender can select one group of weapons from those available to fighters for weapon training. As long as the creche defender maintains psionic focus, he gains an additional +1 bonus on attack rolls with weapons from the chosen group. If he expends his psionic focus, he can add +1d6 damage to a damage roll with a weapon from his chosen group. The creche defender can decide to expend his focus after making his attack roll but must do so before making the damage roll. Every four levels after 5th (9th, 13th, and 17th), the creche defender becomes further trained with another group of weapons. He gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls with weapons from the chosen group while maintaining psionic focus and can expend his psionic bonus to deal +1d6 bonus damage with them, as normal. In addition, the attack bonuses granted by previous weapon groups increase by +1 while maintaining psionic focus, and when the creche defender expends his psionic focus to deal bonus damage, that bonus damage increases by +1d6. The creche defender also adds the attack bonus to any combat maneuver checks made with weapons from his chosen weapon groups while maintaining psionic focus. This bonus also applies to his Combat Maneuver Defense when defending against disarm and sunder attempts made with weapons from this group while he maintains psionic focus.

archetype-fighter-tribal-defender-lizard.body shield: At 2nd level, when fighting defensively or using total defense, a tribal defender can, as an immediate action, grant an adjacent allied creature a natural armor bonus to AC equal to his own until the beginning of his next turn. The tribal defender can use this ability only when he is wearing no armor, light armor, or medium armor.
archetype-fighter-tribal-defender-lizard.covering guard: At 3rd level, when the tribal defender is fighting defensively or using total defense, allied creatures that are adjacent to him gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves. Every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, and 15th), this bonus increases by +1 each time, to a maximum of +4.
archetype-fighter-tribal-defender-lizard.get behind me: At 6th level, when an adjacent ally makes a Reflex saving throw, the tribal defender may, as an immediate action, roll the same saving throw as if he were the one subject to the effect requiring it. He must declare that he is using this ability before his ally has rolled the save. If this save is successful, the ally takes no damage or ill effects from the effect that triggered the save; however, the tribal defender suffers half of any damage that would normally be dealt by the effect. Failure indicates that the original target of the effect takes damage as normal, and the tribal defender still takes half damage.
archetype-fighter-tribal-defender-lizard.savior’s dash: At 10th level, when an ally within range of his base land speed is targeted by a melee attack, a tribal defender may immediately move up to his speed, but he must end his movement adjacent to the attacked ally. Using this ability also uses up the tribal defender’s move action for the coming turn.
archetype-fighter-tribal-defender-lizard.savior’s block: At 14th level, when a tribal defender uses savior’s dash, he can also make an attack roll to parry the melee attack that triggered his movement. If his result is greater than the attacking creature’s result, the creature’s attack against the adjacent ally automatically misses.
archetype-fighter-tribal-defender-lizard.unrivaled protector: At 18th level, a tribal defender is merely staggered rather than disabled or unconscious when at 0 hp or dying. While he is fighting defensively or using total defense, allies adjacent to him gain DR 5/— and are not subject to critical hits.

archetype-fighter-biathlete.weapon and armor proficiency: A biathlete is not proficient with heavy armor and tower shields. Instead, he gains the Snow Bum feat at 1st level as a bonus feat. This bonus feat is in addition to the bonus feat normally gained at 1st level. This alters the fighter’s weapon and armor proficiency.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.skills: A biathlete gains Acrobatics ( Dex ) and Stealth ( Dex ) as class skills, and removes Ride. This alters the fighter’s class skills.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.carver (ex): At 2nd level, a biathlete’s base speed while ice skating or skiing increases by +5 feet. His base speed while ice skating or skiing increases by +5 feet for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.double diamond (ex): At 3rd level, a biathlete can take 10 on Acrobatics checks made to perform tasks on ice skates and skis even while distracted or threatened. He can take 20 on these same Acrobatics checks once per day for every five fighter levels he possesses, up to a maximum of four times per day at 20th level. This ability replaces armor training 1 and 4.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.balanced fighter (ex): At 5th level, when a biathlete ice skates or skis at least 5 feet before attacking, he gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls. This bonus increases by +1 for every six levels beyond 5th. This ability replaces weapon training 1.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.fly like an eagle (ex): At 7th level, a biathlete adds his level to all Acrobatics checks made to jump, both for vertical jumps and horizontal jumps, while ice skating or skiing. This ability replaces armor training 2.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.passing shot (ex): At 9th level, a biathlete gains the benefits of the Spring Attack feat, so long as he is ice skating or skiing. He must still succeed on an Acrobatics check to perform tasks while ice skating or skiing. When he attacks, he is considered to be flanking his target if at least one ally threatens that opponent, regardless of the biathlete’s actual positioning. If he makes an attack with a slashing weapon, the attack deals 1d6 additional points of damage. This bonus damage increases to 2d6 at 13th level and 3d6 at 17th level. This ability counts as the Spring Attack feat for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites, but only while the biathlete ice skates or skis. This ability replaces weapon training 2, 3, and 4.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.big air (ex): At 11th level, a biathlete on ice skates or skis takes damage from a fall as if the fall were 20 feet shorter than it actually is as long as he lands on an icy surface in the case of ice skates or an icy or snowy surface in the case of skis. At 13th level and every two levels thereafter the distance he can safely fall increases by +10 feet. This ability replaces armor training 3.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.ten eighty (ex): At 19th level, a biathlete who is ice skating or skiing cannot be flanked. This ability replaces armor mastery.
archetype-fighter-biathlete.invert (ex): At 20th level, a biathlete gains the benefits of the Whirlwind Attack feat so long as he is ice skating or skiing. He may also use the Whirlwind Attack feat as a standard action. This ability counts as the Whirlwind Attack feat for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites, but only while the biathlete ice skates or skis. This ability replaces weapon mastery.

archetype-fighter-road-warrior-fighter-a.weapon and armor proficiencies: The road warrior gains proficiency in dire flails and spiked chains but is not proficient with heavy armor or tower shields.
archetype-fighter-road-warrior-fighter-a.mechanical expert (ex): A road warrior gains 2 bonus skill points per level that must be spent on Craft (mechanical) and Knowledge (engineering).
archetype-fighter-road-warrior-fighter-a.bonded mech (ex): The road warrior gains a bonded mech*, treating his class level as his pilot level. This ability replaces the bonus feats normally gained at 1st, 4th, 8th, 12th, and 16th levels.
archetype-fighter-road-warrior-fighter-a.full-throttle combatant (ex): Starting at 2nd level, the road warrior gains a +1 bonus on Will saves against fear and to Acrobatics checks attempted while driving. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces, but otherwise counts as, the fighter’s bravery class feature.
archetype-fighter-road-warrior-fighter-a.moving target (ex): At 7th level, whenever the road warrior is driving his mech and moves at least 30 feet in a round, both he and his mech gain a +2 dodge bonus to AC until the start of his next turn. If the road warrior’s mech has the nitroboost Mech Enhancement and he activates it before or during his movement, he instead gains a +4 dodge bonus to AC from this ability. The road warrior never gains the ability to move at his normal speed while wearing heavy armor from the armor training class feature.

archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.aetherite familiarity: An aether soldier’s intense training and long-term handling of aetherite makes them well acquainted with the material’s inner working, and with other materials producing similar effects. At 1st level, an aether soldier adds Knowledge (arcana) to his list of class skills and removes Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Handle Animal. In addition, he gains a +2 insight bonus on all Knowledge (arcana) checks involving aetherite.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.aether bond (su): At 1st level, an aether soldier gains a free masterwork melee weapon crafted from refined aetherite. This functions as a wizard’s arcane bond with a weapon. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.arcane strike: At 2nd level, an aether soldier gains Arcane Strike as a bonus feat even if he does not meet the prerequisites, using his fighter level as his effective caster level. An aether soldier may only use Arcane Strike with natural attacks, unarmed strikes, or his aether bond weapon. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.indomitable will (ex): At 2nd level, an aether soldier gains a +1 morale bonus to all Will saves to resist charm and compulsion effects. This bonus increases by 1 at 6th level and every four levels thereafter to a maximum of +5 at 18th level. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.arcane resilience (su): At 3rd level, whenever an aether soldier gains armor training, he may instead choose to gain a cumulative +1 bonus on all saves against spells, spell-like abilities, and supernatural effects rather than the benefits of armor training. This ability modifies armor training.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.arcane augmentation (su): At 5th level, whenever the aether soldier uses Arcane Strike he may sacrifice some of the enhancement bonus provided by the feat to grant his aether bond weapon magic weapon enhancements with equal value to the amount of enhancement bonus sacrificed. He may grant the following special abilities: ghost touch at 5th level, vicious at 9th level, limning at 13th level, and nullifying at 17th level. This ability replaces all levels of weapon training.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.shield against magic (su): At 19th level, an aether soldier gains spell resistance equal to 11 + his level. This spell resistance is always in effect and an aether soldier must spend a move action to willingly lower it. This ability replaces armor mastery.
archetype-fighter-aether-soldier.aether weapon master (ex): At 20th level, an aether soldier gains the fighter’s weapon mastery ability, but this ability only functions with the aether soldier’s aether bond.

archetype-fighter-consecrated-champion.class skills: A consecrated champion gains Knowledge (religion) as a class skill.
archetype-fighter-consecrated-champion.smite evil ( su ): Once per day, a consecrated champion can call out to the powers of good to aid him in his struggle against evil. As a swift action, the consecrated champion chooses one target within sight to smite. If this target is evil, the consecrated champion adds his Cha bonus (if any) to his attack rolls and adds his consecrated champion level to all damage rolls made against the target of his smite. If the target of smite evil is an outsider with the evil subtype, an evil-aligned dragon, or an undead creature, the bonus to damage on the first successful attack increases to 2 points of damage per level the consecrated champion possesses. Regardless of the target, smite evil attacks automatically bypass any DR the creature might possess. In addition, while smite evil is in effect, the consecrated champion gains a deflection bonus equal to his Charisma modifier (if any) to his AC against attacks made by the target of the smite. If the consecrated champion targets a creature that is not evil, the smite is wasted with no effect. The smite evil effect remains until the target of the smite is dead or the next time the consecrated champion rests and regains his uses of this ability. At 4th level, and at every three levels thereafter, the consecrated champion may smite evil one additional time per day, to a maximum of seven times per day at 19th level. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level and weapon training 1, 2, 3, and 4.
archetype-fighter-consecrated-champion.hallowed ( ex ): Starting at 2nd level, a consecrated champion gains a +1 bonus on Fortitude saving throws against negative energy. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.

archetype-fighter-harrier.class skills: A harrier gains Acrobatics and Knowledge (geography) as class skills and loses Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Knowledge (engineering) as class skills.
archetype-fighter-harrier.weapon and armor proficiency: A harrier is proficient with all simple and martial weapons and shields (but not tower shields). He is not proficient with any armor.
archetype-fighter-harrier.sure-footed ( ex ): Starting at 2nd level, a harrier gains a +1 bonus on saving throws against entanglement. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-harrier.fast movement ( ex ): At 3rd level, and every 3 levels thereafter, a harrier gains a +10-foot enhancement bonus to his land speed. A harrier in armor or carrying a medium or heavy load loses this extra speed.
archetype-fighter-harrier.shield mastery ( ex ): At 19th level, a harrier gains DR 5/— whenever he is using a shield. This ability replaces armor mastery.

archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.class skills: A knife fighter gains Acrobatics as a class skill and loses Knowledge (dungeoneering) as a class skill.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.weapon and armor proficiency: A knife fighter is not proficient with heavy armor or tower shields.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.deadly daggers ( ex ): At 1st level, daggers wielded by a knife fighter deal damage based upon his level and not the weapon type. The damage for Small, Medium, and Large knife fighters is given in the Table: Knife Fighter Dagger Damage. The knife fighter can decide to use the weapon’s base damage instead of the deadly dagger damage—this decision must be declared before the attack roll is made. (If the weapon’s base damage exceeds the deadly dagger damage, its damage is unchanged.) This increase in damage does not affect any other aspect of the weapon, and doesn’t apply to alchemical items, bombs, or other weapons that deal only energy damage. This ability replaces armor training 1, 2, 3, and 4 and armor mastery. Table: Knife Fighter Dagger Damage Level Damage (Small ) Damage (Medium) Damage (Large) 1st–4th 1d4 1d6 1d8 5th–9th 1d6 1d8 2d6 10th–14th 1d8 1d10 2d8 15th–19th 1d10 2d6 3d6 20th 2d6 2d8 3d8
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.unarmed training ( ex ): The knife fighter engages enemies up close and personal and often must use head butts, knees, elbows, punches, and kicks to supplement his blade work. He gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.parrying blade ( ex ): At 2nd level, a knife fighter wielding a dagger and wearing light or no armor and not using a shield gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC. This bonus increases for every four levels beyond 2nd (to a maximum of +5 at 18th level). This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.knife expert ( ex ): At 5th level, a knife fighter gains a +1 bonus on attack, damage, and combat maneuver checks with daggers. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 5th. This ability replaces weapon training 1.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.quick hands ( ex ): At 9th level, a knife fighter can focus all of his attacks from a full-attack action on a single target while wielding a dagger in one hand and his other hand is free. If he hits with at least two of these attacks, as an immediate action he may make a single disarm, dirty trick, or trip combat maneuver at the same target using his highest base attack using an unarmed strike. Unless he has the appropriate Improved Disarm, Improved Dirty Trick, or Improved Trip feat, this provokes attacks of opportunity. This ability replaces weapon training 2.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.double step ( ex ): At 13th level, while wielding a dagger, a knife fighter who takes a 5-ft. step and hits with at least one attack in a full-attack action may take another bonus 5-ft. step at the end of his turn. This ability replaces weapon training 3.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.lightning hands ( ex ): At 17th level, while wielding a dagger and his other hand free and adjacent to two or more foes, the knife fighter who successfully hits one foe with a dagger attack may, as an immediate action, make a disarm, dirty trick, or trip combat maneuver against one other adjacent foe using his highest base attack using an unarmed strike without provoking an attack of opportunity. He may use this ability only once per round. He may still use his quick hands ability if the situation allows. This ability replaces weapon training 4.
archetype-fighter-knife-fighter.weapon mastery ( ex ): A knife fighter must choose the dagger.

archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.hit dice and base attack: A man-at-arms’s hit die is a d8, and his base attack is equal to 3/4 of his level, as a rogue. This alters the fighter’s normal hit dice and base attack.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.weapon training (ex): A man-at-arms gains weapon training at 1st level, and every 4 levels thereafter (5th, 9th, and so on). The bonuses only apply when he wields a two-handed melee weapon. This alters weapon training.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.warbreaker (ex): Men-at-arms gain Great Cleave as a bonus feat at 1st level, even if they don’t meet the prerequisites (A man-at-arms must still meet the other prerequisites of feats with Cleave or Great Cleave as a prerequisite). At 2nd level, they no longer take a -2 penalty to AC when using Cleave or Great Cleave. At 4th level, they gain Improved Cleaving Finish. At 6th level, they gain Improved Surprise Follow-Through. At 8th level, they gain Cleave Through. At 10th level, they gain All-Consuming Swing. This replaces the bonus feats gained at the listed levels.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.slam (ex): At 2nd level, a man-at-arms treats his two-handed melee weapons as light, one-handed weapons when grappling, swallowed whole, or any other situation where such a weapon is required.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.adrenaline rush (ex): At 3rd level, when a man-at-arms confirms a critical hit with a two-handed melee weapon against a creature with total hit dice equal to or greater than his fighter level -3, or if he reduces that creature to 0 or fewer hit points, the man-at-arms gains temporary hit points equal to twice his fighter level. These temporary hit points last up to 1 minute. This replaces armor training 1.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.vital striker (ex): At 6th level, a man-at-arms qualifies to take Vital Strike as a feat, regardless of his base attack. At 11th level, he also qualifies to take Improved Vital Strike, and at 16th level, he qualifies to take Greater Vital Strike. He must still meet the other prerequisites for these feats.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.hero’s charge (ex): At 7th-level, a man-at-arms does not provoke attacks of opportunity for leaving threatened squares when charging. At 11th level, he can charge after moving only 5 feet. At 15th level, he can ignore difficult terrain when charging if he could reach his target under normal circumstances. This replaces armor training 2, 3, and 4.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.whirlwind attack (ex): At 12th level, men-at-arms gain Whirlwind Attack as a bonus feat, even if they don’t meet the prerequisites. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 12th level.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.colossus smash (ex): At 14th level, a man-at-arms ignores DR /magic with any two-handed weapon he wields. At 16th level, he ignores DR /adamantine, and at 18th level, he ignores any damage reduction other than DR /—. This replaces the bonus feats gained at those levels.
archetype-fighter-man-at-arms.bladestorm (ex): At 19th level, a man-at-arms can take a 5-foot step after hitting a creature that would grant him adrenaline rush with an attack, up to his movement speed. He does not draw attacks of opportunity for leaving threatened squares while moving in this way, but he must move after the attack resolves. He cannot, for example, hit two creatures with Cleave then move 10 feet. This replaces armor mastery and the bonus feat gained at 20th level.

archetype-fighter-chain-lasher.formidable chains ( ex ): At 2nd level, a chain lasher using a weapon in the Flails weapon group can make an Intimidate check to demoralize an opponent as a move action. At 10th level, he can do so as a swift action. At 18th level, he can demoralize a foe as a free action once per round. This ability replaces bravery.
archetype-fighter-chain-lasher.chain versatility ( ex ): At 3rd level, a chain lasher may use a weapon of his size from the Flails weapon group as a one-handed weapon. He may use a buckler or shield in the other hand. He must choose a single side of a double weapon to utilize but can use a move action to transition to the other side. This ability replaces armor training 1.
