They use the same spells per day as a paladin, though they may prepare any spell from the cleric spell list and the list provided by their domain. They use their Wisdom modifier for their spellcasting ability modifier. This ability replaces all instances of slow fall, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels, and quivering palm for the monk. For the unchained monk, this ability replaces the ki power gained at 4th, 10th, and 16th levels, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels and the style strike gained at 17th level.
archetype-monk-divine-ascetic-monk-arche.divine strike (su): At 4th level, a divine ascetic can deliver melee touch spells as part of a full attack action. At 8th level, they are also able to deliver ranged touch attacks as melee touch attacks during the full attack action.

archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.sense the soul (sp): At 1st level, a divine dragon monk can cast detect evil and detect magic at will as spell-like abilities using their class level as the caster level. This ability replaces the bonus feat granted at 1st level.
archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.smite evil (su): At 1st level, a divine dragon monk gains smite evil as a paladin of their class level. This ability replaces flurry of blows.
archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.touch of the fire dragon (su): At 1st level, a divine dragon monk can cause their unarmed strikes to burst into flame. As a swift action, they can deal an additional 1d4 fire damage per 2 class levels on their next unarmed strike. A divine dragon monk can use this ability a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.scales of the metal dragon (ex): At 2nd level, a divine dragon monk has divinely inspired resilience. Anytime they succeed on a spell effect that would impose a partial or half effect on a Fortitude or Will save, they instead are unaffected. This ability replaces evasion and improved evasion.
archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.resilience of the earth dragon (ex): At 5th level, a divine dragon monk is immune to stunning and sleep and effects that impose slow. This ability replaces purity of body.
archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.purity of the water dragon (su): At 11th level, a divine dragon monk, regains 1 hit point per hour. Additionally, they can make a Fortitude save once per hour to recover ability score damage as if resting for 24 hours. The DC for the Fortitude save is 10 plus the ability score to be healed minus the total damage to the ability score. This ability replaces diamond body for the monk. The unchained monk gains this ability at 12th level and it replaces the ki power gained at that level.
archetype-monk-divine-dragon-monk-monk-a.blending of the wood dragon (sp): At 15th level, a divine dragon monk can cast greater invisibility a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. The caster level for this effect is their class level. This ability replaces quivering palm for the monk or all style strikes for the unchained monk.

archetype-monk-healer-monk-monk-archetyp.lay on hands (su): At 3rd level, a healer monk gains lay on hands as a paladin of their class level. Instead of uses per day, they expend a ki point to use this ability and they use their Wisdom modifier in place of their Charisma modifier. This ability replaces still mind, purity of body, wholeness of body and diamond body for the monk. For the unchained monk, they instead gain this ability at 4th level, replacing still mind, purity of body, and the ki powers at 8th and 12th levels.
archetype-monk-healer-monk-monk-archetyp.mercies (su): When gaining a bonus feat from their monk levels, a healer monk may instead choose to gain a mercy available to the paladin. This ability modifies bonus feats but does not prevent another archetype from replacing those bonus feats.

archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.planar combatant (ex): At 1st level, a monk of many worlds gains Bluff and Knowledge (planes) as class skills, but they lose Knowledge (history), Knowledge (religion), and Ride as class skills.
archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.phasing strike (su): At 1st level, a monk of many worlds can make an attack that phases through planes and through their opponent’s defenses. As a swift action, the monk of many worlds can make a feint attempt with a bonus to the attempt equal to 1/2 their class level. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to their class level. At 6th level, the strike is always considered to have the ghost touch property when this ability is used. At 12th level, all of a monk of many worlds’ unarmed attacks have the ghost touch property. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.dimension slip (su): Beginning with 3rd level, a monk of many worlds can shift 5 feet into any unoccupied space as an immediate or swift action. If this shift would put them beyond the range of an attack or area of effect, they are unaffected but the attack is still made, if applicable. This ability is usable once per day plus 1 per 3 levels after 3rd. This ability replaces fast movement.
archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.dimensional charge (su): Starting with 4th level, a monk of many worlds can slip between dimensions while making a charge. This allows them to triple their speed on a full-round charge attack. At 12th level, a monk of many worlds does not suffer the AC penalty from charging and may turn any number of times while charging. This ability replaces all instances of slow fall for the monk and the ki powers gained at 4th and 12th levels for the unchained monk.
archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.far strike (su): At 6th level, a monk of many worlds can open a small gate with an attack. They may make a single attack as a full-round action to attack a creature within 30 feet. At 12th level, this increases to 60 feet. This attack can be modified by Vital Strike or its improvements. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 6th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.dimensional jump (sp): At 10th level, a monk of many worlds can cast dimension door as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces the bonus feat at 10th level, and diamond body for the monk, or the 10th-level ki power for the unchained monk.
archetype-monk-monk-of-many-worlds-monk-.multi-dimensional strike (su): At 15th level, a monk of many worlds can make their attacks through a dimensional portal they create and use their full attack or flurry of blows to attack any creature within 30 feet. The attacks can target multiple creatures or the same creature at their discretion. These attacks automatically gain the free feint attempt from the phasing strike ability. This ability is usable a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces quivering palm for the monk, or all instances of style strike for the unchained monk.

archetype-monk-mystic-fist-monk-archetyp.energetic fist (su): At 2nd level, a mystic fist can empower their strikes as a swift action to deal 1d6 energy damage. Doing so expends one of their daily uses of stunning fist. The energy damage is chosen between acid, cold, electricity, or fire, chosen when the ability is used. If the attack misses, the use of the ability is lost. At 8th level, the attack also deals an extra 1d10 of the energy damage on a critical hit, increased by the multiplier like a burst weapon. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-monk-mystic-fist-monk-archetyp.spell casting: At 4th level, a mystic fist gains the ability to cast spells. They use the same spells per day and spells known as a bloodrager, though they may choose any spell available to a sorcerer or wizard when learning spells. They use their Wisdom modifier for their spellcasting ability modifier. This ability replaces all instances of slow fall, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels, and quivering palm.
archetype-monk-mystic-fist-monk-archetyp.mystic strike (su): At 4th level, a mystic fist can deliver melee touch spells as part of a full attack action. At 8th level, they are also able to deliver ranged touch spell attacks as melee touch attacks during the full attack action.

archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.tattoo (su or sp): Beginning with 1st level, a tattooed monk gains a magical tattoo that empowers them. The tattoo choices are detailed below. They gain another tattoo at 2nd level and every 4 levels thereafter. These tattoos replace the monk’s bonus feats. Activating a tattoo is a swift action unless otherwise stated or if it is constant. The caster level, if applicable, for these tattoos is equal to the tattooed monk’s class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.bamboo or bear (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to his Constitution score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.bat or orchid (su): A character with this tattoo gains the power of good fortune, usable once per day. This ability allows the tattooed monk to reroll one d20 roll that they have just made. The character must take the result of the reroll, even if it’s worse than the original roll. The character must declare the reroll before the result of the original roll has been determined.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.black star or centipede (sp): Once per week, a character with this tattoo can cast shadow walk as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level. This ability allows the tattooed monk to cross great distances, but they must end their journey on the material plane. A tattooed monk must be at least 10th level to gain this tattoo.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.bull or oni (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Strength score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.cat or fire (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Dexterity score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.chameleon or kitsune (sp): A character with this tattoo can use an alter self effect once per day per tattoo they possess. This benefit lasts for 1 hour per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.cherry blossom or eagle (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Charisma score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.chrysanthemum or peony (su): Every hour that a character with this tattoo is in direct sunlight, they heal a number of hit points equal to their level. A daylight spell does not provoke this fast healing; the character must be exposed to real sunlight.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.crab or tortoise (su): A character with this tattoo gains damage reduction 2/magic. This damage reduction improves by 2 for each additional tattoo they possess.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.crescent moon or ghost (sp): Once per day, a character with this tattoo can use ethereal jaunt as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level. A tattooed monk must be at least 14th level to gain this tattoo.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.deer or lion (su): A character with this tattoo gains the Diehard feat.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.dragon or tiger (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can fight unarmed with a +1 bonus on all attack rolls and deal an extra 1d6 points of damage with a successful attack. This burst of martial arts ferocity lasts for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.dragonfly or wind (su): Once per day, a character with this tattoo gains a dodge bonus to their AC equal to the number of tattoos they possess. This benefit lasts for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.falcon or historical hero (su): A character with this tattoo is immune to fear (magical or otherwise). Allies within 10 feet of them gain a morale bonus on their saving throws against fear effects equal to the tattooed monk’s Charisma bonus (if any) plus the number of tattoos they possess.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.fox or snake (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Intelligence score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.full moon or mystic knot (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can gain a +2 luck bonus on a single attack roll, skill check, or ability check.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.ginseng or sun (su): A character with this tattoo can heal wounds in another character by touch. Each day they can heal 1d6 hit points per tattoo they possess. A tattooed monk cannot heal themselves with this ability. This tattoo is usable a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.horse or wasp (sp): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can use haste on themselves for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.lotus or spider (su): To use this tattoo, a character must have the Stunning Fist feat. Instead of a Stunning Fist attack, a character with this tattoo can make an attack that delivers a contact poison. The poison’s save DC is equal to 10 + the tattooed monk’s class level + their Constitution modifier. The poison’s initial and secondary damage is 2 points of Constitution damage. Using this tattoo counts as one of the character’s Stunning Fist attacks for that day.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.monkey or spy (su): A character with this tattoo gains a +1 competence bonus per tattoo they possess on all Acrobatics, Climb, Disable Device, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth checks.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.mountain or pine tree (su): A character with this tattoo can activate it to take on the immovability for as much as 1 round per class level, gaining phenomenal durability though they cannot move from the spot where they stand. They gain a +4 bonus to their Constitution and Wisdom scores. The increase in Constitution increases the tattooed monk’s hit points by 2 points per level, but these hit points go away when the ability’s duration expires or when the character chooses to end it as a free action. These extra hit points are not lost first the way temporary hit points are. While using this tattoo, the tattooed monk takes a –20 penalty on any Dexterity -based skill checks and reduces their speed to 10. They are immune to bull rush and trip attacks. The tattooed monk may use this ability once per day per tattoo they possess.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.ocean or sky (su): A character with this tattoo never needs to eat, sleep, or drink.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.owl or tidal wave (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Wisdom score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.phoenix or yin yang (su): A character with this tattoo gains SR equal to their class level + 15. A tattooed monk must be at least 10th level to gain this tattoo.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.rabbit or scorpion (su): As an immediate action usable once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can force an opponent attacking them to use their lowest ability score modifier instead of their Strength or Dexterity score modifier when making the attack roll. The tattooed monk must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed in order to use this ability.
archetype-monk-tattooed-monk-monk-archet.thief or white mask (su): A character with this tattoo is immune to detect thoughts, detect lies, and any attempt to magically discern their alignment. They also gain a +10 bonus on all Bluff checks.

archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.blind-fight: At 1st level, a transcendent monk gains Blind-Fight as a bonus feat. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level.
archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.uncanny dodge (ex): At 2nd level, a transcendent monk gains the ability to react to danger before their senses would normally allow them to do so. They cannot be caught flatfooted, nor do they lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A transcendent monk with this ability can still lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action. If a transcendent monk already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge instead. This ability replaces evasion.
archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.preternatural sense (ex): At 3rd level, a transcendent monk gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC against attacks by traps. Additionally, they gain a +1 bonus on Perception checks to avoid being surprised by a foe. These bonuses increase by 1 every 3 levels thereafter (to a maximum of +6 at 18th level). This ability counts as trap sense for any feat or class prerequisite. The bonuses gained from this ability stack with those gained from trap sense (if the transcendent monk has trap sense from another class). This ability replaces still mind.
archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.blindsense (ex): At 5th level, a transcendent monk gains blindsense out to 20 feet. This ability replaces purity of body.
archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.cast out the mind (sp): At 7th level, a transcendent monk can cast scrying as a spell-like ability once per day. The transcendent monk uses their class level and their Wisdom modifier for the spell. This ability replaces wholeness of body.
archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.improved uncanny dodge (ex): At 9th level, a transcendent monk can no longer be flanked. This defense denies enemies the ability to sneak attack the transcendent by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least 4 more levels in a class that provides sneak attack than the transcendent monk has monk levels. If the transcendent monk also has uncanny dodge from another class, levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum level required to flank the transcendent monk. This ability replaces improved evasion.
archetype-monk-transcendent-monk-monk-ar.blindsight (ex): At 10th level, a transcendent monk gains blindsight out to 20 feet in place of their blindsense. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 10th level.

archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.spiritual frenzy (ex): At 1st level, a warrior-monk can enter a religiously-inspired frenzy of combat. This frenzy lasts for 1 minute and can be used a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. While in this frenzy, the warrior-monk gains a +4 morale bonus to Strength and Dexterity and a +2 morale bonus to Will saves. Additionally, they gain use of their flurry of blows and fast movement abilities. Those two abilities are not usable outside of their spiritual frenzy. Entering this frenzy is a free action usable on their turn. While in this frenzy, the warrior-monk is unable to use any Charisma -, Wisdom -, or Intelligence -based skills, cast spells, or use any ability or feat that requires concentration, like Combat Expertise. The warrior-monk can end their spiritual frenzy at any time as a free action. At the end of this frenzy, the warrior-monk is fatigued for the number of rounds spent in the spiritual frenzy. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level and modifies flurry of blows and fast movement.
archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.focused weapon (ex): At 1st level, a warrior-monk is trained in the use of a weapon of their religious order. They choose one melee weapon, which cannot be changed later. They gain Weapon Focus for this weapon and treat it as a monk weapon. The weapon’s damage is treated as the greater of the weapon’s normal damage or their unarmed damage. Any abilities or feats delivered through a monk’s unarmed strike can be delivered through the focused weapon. The traditional weapon for these warrior-monks is the naginata. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.diehard (ex): At 2nd level, a warrior-monk hones their body and mind to be resilient in combat. They gain Diehard as a bonus feat. If they are using spiritual frenzy, they are not staggered while below 0 hp. This ability replaces evasion.
archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.mettle (ex): At 9th level, a warrior-monk becomes very resilient in their body and mind. Anytime they succeed on a spell effect that would impose a partial effect on a Fortitude or Will save, they instead are unaffected. This ability replaces improved evasion.
archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.greater spiritual frenzy (ex): At 12th level, a warrior-monk increases the bonuses to Strength and Dexterity gained from spiritual frenzy to +6 and the bonus to Will saves increases to +3. This ability replaces abundant step.
archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.tireless spiritual frenzy (ex): At 17th level, a warrior-monk is no longer fatigued when ending their spiritual frenzy. This ability replaces timeless body.
archetype-monk-warrior-monk-monk-archety.master spiritual frenzy (ex): At 20th level, a warrior-monk’s frenzy is beyond compare. The bonuses to Strength and Dexterity from their spiritual frenzy increase to +8, and their bonus to Will saves increases to +4. This ability replaces perfect self.

archetype-monk-grounded-spirit-monk-arch.temper the ephemeral (su): A grounded spirit understands the impact of magic on the world but also knows that magic is just another force of nature no different than the wind and can be overcome like any other. A grounded spirit uses Intelligence in place of Wisdom to determine the effectiveness of all monk abilities that normally rely on Wisdom.
archetype-monk-grounded-spirit-monk-arch.spellhardened (su): The bonus a grounded spirit gains to AC beyond their Intelligence modifier, gained at 4th level and every four levels thereafter, also applies on saves against spells and spell-like abilities. This ability modifies the monk ’s AC bonus.
archetype-monk-grounded-spirit-monk-arch.redirect the energy (su): At 4th level, the grounded spirit has learned to make enemy power their own. Whenever a grounded spirit successfully saves against an enemy spell or spell-like ability they gain a ki point. This does not allow the grounded spirit to have more than their normal maximum number of ki points. This ability replaces slow fall. Bonus Feats: Add the following feats to the list of bonus feats available to the monk at the listed level. This ability modifies bonus feats. 2nd – Disruptive 6th – Spellbreaker 10th – Shatterspell, Sunder Blessing 14th -Teleport Tactition
archetype-monk-grounded-spirit-monk-arch.stifle the flow (su): At 9th level, the grounded spirit can extend mastery of their own energy to the energies of others. Whenever an opponent fails their saving throw against the grounded spirit’s stunning fist, for one minute or until the next time that opponent casts a spell or uses a spell-like ability that opponent must succeed at a concentration check with a DC of 20 + twice the level of the spell being cast or the spell-like ability being used. Failure means the spell or spell-like ability fails and is expended with no effect. This ability replaces improved evasion.
archetype-monk-grounded-spirit-monk-arch.sever spirit (su): At 15th level, the grounded spirit has learned to block another’s ties to whatever source powers their magic. As a full round action a grounded spirit can send forth a wave of their own energy at a target within 30 ft. as a ranged touch attack or as a melee touch attack. If successful the target takes damage as though from the grounded spirit’s unarmed strike and must make a Fortitude save (DC of 10 + 1/2 the grounded spirit’s level + the grounded spirit’s Intelligence modifier) or lose the ability to cast spells or activate spell-like abilities. The target makes a new save each day when they would normally regain their spells or recharge spell-like abilities. This condition can be removed by a break enchantment spell or more powerful magic. Treat the caster level as equal to the grounded spirit’s class level to determine the strength of the effect for the purposes of such spells. This ability replaces quivering palm.
archetype-monk-grounded-spirit-monk-arch.ki expertise: The above expertise may be exchanged for any of the following monk abilities. high jump (5th), wholeness of body (7th), diamond body (11th), abundant step (12th), diamond soul (13th), timeless body (17th), tongue of the sun and moon (17th), empty body (19th), and perfect self (20th). If the expertise requires spending a charge of stolen magic the grounded spirit may substitute 2 ki points and if the expertise refers to spelljack level it uses grounded spirit level instead.

archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.weapon and armor proficiencies: At 1st level, an iron-skinned monk gains proficiency with the gauntlet, spiked gauntlet, cestus, and armor spikes. Additionally, the iron-skinned monk gains proficiency in light armor. This alters the monk’s weapon and armor proficiencies.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.iron skinned style (ex): An iron-skinned monk uses their unarmed damage progression instead of the normal damage for cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and armor spikes and they may make their flurry of blows or stunning fist attacks with these weapons. All abilities of the monk function while they are wearing light or no armor but still not while they are carrying a medium or heavy load. This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 1st level and an iron-skinned striker does not add their Wisdom bonus to their AC, though they still gain an improved AC bonus at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter even while wearing light armor.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.ki like iron (su): When the iron-skinned monk gains a ki pool (at 4th level for the monk) they gain a new use for that ability. When making a combat maneuver check the iron skinned monk may expend a point of ki to avoid an attack of opportunity from their target and adds their Wisdom bonus (minimum 1) to the combat maneuver check. Beginning at 7th level, cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and armor spikes carried by the iron-skinned monk also benefits from ki strike. This ability modifies ki strike.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.ever vigilant (ex): At 5th level, all squares the iron-skinned monk threatens with a melee weapon or unarmed strike, are considered difficult terrain for enemies. This ability applies even to jumping, flying, and incorporeal foes, as well as swarms, so long as the iron-skinned monk wields a melee weapon or unarmed strike capable of affecting them. The iron-skinned monk must be aware of the enemy to affect them. The iron-skinned monk also provides cover but not total cover to adjacent allies if their square lies between the ally and the origin of the attack or effect that includes the ally as a target. This ability replaces purity of body.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.bulwark (ex): At 10th level, the iron-skinned monk has learned to defend against some kinds of magic. If they are wearing gauntlets or cestus they may expend a point of ki and deflect a ray effect that targets them as an immediate action causing it to harmlessly dissipate. If the iron-skinned monk expends an additional point of ki they make a Reflex save against that ray using whatever the save DC vs the effect would normally be, even if it does not allow one. If they succeed they may redirect the ray to a target of their choice. The target must be within range of the spell as though the ironskinned monk was the point of origin. This redirection uses the same attack roll result by the original caster. This ability replaces improved evasion.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.steel reserves (ex): Beginning at 10th level, the ironskinned monk gains 2 bonus temporary ki at the beginning of each combat. This ki is used first before their normal pool of ki and if this bonus ki remains at the end of combat, it is lost. This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 10th level.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.steel skinned master (ex/su): Beginning at 15th level, the iron-skinned monk treats cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets and armor spikes as though they were one size larger for the purpose of their unarmed damage progression. Furthermore they may spend a ki point to emulate the effects of stoneskin on themselves as a standard action using their character level as the caster level, while under the effects of this stoneskin effect they are also not subject to critical hits or precision damage. This ability replaces quivering palm for the monk.
archetype-monk-iron-skinned-monk-monk.unyielding iron: Beginning at 19th level, while the iron-skinned monk still has at least one point of ki in their pool they cannot be moved from their square by the force of another creature, spell, spell-like, or supernatural ability, or by other means. Natural forces such as gravity still affect the iron-skinned monk, though a tidal wave, gust of wind, or other such phenomenon may not as long as the iron-skinned monk is standing on a surface which can support their weight. This ability replaces empty body for the monk.

archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.hidden step (ex): The monk of the darkened hand learns techniques to hide among the shadows. Beginning at 2nd level, they gain a bonus to their Stealth checks equal to 1/2 their class level while in areas of dim light or darkness. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.uncanny dodge (ex): Starting at 3rd level, the monk of the darkened hand cannot be caught flat-footed, even if the attacker is invisible. They still lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A monk of the darkened hand with this ability can still lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against them. If the monk of the darkened hand already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge instead. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 3rd level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.shadow split (sp): Beginning at 4th level, as a standard action a monk of the darkened hand can spend a point of ki to split off a part of their own shadow to cast silent image as a spell like ability. The DC for this spell-like ability is 10 + 1/2 the monk of the darkened hand’s class level + their Wisdom modifier and they use class level for the caster-level-dependent variables. This ability replaces slow fall at 4th level. They gain slow fall 10 ft. at 6th level, then the distance increases by 10 at 12th, 16th and 20th levels, when it reaches its maximum of 40 ft.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.hide in plain sight (su): At 6th level, a monk of the darkened hand can use the Stealth skill even while being observed as long as they are in an area of dim light or darker. They need not have cover to do so. This ability replaces fast movement gained at 6th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.shadow calling (sp): At 8th level, a monk of the darkened hand’s connection to the plane of shadow allows them to create creatures and effects out of the power of that plane. They can expend 2 ki points to cast shadow conjuration as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level and their Wisdom bonus to determine the DC. At 14th level, this becomes greater shadow conjuration. This ability replaces the slow fall gained at 8th and 14th levels.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.shadow step (su): At 9th level, a monk of the darkened hand can expend a point of ki to travel between shadows as if using the spell dimension door. However, unlike that spell, the teleportation must begin and end in an area of dim light or darker. A monk of the darkened hand can travel up to 5 feet per class level per point of ki spent in this manner. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 9th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.defensive roll (ex): At 10th level, the monk of the darkened hand can expend 3 ki points to attempt to avoid a lethal blow. This functions as the rogue’s advanced talent of the same name. This ability replaces the slow fall gained at 10th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.improved uncanny dodge (ex): At 12th level, a monk of the darkened hand can no longer be flanked. This defense denies a rogue the ability to sneak attack the monk of the darkened hand by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than the target has monk levels. If a character already has uncanny dodge from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank the character. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 12th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.shadow blast (sp): At 14th level, the monk of the darkened hand learned to harness the power of the shadow plane to deal devastating effects against their enemies. They can spend 2 ki points to cast shadow evocation as a spell like ability, using their class level as their caster level and their Wisdom modifier for the DC. At 18th level, this increases to greater shadow evocation. This ability replaces the slow fall gained at 14th level and the fast movement gained at 18th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.slippery mind (ex): At 15th level, a monk of the darkened hand becomes yet more resilient to enchantment spells. This functions as the rogue’s advanced talent of the same name. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 15th level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-darkened-hand.shadow self (su): At 20th level, the monk of the darkened hand gains DR 10/- and a +2 luck bonus on all saving throws while in an area of dim light or darker. Additionally, all abilities use one fewer ki points when in an area of dim light or darker. This ability replaces perfect self.

archetype-monk-lone-wolf-monk-archetype.charismatic stranger (ex): A lone wolf monk uses Charisma instead of Wisdom to determine the effects of all his monk class features. If he ever abandons this way, he loses access to all his monk abilities until he gains a new level.
archetype-monk-lone-wolf-monk-archetype.resolve (ex): At 4th level, a lone wolf gains the resolve samurai ability. Each use of this ability costs him 3 ki points. This replaces the 4th and 8th-level ki powers.
archetype-monk-lone-wolf-monk-archetype.greater resolve (ex): At 12th level, the lone wolf gains greater resolve. This replaces the 12th and 16th-level ki powers. Perfect Resolve: At 20th level, a lone wolf becomes a magical creature. He is forevermore treated as an outsider rather than as a humanoid (or whatever his creature type was) for the purpose of spells and magical effects. Additionally, the lone wolf gains the samurai ’s true resolve ability. Unlike other outsiders, the monk can still be brought back from the dead as if he were a member of his previous creature type. This modifies perfect self and replaces the 20th-level ki power.

archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.weapon proficiencies: Ring dancers gain proficiency with dancing rings, and lose proficiency with shortspears, slings, and spears. This alters the monk’s weapon proficiencies.
archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.immortal (su): When a ring dancer first becomes attuned to their dancing rings (see ki rings), he also becomes immortal. He ceases to age naturally and cannot die of old age unless separated from his dancing rings for longer than one week per monk level.
archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.ki rings (ex): At 1st level, a ring dancer receives dancing rings that he wears as part of his outfit. These dancing rings may be inherited from a family member, discovered before the bard set out to adventure, or otherwise obtained as part of becoming a ring dancer. These dancing rings are specially attuned to the ring dancer and only function for him. If stolen, they are worth only 4d10 gp. A ring dancer’s dancing rings can be used to perform any unarmed strike the ring dancer could make with his fists, as well as the bull rush, disarm, drag, reposition, or trip combat maneuvers. When using his dancing rings to bull rush or drag, the ring dancer doesn’t have to move unless failing to do so would put his rings out of range to use the maneuver. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.deadly rings (su): At 20th level, when a ring dancer threatens a critical hit with his dancing rings, he can spend 2 ki points to automatically confirm the critical hit and have the ring’s damage multiplier increased by 1 (x4 becomes x5, for example). In addition, he cannot be disarmed while wielding dancing rings. This ability replaces perfect self.
archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.air walk (sp): A ring dancer with air walk can spend 2 ki points from his ki pool and use his dancing rings to cast air walk, manipulating them into steps up which he can ascend. He cannot attack with the dancing rings while using them in this way. This effect lasts for one round per monk level. A monk must be 8th level and have the ring step ki power before selecting this power.
archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.ring blast (su): A ring dancer with ring blast can spend 1 ki point from his ki pool to make a ranged touch attack using his dancing rings as a standard action. The attack has a range of 50 feet and deals the dancing rings’ normal damage plus 1d6 force damage per enhancement bonus the rings’ possess. This force damage is is multiplied on a critical hit.
archetype-monk-ring-dancer-monk-archetyp.ring step (su): A ring dancer with ring step can use his dancing rings in combination with slow fall when no wall is within reach, manipulating them into steps down which he can descend. He cannot attack with the dancing rings while using them in this way. A monk must be 6th level and have the slow fall ki power before selecting this ki power.

archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.weapon and armor proficiencies: Skyline enforcers are proficient with autograpnels, grapnel gauntlets, nets, and whips. They are proficient with light and medium armor, but are affected in the same way a monk is if wearing armor.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.cable master (ex): Skyline enforcers are skilled with grapnel equipment. The skyline enforcer gains Equipment Trick (grapnel) as a bonus feat (see below). For the purposes of meeting grapnel trick requirements, the skyline enforcer is considered to have two additional ranks in Acrobatics as long as the skyline enforcer is not wearing armor or carrying a medium or heavy load. This ability replaces the monk’s stunning fist ability at 1st level.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.danger sense (su): At 3rd level, skyline enforcers develop a sixth-sense that warns them of danger. The skyline enforcer may reroll a failed Perception check made against an opponent’s Stealth check, a failed Sense Motive check, or gain a +2 insight bonus on a Reflex save. The skyline enforcer can use this ability once per day. The skyline enforcer gains an additional daily use of this ability at 6th level and every 3 levels above 6th, to a maximum of 6 uses at 18th level. This ability replaces the monk’s still mind ability at 3rd level.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.cable swing (ex): At 5th level, skyline enforcers master the ability of moving through the air using their grapnel gauntlets. While wearing a pair of grapnel gauntlets, the skyline enforcer can expend one use of each grapnel gauntlets in order to fly up to a distance of 60 feet with a Good maneuverability. There must be at least two suitable structures above the skyline enforcer to attach their grapnel to along the path of their movement and the skyline enforcer must land on a suitable surface at the end of their movement. The skyline enforcer can use their Acrobatics skill instead of their Fly skill for Fly skill checks while moving in this way. This ability replaces the monk’s purity of body ability at 5th level.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.wall runner (ex): At 17th level, skyline enforcers become so adept at moving through the rooftops that they can run up walls. The skyline enforcer gains a climb speed equal to their racial base speed, including the usual +8 racial bonus on all Climb checks. This ability replaces the monk’s timeless body ability at 17th level.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.grapnel expert (ex): At 17th level, skyline enforcers can use any rope-like item—including whips, chains, cables, and lengths of cloth—as a grapnel, even if it has no grapnel attached to the end. Skyline enforcers can use such items and other grapnel equipment to replace both uses of their grapnel gauntlets for the purposes of their cable swing ability, doubling the item’s length for their fly speed, up to a maximum total fly speed of 120 feet. For example, a skyline enforcer with a 40-foot rope would have a fly speed of 80 feet when using this ability. The item is attached and detached as part of the move action, and the skyline enforcer has the option of having the item detached at the end of their movement. Additionally, the skyline enforcer’s maneuverability while using grapnel gauntlets increases to Perfect. This ability replaces the monk’s tongue of the sun and moon ability at 17th level.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.arrested fall (ex): At 19th level, a skyline enforcer can use grapnel equipment to slow or arrest the fall of themselves or allies. As a swift action, if the skyline enforcer is within arm’s reach of a wall, then the skyline enforcer deploys their grapnel and confers their slow fall ability on an ally within the range of their grapnel. Alternatively, the skyline enforcer deploys their grapnel and extends the range of their slow fall ability to the range of their grapnel, also as a swift action. In either case, the skyline enforcer may choose to halt the fall, in which case no falling damage is taken. This ability replaces the monk’s empty body ability at 19th level.
archetype-monk-skyline-enforcer-monk-arc.slingshot (ex): At 20th level, skyline enforcers can unleash a powerful aerial attack on a foe. After moving using their cable swing ability, a skyline enforcer can make a single attack against an adjacent opponent using either their highest base attack bonus or their Acrobatics skill, whichever is highest. A hit deals the skyline enforcer’s unarmed damage + 1 for every 10 feet the skyline enforcer moved. In addition, the skyline enforcer may make a bull rush attempt as a free action if the attack hit, using any additional unused movement they have available. This ability replaces the monk’s perfect self ability at 20th level.

archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.harmonic resonance (ex): As long as a corite harmonicist is unarmored, he gains a deflection bonus to AC equal to his Wisdom bonus (as normal for deflection bonuses, this applies to his CMD as well). At 4th level, and every four levels thereafter, this deflection bonus increases by +1 (to a maximum equal to his Wisdom bonus + 5 at 20th level). Unlike a normal monk ’s AC bonus, this bonus applies even if the corite harmonicist is immobilized or helpless, and even if he carries a medium or heavy load, but not if he wears any armor or wields a shield. This ability modifies the AC bonus class feature.
archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.sonic strike (su): Beginning at 1st level, a corite harmonicist can deliver a sonic strike as a full-round action. If he does, he may make a single melee attack at his full base attack bonus. If the attack hits, it deals an additional amount of sonic damage equal to his unarmed strike damage. At 6th level, this bonus damage increases to twice his unarmed strike damage. At 11th level, it increases further to be equal to three times his unarmed strike damage, and at 16th level, it increases to be equal to four times his unarmed strike damage. When calculating the bonus sonic damage applied in this way, only the corite harmonicist’s base unarmed damage is counted: any bonuses due to a high Strength score, amulet of mighty fists, or other sources do not apply. The corite harmonicist cannot use this ability in conjunction with damage-increasing feats, such as Vital Strike, nor is this bonus damage multiplied in the result of a critical hit. This ability replaces the flurry of blows class feature.
archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.ki pool (su): When he gains a ki pool at 4th level, a corite harmonicist cannot spend points from his ki pool to make additional attacks when making a flurry of blows attack, increase his speed, or gain a dodge bonus to AC. Instead, by spending 1 point from his ki pool as a swift action, a corite harmonicist can do any of the following: Infuse a held weapon (or his own unarmed strike ) with sonic energy, causing it to deal an additional amount of sonic damage equal to his unarmed strike damage on the first successful hit made with it this round (this stacks with the sonic strike class feature). Increase his racial damage reduction by an amount equal to his Wisdom modifier for 1 round. Increase the deflection bonus to AC granted by this class by +4 for 1 round. This ability modifies the ki pool class feature.
archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.intense glow (sp): Beginning at 5th level, a corite harmonicist gains better control of his inner light. By spending 1 point from his ki pool as a swift action, the corite harmonicist can affect himself as though with the spell daylight, except that it is treated as though its spell level were equal to 1/2 his monk level (rounded down) for the purposes of determining which darkness spells can counter or dispel it. The caster level for this effect is equal to the corite harmonicist’s monk level. This ability replaces the high jump class feature.
archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.ranged pulse (su): Beginning at 5th level, a corite harmonicist can deliver a sonic pulse at a range. Doing so is a full-round action and requires that the corite harmonicist make a ranged attack, which has a maximum range of 60 feet. If the attack hits, it deals an amount of sonic damage equal to the bonus damage granted by the corite harmonicist’s sonic strike class feature. This ability replaces the purity of body class feature.
archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.widened pulse (su): Beginning at 11th level, by spending 2 ki points, as a full-round action, a corite harmonicist can direct a wave of sonic energy from his body. The corite harmonicist may choose whether this takes the form of a 20-foot-radius burst, a 30-foot cone, or a 60-foot line. Each other creature in the area suffers an amount of sonic damage equal to the bonus damage granted by the corite harmonicist’s sonic strike class feature. A successful Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 the corite harmonicist’s monk level + the corite harmonicist’s Wisdom modifier) halves this damage. This ability replaces the diamond body class feature.
archetype-monk-corite-harmonicist-monk-a.synchronous step (sp): At 12th level, a corite harmonicist can match his own harmonic resonations (or those of a touched creature) with those of objects in order to pass through them, or temporarily create openings in them. By spending 2 points from his ki pool as a standard action, he can replicate the effects of earthglide or passwall. This ability replaces the abundant step class feature.

archetype-monk-trox-grappler-larval-trox.improved grapple (ex): At 1st level, a trox grappler gains Improved Grapple as a bonus feat, even if he does not meet the prerequisites. Beginning at 4th level, when the trox grappler would pin an opponent he grapples, he can instead apply a condition to that creature. A successful saving throw (DC 10 + half the monk’s level + his Wisdom modifier) negates the effect. The trox grappler must choose which condition will apply before the grapple attempt is made. These effects do not stack with themselves (a creature sickened by Improved Grapple cannot become nauseated if pinned again), but additional successes do increase the duration. At 4th level, he can choose to make the target fatigued. At 8th level, he can make the target sickened for 1 minute. At 12th level, he can make the target staggered for 1d6+1 rounds. At 16th level, he can permanently blind or deafen the target. At 20th level, he can paralyze the target for 1d6+1 rounds. This replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-trox-grappler-larval-trox.shed size (ex): At 6th level, a trox grappler gains Shed Size as a bonus feat. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 6th level.
archetype-monk-trox-grappler-larval-trox.grabbing appendages (ex): At 7th level, a trox grappler gains Grabbing Appendages as a bonus feat. This replaces ki pool ( cold iron /silver).
archetype-monk-trox-grappler-larval-trox.powerful growth (ex): At 10th level, a trox grappler gains Powerful Growth as a bonus feat. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 10th level.
archetype-monk-trox-grappler-larval-trox.grab (ex): At 14th level, a trox grappler that hits a creature with an unarmed strike can attempt to enter a grapple with that creature as a free action. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 14th level.
archetype-monk-trox-grappler-larval-trox.awesome blow (ex): At 18th level, a trox grappler gains Awesome Blow as a bonus feat that he can use only while grappling a Small or Medium creature. The trox uses his grappled opponent as his weapon, dealing 1d6 + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage to both the grappled opponent and the struck creature. The trox grappler can choose to release his grappled opponent as part of this maneuver, sending it flying along with the struck creature. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 18th level. Growth Mutagen ( Alchemist Mutagen Option) Larval trox can create a special mutagen that they can drink to temporarily metamorphose to their proper form. When the trox imbibes his growth mutagen, he becomes Large, which grants him a +2 size bonus to Strength, +2 natural armor, and a +1 size bonus to both CMB and CMD, but he takes a -2 penalty to Dexterity and a -1 penalty to attacks and AC (including touch and flat-footed ). The trox’s space becomes 10-ft. x 10-ft. and his base speed increases to 40 feet, but his reach is unchanged. At the end of the mutagen’s duration, the larval trox is fatigued. This fatigue lasts until the trox rests 1 minute for every 10 minutes of the mutagen’s duration. A larval trox using this option can still choose mutagen as an alchemist’s discovery.

archetype-monk-varnished-monk-dryant-mon.varnished flesh (su): At 2nd level, a varnished monk gains the bitter pill alchemist discovery. At 6th level, she gains the preserve organs discovery. At 10th level, she gains the mummification discovery. At 14th level, she gains the nauseating flesh discovery. At 18th level, she gains the spontaneous healing discovery. This replaces the bonus feats gained at the listed levels.

archetype-monk-mystic-vocalist-monk-arch.class skills: A mystic vocalist adds Knowledge (arcana) and Linguistics to his list of class skills, and removes Ride. This alters class skills.
archetype-monk-mystic-vocalist-monk-arch.vocal assault (su): At 5th level, a mystic vocalist can make a vocal assault a number of times per day equal to 1 + 1/2 his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1, rounded down). For every four levels beyond 5th, a mystic vocalist gains one additional use of this ability per day, to a maximum of 4 + 1/2 his Wisdom modifier at 17th level. Only one vocal assault can be attempted per round. The following are the different types of vocal assaults that become available to a mystic vocalist at specified levels: sound burst (5th level), ear-piercing scream (7th level), screech (10th level), thundering drums (13th level). To use this ability, a mystic vocalist must forgo any one of his attacks in the round (regardless of whether the attack is part of a flurry of blows or not), substituting a vocal assault instead. In place of the attack forfeited, a mystic vocalist names the vocal assault he wishes to use and attempts a melee touch attack against the target. If the attack is successful, the target suffers the effects as stated in the vocal assault’s description. Regardless of the range or targets listed in the description of the vocal assault, only the target of the mystic vocalist’s melee touch attack is affected. For the purpose of determining the saving throw DC and amount of damage inflicted, use the mystic vocalist’s monk level. This is a supernatural ability which uses only the mystic vocalist’s voice- no other components are necessary to create the effects of the vocal assaults. This replaces style strike.
archetype-monk-mystic-vocalist-monk-arch.varied progression: At 9th level, a mystic vocalist gains tongue of the sun and moon. At 13th level, he gains improved evasion. This alters the levels at which tongue of the sun and moon and improved evasion are gained.
archetype-monk-mystic-vocalist-monk-arch.sonic supremacy (sp): At 14th level, a mystic vocalist can cast echolocation and primal scream once each per day as spell-like abilities, with a caster level equal to his mystic vocalist level. At 17th level, a mystic vocalist can cast resonating word as a spell-like ability one per day. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 14th level and timeless body.

archetype-monk-student-of-the-subtle-bod.class skills: A student of the subtle body adds Heal to his list of class skills, and removes either Knowledge (history) or Ride. This alters class skills.
archetype-monk-student-of-the-subtle-bod.vital knowledge (ex): A student of the subtle body learns to hit smarter, not harder. At 1st level, a student of the subtle body can use his Intelligence modifier in place of his Strength modifier on attack and damage rolls with unarmed strikes or monk weapons. This replaces the 1st level bonus feat.
archetype-monk-student-of-the-subtle-bod.ki pool (su): A student of the subtle body gains ki pool at 2nd level rather than 3rd level. This alters ki pool.
archetype-monk-student-of-the-subtle-bod.distillations (su): At 2nd level, a student of the subtle body can imbue therapeutic oils with a portion of his own ki energy to create a number of curative distillations equal to 1/2 his student of the subtle body level plus his Intelligence modifier. Each morning, after 8 hours of rest or meditation, a student of the subtle body can spend 10 minutes of preparation and 1 ki point to create his distillations. A distillation, once created, remains potent for 1 day before becoming inert, so a student of the subtle body must re-prepare his distillations every day. A distillation immediately becomes inert if it leaves the student of the subtle body’s possession for longer than 1 round, reactivating as soon as it returns to his keeping. (This allows a student of the subtle body’s distillation to cure a creature other than himself as long as the creature ingests the distillation on the same round in which the student of the subtle body gave it to the creature.) A student of the subtle body’s distillations cure 1d6 points of damage for every two levels the student of the subtle body possesses. This replaces the 2nd level bonus feat and all instances of style strike.
archetype-monk-student-of-the-subtle-bod.anatomical awareness (ex): At 3rd level, a student of the subtle body adds half his class level to all Heal skill checks. Additionally, a student of the subtle body can make a Heal skill check to determine the strengths and weaknesses of a living creature in place of the standard Knowledge skill check that would normally be required. If a student of the subtle body successfully uses Heal to identify a strength or weakness of a creature, he gains a +1 competence bonus on attack and damage rolls against creatures of that type for a number of minutes equal to his student of the subtle body level. This bonus increases by +1 at 7th level and every four levels thereafter. This replaces ki strike and timeless body.

archetype-monk-lausatuuk.skills: A lausatuuk adds Disguise to his list of class skills and removes Ride. This alters the monk’s class skills.
archetype-monk-lausatuuk.weapon and armor proficiency: A lausatuuk is proficient with the battleaxe, greataxe, greatsword, handaxe, longspear, longsword, short sword, shortspear, spear, and throwing axe, instead of a monk’s usual weapon proficiencies. This alters the monk’s weapon and armor proficiency.
archetype-monk-lausatuuk.flurry of blows (ex): Starting at 1st level, a lausatuuk can make a flurry of blows using unarmed strikes only. He may not make a flurry of blows with any other weapons, including special monk weapons. A lausatuuk’s flurry of blows alters and otherwise functions as normal for a monk of his level. Bonus Feats A lausatuuk loses the ability to take Gorgon’s Fist, Medusa’s Wrath, and Scorpion Style as bonus feats. He adds Improved Dirty Trick to his list of bonus feats. At 6th level, he also adds Greater Dirty Trick to his list of bonus feats. This alters the monk’s bonus feats.
archetype-monk-lausatuuk.underhanded (ex): At 1st level, as an immediate action, a lausatuuk can make a dirty trick combat maneuver check against any target he successfully hit at least twice with his unarmed strike during his turn. This combat maneuver check does not provoke an attack of opportunity. At 6th level, a lausatuuk can take a 5-foot step before or after performing a dirty trick combat maneuver so long as he ends adjacent to his target. If he takes this step, he cannot take another during his next turn. If at least one of his hits with an unarmed strike is a confirmed critical, taking the 5-foot step granted by underhanded does not prevent him from taking a 5-foot step during his next turn. A lausatuuk can use this ability a number of times per day equal to his monk level, but no more than once per round. This ability replaces Stunning Fist.
archetype-monk-lausatuuk.ki trickster (su): At 3rd level, a lausatuuk gains a pool of ki points equal to his Wisdom modifier. The pool increases to 1/2 his monk level + his Wisdom modifier at level 4. This ability alters ki pool.
archetype-monk-lausatuuk.ninja trick: At 3rd level, a lausatuuk gains one of the following ninja tricks: darkvision, fast stealth, shadow clone, slow metabolism, style master, sudden disguise, vanishing trick, ventriloquism, and wall climber. The lausatuuk uses his monk level as the caster level for the preceding ninja tricks. His monk levels stack with any ninja levels he possesses when determining his caster level for all ninja tricks. He gains an additional ninja trick for every four levels of lausatuuk gained after 3rd level. Otherwise, this works as the ninja’s ninja trick ability. This ability replaces still mind and purity of body.
archetype-monk-lausatuuk.master trick: At 11th level and every four levels thereafter, a lausatuuk can choose one of the following master tricks in place of a ninja trick: ghost step, invisible blade, master disguise, see the unseen, and shadow split. The lausatuuk uses his monk level as the caster level for the preceding ninja tricks. His monk levels stack with any ninja levels he possesses when determining his caster level for all ninja tricks and master tricks. This ability replaces diamond body, diamond soul, and timeless body.

archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.shivering fist (ex): At 1st level, a monk of the katabatic winds gains Shivering Fist as a bonus feat, even if he does not meet the prerequisites. He may attempt a shivering attack a number of times per day equal to his monk level, plus one more time per day for every 4 levels he has in classes other than monk. At 8th level his shivering fist attack deals an additional 1d6 points of cold damage. The bonus damage increases to 2d6 points of cold damage at 16th level. This ability replaces Stunning Fist.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.neither cold nor magic (ex): At 2nd level, a monk of the katabatic winds gains cold resistance 5 and suffers no penalty to speed or on Acrobatics, Climb, or Stealth checks in snowy or icy terrain. At 6th level and every three levels thereafter, his speed moving across snowy and icy terrain increases by +10 feet. At 9th level, his cold resistance increases to 10 and for a number of rounds per day equal to his monk level he can move normally when magical effects would impede his movement, as if he were affected by freedom of movement. These rounds need not be consecutive, but must be used in 1-round increments. This ability alters fast movement and replaces evasion and improved evasion.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.cold fire (ex): At 3rd level, a monk of the katabatic winds gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against firebased attacks. This ability replaces still mind.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.frozen strike (su): At 3rd level, a monk of the katabatic winds can charge his unarmed strike as a swift action so it ignores the natural armor bonus of any creature with the fire subtype. This benefit lasts for a number of rounds per day equal to the monk’s class level. These rounds need not be consecutive, but must be used in 1-round increments. This ability does not bypass enhancement bonuses to natural armor, such as those gained from barkskin or an amulet of natural armor. This ability replaces maneuver training.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.ki pool (su): When making a ki strike, as a swift action he can wreath his fists, feet, elbows, and knees in frigid air. When he activates this ability, half the damage dealt by his unarmed strikes is bludgeoning damage, and the other half is cold damage. He may use a swift action to deactivate this effect. This ability alters ki pool and replaces purity of body.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.katabatic blast (su): At 11th level, as a standard action costing 2 ki points, the monk may open his mouth and unleash a powerful blast of frigid air in a 5- foot-diameter, 30-foot line lasting until the beginning of his next turn. The direction of the wind is away from his location and remains constant in that direction until the wind subsides. Creatures caught in the katabatic blast are knocked prone and take bludgeoning damage equal to the monk’s unarmed strike damage + his Wisdom modifier in addition to cold damage also equal to the monk’s unarmed strike damage + his Wisdom modifier. A successful Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the monk’s level + his Wisdom modifier) halves the damage and prevents being knocked prone. A creature beginning its turn wholly or partially within the katabatic blast must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the monk’s level + his Wisdom modifier) or be pushed 10 feet in the direction the wind is blowing, take 1d6 nonlethal damage, and be knocked prone. A successful Fortitude save negates the preceding effects. This ability replaces diamond body.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.frozen palm (su): Starting at 15th level, a monk of the katabatic winds can transform a living creature he hits into solid ice. He can use this frozen palm attack once per day, and he must announce his intent before making his attack roll. Creatures immune to cold damage cannot be affected. Otherwise, if the monk strikes successfully and the target takes damage from the blow, the frozen palm attack succeeds. If the target fails its Fortitude saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 the monk’s level + the monk’s Wisdom modifier), the subject along with all its carried gear, is helpless and encased in solid ice, as the icy prison (Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Ultimate Magic) spell, using the monk’s class level as the caster level. This ability replaces quivering palm.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-katabatic-win.cold self: At 20th level, a monk of the katabatic winds foregoes becoming a magical being and instead becomes the living embodiment of the poles. The monk gains the air and cold subtypes, granting him a fly speed of 40 feet with perfect maneuverability. This ability replaces perfect self.

archetype-monk-quack-fu-monk.way of life armor class bonus (ex): When unarmored and unencumbered, the quack-fu monk adds her Charisma bonus (if any) as a dodge bonus to her Armor Class and Combat Maneuver Defense. This bonus increases by 1 at level four and for every four quack-fu monk levels thereafter, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. She loses these bonuses when she loses her Dexterity bonus to Armor Class, when she is immobilized or helpless, when she wears any armor, when she uses a shield, or when she carries a medium or heavy load. The quack-fu monk can substitute Charisma for Wisdom for the prerequisites of style feats. This is a modification to the monk’s armor class bonus class feature.
archetype-monk-quack-fu-monk.aggressive stance (ex): A quack-fu monk of 3rd level or higher counts as one size category larger (up to Medium size ), but only to determine what size creatures he can use combat maneuvers against. At level 9 this ability improves, counting as two size categories larger (up to Large size ). At level 15 it improves again, counting as three size categories larger (up to huge size ). Aggressive stance stacks with other similar abilities, such as the In Your Face feat. This ability replaces Still Mind.
archetype-monk-quack-fu-monk.style strike (ex): Add the following to the quack-fu monk’s style strike options. This move comes from sumo. Grabbing Slap: The sumotori slaps and grabs an opponent in one move. If the attack hits, the sumotori can make a free grapple check to start, escape, or maintain a grapple (using the base attack bonus of the attack used to hit the foe). A grabbing slap does damage as an unarmed strike, it does not deal grapple damage. The sumotori must attack with a fist to use this style strike.

archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.weapon and armor proficiencies: Madmen are proficient with unarmed strikes, but not with any other weapon or any kind of armor. For madmen, monk class features that work with any monk weapon instead function only with unarmed strikes.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.insanity defense (ex): At 1st level, a madman adds his Strength and Constitution modifiers on Fortitude saving throws, his Dexterity and Intelligence modifiers on Reflex saving throws, and his Wisdom and Charisma modifiers on Will saving throws. These replace the usual ability score modifiers on his saving throws, and no effect can change the ability modifiers that a madman uses for his saving throws, though effects that add new ability modifiers to saving throws (such as a paladin ’s divine grace) function normally. When unarmored and unencumbered, the madman adds his Wisdom modifier to his AC and CMD, even against touch attacks or when flat-footed, and he also retains his Dexterity bonus to AC and CMD even when flat-footed. He loses these benefits when he is immobilized or helpless, when he wears any armor, when he carries a shield, or when he carries a medium or heavy load. His AC bonus does not increase as he levels. No effect can change the ability modifiers that a madman uses for AC and CMD, though effects that add new ability modifiers to AC and/or CMD function normally. This ability alters AC bonus, but counts as that ability for the purposes of prerequisites and requirements.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.lunacy fist (ex): At 1st level, a madman adds both his Strength and Intelligence modifiers on attack rolls with unarmed strikes and to his combat maneuver bonus instead of just his Strength modifier. He adds both his Constitution and Charisma instead of his Strength modifier to damage rolls with unarmed strikes. No effect can change the ability modifiers that a madman uses for attack and damage rolls with unarmed strike or for his combat maneuver bonus, though effects that add new ability modifiers to attack rolls or damage rolls function normally. A madman’s unarmed strikes deal damage that is bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing. For the purposes of prerequisites and requirements, this ability counts as the Weapon Finesse feat. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.mad skills (ex): At 1st level, a madman’s abuse of his body allows him to use his abilities in unconventional ways. He adds a modifier to ability and skill checks equal to an ability modifier other than the one that ability or skill check is based on, as given in Table 1-2: Mad Skills Modifiers. Table 1-1: Mad Skills Modifiers Add a modifier equal to… To ability and skill checks based on… Strength modifier Dexterity Dexterity modifier Constitution Constitution modifier Intelligence Intelligence modifier Wisdom Wisdom modifier Charisma Charisma modifier Strength However, each of these modifiers cannot add more to an ability or skill check than his class level. They have no minimum, and may be negative. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.psychotic flurry (su): Starting at 1st level, a madman can make a psychotic flurry as a full-attack action. When doing so, he may make one additional attack, taking a –2 penalty on all of his attack rolls, as if using the Two-Weapon Fighting feat. For the purpose of these attacks, the madman’s base attack bonus from his monk class levels is equal to his madman level. For all other purposes, such as qualifying for a feat or a prestige class, the madman uses his normal base attack bonus. At 8th level, the monk can make two additional attacks when he uses psychotic flurry, as if using Improved Two-Weapon Fighting (even if the madman does not meet the prerequisites for the feat). At 15th level, the monk can make three additional attacks using psychotic flurry, as if using Greater Two-Weapon Fighting (even if the madman does not meet the prerequisites for the feat). A madman cannot use any weapon other than an unarmed strike in a psychotic flurry. A madman may substitute disarm, sunder, and trip combat maneuvers for unarmed attacks as part of a psychotic flurry. A madman also learns one psychosis at each odd level, which he uses by substituting psychoses for unarmed attacks as part of a psychotic flurry. The saving throw DC for psychoses is 10 + half the madman’s level + the madman’s lowest ability modifier + the madman’s second-lowest ability modifier. This ability alters flurry of blows, and replaces still mind, purity of body, wholeness of body, improved evasion, diamond body, diamond soul, quivering palm, timeless body, and empty body. This ability counts as flurry of blows for the purposes of prerequisites.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.freak physiology: At 2nd level, 6th level, 14th level, and 18th level, a madman increases his two lowest ability scores by 1 each. In the case of a tie, the madman may choose which ability score to improve. At 10th level and 20th level, he increases all of his ability scores by 1 each. This ability replaces the bonus feats gained at 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th levels.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.psychotic break: At 20th level, a madman learns one of the psychotic breaks below. The chosen psychotic break is automatically triggered when every attack, combat maneuver, or psychosis in a psychotic flurry is successful.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.elemental breakdown: The madman releases a massive explosion of elemental energy. This has three components: An explosion of fire, dealing 5d6 fire damage in a 20-foot spread. A successful Reflex save halves the damage. Three bolts of lightning, each dealing 3d6 electricity damage along a 60-foot line extending away from the madman (the electricity damage does not stack if bolts overlap). A successful Reflex save halves the damage. A barrage of icicles, dealing 1d6 cold damage to up to twenty creatures within 120 feet. No creature can be struck by more than one icicle. A successful Reflex save negates the damage. Creatures subject to more than one effect make multiple saves. The madman himself is immune to these effects.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.repetition expecting change: The madman can make another attack at his highest base attack bonus, which is considered part of the same psychotic flurry. If that attack is successful, this psychotic break triggers again, allowing another attack, so once the madman succeeds on all the attacks in his original psychotic flurry, he may continue attacking until an attack is unsuccessful. He still may not use any psychosis more than once in the same psychotic flurry.
archetype-monk-madman-monk-archetype.true schism: The madman creates a copy of himself and all of his equipment. The copy acts completely independently, but is still the madman. At the end of the madman’s next turn, one of the madmen and all of his equipment—even if that equipment has left his possession—disappears. The madman that stays need not be the “original.” Artifacts are not copied. Anything in the possession of the madman that disappears that was not copied (including artifacts, or objects picked up during the round) falls to the floor. This ability replaces perfect self.

archetype-monk-monk-of-the-silver-fist.weapon and armor proficiency: A monk of the silver fist gains proficiency with gauntlets and bucklers in addition to their normal weapon and armor proficiencies.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-silver-fist.maneuvers: A monk of the silver fist begins his career with knowledge of three martial maneuvers. The disciplines available to him are Eternal Guardian, Iron Tortoise, and Mithral Current. A monk of the silver fist gains Bluff and Perform as class skills. Once the monk of the silver fist knows a maneuver, he must ready it before he can use it (see Maneuvers Readied, below). A maneuver usable by monk of the silver fist is considered an extraordinary ability unless otherwise noted in it or its discipline’s description. A monk of the silver fist’s maneuvers are not affected by spell resistance, and he does not provoke attacks of opportunity when he initiates one. The monk of the silver fist learns additional maneuvers at higher levels, as indicated on Table: Archetype Maneuver Progression. The maximum level of maneuvers gained through monk of the silver fist levels is limited by those listed in that table as well, although this restriction does not apply to maneuvers added to his maneuvers known through other methods, such as prestige classes or the Advanced Study feat. A monk of the silver fist must meet a maneuver’s prerequisite to learn it. See Systems and Use for more details on how maneuvers are used. Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even numbered initiator level thereafter (6th, 8th, 10th, and so on), the monk of the silver fist can choose to learn a new maneuver in place of one he already knows. In effect, he loses the old maneuver in exchange for the new one. He can choose a new maneuver of any level he likes, as long as he observes the restriction on the highest-level maneuvers he knows; the monk of the silver fist need not replace the old maneuver with a maneuver of the same level. He can swap only a single maneuver at any given level. A monk of the silver fist’s initiation modifier is Wisdom, and each monk of the silver fist level is counted as a full initiator level.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-silver-fist.maneuvers readied: A monk of the silver fist can ready all three of his maneuvers known at 1st level, and as he advances in level and learns more maneuvers, he is able to ready more, but must still choose which maneuvers to ready. A monk of the silver fist must always ready his maximum number of maneuvers readied. He readies his maneuvers by meditating or performing martial katas for ten minutes. The maneuvers he chooses remain readied until he decides to practice again and change them. The monk of the silver fist does not need to sleep or rest for any long period of time in order to ready his maneuvers; any time he spends ten minutes meditating, he can change his readied maneuvers. A monk of the silver fist begins an encounter with all his readied maneuvers unexpended, regardless of how many times he might have already used them since he chose them. When he initiates a maneuver, he expends it for the current encounter, so each of his readied maneuvers can be used once per encounter (unless he recovers them, as described below). In order for the monk of the silver fist to recover maneuvers, he must take a full-round action, moving up to his speed, then granting an adjacent ally (including himself) an insight bonus to their AC and on saving throws equal to his monk of the silver fist initiation modifier for one round. If he does so, he recovers a number of expended maneuvers equal to his monk of the silver fist initiation modifier (minimum 2). Alternately, the monk of the silver fist may center himself and realign his ki, recovering a single maneuver as a standard action.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-silver-fist.stances: A monk of the silver fist begins his career with knowledge of one stance from any discipline open to monks of the silver fist. At 4th, 7th, 11th, and 13th levels, he can select an additional stance to learn. The maximum level of stances gained through monk of the silver fist levels is limited by those listed in Table: Archetype Maneuver Progression. Unlike maneuvers, stances are not expended and the monk of the silver fist does not have to ready them. All the stances he knows are available to him at all times, and he can change the stance he is currently maintaining as a swift action. A stance is an extraordinary ability unless otherwise stated in the stance or discipline description. Unlike with maneuvers, a monk of the silver fist cannot learn a new stance at higher levels in place of one he already knows. This ability replaces flurry of blows and stunning fist.
archetype-monk-monk-of-the-silver-fist.gauntlet strike (ex): At 1st level, the monk of the silver fist becomes an expert in wielding gauntlets. He gains Improved Unarmed Strike and Weapon Focus ( gauntlet ) as bonus feats, even if he does not meet their prerequisites. A monk of the silver fist deals more damage with his gauntlet attacks than a normal person would, as shown below. For the purposes of the monk of the silver fist’s abilities and feats, a gauntlet is any weapon worn over the hands or fingers to aid in punching, including brass knuckles, normal gauntlets, rope gauntlets, and spiked gauntlets. Level Small Medium Large 1-4 1d4 1d6 1d8 5-9 1d6 1d8 2d6 10-14 1d8 1d10 2d8 15-19 1d10 2d6 3d6 20 2d6 2d8 3d8 This ability replaces unarmed strike.
