archetype-vigilante-alchemical-scoundrel.persistent mutagen* (ex): An alchemical scoundrel gains the persistent mutagen class feature of the alchemist which also affects their cognatogen and inspiring cognatogen. An alchemical scoundrel must possess the mutagen, cognatogen, or inspiring cognatogen discovery and be 12th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-alchemical-scoundrel.splash technician (ex): An alchemical scoundrel gains Splash Sniper as a bonus feat, although they must meet the prerequisites for it. They can also reduce their hidden strike or sneak attack damage by 1 die to increase the DC of any splash weapon they use to deal hidden strike or sneak attack damage (including bombs) by +1. At 6th level and every 6 levels thereafter, they can reduce their hidden strike or sneak attack damage by an additional die to further increase the DC of any splash weapon they use by an additional +1.
archetype-vigilante-alchemical-scoundrel.smoking bomber (su): An alchemical scoundrel gains the smoke bomb discovery. At 8th level they gain the stink bomb discovery. At 14th level, they gain the inferno bomb discovery. If the alchemical scoundrel has the bomb tinkerer talent, they can change the type of damage their inferno bomb ’s incendiary cloud effect deals, although they can’t select sonic or force for the damage type. An alchemical scoundrel must possess the bomb adept talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-alchemical-scoundrel.sniping bomber* (ex): An alchemical scoundrel gains the explosive missile discovery. At 10th level, they can make a second attack with this discovery at a -6 penalty as a full?round action, also applying a bomb to the attack. If the alchemical scoundrel also has the fast bombs discovery, they can use the explosive missile discovery as the first attack in a full-attack action. An alchemical scoundrel must possess the bomb adept talent and be 6th level or higher to select this talent. This ability alters vigilante talents.

archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.weapon and armor proficiencies: An arsenal summoner is proficient with heavy armor. This alters A vigilante’s normal armor and weapon proficiencies.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.anima union (su): At 1st level, the arsenal summoner gains a powerful sentient weapon called an anima, whose weapon type is chosen by the vigilante. An anima can be any melee or ranged weapon properly sized for the arsenal summoner (including shields) except for armor spikes, and the arsenal summoner is always treated as proficient with their anima. The arsenal summoner chooses the anima’s type upon gaining this class feature, and once chosen, it can’t be changed. An anima is treated as a magus ‘ black blade for how it interacts with other abilities (see the black blade), although it is not required to be a one-handed slashing weapon, rapier, or swordcane. A vigilante with this class feature cannot have a familiar of any kind, even from another class. This ability replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.anima damage (su): Whenever the arsenal summoner hits with their anima, the weapon damage is based on their level and not the weapon type. The damage for Medium arsenal summoners is listed on Table 6-1: Anima Progression; see the table below for Small and Large arsenal summoners. The arsenal summoner can decide to use the weapon’s base damage instead of the anima damage—this must be declared before the attack roll is made. (If the weapon’s base damage exceeds the anima damage, its damage is unchanged.) This increase in damage does not affect any other aspect of the weapon, and doesn’t apply to alchemical items, bombs, or other weapons that only deal energy damage. archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.alertness (ex): While an arsenal summoner is wielding their anima, they gain the Alertness feat.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.telepathy (su): While an arsenal summoner is wielding or carrying their anima, they can communicate telepathically with the blade in a language that the arsenal summoner and the anima share.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.unbreakable (ex): An anima is immune to the broken condition. If broken, the anima is unconscious and powerless until repaired, losing this ability until repaired. An arsenal summoner’s anima cannot be destroyed unless the arsenal summoner dies, repairing itself to full hit points if the arsenal summoner is brought back to life.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.teleport anima (sp): A once per day whenever an arsenal summoner is in their vigilante identity, they can call their anima from as far as 1 mile away (but not from another plane) as a full-round action, causing it to instantaneously teleport to their hand. At 5th level and every 5 levels afterwards, the arsenal summoner can teleport their anima an additional time.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.mundane anima (su): At 3rd level, while an arsenal summoner is not in their vigilante identity, their anima takes the form of a mundane object, such as a cane, book, or other similar object. If the arsenal summoner makes an attack with their mundane anima, it transforms into its normal form, suppressing this effect for 5 minutes. Exposing an anima like this forces an arsenal summoner to make a disguise check or risk their identity being exposed.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.anima loyalty (su): At 20th level, once per week if the arsenal summoner would be killed, their anima can cast a maximized breath of life spell on them. The anima cannot do this if it is not within 5 ft. of the arsenal summoner or if the arsenal summoner is killed by a death effect.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.bonded armor (su): At 2nd level, an arsenal summoner can select 1 specific set of armor with which they are proficient, spending 24 hours to bond to it. As part of the bonding process, the arsenal summoner places arcane mark with a caster level equal to the arsenal summoner’s class level onto their bonded armor. Whenever the arsenal summoner is in their vigilante identity, they can choose to summon their bonded armor as though using the instant summons spell as full-round action a number of times per day equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1), donning it instantly. This armor can be summoned from up to 1 mile away (but not from another plane) and possesses a +1 enhancement bonus to its AC. At 5th level and every 3 levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1 (up to a +5 enhancement at 14th level) whenever it is summoned with this ability. Only one set of armor can benefit from this enhancement bonus at a time. If an arsenal summoner’s bonded armor’s arcane mark is removed or their bonded armor is destroyed, they can spend 8 hours and 100 gp per level to bond to a new set of armor. An arsenal summoner can spend 24 hours, breaking their connection between their bonded armor, to bond to a new set of armor in this fashion without cost as long as the previously bonded armor is within 30 ft. of the new armor. No creature other than the arsenal summoner can wear their bonded armor, providing no armor bonus to AC and doubling its armor check penalty to all any other creature that wears it. The bonded armor treats any other wearer as though they were not proficient with the armor regardless of if they normally would be. This ability replaces the 2nd, 8th, and 16th level vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.arsenal talents (ex): An arsenal summoner can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.additional armory (ex): The arsenal summoner can bond to an additional set of armor. At 12th level, they can bond to a third set of armor. If the arsenal summoner has the bonded shield talent, they can bond a shield to each additional set of armor. An arsenal summoner must be 6th level to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.advanced armor training (ex): The arsenal summoner gains an advanced armor training. This talent can be selected multiple times, each time selecting a different advanced armor training, but an arsenal summoner must have the armor training talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.advanced weapon training (ex): The arsenal summoner gains an advanced weapon training. This talent can be selected multiple times, each time selecting a different advanced weapon training, but an arsenal summoner must have the weapon training talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.anima armor (ex): The arsenal summoner’s bonded armor and anima fuse, although only a suit of armor with either armor spikes, gauntlets, or spiked gauntlets can be an anima armor (if the armor doesn’t normally come with gauntlets or spiked gauntlets, the anima summoner can spend 1 hour to bond a set of gauntlets or spiked gauntlets to a suit of armor, treating them as part of the suit of armor). The anima armor’s armor spikes, gauntlets, and spiked gauntlets are treated as though they were an anima for anima damage and the anima’s enhancement bonus. The anima’s mind still exists inside of the bonded armor, and they can converse with it while wearing it. The arsenal summoner can’t use the anima’s teleport anima ability, but they treat their anima armor as though it was made of living steel. At 8th level, they also treat it as though it was made of mithral. At 14th level, they also treat it as though it was made of adamantine. This ability supersedes any material of which the anima armor is already made. If the arsenal summoner has the additional armory talent, they can spend 24 hours to switch which bonded armor is their anima armor. An arsenal summoner with this talent cannot select the anyblade, assimilated anima, or dual arsenal talents.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.anyblade (su): Whenever the arsenal summoner summons their anima with the teleport anima class feature, they can have the blade take a different form, treating it as any other weapon which could qualify to be an anima. Any feats that the arsenal summoner possesses that would only apply to a specific weapon (such as Weapon Focus ) apply to their anima unless the anima’s new form would make that feat an invalid choice. The anima retains this new form until the arsenal summoner dismisses it as a free action or 24 hours have passed, whichever comes first. The arsenal summoner can spend 8 hours to permanently change the form of their anima to another type of weapon.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.armor training (ex): The arsenal summoner gains the armor training 1 class feature.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.assimilated anima (ex): The arsenal summoner and their anima become one, treating the arsenal summoner’s unarmed strikes as though they were an anima for anima damage and the anima’s enhancement bonus, as well as gaining the Improved Unarmed Strike feat. The anima’s mind still exists inside of the arsenal summoner, and they can converse with it at will, although they never risk coming into conflict with the anima’s ego. Once per day, whenever an arsenal summoner fails a Will save, they can reroll that save, allowing their anima to make a saving throw as well. At 5th and every 5 levels afterwards, the arsenal summoner can reroll an additional will save per day. An arsenal summoner with this talent cannot select the anima armor, anyblade, or dual arsenal talents.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.bonded shield (ex): The arsenal summoner can choose to bond with a shield, treating it as a part of a set of bonded armor. When summoned, the arsenal summoner splits the enhancement bonus gained from their bonded armor class feature between the two however they wish. An arsenal summoner with a shield as their anima can use this talent to connect it to their bonded armor as though it was a normal shield. If they do, the arsenal summoner can summon both with either their teleport anima or bonded armor class feature.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.dual arsenal (su): Whenever the arsenal summoner uses their teleport blade ability, they can also create a copy of their anima. The copy possesses an enhancement bonus equal to the enhancement bonus provided by the anima class feature. This copy lasts for 1 minute per 2 levels the arsenal summoner possesses. At 6th level, this copy lasts for 10 minutes per 2 levels the arsenal summoner possesses. At 10th level this copy lasts for 1 hour per 2 levels the arsenal summoner possesses. At 14th level this copy lasts for 24 hours or until dismissed, whichever comes first. If the arsenal summoner spends an anima point, each weapon must be granted a bonus to attack and damage separately, although they can spend 2 anima points simultaneously to do so.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.mutable anima (su): The arsenal summoner can exchange a +1 bonus on their anima’s attack and damage rolls from their anima pool to treat it as though it was made of mithril or cold iron. An arsenal summoner also add the following abilities to those it can bestow with the anima pool: brilliant energy, ghost touch, planar, returning, shadowshooting, and throwing. At 12th level, the arsenal summoner can instead exchange a +2 bonus on their anima’s attack and damage rolls from their anima pool to treat it as though it was made of adamantine. An arsenal summoner can also add the following abilities to those it can bestow with the anima pool: anarchic, axiomatic, designating (greater)UE, holy, lucky (greater)UE, reliable (greater)UE, and unholy. At 18th level, the arsenal summoner can add the following abilities to their anima pool: bane and phase locking. An arsenal summoner must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.social armory (su): The arsenal summoner can don their bonded armor or call their anima to their hand while they aren’t in their vigilante identity as a swift action. The arsenal summoner also treats their armor as though it has the glamered enhancement while not in their vigilante identity.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.weapon training (ex): The arsenal summoner gains the weapon training 1 class feature. An arsenal summoner must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.anima pool (su): At 3rd level, an arsenal summoner gains an anima pool with a number of anima points equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). This pool refreshes once per day after the arsenal summoner has rested for 8 hours. An arsenal summoner can spend 1 point from their anima pool as a swift action to grant their anima a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 minute. For every 4 levels after 1st, this bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +5 at 17th level. At 5th level, an arsenal summoner can exchange the bonus on their anima’s attack and damage rolls from the anima pool with a weapon enhancement of an equal amount from the following list: adaptive (+1), dancing, designating (lesser)UE, endless ammunition, flaming, flaming burst, frost, icy burst, keen, lucky, reliable, shock, shocking burst, speed, or vorpal. An arsenal summoner cannot add an enhancement to their anima for which it would be ineligible (such as an adaptive longsword). Adding these properties consumes an amount of bonus equal to the property’s base price modifier. These properties are added to any the weapon already has, but duplicates do not stack. These bonuses and properties are decided when the anima pool point is spent and cannot be changed until the next time the arsenal summoner uses this ability. These bonuses do not function if the weapon is wielded by anyone other than the arsenal summoner. An arsenal summoner can only enhance one weapon in this way at one time. If they use this ability again, the first use immediately ends. This ability replaces unshakable and frightening appearance.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.astral armory (su): At 5th level, an arsenal summoner can store their anima and bonded armor in a pocket dimension which only they can access, being able to summon it regardless of distance or which plane it currently resides. The arsenal summoner can spend 1 minute to access their astral armory, either to remove or return their anima or bonded armor into the pocket dimension. A damaged anima or bonded armor inside of this pocket dimension heals 1 hit point per hour. This ability replaces startling appearance and stunning appearance.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.arsenal deity (ex): At 20th level, an arsenal summoner can select one of the following abilities:
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.armor mastery (ex): The arsenal summoner gains the armor mastery class feature.
archetype-vigilante-arsenal-summoner-vig.weapon mastery (ex): The arsenal summoner gains the weapon mastery class feature. This ability replaces vengeance strike.

archetype-vigilante-beast-born-vigilante.animal companion (ex): At 1st level, a beast born forms a bond with an animal companion. A beast born may begin play with any of the animals available to a druid. This animal is a loyal companion that accompanies the beast born on their adventures. This ability functions like the druid animal companion ability (which is part of the nature bond class feature). The beast born’s effective druid level is equal to their beast born level. If a character receives an animal companion from more than one source, their effective druid levels stack for the purposes of determining the companion’s statistics and abilities. A beast born must take care when changing from one identity to another, including making any changes necessary to ensure that their animal companion is not associated with their social identity and vice versa (although if anyone suspects them of being anything other than what they appear to be while in their social identity, they need not make a separate Disguise check for their animal companion). The beast born always requires 1 minute to change identities, regardless of other effects that reduce the time required, and they cannot choose the immediate change or quick change social talents. While transformed into an animal, the beast born can attempt to appear to be a normal member of their animal’s type, but doing so imposes a –10 penalty on their Disguise check. The bonus provided by seamless guise still applies to the beast born’s attempts to appear to be an ordinary animal. As a standard action, a beast born can touch their animal companion to transform it into a similar Tiny animal to allow it to hide easily or even blend in and act as a spy. For instance, a tiger could be transformed into a housecat, a wolf could be transformed into a Tiny dog, a dire bat could be transformed into a Tiny flying fox, and so on. This functions as a polymorph effect, and the animal companion gains a +2 size bonus to Dexterity and a –4 size penalty to Strength (use the polymorph table to adjust its ability score if the animal companion is larger than Medium). A beast born can return their animal to its normal form by touching it again as a swift action, and when a vigilante enters or leaves their vigilante identity, they can choose to change their animal companion’s form as a swift action as long as it is within 30 ft. of them. This ability alters dual identity and replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-beast-born-vigilante.beast bred (su): At 1st level, a beast born can transform into a small, harmless animal as per the harmless form spell as a standard action at will (even if they would not normally be a valid target for that spell). At 4th level, a beast born gains the wild shape class feature of a druid of their level, gaining an additional use of this ability at 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter. A beast born treats their beast born level as their druid level to determine which forms they can take with this ability, although they cannot transform into an elemental or plant with this ability. This ability replaces the 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 20th level vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-beast-born-vigilante.beast within (su): At 20th level, whenever a beast born uses their beast bred ability, they gain the benefits of an animal growth spell. This ability replaces vengeance strike.

archetype-vigilante-consumed-vigilante-v.social talents (ex): A consumed vigilante can never gain any social talents or select the Extra Social Talent feat. If the consumed vigilante would gain a social talent, they instead gain the Skill Focus feat or a feat which has Skill Focus as a prerequisite. This ability alters social talents.
archetype-vigilante-consumed-vigilante-v.focused body (su): At 1st level, a consumed vigilante needs only half as much food to avoid starvation, half as much water to avoid dehydration, and half as much sleep to heal injuries, avoid and recover from fatigue or exhaustion, and prepare spells. At 7th level, this is reduced to ¼th as much food, water, and sleep. At 13th level, a consumed vigilante no longer has to eat, drink, or sleep, although they still only require ¼th the amount of sleep to heal injuries and prepare spells. This ability replaces the 1st, 7th, and 13th level social talents.
archetype-vigilante-consumed-vigilante-v.word of mouth (ex): At 3rd level, a consumed vigilante’s accomplishments proceed them, treating them as though they had the renown social talent, although the consumed vigilante does not have to spread their own fame (they must still spend a week in the location in which they would be renowned). At 9th level, they are treated as though they had the great renown social talent and must spend only 3 days in the location which they would be renowned. At 15th level, they are treated as though they possessed the incredible renown social talent and must spend only 1 day in the location in which they would be renowned. This replaces the 3rd, 9th, and 15th level social talents.
archetype-vigilante-consumed-vigilante-v.concentrated mind (ex): At 5th level, a consumed vigilante learns how to focus their thoughts on only a single goal, gaining a +2 insight bonus to Will saving throws against mind-affecting effects. At 8th level and every 3 levels afterwards, this morale bonus increases by +1. At 11th level, a consumed vigilante also adds this morale bonus to saving throws against fatigue, exhaustion, sickening, and nausea. At 17th level, a consumed vigilante also adds this morale bonus to saving throws against death effects and paralysis. This ability replaces the 5th, 11th, and 17th level social talents.
archetype-vigilante-consumed-vigilante-v.truly nameless (su): At 19th level, a consumed vigilante cannot be scryed upon, and any attempts to do so automatically fail. All Knowledge (local) checks pertaining to them increase their DC by +15 to learn anything more than their assumed identity. This ability replaces the 19th level social talent.

archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.draconic identity (su): While a dragon champion is in their vigilante identity, they are treated as though they possessed the dragon type (in addition to any other type they possess) for all spells and other effects, being treated as a dragon when it would be more favorable to them. A dragon champion must select one exemplar dragon, basing their abilities off of that dragon. A dragon champion can select from the following dragons, each one associated with its energy type: Dragon Color/Type Damage Type Red, Brass, Gold fire Black, Green, Copper acid Blue, Bronze electricity White, Silver cold If the dragon champion has the draconic bloodline class feature from either the sorcerer or bloodrager class, they must select the same type as they did with that class feature. A dragon champion can choose to manifest or hide any draconic talents they possess while not in their vigilante identity as a move action, and each draconic talent they manifest while in an identity other than their vigilante identity causes them to suffer a -5 penalty on all Disguise checks and cannot benefit from the seamless guise class feature when these features are manifested. A dragon champion manifesting a dragon talent while in an identity other than their vigilante identity must make a Disguise check as though they used a vigilante talent while in their social identity, although upon making a successful Disguise check, anyone who failed this check sees nothing odd about the dragon champion. This ability alters dual identity, although it doesn’t prevent a character from taking another archetype which also alters dual identity.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.draconic talents (ex or su): A dragon champion can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.brutal bite (su): The dragon champion cloaks their jaw in draconic energy manifesting as a bite attack. This bite attack is treated as a primary natural attack and deal 1d6 damage (1d4 damage for small dragon champions). At 6th level, the dragon champion increases the critical threat range of their bite attack by by 1 (this stacks with the Improved Critical feat and the keen weapon enhancement, but is applied last) and applies 1 + 1/2 their Strength modifier on attacks made with this bite attack. At 12th level, the dragon champion’s reach with their bite attack increases by 5 feet. At 18th level, the dragon champion instead applies two times their Strength modifier on attacks made with this bite attack. If the dragon champion possess the dragon claws talent, the damage die of their bite becomes equal to that of their claws unless it would be lower.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.draconic resistance (su): The dragon champion’s body becomes incredibly resilient, gaining resist 3 against their exemplar dragon’s element. At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, this energy resistance increases by 3, becoming immunity at 16th level. In addition, the dragon champion’s natural attacks gained through draconic talents surge with power, dealing +1d4 energy damage of their exemplar dragon’s energy type. At 8th level this increases to +1d8 and at 16th level it increases to +2d8.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.dragon claws (su): The dragon champion sheathes their hands in draconic energy manifesting as a pair of claws. These claws are treated as a primary natural attack and deal 1d4 damage (1d3 damage for small dragon champions). At 6th level and every six levels thereafter, these claws increase their damage die by 1 size (1d6 at 6th, 1d8 at 12th, and 2d6 at 18th).
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.dragon slayer’s blade (su): The dragon champion can channel their wyrm breath into a weapon they are currently wielding (including unarmed strikes) as an attack action, allowing them to make a single attack with it (this can be used with the Vital Strike feat, one punch assault vigilante talent [Legendary Villains: Vigilantes], or an iaijutsu slash from the mercurial duelist archetype, being treated as an iaijutsu talent for the limit of iaijutsu talents that can be applied to an iaijutsu slash). This attack deals additional damage equal to the dragon champion’s breath weapon upon a successful hit, being treated as the wyrm breath talent for the purposes of ignoring energy resistance and immunity. A dragon champion must have the wyrm breath talent and be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.fearsome facade (su): The dragon champion’s presence is terrifying to others, gaining the Dazzling Display feat, being treated as though they had the Weapon Focus feat for all natural weapons gained with draconic talents and the draconic bloodline for the purposes of using this feat. At 6th level, they can use the Dazzling Display feat as a move action. At 12th level, they can use the Dazzling Display feat as a swift action. At 18th level, any creature demoralized by the dragon champion using their Dazzling Display feat is frightened instead of shaken for the duration of the demoralization. A dragon champion must have either the brutal bite, dragon claws, tyrant tail talent or the draconic bloodline power to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.great wyrm breath (su): The dragon champion’s breath weapon increases to a 30 ft. cone or a 60 ft. line and adds +2 damage to each d6 of damage it deals. At 16th level, it again increases to a 45 ft. cone or 90 ft. line. A dragon champion must have the wyrm breath talent and be 8th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.steel scales (su): The dragon champion’s skin gleams with a coat of shimmering scales, gaining a +1 natural armor bonus and DR 1/magic (this damage reduction stacks with similar damage reduction ). At 6th level and every four levels afterwards, this natural armor bonus and damage reduction increases by +1.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.true dragon blood (ex): The dragon champion’s draconic talents (except for the fearsome facade or wyrm breath talents as well as talents which require those talents as a prerequisite) are now extraordinary abilities instead of supernatural abilities. The dragon champion gains a +1 bonus on all Intimidate and Diplomacy checks for each draconic talent they manifest. For every two draconic talents the dragon champion manifest (including this one), they treat their dragon champion level as 1 higher for the effects of the manifested talents. A draconic champion must have either the brutal bite, dragon claws, steel scales, tyrant tail, or wings of the beast talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.tyrant tail (su): The dragon champion can form a strong tail behind them made of draconic energy, granting them a tail attack. This tail attack is treated as a secondary natural attack and deals 1d6 damage (1d4 for small dragon champions). At 6th level, trip attempts made with this tail attack gain a +2 bonus and if the dragon champion’s trip attempt fails by 10 or more, they can’t be tripped in return. At 12th level, this tail is treated as a primary natural attack. At 18th level, whenever the dragon champion makes a successful attack with their tail, they can make a free trip attack with it. If the dragon champion possesses the dragon claws talent, the damage of their tail attack becomes equal to that of their claws unless it would be lower.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.wings of the beast (su): The dragon champion forms a spectral pair of wings, granting them a fly speed of 40 ft. with average maneuverability. At 12th level, their flight speed increases to 60 ft. with good maneuverability, while at 18th level their flight speed increases to 100 ft. with perfect maneuverability. A dragon champion must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dragon-champion-vigi.wyrm breath (su): The dragon champion gains the ability to channel their draconic might into a breath weapon. This breath weapon deals 1d6 damage determined by the dragon champion’s exemplar dragon. This breath weapon can either be a 15 ft. cone or a 30 ft. line, and the dragon champion must wait 1 round after using their breath weapon before using it again. At 4th level and every three levels afterwards, the damage of the dragon champion’s breath weapon increases by +1d6 damage. At 6th level the dragon champion’s breath weapon ignores up to 10 points of energy resistance against the energy type it deals. At 12th level, the dragon champion instead ignores up to 20 points of energy resistance. At 18th level, the dragon champion’s breath weapon ignores all energy resistance and immunity. Wyrm breath is treated as the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purposes of feats and other abilities which require it.

archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.aura of evil (ex): The power of a dread champion’s aura of evil (see the detect good spell) is equal to their dread champion level. A paladin who uses smite evil on a dread champion deals 2 points of damage per paladin level on their first successful attack.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.smite good (su): A dread champion gains the smite good class feature of the antipaladin, treating their dread champion level as their antipaladin level for the purpose of how much damage they deal with this ability. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, they can smite good 1 additional time per day. This ability replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.malice sight (su): At 1st level, a dread champion gains the detect good class feature of the antipaladin. This replaces the 1st level social talent.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.dread talents (su): A dread champion can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.aura of cowardice (su): A dread champion gains the aura of cowardice class feature of the antipaladin.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.dedicated smite (su): A dread champion treats all good foes as though they were outsiders with the good subtype when determining how much damage their smite deals. A dread champion must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.fiendish companion (su): A dread champion gains the fiendish boon class feature, although they are only able to gain the service of a fiendish servant. A dread champion must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.limited unholy resilience (su): A dread champion gains a bonus equal to their Charisma modifier (if any) on their saving throws; this bonus cannot exceed the dread champion’s class level.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.protective resilience (su): If a dread champion is wearing light armor or no armor, they gain a bonus equal to their Charisma modifier (if any) to their armor class; this bonus cannot exceed the dread champion’s class level.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.reckless smite (su): A dread champion treats all neutral creatures as good for their smite good. A dread champion must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.villainous smite (su): While a dread soul is smiting a foe, they treat their BAB as equal to their character level for the purpose of attacks being made against the target of their smite. Spellcasting At 4th level, a dread champion can cast divine spells as an antipaladin and uses the antipaladin’s spell list. A dread champion who is lawful evil replaces protection from law with protection from chaos, magic circle against law with magic circle against chaos, and dispel law with dispel chaos. A neutral evil dread champion can choose to replace these spells once they gain this class feature. Once the choice to replace these spells has been made, it cannot be changed. This ability replaces the 4th, 8th, 12th, and 16th level vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.cruel smite (su): At 5th level, a dread champion gains a cruelty, treating their dread champion level as their effective antipaladin level for which cruelty they can select. Whenever the dread champion uses their smite, once per round as a free action they can apply one cruelty to the target of their smite upon a successful hit. At 10th level and every 5 levels thereafter, they can select an additional cruelty, although they can only apply 1 cruelty to their smite at a time. This ability replaces startling appearance and stunning appearance.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.masked evil (su): At 5th level, a dread champion is treated as though under the constant effect of an undetectable alignment spell with a caster level equal to their vigilante level. At 9th level, this instead changes to aura alteration (although they can only manipulate their alignment aura), and at 13th level they can also manipulate their emotion, health, and magical aura with this ability. This ability replaces the 5th, 9th, and 13th level social talents.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.aura of despair (su): At 11th level, a dread champion gains the aura of despair class feature of the antipaladin. This ability replaces frightening appearance.
archetype-vigilante-dread-champion-vigil.dominant cruelty (su): At 20th level, whenever the dread champion uses their cruel smite, their foe must roll their saving throw twice, taking the lower result. This ability replaces vengeance strike.

archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.dynamic specialization (ex): A dynamic striker must choose to be either a brawler dynamic strike or a technician dynamic strike. A brawler dynamic striker is treated as an avenger vigilante for the purpose of their base attack bonus and which talents they can select. A technician dynamic striker gains the studied combat class feature of an Investigator of their level (with a minimum bonus on attack rolls of +1), This effect lasts for a number of rounds equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) or until they deal damage with a knockout blow, whichever comes first. A dynamic striker can only benefit from this ability when making an attack with an unarmed strike, cestus, gauntlet, spiked gauntlet, or rope gauntlet. This ability replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.martial arts talents (ex or su): A dynamic striker can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents. A dynamic striker also uses their Wisdom modifier to determine the saving throws of their vigilante talents instead of their Charisma modifier, and if a vigilante talent requires an attack roll, they must make this attack roll with an unarmed strike.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.cross counter (ex): Whenever they successfully deflect an attack with their cross guard, the dynamic striker can spend an additional use of their cross guard to make an attack of opportunity against the foe whose attack they deflected. Only a tactical dynamic strike can select this talent, and they must be 4th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.crush counter (ex): Whenever the dynamic striker uses their cross counter, if their attack roll exceeds their foe’s AC by 10 or more, it is treated as a critical threat. At 20th level, it is treated as a critical hit. Only a tactical dynamic striker can select this talent, and they must have the cross counter talent and be 14th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.dynamic roll (ex): Whenever a dynamic striker makes a full?attack action, they can designate it as a dynamic roll. When a dynamic striker makes a dynamic roll, each time they make a successful attack against the same foe, they gain a cumulative +1 circumstance bonus to their attack and damage rolls against that foe until the beginning of their next turn (up to a maximum of the dynamic striker’s Wisdom modifier). Whenever the dynamic striker misses an attack, this bonus is reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 0). At 8th level, if the dynamic striker makes 4 or more successful attacks against the same foe, that foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or become staggered for 1 round. At 14th level, if the dynamic striker makes 6 or more successful attacks against the same foe, that foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or fall unconscious for 1d3 rounds. After using this talent, the dynamic striker is flat-footed for 1 round or the next time they are attacked. A dynamic striker must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.effortless counter (ex): Whenever a dynamic striker uses their cross guard to successfully deflect an attack, if their attack roll exceeds their foe’s by 10 or more, the dynamic striker does not need to spend an additional use of their cross guard to use their cross counter. Only a tactical dynamic striker can select this talent, and they must have the cross counter talent and be 8th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.finesse fist (ex): When making an attack with an unarmed strike, the dynamic strike can use their Dexterity modifier in place of their Strength modifier on attack and damage rolls.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.ki pool (su): The dynamic striker gains the ki class feature of the unchained monk, although if they are not lawful, they can pick a different component of their alignment when they reach 13th level, treating their unarmed strikes as that alignment for the purpose of damage reduction. Technical dynamic strikers can spend 1 ki point to use their cross guard ability.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.ki power (su): The dynamic striker gains a ki power of their choice as per the unchained monk class feature. A dynamic striker must have the ki power talent to select this power, and they can select this talent multiple times, each time selecting a different ki power.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.limited flurry of blows (ex): The dynamic striker gains the flurry of blows class feature of a monk of their dynamic striker level. After using this talent, the dynamic strike is fatigued for 1 round and cannot use their cross guard ability until the beginning of their next round. Only a technician dynamic striker can select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.martial training (ex): The dynamic striker can treat their dynamic striker level as their monk level for the purpose of meeting the prerequisites of feats and also gain a single combat feat for which they qualify.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.shadow boxing (ex): If the dynamic striker has no uses of their cross guard ability, they can spend 5 minutes practicing to regain 1 use of it. Only a technical dynamic striker can select this talent, and they must be 4th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.speed study (ex): The dynamic striker gains the quick study investigator talent as well as removing the limit on the number of times a dynamic striker can target someone with their studied combat. Only a technician dynamic striker can select this talent, and they must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.stunning versatility (ex): The dynamic striker gains the stunning fist class feature as a monk of their dynamic striker level.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.style counter (ex): The dynamic striker gains a style strike as per the unchained monk class feature, being able to use it whenever they use their cross counter talent. If the dynamic striker has the style knockout talent, they can use any style strike gained with that talent with their cross counter. Only a tactical dynamic striker can select this talent, and they can select this talent multiple times, each time selecting a different style strike, and must have the cross counter talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.style knockout (ex): The dynamic striker gains a style strike as per the unchained monk class feature, being able to use it whenever they make a knockout blow. If the dynamic striker has the style counter talent, they can use any style strike gained with that talent with their knockout blow. Only a tactical dynamic striker can select this talent, and they can select this talent multiple times, each time selecting a different style strike, and must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.style strike (ex): The dynamic striker gains a style strike as per the unchained monk class feature, being able to use it whenever they make a full-attack action. At 14th level, a dynamic striker can use a second style strike while making a full-attack action, either the same style strike twice or another if they select this talent a second time. Only a brawler dynamic striker can select this talent, and this talent can be selected multiple times, each time gaining a new style strike.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.trained fist (ex): The dynamic striker gains weapon training 1 for the close weapon group, although they treat the close weapon group as including only unarmed strikes, brass knuckles, cestuses, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and rope gauntlets. Only a brawler dynamic striker can select this talent, and they must be 8th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.vacuum fist (su): The dynamic striker can attack foes 15 ft. from themselves, attacking with their raw ki. At 8th level, this range increases to 30 ft. At 14th level, this range increases to 45 ft. This talent is treated as a ranged attack of one size smaller than the mercurial duelist for how wind and other effects affect it. A dynamic striker must have the ki talent to select this talent. This ability alters vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.dynamic training (ex): At 3rd level, a brawler dynamic striker gains the vicious impact ability, while a technician dynamic striker gains the cross guard ability.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.vicious impact (ex): A brawler dynamic striker’s unarmed strikes deal damage as though they were a monk of their dynamic striker level.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.cross guard (ex): A number of times per day equal to the dynamic striker’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), when a creature being targeted by their studied combat makes an attack against the dynamic striker, the dynamic striker can attempt to deflect that attack. The dynamic striker makes an attack roll as though making an attack of opportunity; for each size category the attacking creature is larger than the dynamic striker, the dynamic striker takes a –2 penalty on this roll. If their result is greater than the attacking creature’s result, the creature’s attack automatically misses. The dynamic striker must declare the use of this ability after the creature’s attack is announced, but before its attack roll is made. A dynamic striker can only use this ability with an unarmed strike, cestus, gauntlet, spiked, gauntlet, or rope gauntlet. Each time the dynamic striker confirms a critical hit or reduces a creature to 0 or fewer hit points with an unarmed strike, cestus, gauntlet, spiked gauntlet, or rope gauntlet while in the heat of combat, they regain 1 use of this ability (up to an amount equal to their Wisdom modifier). Confirming a critical hit or reducing a creature to 0 or fewer hit points against a helpless or unaware creature or on a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the dynamic striker’s character level does not restore a use of this ability. This ability replaces unshakable and frightening appearance.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.advanced dynamic technique (ex): At 5th level, a brawler dynamic striker gains the dynamic flurry ability while a technician dynamic striker gains the knockout blow ability.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.dynamic flurry (ex): A dynamic striker gains the flurry of blows class feature as an unchained monk of their dynamic striker level.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.knockout blow (ex): A dynamic striker gains the ability to pick out the most vulnerable point on a foe. They can make a knockout blow against the target of their studied combat as a free action, upon successfully hitting their studied target with a melee attack, to deal additional damage. The damage is 1d6 at 5th level, and increases by 1d6 for every 3 levels thereafter (to a maximum of 6d6 at 20th level). The damage of a knockout blow is precision damage and is not multiplied on a critical hit; creatures that are immune to sneak attacks are also immune to knockout blows. The dynamic striker must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot. A dynamic striker cannot use knockout blow against a creature with total concealment. This ability replaces startling appearance and stunning appearance.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.perfect dynamic mastery (ex): At 20th level, a brawler dynamic striker gains the perfect strike ability, while a tactical dynamic striker gains the perfect knockout ability.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.perfect strike (ex): A dynamic striker ignores all damage reduction and hardness on attacks made with their unarmed strikes.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.perfect knockout (ex): A dynamic striker can spend 1 use of their cross guard to maximize all damage done with their knockout blow. This ability replaces vengeance strike.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.lone identity (ex): Rather than focusing on maintaining a second identity, an exposed vigilante instead prefers to focus on their skills. A vigilante gains 1 additional skill point for each vigilante level they possess as well as an additional social talent at 1st level. This ability replaces dual identity and seamless guise.
archetype-vigilante-dynamic-striker-vigi.social talents (ex): An exposed vigilante cannot gain the following social talents: case the joint, everyman, feign innocence, immediate change, many guises, quick change, or any other that would rely on them possessing more than 1 identity, although they are always treated as though they were in their social identity for the effects of social talents. Special: A vigilante who has had their identity exposed can spend 1 week to gain this archetype, trading out all social talents that require a second identity with new ones. A vigilante with this archetype can also spend 1 week to remove this archetype, losing the additional skill points and social talent gained with this archetype in the process. A vigilante can only gain or lose this archetype once in this fashion.

archetype-vigilante-focused-hunter-vigil.familiar terrain (ex): At 5th level, a focused hunter may select a type of terrain from the Favored Terrains table. The focused hunter gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks when they are in this terrain. A focused hunter traveling through their favored terrain normally leaves no trail and cannot be tracked (though they may leave a trail if they so choose). A focused hunter also adds half their level to Survival skill checks made to follow tracks even if they aren’t in a familiar terrain. At 10th and every 5 levels thereafter, the focused hunter may select an additional favored terrain. In addition, at each such interval, the skill bonus and initiative bonus in any one favored terrain (including the one just selected, if so desired), increases by +2. If a specific terrain falls into more than one category of favored terrain, the focused hunter’s bonuses do not stack; they simply use whichever bonus is higher. This ability replaces startling appearance.
archetype-vigilante-focused-hunter-vigil.hide in plain sight (ex): At 11th level, a focused hunter gains the hide in plain sight vigilante talent, and they do not have to be within 10 ft. of dim light to hide as long as they are in one of their favored terrains. If they already possess this talent, they can select another for which they would qualify. This ability replaces frightening appearance.
archetype-vigilante-focused-hunter-vigil.terrain master (ex): At 17th level, whenever a focused hunter is in one of their favored terrains, they can spend a swift action to gain total concealment. This concealment is lost if the focused hunter attacks any creature as per invisibility. This ability replaces stunning appearance.

archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.luck thief (su): At 1st level, a fortune thief gains access to a pool of luck, granting them the supernatural ability to draw upon the misfortune of others. They gain a hex of their choice from the witch class. Whenever a creature fails a save against a hex originating from the fortune thief, the fortune thief gains 1 luck point, being able to possess a number of luck points equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Whenever a fortune thief gains a luck point, it lasts indefinitely until they spend it or die, although their luck does not refill after resting. A fortune thief can spend 1 luck point as a free action to reroll 1 skill check or gain a +1 luck bonus to attack and damage rolls for a number of rounds equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). For every 4 levels beyond 1st, this luck bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +5 at 17th level. A fortune thief can only gain 1 luck point from a creature, needing to wait 1 week before being able to gain another luck point from that creature, and a creature that voluntarily fails a save against the fortune’s thief does not provide any luck points. A creature must have a number of Hit Dice equal to or greater than half the fortune thief ’s character level or the fortune thief does not gain any luck points when they fail a save against a non-harmless hex. A fortune thief can use their Charisma modifier to determine the save DC and other effects of hexes, including those gained from other classes. This ability replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.fortune talents (su): A fortune thief can select a hex instead of a vigilante talent, and is treated as though they possessed the hex class feature of the witch for the purposes of selecting the Extra Hex feat. A fortune thief can also select any of the following vigilante talents in addition to general vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.always lucky (su): Whenever a fortune thief rests for 8 hours, if they don’t possess any luck points, they gain 1 luck point. At 10th level, if they have 1 or less luck points after resting for 8 hours, they instead increase their luck points to 2. The fortune thief can only benefit from this ability once every 24 hours.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.hex strike (ex): A fortune thief gains the Hex Strike feat, although they can choose to apply it to a melee weapon other than an unarmed strike. Once this weapon is selected, it cannot be changed. If the fortune thief chooses to apply it to their unarmed strikes, they gain Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat if they don’t already have it. A fortune thief does not need to meet the prerequisites for these feats.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.hoarded luck (ex): Whenever a fortune thief has three or more luck points, they gain a +1 luck bonus on attack and damage rolls, AC, skill checks, and saving throws. For each two luck points beyond three the luck thief possesses, this bonus increases by +1.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.hot streak (su): Whenever a fortune thief spends a luck point to gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls or AC, this bonus lasts for an additional number of rounds equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.impossibly lucky (su): Whenever a fortune thief spends a luck point to reroll a skill check, attack roll, or saving throw, they gain a luck bonus on this roll equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). A fortune thief must be 8th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.improved luck (su): A fortune thief increases the amount of luck they can possess by 2. At 8th level and every 4 levels afterwards, the amount of luck the fortune thief can possess is increased by an additional 1. A fortune thief must be 4th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.lucky dodge (su): As a free action, a fortune thief can spend a luck point to gain a luck bonus to their AC equal to their charisma modifier until the beginning of their next round. At 6th level, this bonus is doubled against attack rolls to confirm critical hits. At 12th level, the fortune thief gains a 50% chance to ignore critical hits or sneak attacks while this talent is active. At 18th level, this is increased to a 75% chance to ignore critical hits or sneak attack.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.lucky hit (su): As a free action, a fortune thief can spend a luck point to reroll an attack or damage roll. At 8th level, the fortune thief can spend 3 luck points to make an additional attack at their highest base attack bonus. At 16th level, when the fortune thief spends luck points to make an additional attack, they can roll that attack roll twice, taking the better result.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.lucky save (su): As an immediate action, a fortune thief can spend 2 luck points to reroll one saving throw, although they must accept the results of this new saving throw, even if it is worse than the original. At 8th level, the fortune thief can instead spend 2 luck points to force a creature to reroll any critical threat made against them.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.major hex (su): A fortune thief gains a major hex and can select major hexes with the Extra Hex feat and in place of a vigilante talent. A fortune thief must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.savage hex (su): Whenever a fortune thief uses a hex against a creature, on a failed save the creature also takes damage equal to the fortune thief ’s level.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.split hex (su): A fortune thief gains the Split Hex feat. The fortune thief does not need to meet the prerequisites for this feat. A fortune thief must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.split hex, improved (su): A fortune thief gains the Split Major Hex feat. The fortune thief does not need to meet the prerequisites for this feat. A fortune thief must have the split hex and major hex talents and be 18th level or higher to select this talent. This ability alters vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-fortune-thief-vigila.ultimate luck (su): At 20th level, a fortune thief learns a grand hex, and any creature that fails a save against a grand hex grants them 2 luck points. A fortune thief can spend all of their luck points (minimum 1) whenever they would be reduced to 0 or lower hit points as an immediate action, negating all damage they would receive until the beginning of their next round. This ability replaces vengeance strike.

archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.weapon and armor proficiencies: Masked grapplers are not proficient with martial weapons or medium armor. This alters A vigilante’s weapon and armor proficiencies.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.grappling genius (ex): At 1st level, a masked grappler gains the Improved Unarmed Strike and Improved Grapple feat, using their masked grappler level in place of their base attack bonus when calculating their Combat Maneuver Bonus when making grapple combat maneuvers. Base attack bonuses granted from other classes are unaffected and are added normally. Whenever a masked grappler deals damage with a grapple check (including submissions and techniques), they deal additional damage equal to 1/2 their masked grappler level (minimum 1). At 6th level, the masked grappler gains the Greater Grapple feat. This ability replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.grappling talents (ex): At 2nd level, a masked grappler can select two new types of vigilante talents; submissions and techniques. The masked grappler can use one of these techniques whenever they successfully maintain a grapple or pin. Submissions and techniques deal damage as if the masked grappler chose to deal damage with their grapple, and after using a technique, the grapple is ended for both the masked wrestler and their foe. Using a technique or submission ends the masked grappler’s turn. If a masked grappler continues to use a submission which causes their foe to suffer a penalty, that penalty is increased by 1 for each round the submission is maintained as well as resetting the duration of the penalty. A masked grappler using a submission talent must use the grapple check needed to maintain a grapple to continue the submission or end the submission. Each round the masked grappler maintains a submission, their opponent suffers a -1 penalty against saving throws for that submission. The masked grappler uses their Constitution modifier to determine the saving throws of their vigilante techniques in place of their Charisma modifier, and they must select either a submission or technique for their first vigilante talent. A masked grappler can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.anklelock (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler twists the ankle of a foe as hard as they can, attempting to snap their foe’s ankle. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or have their base land speed be reduced by 10 feet (to a minimum of 0 feet) and take a -3 penalty to reflex saves for 1 minute. At 8th level this penalty increases to 15 ft. and -4. This talent does not work on foes without legs.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.armbar (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler manages to wrench a foe’s arm or other limb, attempting to snap it. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or take a -1 penalty on all attacks for 1 minute. At 6th level, this penalty increases to -2. At 12th level this penalty increases to -3. This talent does not work on foes without limbs.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.bearhug (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler grabs a foe and squeezes the life from out of them. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or be fatigued for 1 minute. At 10th level, the foe is instead exhausted.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.bodyslam (ex): [technique]: A masked grappler is capable of lifting creatures up to one size larger than themselves or smaller into the air and dropping them onto their back, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. Both you and your foe fall prone after this technique. At 10th level, this talent deals additional damage equal to twice the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier, and they no longer fall prone after using it. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.chokehold (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler wraps their limbs around the foe’s airway, cutting off their breathing. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or have the air expelled from their lungs, and must make saves against drowning as long as the submission is maintained. A masked grappler must be 8th level or higher to select this talent, and does not work on foes without heads or foes that do not need to breathe.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.frog splash (ex): Whenever a masked grappler is standing on a solid surface 5 ft. or higher than a prone foe, they can make an Acrobatics check to jump into the foe’s square, making an unarmed strike against them which deals two times as much damage. If the attack is successful, the masked grappler can make a grapple check as a swift action to pin them. For every 10 ft. that the masked grappler falls to make this attack, they deal an additional +1d6 damage, and the masked grappler only takes falling damage if they miss with this attack. At 6th level and every 6 levels afterwards, the masked grappler can treat themselves as 10 ft. higher for the purposes of how much damage this talent deals.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.full nelson (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler pins the arms of their foe behind them, applying pressure to their arms. The foe must make a Reflex saving throw or be flat?footed for the duration of this submission, providing cover to the masked grappler. At 6th level, all attacks against a foe in this submission gain +2 precision damage. This damage increases to +4 at 12th level and +6 at 18th level, and this submission does not work on foes without arms.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.hard whip (ex): [technique]: A masked grappler whips their foe forward, forcing them 30 feet in a direction of their choice. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity, and if the foe’s movement is stopped by a solid barrier such as a wall, they take 1d6 damage and are bounced in the opposite direction for the remaining distance. Foes that enter a square threatened by the masked grappler after being bounced provoke an attack of opportunity from them, which must be made with an unarmed strike. This movement is ended if the foe would be bounced twice. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.hurricanrana (ex): [technique]: A masked grappler jumps onto their foe and throws them forward with their legs, disorientating them. The foe must make a Reflex saving throw or be flat-footed for 1 round. At 8th level, the foe is flat-footed for 2 rounds. At 16th level, the foe is flat-footed for 3 rounds.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.joint lock (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler knows how to break bones with their submissions. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or take 1d3 Dexterity damage. At 12th level, this damage increases to 1d4 Dexterity damage. At 16th level, this damage increases to 1d6 Dexterity damage. A masked grappler must be 8th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.lightweight grappler (ex): A masked grappler uses their Dexterity modifier in place of their Strength modifier for grapple checks and in place of their Constitution modifier when determining the damage of techniques and submissions.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.kip up (ex): Whenever a masked grappler is prone, they can stand as a swift action that does not provoke opportunity. They can also choose to stand as a move action, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to their Strength modifier (minimum 1) to a creature within their reach. At 8th level, they deal damage equal to two times their strength modifier with this talent. At 16th level, they deal damage equal to three times their Strength modifier.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.nerve pinch (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler’s knowledge of anatomy allows them to specifically target their foe’s nerves, lowering their defenses. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or take a -2 penalty to all saving throws for 1 minute. At 10th level, this penalty increases to -3.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.piledriver (ex): [technique]: A masked grappler can lift up a large or smaller creature and drive their head into the ground with tremendous force, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or suffer 1d3 Constitution damage, falling prone regardless of the saving throw. A masked grappler must be 14th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.pinning submission (ex): A masked grappler increases the damage of submissions to pinned foes by an amount equal to their Constitution modifier. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher and have at least 1 submission talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.pinning suplex (ex): [technique]: A masked grappler is capable of both dealing damage and keeping an opponent close, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. Unlike a normal technique, a pinning suplex doesn’t break a grapple, and the masked grappler can attempt a grapple check to pin their foe as a swift action before the end of their round (this has no additional effect against a foe who is already pinned ). A masked grappler must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.running dropkick (ex): A masked grappler can choose to fly at an opponent without thinking, dealing two times their unarmed strike damage on a charge attack. After this attack, the masked grappler falls prone. At 16th level, this attack deals three times their unarmed strike damage. A masked grappler must be 8th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.sleeper hold (ex): [submission]: A masked grappler can wrap their arms around a foe’s neck, slowly putting them to sleep. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or become unconscious for 1d3 rounds. Continuing to use this submission does not reset the duration. A masked grappler must be 10th level or higher to select this talent and does not work on foes without heads.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.stiff clothesline (ex): Whenever the masked grappler makes a charge attack using an unarmed strike, if their charge attack is successful, they can make a trip attempt as a swift action (this trip attempt does not provoke an attack of opportunity ). If the masked grappler uses the hard whip talent, they can use this talent as an attack of opportunity without needing to make a charge attack.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.stunner (ex): [technique]: A masked grappler can strike their opponent with a vicious one two combination, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or be stunned for 1 round, falling prone regardless of the saving throw. A masked grappler must be 14th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.team up (ex): When a masked grappler is grappling someone with one or more creatures assisting them, they can add the Strength modifier of one of those other creatures to the damage of a technique. At 10th level, they can add two times that creature’s Strength modifier. A masked grappler must have at least 1 technique talent to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.technical specialist (ex): Whenever a masked grappler has a foe pinned, that foe must make two successful grapple checks to end the pin, the first successful grapple check simply bringing them back to being grappled instead of pinned. At 8th level, the foe must make three successful grapple checks, needing to succeed at two to bring them to being grappled instead of pinned. At 16th level, the masked grappler suppresses any freedom of movement spell or effect the target may have.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.tenacious grappler (ex): Whenever a masked grappler uses a technique talent against a foe, they can attempt to grapple that foe as a swift action before their round ends. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher to select this talent. This alters vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.signature move (ex): At 5th level, a masked grappler learns how to make one submission or technique their own, adding a special flourish or secret technique to make it all the more devastating. The masked grappler must select 1 submission or technique, designating it as their signature move. Whenever they use their signature move, it deals an additional +1d6 damage and increases any DC associated with it by 1. Whenever a masked grappler gains a new vigilante talent, they can choose to change their signature move. This ability replaces startling appearance.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.chain grappler (ex): At 11th level, whenever the masked wrestler uses a submission or technique, they make two grapple checks, making the second with a -5 penalty. If both grapple checks overcome their foe’s CMD, they deal two times as much damage with that submission or technique. This ability replaces frightening appearance.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.finishing move (ex): At 17th level, a masked grappler has honed their moves to a fine edge, instead imbuing it with much more power. The masked grappler changes their signature move into their finishing move. Whenever the masked grappler uses their finishing move, it deals an additional +3d6 damage and increases any DC associated with it by 2. A masked grappler also designates another submission or technique to be their signature move. This ability replaces stunning appearance.
archetype-vigilante-masked-grappler-vigi.master technician (ex): At 20th level, a masked grappler’s moves all have their own flare, everything they do becomes unique to them. All of the masked grappler’s submissions and techniques are treated as signature moves, and they can designate a second submission or technique as a finishing move. This ability replaces vengeance strike.

archetype-vigilante-mech-renegade-vigila.delayed vigilante specialization: The morphmech renegade does not select a vigilante specialization until 2nd level. This alters vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-mech-renegade-vigila.bonded mech: The morphmech renegade gains a bonded mech, treating his class level as his pilot level. This replaces the vigilante talents gained at 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th levels.
archetype-vigilante-mech-renegade-vigila.pilot’s entrance (su): Starting at 5th level, whenever the morphmech renegade assumes his vigilante identity, he may call his mech to his location as part of the action used to change identities. The mech appears as soon as the change is complete, and the morphmech renegade may enter his mech as a free action. This ability does not work if either the mech or the morphmech renegade is in an area where teleportation does not function. This replaces startling appearance.
archetype-vigilante-mech-renegade-vigila.morphic mech (ps): Starting at 11th level, the morphmech renegade gains the ability to use reconfiguration* as a psi-like ability a number of times per day equal to 1/2 his vigilante level. This replaces frightening appearance.
archetype-vigilante-mech-renegade-vigila.turbo morph (ps): At 17th level, the morphmech renegade may expend two uses of his reconfiguration psilike ability to use the ability as a swift action. Alternatively, he may expend three uses to use mechanical combination* as a psi-like ability as a swift action with a manifester level equal to his vigilante level. This ability replaces stunning appearance.

archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.noble vigilante (ex): A noble soul’s vigilante alignment must be good, and their vigilante identity and their social identity must be within one step of each other on the alignment axis. In addition, if the noble soul’s social identity is not good, they can’t use their righteous vision, heroic specialization, or spellcasting class features.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.heroic specialization (su): At 1st level, a noble soul must choose to be either a crusader or a healer. A crusader gains the smite evil class feature of a paladin, treating their noble soul level as their paladin level for the purpose of how much damage they deal with this ability. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, they can smite evil 1 additional time per day. A healer gains the lay on hands class feature of a paladin, treating their vigilante level as their paladin level to determine how much they heal with this ability. A healer can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 1/2 their vigilante level plus their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). This replaces vigilante specialization.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.noble aura (su): At 1st level, a noble soul gains the aura of good class feature of a paladin while in their vigilante identity.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.righteous vision (su): At 1st level, a noble soul gains the detect evil class feature of a paladin. This ability replaces the 1st level social talent.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.heroic talents (su): A noble soul can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.avenging smite (su): While a noble soul is smithing a foe, they treat their BAB as equal to their character level for the purpose of attacks being made against the target of their smite. Only a crusader noble soul can select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.divine mount (su): A noble soul gains the divine bond class feature, although they can only select to gain a mount with this talent. A noble soul must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.focused smite (su): A noble soul treats all evil foes as though they were outsiders with the evil subtype when determining how much damage their smile deals. Only a crusader noble soul can select this talent, and they must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.limited divine grace (su): A noble soul gains a bonus equal to their Charisma modifier (if any) on their saving throws; this bonus cannot exceed the noble soul’s character level.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.heroic courage (su): A noble soul gains the aura of courage class feature of a paladin.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.life link (su): A noble soul gains the life link revelation of a life mystery oracle.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.mercy (su): A noble soul gains a mercy as a paladin of their level. Only a healer noble soul can select this talent, and they must be 4th level or higher to select this talent, although they can select it multiple times, each time gaining a different mercy.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.protective grace (su): If a noble soul is wearing light armor or no armor, they gain a bonus equal to their Charisma modifier (if any) to their armor class; this bonus cannot exceed the noble soul’s character level. Holding a shield does not affect this talent.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.unbound smite (su): A noble soul treats all nongood creatures as evil for the purpose of their smite evil. Only a crusader noble soul can select this talent, and they must be 6th level or higher to select this talent. This ability alters vigilante talents. Spellcasting At 4th level, a noble soul can cast divine spells as a paladin and uses the paladin’s spell list. A noble soul who is chaotic good replaces protection from chaos with protection from law, magic circle against chaos with magic circle against law, and dispel chaos with dispel law. A neutral good noble soul can choose to replace these spells once they gain this class feature. Once the choice to replace these spells has been made, it cannot be changed. This ability replaces the 4th, 8th, 12th, and 16th level vigilante talents.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.ultimate nobility (su): At 20th level, a crusader noble soul gains the true justice ability, while a healer noble soul gains the true compassion ability:
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.true compassion (su): The noble soul treats their lay on hands as the heal and breath of life spells for which conditions it can remove and how it interacts with dead creatures.
archetype-vigilante-noble-soul-vigilante.true justice (su): The noble soul auto confirms all critical threats made while using their smite evil. This ability replaces vengeance strike.

archetype-vigilante-outrageous-lyricist-.vibrant transformation (su): An outrageous lyricist gains the transformation of the magical child archetype.
