archetype-bard-sublime-bard-archetype.leadership: At 10th level, a sublime gains Leadership as a bonus feat. This replaces jack of all trades.

archetype-bard-beguiling-performer-bard-.performative magic (ex): While the beguiling performer has their bardic performance active, they may disguise their spellcasting by making a Perform check, using the perform type that matches their bardic performance method, opposed by an observer’s Sense Motive. On a failure, the observer is considered flat-footed to any spell attack roll and they do not know you are casting a spell until they suffer its effects. This ability replaces countersong.
archetype-bard-beguiling-performer-bard-.surprise spell (su): Beginning at 5th level, If a target is unaware of the beguiling performer’s spellcasting, either because they are flat-footed or because the beguiling performer succeeded in using the performative magic ability, the DCs of the spell cast is increased by 1. This bonus increases by 1 every 5 levels thereafter. This ability uses 3 rounds of bardic music to activate and is a free action. This ability replaces lore master.

archetype-bard-necrodancer-bard-archetyp.spiritual accompaniment (su): At 1st level, the bard can call up a group of spirits as a standard action to aid in their performance. The spirits can only be called when the necrodancer has their performance active. The spirits always provide the other performance type to increase which performances may be made. For example, if the necrodancer is playing a lute and providing an auditory component, the spirits dance and caper providing a visual component. Additionally, when the necrodancer ceases maintaining their performance, the spirits maintain the benefits for 1 additional round per 4 class levels of the necrodancer. This benefit does not stack with Lingering Performance. These spirits cannot be called up in an area affected by consecrate or any other area that prevents undead from being created. Additionally, if the spirits, or the necrodancer are affected by a spell that deals positive energy damage or destroys undead, the spirits are destroyed, but can be summoned again after 1d6 rounds. This ability replaces bardic knowledge.

archetype-bard-war-chanter-bard-archetyp.inspire toughness (su): At 1st level, a war chanter can use their performance to inspire toughness in their allies (including themselves). Any affected allies gain temporary hit points equal to 1/2 the war chanter’s class level (minimum 1). These temporary hit points are refreshed each round the performance is maintained and any remaining temporary hit points remain for 5 rounds after the performance ends. This ability replaces fascinate.
archetype-bard-war-chanter-bard-archetyp.inspire recklessness (su): At 6th level, a war chanter can instill a war fervor into their allies. The allies who choose to accept the benefit take a -3 penalty to AC to gain a +3 morale bonus to attack rolls. This increases by 1, for the penalty and bonus, at 10th level and every 4 levels thereafter. This ability replaces suggestion.
archetype-bard-war-chanter-bard-archetyp.inspire legion (ex): At 10th level, the war chanter extends the radius of their performance out to 60 feet. This ability replaces jack-of-all-trades and the versatile performance gained at 10th level.
archetype-bard-war-chanter-bard-archetyp.inspire despair (su): At 18th level, when you use inspire courage, all enemies within the radius must make a Will save DC (10 + 1/2 the war chanter’s class level + their Charisma modifier) or take a penalty to saving throws against charm and fear effects and attack and weapon damage rolls. The penalty is equal to the bonus provided by inspire courage. This ability replaces mass suggestion.

archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.emotional knack (ex): An emotionist adds half their class level (minimum 1) to Diplomacy checks to improve attitude or alleviate despair, Bluff checks to induce or alleviate despair or to hide your emotional state via deceive or lie, Intimidate checks to demoralize, induce despair, or exhort morale, and Sense Motive checks to discern emotional state via hunch or opposing a Bluff check.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.inspire doubt (su): A 1st level emotionist can use their performance to inspire doubt in their enemies. To be affected, a target must be able to perceive the emotionist’s performance. An affected target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier) or be affected by the doubting condition for as long as the performance is maintained. This ability cannot raise the target’s condition above doubting. If the saving throws succeeds, the target is immune to the inspire doubt ability for 24 hours. Inspire doubt is a mind-affecting, emotion and despair effect. Inspire doubt can use audible or visual components. The emotionist must choose which component to use when starting his performance. This ability replaces fascinate.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.inspire hope (su): A 1st level emotionist can use their performance to inspire hope in their allies (including themselves), bolstering them against despair and improving their combat abilities. To be affected, an ally must be able to perceive the emotionist’s performance. An affected ally receives a +1 morale bonus on saving throws against fear and despair effects, attack rolls and weapon damage rolls. At 5th level, and every six emotionist levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +4 at 17th level. Inspire hope is a mind-affecting, emotion and hope ability. Inspire hope can use audible or visual components. The emotionist must choose which component to use when starting his performance. This ability replaces inspire courage.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.inspire rage (su): A 3rd level emotionist can use their performance to inspire fervor and rage in a target. The target must be within 30 feet and able to see and hear the emotionist. If the target is unwilling they may make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier). If they succeed, they may not be affected by inspire rage for 24 hours. An affected creature enters a rage gaining a +2 bonus on melee attack rolls, damage rolls and thrown weapon damage rolls, and Will saving throws. In addition, they take a -2 penalty on AC. The target also gains +2 temporary hit points per HD. These temporary hit points are lost first when the target takes damage, disappear when the performance ends, and are not replenished if the target enters a rage or is affected by inspire rage again within 1 minute of the ending of the performance. While under this effect, the target cannot use any Charisma -, Dexterity -, or Intelligence -based skill (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride ) or any ability that requires patience or concentration (such as spellcasting). At the end of the performance, the target is fatigued for a number of rounds equal to the rounds spent under the effect of the performance. If the target falls unconscious, they are no longer affected by the performance. At 11th and 20th levels the bonuses provided increase by 1 and the temporary hp per HD increase by 1. Inspire rage is a mind-affecting, emotion and hope ability. Inspire rage can use audible or visual components. This ability replaces inspire competence.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.emotional master: At 5th level, an emotionist becomes a master at eliciting or alleviating emotions and can take 10 on any skill check detailed in the emotional knack ability above. In addition, once per day, the bard can take 20 on any such skill check as a standard action. He can use this ability one additional time per day for every six levels he possesses beyond 5th, to a maximum of three times per day at 17th level.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.incite dread (sp): A 6th-level or higher emotionist can easily turn one’s doubts into fear as a standard action. They may target any enemy within 30 ft., that is able to see or hear the emotionist, and is currently subject to a despair effect by one of their performances. The target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier) or be frightened for 1d6 rounds. If the creature succeeds at the saving throw or the frightened duration ends, they are shaken for as long as they are within 30 feet of the emotionist while they are maintaining the despaireffect-inducing performance. Incite dread does not disrupt the underlying performance. Incite dread is a mind-affecting, fear effect, and it relies on audible and visual components. This ability replaces suggestion.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.heroic encouragement (sp): A 9th-level or higher emotionist can spur their already hopeful allies into great heroics as a standard action. The affected ally must be within 30 feet, that is able to see or hear the emotionist, and is currently subject to a hope effect by one of their performances. The ally gains temporary hit points equal to 2d10 plus their Con modifier, and their morale bonuses from the hope effect are doubled. This effect lasts for 1d4 rounds. Heroic encouragement is a mind-affecting, emotion and hope effect, and it relies on audible and visual components. Heroic encouragement does not disrupt the underlying performance. This ability replaces inspire greatness.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.dirge of despair (su): An emotionist of 8th level or higher can use his performance to foster a sense of immense despair in his enemies, causing them to become despairing. To be affected, an enemy must be within 30 feet and able to see and hear the emotionist’s performance. The effect persists for as long as the enemy is within 30 feet and the emotionist continues the performance. The performance cannot cause a creature to become hopeless, even if the targets are already doubting from another effect. Dirge of despair is a mind-affecting, emotion and despair effect, and it relies on audible and visual components. This ability replaces dirge of doom.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.calming performance (su): An emotionist of 12th level or higher can use their performance to create an effect equivalent to the mass cure serious wounds, using the emotionist’s level as the caster level. In addition, this performance removes the doubting, despairing, and shaken condition from all those affected. Using this ability requires 4 rounds of continuous performance, and the targets must be able to see and hear the emotionist throughout the performance. Calming performance relies on audible and visual components. This ability replaces soothing performance.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.hopeless harmonic (su): An emotionist of 14th level or higher can use their performance to cause hopelessness in their enemies. To be affected, an enemy must be able to hear the emotionist perform and be within 30 feet. Each enemy within range receives a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier) to negate the effect. If the save succeeds, the creature is immune to this ability for 24 hours. If the save fails, the target becomes hopeless for as long as the target can hear the bard’s performance. Hopeless harmonic relies on audible components. This ability replaces frightening tune.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.hope beyond despair (sp): An emotionist of 15th level or higher can use their performance to help their allies push past any doubts or despair they might have. Any ally affected by heroic encouragement also has one despair or fear effect of the ally’s choice removed (with the exception of curses). This ability replaces inspire heroics.
archetype-bard-emotionist-bard-archetype.mass dread (sp): This ability functions just like incite dread, but allows an emotionist of 18th level or higher to incite dread into any number of creatures that they have already affected by a despair-effect-inducing performance. Incite dread is a mind-affecting, fear effect, and it relies on audible and visual components. This ability replaces mass suggestion.

archetype-ranger-bounty-hunter-ranger-ar.quarry (ex): Beginning at 1st level, as a standard action bounty hunter can denote one target within their line of sight, or for 1 hour review a bounty or use Diplomacy to gather information, to designate a target as their quarry. Whenever they are following the tracks of their quarry, a bounty hunter can take 10 on their Survival skill checks while moving at normal speed, without penalty. In addition, they receive a +2 insight bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, Perception checks, Sense Motive checks, Survival checks, and Diplomacy checks to gather information made against their quarry. Additionally, all critical threats are automatically confirmed. They can dismiss this effect at any time as a free action, but they cannot select a new quarry for 24 hours. If the bounty hunter sees proof that their quarry is dead, or if they have successfully subdued them via non-lethal damage, they can select a new quarry after waiting 1 hour. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, the bonuses against the quarry increase by +2. At 11th level, the bounty hunter can designate a quarry as a free action within line of sight or take 10 minutes to review a bounty or gather information via Diplomacy. Additionally if the quarry is killed or subdued, the bounty hunter can select a new quarry after 10 minutes. Finally, the bounty hunter can take 20 to follow the tracks of their quarry. This ability replaces favored enemy and the quarry gained at 11th level.
archetype-ranger-bounty-hunter-ranger-ar.bring ‘em back alive (ex): It is very important for a bounty hunter to be able to cash in on their marks. At 1st level a bounty hunter can choose to do non-lethal damage with any weapon with which they are proficient without penalty. In addition, the bounty hunter increases the damage bonus from the quarry ability by 50% when dealing non-lethal damage to their quarry. This ability replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-bounty-hunter-ranger-ar.crippling strike (ex): Bounty hunters learn to efficiently slow the reflexes and defenses of their marks. At 7th level, as a swift action the bounty can deal 2 Dexterity damage to their quarry on a successful hit. This ability is usable a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces woodland stride and improved quarry.
archetype-ranger-bounty-hunter-ranger-ar.track the unseen (su): At 10th level, the bounty hunter gains the ability to track their marks even while the mark is benefiting from pass without trace or similar magic, though at a -10 penalty. This ability replaces the combat style feat gained at 10th level.
archetype-ranger-bounty-hunter-ranger-ar.master bounty hunter (ex): A bounty hunter of 20th level becomes a master of their craft. They can always move at full speed while using Survival to follow the tracks of their quarry without penalty. They can, as a standard action, make a single attack against their quarry at their full attack bonus. If the attack hits, the target takes damage normally and must make a Fortitude save or be rendered unconscious. The DC of this save is equal to 10 + 1/2 the bounty hunter’s level + their Wisdom modifier. On a failure, the target is dealt non-lethal damage equal to their remaining hit points. A successful save halves this damage or deals the weapon’s normal damage as non-lethal damage, whichever is higher. A bounty hunter can use this ability a number of times equal to 3 + their Wisdom modifier, but not against the same creature more than once in a 24-hour period. This ability replaces master hunter.

archetype-ranger-dark-hunter-ranger-arch.improved stonecunning (ex): The dark hunter gains stonecunning as the dwarven ancestral trait. If the dark hunter already has stonecunning, the bonus provided doubles. This ability replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-dark-hunter-ranger-arch.stone hue (su): At 1st level, he dark hunter taps into latent magical energies of the deep dark realms to aid in their stealth. They gain a bonus on Stealth checks equal to 1/2 their class level if they are within 5 feet of a stone or earth wall. This ability replaces endurance.
archetype-ranger-dark-hunter-ranger-arch.improved darkvision (ex): At 3rd level, the dark hunter gains or improves their darkvision by 30 feet. This distance increases by 30 feet at 8th, 13th, and 18th levels.
archetype-ranger-dark-hunter-ranger-arch.underground scout (ex): Beginning with 3rd level, the dark hunter must select underground as their favored terrain. The bonus to underground as their favored terrain increases by +2 at 8th, 13th, and 18th levels. This ability modifies favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-dark-hunter-ranger-arch.sneak attack (ex): At 4th level, the dark hunter gains a 1d6 sneak attack as the rogue ability of the same name. This ability increases by 1d6 for every 3 levels thereafter. This ability replaces hunter’s bond.

archetype-ranger-foehunter-ranger-archet.uncanny dodge (ex): At 2nd level, the foehunter gains uncanny dodge as the barbarian class feature. This ability replaces the combat style feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-ranger-foehunter-ranger-archet.sneak attack (ex): At 4th level, the foehunter gains a 1d6 sneak attack as the rogue ability of the same name. This ability increases by 1d6 for every 3 levels thereafter. This ability replaces hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-foehunter-ranger-archet.improved uncanny dodge (ex): At 8th level, the foehunter gains improved uncanny dodge as the barbarian class feature, using their ranger level as their barbarian level. This ability replaces the favored terrain gained at 8th level.
archetype-ranger-foehunter-ranger-archet.dodge critical (ex): At 10th level, the foehunter is adept at dodging the powerful attacks of their sworn foes. If subject to a confirmed critical hit by a favored enemy, the foehunter may roll a Reflex save (DC equal to the 20 + the enhancement bonus of the attacking weapon, if any). If successful the attack is converted to a normal hit. The foehunter must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to the foehunter’s Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces the combat style feat gained at 10th level.

archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.mettle (ex): At 1st level, a forward vanguard gains a Mettle pool that is refreshed each day. The pool’s maximum is equal to the forward vanguard’s Wisdom modifier, plus any feats and special abilities that increases the pool maximum. Some abilities may restore points to this pool during the day. But the forward vanguard may not have more points of Mettle than the pool’s maximum. The forward vanguard may expend Mettle to gain one of the following benefits. As an immediate action they may gain a bonus equal to their Wisdom modifier on the next non-Will saving throw. The bonus must be used before the beginning of their next turn. As part of making a Dexterity check to gain a bonus equal to their Charisma bonus. The defender of the faith may restore a point of Mettle to your pool in the following ways. If the defender of the faith uses the aid another action to assist an ally’s skill check and the ally would have failed the check without the vanguard’s action If the defender of the faith uses the aid another action to improve an ally’s AC and the ally would have been hit without the their action If an ability which expends Mettle allows for the use of an attack of opportunity, the attack of opportunity allowed by that ability may be taken even while using the total defense action.
archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.survival training (ex): At 1st level, the forward vanguard is a master of scouting and tracking. They gain a bonus equal to 1/2 their forward vanguard levels on Knowledge (nature), Knowledge (geography), Survival and Stealth checks. This ability replaces track and wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.guerrilla tactics (ex): The forward vanguard is an expert at hit-and-run tactics. At 2nd level, they gain Dodge and Run as bonus feats and at 3rd level, they gain Mobility as a bonus feat. They need not meet the prerequisites for these bonus feats. At 6th level, if the forward vanguard moves 10 feet or more in a round and makes a single attack they add an additional damage die to their attack as per the Vital Strike feat. An additional die is added at 11th as per the Improved Vital Strike feat and 16th level as per the Greater Vital Strike feat. The additional die of damage are only applied if the forward vanguard is wearing light or nor armor, though may be used in conjunction with a charge. This ability is treated as the iteration of Vital Strike the level notates for prerequisite purposes. This ability replaces the combat style feats gained at 2nd, 6th, 10th and 14th levels.
archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.screen them (ex): At 3rd level, the forward vanguard may charge forth to defend an ally. The forward vanguard may elect to place themselves in the path of danger in order to protect an ally. When rolling initiative, they may select a target as a charge. This selection may not change for the duration of the encounter. If the charge is the target of an attack, the forward vanguard may make a move as an immediate action to get themselves within 5 feet of their charge. Then they enter the square occupied by the charge and receive the attack in their place. To do so, the forward vanguard must make an Acrobatics check with a DC equal to 1/2 the feet required to be moved up to the forward vanguard’s double move distance. However, any movement used in this ability is deducted from the forward vanguard’s movement in their next turn. The attack automatically hits the forward vanguard. The charge is placed in any empty square adjacent to them of the forward vanguard’s choice. The forward vanguard may declare the use of this ability after knowing whether their charge will be hit. This ability replace the favored terrains gained at 3rd and 13th levels.
archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.nimble combatant (ex): A forward vanguard needs to be able to weave through their enemies. At 4th level, a forward vanguard may take 10 on Acrobatics to move through threatened squares. At 9th level, the forward vanguard can move at normal speed while using Acrobatics to move through threatened squares. At 15th level, the forward vanguard may take 20 on these Acrobatics checks. This ability replaces hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.charging strikes (ex): At 5th level, as a full-round action, the forward vanguard may make a special charge attack. They may make their full attack anywhere along the line of the charge, though each attack must be against a different target. The attacks must be made in the order the forward vanguard encounters a target and in order of attack iteration, however, they need not attack every creature in the line. For example, a forward vanguard may charge past a creature, attack the next creature in the line at their full base attack bonus and the third encountered creature at their second attack bonus. This ability replaced the favored enemy gained at 5th and 15th levels and quarry gained at 15th level.
archetype-ranger-forward-vanguard-ranger.active maneuvers (ex): At 8th level, the forward vanguard is trained to use their confidence in their skills to enhance their maneuverability. The forward vanguard may spend a point of Mettle to apply their Charisma bonus (if any) to their CMD and touch AC, though their touch AC may not exceed their base AC. At 12th level, the bonus may be applied to their Reflex saves. At 18th level, these bonuses always apply and do not require a point of Mettle to enact. This ability only functions if the forward vanguard is wearing light or no armor. This ability replaces the favored terrains gained at 8th and 18th levels.

archetype-ranger-sanctified-hunter-range.blessed sight (ex): Beginning with 1st level, the sanctified hunter gains a bonus equal to 1/2 their class level to saving throws against illusions. This ability replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-sanctified-hunter-range.sanctified foe (su): At 1st level, you gain your favored enemies bonuses against creatures whose alignment is at least 2 steps away from your deity’s or religion’s alignment. Additionally, if your religion has an anathema against a creature type, like undead, or against a specific creature, they may apply their bonus to them as well. The sanctified hunter does not gain additional favored enemies, though the bonus increases each time they would normally gain a new favored enemy. This ability replaces favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-sanctified-hunter-range.detect alignment (sp): The sanctified hunter can use detect chaos, detect evil, detect good, or detect law. They can only use one of these at any given time. This ability replaces favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-sanctified-hunter-range.holy magics: The sanctified hunter adds all paladin spells to their spell list in addition to ranger spells. This ability modifies spellcasting.

archetype-ranger-titan-hunter-ranger-arc.leg dodger (ex): At 2nd level, the titan hunter gains a +2 dodge bonus to their AC against creatures that are two size categories or more larger than them. This bonus increases to use their favored enemy value if higher. This ability replaces the combat style feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-ranger-titan-hunter-ranger-arc.slippery (ex): At 3rd level, the titan hunter is adept at escaping the grasp of larger foes. If they are grappled by a creature at least two size categories higher than themselves, they add 1/2 their class level to any checks made to escape the grapple. This bonus also applies to Acrobatics checks against such creatures. This ability replaces endurance.
archetype-ranger-titan-hunter-ranger-arc.close shot (ex): At 6th level, the titan hunter does not provoke attacks of opportunity using ranged attacks against creatures at least one size category larger than themselves. This ability replaces the combat style feat gained at 6th level.
archetype-ranger-titan-hunter-ranger-arc.defensive roll (ex): At 14th level, the titan hunter gains defensive roll, as the rogue talent of the same name. This ability replaces the combat style feat gained at 14th level.

archetype-ranger-witch-hunter-ranger-arc.favored enemy (spellcaster) (ex): At 1st level, the witch hunter is adept at hunting down and combating spellcasters. They gain a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks against creatures that can cast spells or use spell-like abilities. Likewise, they gain a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against such creatures. Additionally, they can automatically determine if a creature they observe has the ability to cast spells or use spell-like abilities by succeeding on a Sense Motive check (DC 10 + the CR of the creature). Finally, any spellcaster within 5 feet of the witch hunter has the DC of any concentration check increased by 2. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (10th, 15th, and 20th level), the bonus, and penalty to concentration checks, increases by 2. This ability modifies and replaces the favored enemy ability.
archetype-ranger-witch-hunter-ranger-arc.magical defense (ex): At 1st level, the witch hunter is inured to the magics inflicted upon them. They gain a bonus equal to 1/4 their class level (minimum +1) on saves against spells and spell-like abilities. This ability replaces track and the wild empathy ability.
archetype-ranger-witch-hunter-ranger-arc.harry spellcasting (ex): At 3rd level, the witch hunter gains the Step Up feat, usable only when the target is moving 5 feet to cast a spell or use a spell-like ability. The ranger must otherwise follow the other rules of the feat. This ability replaces the Endurance bonus feat gained at 3rd level.
archetype-ranger-witch-hunter-ranger-arc.aurasight (su): At 8th level, the witch hunter can use the spell detect magic at will as a swift action. They can continue to focus on the spell as a swift action each round. This ability replaces swift tracker.
archetype-ranger-witch-hunter-ranger-arc.cloak of blankness (ex): At 12th level, the witch hunter, and the items on their person, are under a constant nondetection spell effect. The caster level of the effect is equal to the witch hunter’s class level. The witch hunter may raise or lower this protection as a free action. This ability replaces camouflage.
archetype-ranger-witch-hunter-ranger-arc.mental bastion (ex): At 17th level, the witch hunter can empty their mind of thought and feeling, rendering them immune to mind-affecting effects. The witch hunter may raise or lower this ability as a free action. This ability replaces hide in plain sight.

archetype-ranger-big-game-hunter-ranger-.weapon and armor proficiencies: A big game hunter adds proficiency with all firearms to their list of proficiencies.
archetype-ranger-big-game-hunter-ranger-.trophy room (ex): Beginning at first level, a big game hunter must keep a room filled with trophies collected from past hunts, such as taxidermized heads, mounted horns, cured pelts, and complete skeletons. The big game hunter gains a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival skill checks against creatures he has not yet killed and added to the trophy room. Once a specimen of a creature is killed by the big game hunter, the big game hunter no longer receives the bonus from this ability unless the creature has more Hit Dice than the previous one added to the collection. Creatures are specified by their name and creature template, not by type. For example, killing a young red dragons does not exclude vampiric red dragons or an adult red dragon from conferring future bonuses until slain. If a big game hunter loses the collection, the big game hunter must rebuild the collection over a number of months equal to twice the big game hunter’s level at the time of losing the collection. While the collection is being rebuilt the big game hunter does not gain any bonus from this ability. It costs 30 gold pieces a month to maintain the trophy room. This cost includes preparing specimens for the room. This ability replaces favored enemy at 1st level.

archetype-ranger-heart-of-the-forest-ran.tree whisperer (ex): A heart of the forest gains a +1 bonus on saving throws against spells and spell-like abilities of plants, and against spells that use plants to hinder movement (such as entangle ). This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-heart-of-the-forest-ran.verdant breath weapon (su): At 4th level, a heart of the forest gains the verdant assault and pollen cloud breath weapons. The saving throw for both is DC10 + 1/2 the heart of the forest’s level + the heart of the forest’s Constitution modifier. A heart of the forest can use their breath weapon a number of times per day equal to 1/2 their heart of the forest level. The heart of the forest gains additional uses of their breath weapon the same way they would receive additional spells, but they use their Constitution modifier rather than their Wisdom modifier to determine the bonus uses. Each time the heart of the forest would receive a bonus spell of any level from a high Constitution score, they receive one additional use of their breath weapon. Verdant Assault: As a standard action, the heart of the forest can exhale a deadly barrage of greenery in a 60-foot line that deals 1d4 points of bludgeoning damage per heart of the forest level. On a successful save, creatures take half damage. Expelling acorns deals bludgeoning damage, splinters deal piercing damage, and leaves deal slashing damage. The heart of the forest can choose which type of greenery to exhale with each use of this ability. Only one type of greenery can be expelled at a time per use of the breath weapon. Pollen Cloud: As a standard action, the heart of the forest can exhale a cloud of sickening pollen in a 30-foot cone that deals 1d2 points of poison damage per heart of the forest level and causes creatures to become blind and nauseated for 3 rounds. On a successful save, creatures take half damage, are not blinded, and are sickened for 3 rounds. This replaces spells.

archetype-ranger-kinslayer-half-giant.favored enemy: At 1st level, the kinslayer must choose humanoid (giant) as his favored enemy. His future favored enemies may be chosen as normal. In addition, when the kinslayer makes trip attempts against creatures of the humanoid (giant) subtype, he doubles his favored enemy bonus for the trip attempt and can make trip attempts regardless of the creature’s size compared to his own.
archetype-ranger-kinslayer-half-giant.hunter’s companion: The kinslayer must choose an animal companion at 4th level from those normally available to a ranger. When the kinslayer and his animal companion are flanking the same enemy of the humanoid (giant) subtype, the bonus they gain for flanking is increased by 2. In addition, the kinslayer and his animal companion are able to communicate telepathically as long as the kinslayer is maintaining psionic focus, with a range of 100 ft + 10 ft. per ranger level. This communication does not make the animal companion any more intelligent, so this typically results in the kinslayer giving commands to the animal companion or simple questions and answers. This ability replaces hunters bond.
archetype-ranger-kinslayer-half-giant.psionics (ps): Starting at 4th level, the kinslayer gains access to expansion as a psi-like ability usable once per day and an additional time per day every four kinslayer levels thereafter (2 at 8th, 3 at 12th, 4 at 16th, 5 at 20th). The kinslayer may choose to use this psi-like ability on his animal companion instead of on himself, treating the psi-like ability as having a range of touch. At 8th level, the kinslayer gains animal affinity as a psi-like ability usable once per day and an additional time per day every four kinslayer levels thereafter (2 at 12th, 3 at 16th, 4 at 20th). At 11th level, the kinslayer gains mental barrier as a psi-like ability usable once per day and an additional time per day every four kinslayer levels thereafter (2 at 15th, 3 at 19th). At 14th level, the kinslayer gains slip the bonds as a psi-like ability usable once per day and an additional time per day 18th level. All of these psi-like abilities gained are treated as having a manifester level equal to the kinslayer’s class level -3 and are applicable for use with the share spells ability of the animal companion. This ability replaces spellcasting.
archetype-ranger-kinslayer-half-giant.shared favor (ex): Once a kinslayer has reached 7th level, his animal companion is treated as having the kinslayer’s favored enemy ability against humanoid (giant) creatures, with the same bonuses against that favored enemy as the kinslayer’s. This ability replaces woodland stride.

archetype-ranger-cloaked-killer.dual identity (ex): The cloaked killer gains the vigilante’s dual identity class feature. This ability replaces the wild empathy class feature.
archetype-ranger-cloaked-killer.cloaked killer (ex): At 4th level the cloaked killer gains the stalker’s hidden strike ability as a vigilante of his class level -3, allowing him to deal an extra 1d8 points of precision damage on melee attacks (or ranged attacks from within 30 ft.) against foes who are unaware of his presence or who consider him an ally. This extra damage increases by 1d8 at 6th level and every 2 levels thereafter. The cloaked killer can also deal hidden strike damage to a target that he is flanking or that is denied its Dexterity bonus to AC, but in these cases, the damage dice are reduced to d4s. The cloaked killer can deal hidden strike damage against targets with concealment (but not total concealment ). This replaces the spells class feature. Cloaked killers do not gain any spells or spellcasting ability, do not have a caster level, and cannot use spell trigger and spell completion magic items.
archetype-ranger-cloaked-killer.city strider (ex): From 7th level on, the cloaked killer gains partial concealment while moving through crowds, his movement is not impeded by crowds, and he gains a bonus equal to 1/2 his ranger level on Intimidate checks to influence crowds. This replaces the woodland stride class feature.

archetype-ranger-umbral-hunter-ranger-ar.weapon and armor proficiencies: The umbral hunter can cast ninja spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, an umbral hunter wearing medium armor, heavy armor, or a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. A multiclass umbral hunter still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.
archetype-ranger-umbral-hunter-ranger-ar.spell casting: The ranger uses the ninja’s spell list in place of their own as well as gaining spells at 1st level instead of 4th, although they must use a spellbook in place of tattoos and cannot ignore spell components. This ability alters the ranger’s spells.

archetype-ranger-spirit-listener-ranger-.spirit bond (ex): At 4th level, instead of forming a bond with his hunting companions or an animal companion, the spirit listener forms a bond with the spirits of nature dwelling in his favored terrain. He chooses one shaman spirit related to his first favored terrain. He adds that spirit’s 1st–4th level spirit magic spells to his ranger spell list, and can cast these spells spontaneously sacrificing a spell slot of equal level. These are the choices of spirits dwelling in each terrain: Cold: Mammoth, Waves Desert: Flame Forest: Nature, Wood Jungle: Nature, Wood Mountain: Stone, Wind Plains: Mammoth, Nature Planes: Heavens, Life Swamp: Bones, Waves Underground: Bones, Stone Urban: Battle, Lore Water: Waves The spirit listener also gains the spirit ability of his terrain spirit. At 9th level, he gains one hex of his choice from the list of hexes available to his terrain spirit. At 16th level, he gains the greater spirit ability of his terrain spirit. The spirit listener doesn’t need to be in his favored terrain in order to use these abilities. His effective shaman level for them is equal to his shaman level -3. This ability replaces hunter ’s bond, evasion, and improved evasion.
archetype-ranger-spirit-listener-ranger-.spirit–wise (sp): At 12th level, as long as he is within one of his favored terrains, the spirit listener can temporarily bond with a spirit related to that terrain. He gains access to one hex from the list of that terrain’s spirit for 24 hours, but the bond ends if he leaves the spirit’s terrain. If he is in his fixed spirit’s terrain, he can choose a second, temporary hex granted by that terrain’s spirit. The spirit listener can’t forge a temporary bond with more than one spirit at a time, and can’t bond with a new spirit before 24 hours are passed, even if the first bond ends before this time. The spirit listener doesn’t gain access to the spirit magic spells or abilities granted by his wandering terrain spirit. At 17th level, the spirit listener needs no more to stay in one of his favored terrains in order to forge or maintain the bond with that terrain’s spirit. This ability replaces camouflage and hide in plain sight.

archetype-ranger-steelduster-ranger-arch.skills: A steelduster gains Fly and Knowledge (engineering) as class skills and loses Handle Animal and Spellcraft. This alters the ranger’s class skills.
archetype-ranger-steelduster-ranger-arch.bonded mech (ex): The steeduster gains a bonded mech*, treating his class level as his pilot level. This ability replaces wild empathy, spellcasting, and the favored enemy gained at 1st level.
archetype-ranger-steelduster-ranger-arch.mech expertise (ex): Starting at 2nd level, whenever the steeduster would gain a combat style feat, he may select feats from the following list in addition to feats he could normally select: Craft Mech*, Craft Technological Arms and Armor*, Extra Mech Enhancement*, Field Mechanic*, Remote Legion*, Remote Piloting*, Salvage Rigger*, Superior Salvage, Technologist*, and Vehicle Expert*. He does not need to meet the prerequisites for these feats to select them.
archetype-ranger-steelduster-ranger-arch.mechanical scout (ex): At 4th level, if the steelduster selects an animal companion for his hunter’s bond class feature, the steelduster may have his animal companion pilot the steelduster’s mech as if the animal companion were proficient with all armor. The mech can always carry the steelduster’s animal companion in addition to its pilot as long as the companion’s size is smaller than the mech’s. This alters hunter’s bond. This does not make the steelduster incompatible with other archetypes that modify hunter’s bond.

archetype-ranger-totemic-ranger-ranger-a.combat style feat (ex): At 2nd level, a totemic ranger must choose the natural weapon combat style.
archetype-ranger-totemic-ranger-ranger-a.totemic aspect (su): At 3rd level, a totemic ranger selects one shifter aspect. He gains a shifter’s aspect power, but can only shift into his chosen totemic animal’s minor form. He never gains other aspects with level increase. This replaces the first favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-totemic-ranger-ranger-a.wild shape (su): At 8th level, a totemic ranger gains the shifter’s wild shape ability, but can only use it to assume the major form of his totemic animal. This replaces the second favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-totemic-ranger-ranger-a.totemic fury (ex): At 13th level, a totemic ranger gains the shifter’s fury shifter ability. This replaces the third favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-totemic-ranger-ranger-a.hybrid aspect (su): At 18th level, a totemic ranger can use his totemic aspect power to manifest all his totemic animal’s natural weapons or his totemic animal’s movement while maintaining his humanoid form; he could, for example, manifest a falcon’s wings and gain the falcon’s fly speed, or a tiger’s bite and claws to attack. The totemic ranger’s natural attacks deal damage as per his size when in hybrid aspect. This replaces the fourth favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-totemic-ranger-ranger-a.true shifter (su): At 20th level, a totemic ranger can always move at full speed while using Survival to follow tracks without penalty. In addition, he can now use wild shape to assume his totemic animal’s form at will. This replaces master hunter.

archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.weapon and armor proficiency: A bombardier is proficient with all simple weapons and bombs. They are also proficient with light armor, but not with shields.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.bombs (su): A bombardier gains the bombs class feature, as an alchemist of the same level. This replaces favored enemy and master hunter.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.experimental weaponeer (ex): A bombardier gains a competence bonus equal to one-half his ranger level (minimum +1) on Craft (alchemy) checks made to create or identify alchemical weapons, including crafting gunpowder and cartridges for firearms. This bonus also applies on Craft (siege weapons) checks and on Knowledge (engineering) checks made to aim a siege weapon. This replaces track and wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.bomber combat style: At 2nd level, a bombardier adopts a combat style centered around thrown weapons, gaining one of the following as a bonus feat: Distance Thrower, Extra Bombs, Precise Shot, Quick Draw, Point-Blank Shot, Throw Anything, Two-Weapon Fighting. At 6th level, he adds Close-Quarters Thrower, Concentrated Splash, Deafening Blast, Deceptive Exchange, Distracting Explosion, False Opening, and Grenade Expert to the list. At 10th level, he adds Implant Bomb, Pinpoint Targeting, Remote Bomb, and Shot on the Run to the list. This alters combat style feats.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.discovery: At 3rd level and every 5 levels thereafter, a bombardier gains an alchemical discovery, as the alchemist class feature, treating his alchemist level as two levels lower than his ranger level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites. He may gain additional discoveries with the Extra Discovery feat. A bombardier may only select discoveries that modify or affect bombs or extracts. This replaces favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.grenadier (ex): At 3rd level, a bombardier becomes expert in the use of alchemical weapons and grenades. If such a weapon allows a saving throw to negate or reduce its effect, the saving throw’s DC increases by 1 (to a maximum DC of 22). The DC increases by an additional 1 at 7th level and every 4 levels thereafter (to a maximum of 5 higher at 19th level). This does not affect the save DC of bombs. This replaces Endurance.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.extracts: At 4th level, a bombardier gains the ability to prepare a small number of alchemical extracts, which are drawn from the alchemist formula list. A bombardier must choose and prepare his extracts in advance. To prepare or use an extract, a bombardier must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the extract’s level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a bombardier’s extract is 10 + the spell level + the ranger’s Wisdom modifier. Like an alchemist, a bombardier can use only a certain number of extracts of each level per day. His base daily extract allotment is the same as a ranger’s spell allotment, and he receives bonus extracts per day if he has a high Intelligence score. When the ranger spell allotment table indicates that a ranger would get 0 spells per day of a given spell level, a bombardier gains only the bonus extracts he would be entitled to based on his Intelligence score for that level. A bombardier is limited to learning the following extracts, but also may learn additional rare or unique extracts that affect bombs. 1st -bomber’s eye, damp powder, endure elements, fabricate bullets, longshot, targeted bomb admixture, weaken powder 2nd -bullet shield, destabilize powder, empower holy water, full pouch, magic siege engine, protection from arrows, reloading hands, resist energy, shadow bomb admixture, stabilize powder, telekinetic assembly, thunder fire 3rd -bouncing bomb admixture, draconic reservoir, endure elements (communal), lightning lash bomb admixture, named bullet, pellet blast, protection from arrows (communal), protection from energy, resist energy (communal) 4th -arcane cannon, energy siege shot, fire shield, healing warmth, languid bomb admixture, magic siege engine (greater), named bullet (greater), viper bomb admixture, vitriolic mist A bombardier must spend 1 hour per day in quiet study and preparation to regain his daily allotment of extracts. A bombardier learns two 1st-level extracts at 4th level and learns one additional extract each time he gains a level thereafter. He also may learn additional extracts as an alchemist can by studying the formula book of another alchemist or investigator, or the spellbook of a wizard if the spell appears on the wizard class list. Through 3rd level, a bombardier has no caster level. At 4th level and higher, his caster level is equal to his ranger level – 3. This replaces spells.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.heavy weaponer (ex): At 4th level, a bombardier expands her knowledge of explosives, gunpowder, and heavy weaponry of all kinds. She may select one of the following feats as a bonus feat: Amateur Gunslinger, Demolitions Expert, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (firearms), Exotic Weapon Proficiency (siege weapons), Gunsmithing, Master Siege Engineer, Siege Commander, Siege Engineer, Siege Gunner. If the campaign is using advanced technological weapons, a bombardier also may choose Exotic Weapon Proficiency (heavy weaponry) as a bonus feat. A bombardier gains one additional bonus feat every 4 levels after 4th. This replaces hunter’s bond, swift tracker, camouflage, and hide in plain sight.
archetype-ranger-bombardier-ranger-arche.master grenadier (ex): At 7th level, a bombardier learns to use alchemical weapons and grenades with great precision, gaining one of the following benefits each round as a free action. Accurate Toss: When an attack with a thrown splash weapon misses, you can alter the location of the miss by 5 feet in any direction. Deadman Switch: You can prepare a grenade, alchemical weapon, or bomb to go off if you are attacked, allowing you to trigger the grenade or weapon as an immediate action. If you are knocked unconscious, killed, or otherwise rendered helpless (or if you are disarmed or otherwise forced to drop the item), it goes off immediately. The area of the grenade or splash weapon’s blast must be centered on the edge of your space. If the weapon’s activation was triggered as an immediate action in response to the action of a creature adjacent to you, you can make a melee touch attack to target that creature with the weapon. This does not provoke attacks of opportunity. The creature that triggers the weapon’s detonation (whether from an immediate action or from incapacitating you) takes a -2 penalty on any saving throw allowed by the weapon. Double Toss: If you have a splash weapon or grenade in each hand, you can throw both as part of a single standard action. Both attacks take a -4 penalty on their attack rolls. Immediate Blast: A grenade you throw explodes immediately on impact, rather than with a delay. Potent Blast: If the weapon or grenade deals hit point damage, you can increase the damage dealt by an amount equal to your Intelligence modifier. Safe Blast: You can exclude one square in the weapon or grenade’s normal blast radius from its area of effect. A creature in that square is unaffected by the weapon or grenade. Swift Pull: You can draw an alchemical weapon or grenade as a free action, allowing you to make one iterative attack when using the full-attack action. Team Toss: You can throw an alchemical weapon or grenade to an ally within 5 feet times your Intelligence modifier. If the attack hits, your ally catches the weapon before it detonates and can either throw it again as an immediate action using its own attack roll or can simply retain the weapon. At 11th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you can use one more of these benefits each round. You may select the same benefit multiple times per round and can apply the same benefit more than once to the same attack. Damage from potent blast does not stack. This replaces woodland stride, quarry, and improved quarry.

archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.favored enemy (ex): At 1st level, a robot fighter must select constructs as his favored enemy. His favored enemy bonus begins at +2 and increases by 2 at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter; however, he does not gain other favored enemies. His damage bonus from this ability is increased by 50% against constructs with the robot subtype. This alters favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.trap mechanic (ex): A robot fighter adds 1/2 his ranger level as a bonus on Perception and Disable Device checks made to find or disable mechanical traps. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.way of the gun: At 2nd level or any level when a robot fighter would be eligible for a combat style feat, he may instead choose to gain one of the following feats: Amateur Gunslinger, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (firearms only), Gunsmithing, Rapid Reload (firearms only). Like combat style feats, these feats may be used effectively only while wearing light, medium, or no armor. This alters combat style.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.technologist: At 3rd level, a robot fighter gains Technologist as a bonus feat. This replaces Endurance.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.favored terrain (ex): A robot fighter must select urban and underground (in any order) as his first two favored terrains.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.hunter’s bond: A robot fighter must select a companion bond and cannot select an animal companion.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.spells: A robot fighter adds the following spells to his ranger spell list: 1st – body capacitance, detect metal, shock shield, shocking grasp, technomancy 2nd – defensive shock, disable construct, protection from technology 3rd – discharge, heart of the metal, malfunction, rusting grasp 4th – magic circle against technology, rapid repair, rebuke technology, soothe construct, sabotage construct, warp metal. Hunter-Killer (Ex) At 5th level, when a robot fighter confirms a critical hit against a construct, he ignores an amount of hardness equal to his ranger level. If the construct has the robot subtype, he adds one-half his favored enemy bonus to the DC of the robot’s saving throw to avoid being stunned by a confirmed critical hit. This replaces the robot fighter’s second favored enemy. Ruin Prowler (Ex) At 7th level, a robot fighter can move through any sort of rubble or similar broken and rocky terrain, including collapsed buildings, twisted metal and stone, barbed wire, and similar impediments at his normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Rubble, broken metal and stone, and similar areas that are enchanted or magically manipulated affect him normally. This replaces woodland stride. Electromagnetic Pulse (Su) At 10th level, when a robot fighter strikes a creature or an object with a melee or ranged attack, as a swift action he can sacrifice a prepared spell of 3rd level or higher in order to spontaneously cast discharge on that target. If he deals electricity damage to a construct, he can use this ability by sacrificing a spell of 2nd level or higher instead. If the robot fighter is at least 13th level, he can sacrifice a prepared 4th -level spell to cast rebuke technology on the target instead, or a 3rd-level spell if he deals electricity damage to the target construct or object. In addition, as a full-round action, he can sacrifice a prepared spell of any level to release a burst of electromagnetic energy that disrupts the functioning of constructs and technological objects in a burst with a radius of 5 feet times the level of the spell, centered on himself. Living creatures in this area take 1d4 points of nonlethal electricity damage are dazzled for 1 round ( Fort negates). Constructs in the area are affected as discharge and also take 1d6 points of electricity damage per level of the spell sacrificed; this damage is halved on a successful save. Constructs immune to electricity damage can still be affected by this discharge even if they take no damage from the pulse. This replaces the robot fighter’s third favored enemy. Fool Sensors (Ex) At 12th level, a robot fighter can use the Stealth skill to hide from a construct even if he does not have cover or concealment. In addition, a construct cannot automatically detect a robot fighter’s presence or location with exceptional senses such as blindsense, blindsight, scent, or tremorsense; the construct must make Perception checks as normal to notice the robot fighter. If the construct has the robot subtype, it cannot detect the robot fighter with darkvision. This replaces camouflage. Penetrate Defenses (Ex) At 15th level, a robot fighter can confirm critical hits against a robot with a force field, and when a critical hit is confirmed it deals half damage to the target and half damage to the force field; if this reduces the force field to 0 hit points, any leftover damage is applied to the target. When the robot fighter confirms a critical hit against a robot with a force field, the force field’s fast healing is suppressed for a 1d4 rounds. When a robot fighter confirms a critical hit against a construct without a force field, his blow cracks the target’s defensive structure, reducing its hardness or DR by 5 for 1d4 rounds. This replaces the robot fighter’s fourth favored enemy. Antitech Field (Sp) At 17th level, a robot fighter can use antitech field once per day as a spell-like ability, using his ranger caster level. This replaces hide in plain sight. Kill Switch (Su) At 20th level, once per day when a robot fighter strikes a construct with a melee or ranged attack, he can activate a destructive chain reaction that destroys the target. The robot fighter may trigger this self-destruct effect instantly or may trigger it as a free action at any time within one week. Once triggered, the target construct must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC 20 + the robot fighter’s Wisdom modifier) or be instantly reduced to 0 hit points. A successful save negates the effect. A robot fighter may not implant a new kill switch until he has activated the previous one. When fighting constructs with the robot subtype, a robot fighter may use this ability whenever he successfully confirms a critical hit, up to a maximum number of times per day equal to his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). A robot that successfully saves against his kill switch is immune to this effect for 24 hours. This replaces the robot fighter’s fifth favored enemy. Special: At the GM’s options, any of a robot fighter’s class features that apply specifically to constructs with the robot subtype may also apply to androids and/or constructs with the clockwork subtype.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.hunter-killer (ex): At 5th level, when a robot fighter confirms a critical hit against a construct, he ignores an amount of hardness equal to his ranger level. If the construct has the robot subtype, he adds one-half his favored enemy bonus to the DC of the robot’s saving throw to avoid being stunned by a confirmed critical hit. This replaces the robot fighter’s second favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.ruin prowler (ex): At 7th level, a robot fighter can move through any sort of rubble or similar broken and rocky terrain, including collapsed buildings, twisted metal and stone, barbed wire, and similar impediments at his normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Rubble, broken metal and stone, and similar areas that are enchanted or magically manipulated affect him normally. This replaces woodland stride.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.electromagnetic pulse (su): At 10th level, when a robot fighter strikes a creature or an object with a melee or ranged attack, as a swift action he can sacrifice a prepared spell of 3rd level or higher in order to spontaneously cast discharge on that target. If he deals electricity damage to a construct, he can use this ability by sacrificing a spell of 2nd level or higher instead. If the robot fighter is at least 13th level, he can sacrifice a prepared 4th -level spell to cast rebuke technology on the target instead, or a 3rd-level spell if he deals electricity damage to the target construct or object. In addition, as a full-round action, he can sacrifice a prepared spell of any level to release a burst of electromagnetic energy that disrupts the functioning of constructs and technological objects in a burst with a radius of 5 feet times the level of the spell, centered on himself. Living creatures in this area take 1d4 points of nonlethal electricity damage are dazzled for 1 round ( Fort negates). Constructs in the area are affected as discharge and also take 1d6 points of electricity damage per level of the spell sacrificed; this damage is halved on a successful save. Constructs immune to electricity damage can still be affected by this discharge even if they take no damage from the pulse. This replaces the robot fighter’s third favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.fool sensors (ex): At 12th level, a robot fighter can use the Stealth skill to hide from a construct even if he does not have cover or concealment. In addition, a construct cannot automatically detect a robot fighter’s presence or location with exceptional senses such as blindsense, blindsight, scent, or tremorsense; the construct must make Perception checks as normal to notice the robot fighter. If the construct has the robot subtype, it cannot detect the robot fighter with darkvision. This replaces camouflage.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.penetrate defenses (ex): At 15th level, a robot fighter can confirm critical hits against a robot with a force field, and when a critical hit is confirmed it deals half damage to the target and half damage to the force field; if this reduces the force field to 0 hit points, any leftover damage is applied to the target. When the robot fighter confirms a critical hit against a robot with a force field, the force field’s fast healing is suppressed for a 1d4 rounds. When a robot fighter confirms a critical hit against a construct without a force field, his blow cracks the target’s defensive structure, reducing its hardness or DR by 5 for 1d4 rounds. This replaces the robot fighter’s fourth favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.antitech field (sp): At 17th level, a robot fighter can use antitech field once per day as a spell-like ability, using his ranger caster level. This replaces hide in plain sight.
archetype-ranger-robot-fighter-ranger-ar.kill switch (su): At 20th level, once per day when a robot fighter strikes a construct with a melee or ranged attack, he can activate a destructive chain reaction that destroys the target. The robot fighter may trigger this self-destruct effect instantly or may trigger it as a free action at any time within one week. Once triggered, the target construct must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC 20 + the robot fighter’s Wisdom modifier) or be instantly reduced to 0 hit points. A successful save negates the effect. A robot fighter may not implant a new kill switch until he has activated the previous one. When fighting constructs with the robot subtype, a robot fighter may use this ability whenever he successfully confirms a critical hit, up to a maximum number of times per day equal to his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). A robot that successfully saves against his kill switch is immune to this effect for 24 hours. This replaces the robot fighter’s fifth favored enemy. Special: At the GM’s options, any of a robot fighter’s class features that apply specifically to constructs with the robot subtype may also apply to androids and/or constructs with the clockwork subtype.

archetype-ranger-musher.mush team (ex): At 1st level, a musher earns the loyalty and service of a dog or wolf. This ability functions like the druid animal companion ability, which is part of the nature bond class feature, but the musher must take the dog or wolf animal companion. The musher uses his ranger level as his effective druid level. The musher may have more than one animal companion, but he must divide up his effective ranger level between his companions to determine the abilities of each companion. For instance, a 6th-level musher can have one 6th-level companion, one 4th-level and one 2nd-level companion, or two 3rd-level companions. Each time a musher’s ranger level increases, he must decide how to allocate the increase among his animal companions (including the option of adding a new 1st-level companion). When a ranger level is allocated to a particular companion, it cannot be redistributed while that companion is in the musher’s service (he must release the companion or wait until the companion dies to allocate its levels to another companion, which he can do the next time he prepares spells). The share spells animal companion ability applies only to one animal companion of his choice at a time — the musher cannot use it to cast a one-target spell and have it affect all of his animal companions. The musher’s ranger levels stack with any other class feature granting an animal companion. When driving a sled or sleigh using one or more animal companions across snowy or icy terrain, the DCs of all driving checks are reduced by 2, the acceleration increases by 5 feet, and the vehicle’s maximum speed increases by 5 feet for each animal companion pulling the vehicle. This ability replaces favored enemy, and alters hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-musher.canine empathy (ex): A musher’s wild empathy affects only canines. This ability otherwise functions as and replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-musher.mush tactics (ex): At 2nd level, a musher must select the following Intertwined combat style. A character can choose from the following list whenever he gains a combat style feat: Coordinated Defense, Coordinated Maneuvers, Duck and Cover, Lookout, Paired Opportunists, Precise Strike, and Swap Places. At 6th level, he adds Outflank to the list. At 10th level, he adds Coordinated Charge and Seize the Moment to the list. In addition, he can grant all animal companions within 30 feet who can see and hear him one teamwork feat he possesses from his Intertwined combat style as a bonus feat as a standard action. Animal companions retain the use of this bonus feat for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 his ranger level. The musher can use this ability once per day at 2nd level, plus one additional time per day at 8th level and every six levels thereafter to a maximum of four times per day at 20th level. The animal companion does not need to meet the prerequisites of this bonus feat. This alters the ranger’s combat style feat class feature.
archetype-ranger-musher.improved empathic link (su): At 7th level, a musher gains an empathic link with all of his animal companions. This ability functions as the beast master’s improved empathic link ability (Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Ultimate Combat). This ability replaces woodland stride.
archetype-ranger-musher.team intellect (su): At 11th level, the musher’s animal companions gain an effective Intelligence score of 3 when within 30 feet of the musher. The companions can speak one language known by the musher while benefiting from this effective Intelligence. This ability replaces quarry.
archetype-ranger-musher.team coordination (ex): At 19th level, when a musher and one or more of his animal companions threaten the same opponent, they are treated as if they are flanking the opponent regardless of their actual positioning. This ability replaces improved quarry.
archetype-ranger-musher.musher unison (ex): At 20th level, the musher and his animal companions cannot be surprised or flanked. This ability replaces master hunter.

archetype-ranger-guardian-of-the-tropics.weapon and armor proficiency: A guardian of the tropics is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, but is not proficient with any form of armor or shields. This ability modifies the weapon and armor proficiency class feature. Tropical Defense: A guardian of the tropics adds his Wisdom modifier to AC when he wears no armor and does not use a shield. He loses this bonus to AC while flat-footed.
archetype-ranger-guardian-of-the-tropics.tropical offence (su): At 1st level, the guardian of the tropics’ intense bond with his tropical home fills his body, granting him additional combat abilities while fighting in friendly terrain. As long as the guardian of the tropics is in a warm or coastal environment, he gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls. This bonus is doubled against creatures not native to or born in those areas. At 5th level, and every 5 levels thereafter, this bonus increases by a further +1. This ability replaces the favored enemy class feature.
archetype-ranger-guardian-of-the-tropics.spells of the tropics (su): At 2nd level, the guardian of the tropics begins to gain a greater mastery of spells. At 2nd level, the guardian of the tropics gains the ability to cast flare at will, with a caster level equal to his ranger level and saving throw DC equal 10 + 1/2 his ranger level + his Wisdom modifier. At 4th level, the guardian of the tropics gains the ability to cast heat metal as a 1st-level ranger spell. At 8th level, the guardian of the tropics can cast daylight as a 2nd?level ranger spell. At 12th level, the guardian of the tropics can cast fire shield as a 3rd-level ranger spell. At 16th level, the guardian of the tropics can cast tree stride as a 4th-level ranger spell. Tropical Guardian: At 3rd level, the guardian of the tropics gains additional strength while within his tropical home. As long he remains in a warm or coastal environment, the guardian of the tropics gains DR 1/—, as well as a +2 bonus on initiative checks and on Perception, Knowledge (nature), Sense Motive, and Survival checks. At 8th level, and every 5 levels thereafter, the bonus to initiative checks and skill checks increases by a further +2, and the DR is increased by a further +1. This ability replaces the favored terrain class feature. Familiar: At 4th level, a guardian of the tropics gains a familiar in much the same way a wizard does, though he must choose an animal that is native to a warm or coastal environment. His effective wizard level is equal to his ranger level for the purposes of determining what kind of abilities his familiar gains. This ability replaces the hunter’s bond class feature.
archetype-ranger-guardian-of-the-tropics.call the sun (sp): At 9th level, a guardian of the tropics can call upon his deep connection to the tropics in order to cause a small area to be filled with warm tropical sunlight. By spending 3 full rounds chanting, the guardian of the tropics can create warm natural sunlight in the 100-foot-radius spread surrounding him. The sunlight remains for 10 minutes per level. This ability replaces the evasion class feature.
archetype-ranger-guardian-of-the-tropics.call the rain (sp): At 16th level, a guardian of the tropics can chant to summon a torrential downpour of rain. As long he remains outside within a warm or coastal environment, a guardian of the tropics can chant for 1 full round in order to cause the 100-foot-radius spread around him to fill with torrential rain, obscuring vision beyond 10 feet, and granting concealment to characters within 10 feet. The rain also reduces movement speed by half, though characters with woodland stride are immune to this effect. This ability replaces the improved evasion class feature.
archetype-ranger-guardian-of-the-tropics.monsoon warrior (su): A guardian of the tropics is the ultimate champion of his homeland and is an engine of destruction in defense of his tropical home. At 20th level, the guardian of the tropics adds his Wisdom modifier to attack and damage rolls made while in warm or coastal environments. Additionally, while in a warm or coastal environment, whenever the guardian of the tropics successfully confirms a critical hit against a creature which is not native to a warm or coastal environment, that creature must succeed on a Fortitude save or die. This ability replaces the master hunter class feature.

archetype-ranger-blood-hunter-ranger-arc.favored target (ex): At 2nd level, as a move action, a blood hunter can declare a creature type from the ranger favored enemies table as the target of his hunt. The blood hunter then gains a +1 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks against creatures of his selected type and a +1 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against these creatures. A blood hunter can maintain these bonuses against only one creature type at a time; these bonuses remain in effect until either the blood hunter declares a new favored target or 1 hour passes, whichever comes first. At 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th levels, the bonuses on weapon attack rolls, damage rolls, and skill checks against this favored target increase by 1. At 7th level, a blood hunter can declare a favored target as a move or swift action. Favored target is modified by any feat, spell, or effect that specifically works with the favored enemy ranger class feature. Additionally, the favored target ability always grants or uses a minimum of the blood hunter’s full favored target bonus for the purposes of effects that use the value of the ranger’s favored enemy bonus. For example, a blood hunter grants his full favored target bonus to his companion when using the hunter’s bond class feature. This replaces favored enemy, the combat style feat gained at 2nd level, and woodland stride.
archetype-ranger-blood-hunter-ranger-arc.hunting ground (ex): A blood hunter selects only one type of terrain as his favored terrain. The bonuses he gains while in this terrain increase by 2 at 8th level and every 5 levels thereafter. Starting at 4th level, a blood hunter can declare a new terrain as his favored terrain. This requires studying the terrain in a process that requires 1> hour of time within the terrain. Once the new terrain is declared as his favored terrain, it remains his favored terrain until the blood hunter declares a new favored terrain. At 7th level, a blood hunter gains Blessed Hunter as a bonus feat. The territory he chooses with the Blessed Hunter feat must always be a location that matches his favored terrain. When the blood hunter chooses a new favored terrain, he can also choose a new territory with the Blessed Hunter feat. At 10th level, he gains Blessed Hunter’s Stride as a bonus feat. At 13th level, he gains Blessed Hunter’s Focus as a bonus feat, except he treats his ranger level as his hunter level for the purposes of that feat. This alters favored terrain and replaces spells.
archetype-ranger-blood-hunter-ranger-arc.rapid quarry (ex): At nth level, a blood hunter can denote a target as his quarry as part of declaring his favored target. If he dismisses the effects of his quarry as a free action, he can select a new quarry after 1 hour. If his quarry dies, he can select a new quarry after 10 minutes have passed. At 19th level, if his quarry is killed or dismissed, he can select a new one after 1 minute has passed. This alters quarry and improved quarry.

archetype-ranger-lycanthrope-hunter.shapechanger’s bane (ex): At 1st level, a lycanthrope hunter gains the following benefits against creatures with the animal type as well as creatures with the shapechanger subtype. The lycanthrope hunter gains a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks when dealing with these creatures, and a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against them. Additionally, a lycanthrope hunter can attempt Knowledge skill checks untrained when attempting to identify these creatures. At 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level, the lycanthrope hunter’s bonuses against animals and shapechangers increase by 2 (maximum bonus of +10 at 20th level). This ability replaces favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-lycanthrope-hunter.anathema (su): At 5th level, a lycanthrope hunter can spend a swift action to temporarily alter the makeup of the weapons he wields. While this ability is active, all of the lycanthrope hunter’s weapons (including natural weapons ) function as if they were made of a single special material of his choosing (such as alchemical silver ). The weapons gain no special benefits associated with being made from that material except for the ability to overcome particular damage reductions. The lycanthrope hunter can use this ability for a number of minutes per day equal to his ranger level. This duration does not need to be consecutive, but must be spent in 1-minute increments. Melee weapons that leave the lycanthrope hunter’s possession are no longer affected while this ability is active, although ranged weapons that are shot or thrown by the lycanthrope hunter are still affected. The lycanthrope hunter can end this effect as a free action. At 10th level, the lycanthrope hunter can select a second special material that his weapons mimic, and his weapons count as magic for the purposes of overcoming damage reduction while this ability is active. At 15th level, the lycanthrope hunter gains a +4 bonus to confirm critical hits against animals and shapechangers. At 20th level, the lycanthrope hunter automatically confirms critical threats against animals and shapechangers.
archetype-ranger-lycanthrope-hunter.forced form (su): At 8th level, upon confirming a critical hit against an opponent, a lycanthrope hunter can force that opponent to attempt a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + the lycanthrope hunter’s level + the lycanthrope hunter’s Charisma modifier). If the creature fails and it has the shapechanger subtype or is under the effect of any polymorph effect, it immediately reverts to its natural form. If it is already in its natural and unaltered form, this ability has no effect. This ability replaces swift tracker.

archetype-ranger-deeplands-sailor.skilled pilot (ex): A Deeplands sailor adds half his level (minimum 1) to Profession (sailor) and Survival checks to navigate or avoid natural hazards in subterranean waterways. This ability replaces track.
archetype-ranger-deeplands-sailor.keen ear (ex): At 3rd level, a Deeplands sailor learns how to use sound to compensate for poor visibility when facing threats above and below the water. He gains the uncanny dodge rogue ability when underground and either swimming or aboard a boat. At 8th level, he gains improved uncanny dodge under these conditions, treating his Deeplands sailor level as his effective rogue level for the purpose of denying an enemy’s sneak attacks. At 13th level, he gains blindsense with a range of 30 feet against creatures touching water. At 18th level, his blindsense range increases to 60 feet or equal to the range of his darkvision, whichever is greater. If the Deeplands sailor becomes deafened, he loses all benefits of this ability until his hearing is restored. This replaces favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-deeplands-sailor.quick swim (ex): At 7th level, a Deeplands sailor can swim at his full speed as a move action without penalty. This ability replaces woodland stride.
archetype-ranger-deeplands-sailor.subsonic warning (ex): At 8th level as a swift action, a Deeplands sailor can provide the benefits of his keen ear ability to the subjects of his hunter’s bond. This effect lasts for a number of rounds per day equal to the Deeplands sailor’s Wisdom modifier. These rounds need not be consecutive. A deafened creature can’t benefit from a Deeplands sailor’s subsonic warning. This ability replaces swift tracker.
archetype-ranger-deeplands-sailor.hidden depths (ex): At 12th level, a Deeplands sailor can use the Stealth skill to hide while underground or underwater, even if he doesn’t have cover or concealment. At 17th level, he can use the Stealth skill even while being observed when underground or underwater. This ability replaces camouflage and hide in plain sight.

archetype-ranger-seabeast-hunter-gnorri.keen scent (ex): A seabeast hunter develops a unique form of scent that allows him to track creatures underwater. While the seabeast hunter has no special talent for tracking a creature on land, he can track a creature in water by scent, and adds half his level (minimum 1) to Survival skill checks made to follow a creature in this way. For the purposes of tracking via scent in this way, the base Survival check is DC 20. This ability replaces track.
archetype-ranger-seabeast-hunter-gnorri.aquatic combatant (ex): Although a seabeast hunter gains the favored terrain ability at 3rd level as normal, he generally has little use for favored terrains other than water. Due to his focus, he can choose water again when he gains the ability to choose another favored terrain.
