The second time he selects water as his favored terrain, his favored terrain bonus increases to +4 and he no longer takes penalties to attack rolls or damage with any slashing melee weapon when underwater. The third time he selects water as his favored terrain, his favored terrain bonus increases to +6 and he gains freedom of movement when underwater. If he chooses favored terrain a fourth time, his favored terrain bonus in water increases to +8, his swim speed increases by 10 feet (or he gains a swim speed of 10 feet if he lacks one), and he gains blindsense 30 feet while underwater. This ability alters favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-seabeast-hunter-gnorri.sea hunter’s bond (ex): If a seabeast hunter chooses an animal companion, he must choose an animal that has the aquatic subtype or that has a swim speed. This ability alters hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-seabeast-hunter-gnorri.beast hunter (ex): At 7th level, a seabeast hunter’s skill at hunting and evading sea monsters improves. He gains a +2 dodge bonus to AC against creatures of a size category larger than himself (the creature must be at least Huge for most gnorri ). This ability replaces woodland stride.
archetype-ranger-seabeast-hunter-gnorri.claim trophy (su): At 8th level, as a full-round action, a seabeast hunter can claim a trophy from a sea monster. The trophy must be harvested from an aquatic creature or a creature that can swim; this creature must be of a size category at least one larger than the seabeast hunter (the creature must be at least Huge for most gnorri ), and the seabeast hunter must have taken active part in the defeat of the sea monster. Once a trophy is claimed, the seabeast hunter gains a +2 morale bonus on his skill checks and saving throws against creatures of the same species as the trophy he claimed, as long as he wears the trophy in a visible location on his body. A seabeast hunter can claim a new trophy whenever he wishes, but can maintain only a number of trophies equal to his Wisdom bonus (minimum 1) and can only gain the benefit of one at a time. Inactive trophies need not be displayed. Maintained trophies do not rot, but the seabeast hunter must spend 1 minute of effort repairing and preserving them each week to avoid them rotting and losing their power. No further materials are required for this preservation. Reactivating a maintained trophy requires removing any previously active trophy. The seabeast hunter can remove a displayed trophy and exchange it with a maintained trophy carried in an accessible place (such as a belt or pouch) as a standard action. If the maintained trophy is in a bag or otherwise more difficult to access, this is a full-round action. This ability replaces swift tracker.

archetype-ranger-battle-master-ranger-ar.battle focus (ex): As a swift action, you can designate any one creature that you can see as your focus in battle. You receive a +1 bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls against this target. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, this bonus increases by 1, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. You can change your battle focus to a different creature you can see as a swift action, or end your battle focus as a free action. You can use this ability for a number of rounds per day equal to 1/2 your ranger level (minimum 1) + your Wisdom modifier. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. This feature replaces 1st favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-battle-master-ranger-ar.second combat style (ex): At 5th level, you gain a second combat style. You must choose this style from among those available to rangers, and it cannot be the same as the combat style you selected at 2nd level. You treat your ranger level –4 as your effective ranger level for the purposes of which feats you are able to select from your second combat style. You select one feat from this combat style at 5th level, and one additional feat from it when you reach 10th, 15th, and 20th level. As with your first combat style, you do not need to meet the prerequisites for the feats selected. This feature replaces 2nd, 3rd, 4th, & 5th favored enemies and spells.

archetype-ranger-commando-ranger-archety.commando conditioning (ex): You have learned how to steel yourself against a specific type of hostile environment. At 1st level, choose one conditioning style from those listed below. You gain a +2 bonus to any saving throws against the types of effects listed in the conditioning style you select. At 5th level and every five levels thereafter, select an additional conditioning style. In addition, at each such interval, the saving throw bonus for any one conditioning style (including the one just selected, if so desired) increases by +1. If a specific condition or effect falls into more than one category, your conditioning bonuses do not stack; you simply use whichever bonus is higher. Attention Division: Your conditioning bonus applies against effects that cause the confused, dazed, dazzled, staggered, or stunned condition. Caustic Training: Your conditioning bonus applies against effects that would cause the entangled condition and effects that deal acid damage. Combat Chance: Your conditioning bonus applies effects that trigger on a critical hit and effects that would force you to roll multiple times and take the worst result. Counter-Interrogation: Your conditioning bonus applies against pain effects and effects of the enchantment ( charm ) subschool. Extreme Cold: Your conditioning bonus applies against cold dangers and effects that deal cold damage. Extreme Heat: Your conditioning bonus applies against heat dangers and effects that deal fire damage. Gamma Protocols: Your conditioning bonus applies against radiation effects and transmutation spells. Hardened Demeanor: Your conditioning bonus applies against fear effects and effects of the enchantment ( compulsion ) subschool. Storm Training: Your conditioning bonus applies against effects that deal electricity or sonic damage. Temple Body: Your conditioning bonus applies against diseases (other than addiction) and poisons (other than radiation). This feature replaces favored enemy.

archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.weapon and armor proficiency: You are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, with light armor, and with shields (except tower shields). You can cast spells gained from this archetype while wearing light armor and using a shield without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, you incur a chance of arcane spell failure while wearing medium or heavy armor if the spell in question has a somatic component. If you are multiclassed, you still incur the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes. This feature alters weapon and armor proficiency.
archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.cantrips: At 1st level, you learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, from the magus spell list as noted on Table 1–1: Mystic Blade Spells Known. These spells are cast like any other spell (see below), but they do not consume any slots and may be used again. This feature replaces wild empathy. archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.esoteric lore: You do not gain Knowledge (nature) as a class skill, but you do gain Knowledge (arcana) as a class skill. This feature alters class skills.
archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.eschew materials: You gain Eschew Materials as a bonus feat at 3rd level. This feature replaces endurance.
archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.arcane spells: Beginning at 4th level, you gain the ability to cast a small number of arcane spells, which are drawn from the magus spell list, except that only magus spells up to 4th level are considered to be on your spell list. To learn or cast a spell, you must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. You can cast spells you know without preparing them ahead of time. The saving throw DC against one of your spells is 10 + the spell level + your Charisma modifier. Like other spellcasters, you can cast only a certain number of spells of each level per day. Your base daily allotment of spells is given on Table 1–1: Mystic Blade Spells per Day, above. In addition, you receive bonus spells per day if you have a high Charisma score (see Table 1–3 on page 17 of the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook). You do not need to prepare these spells in advance; you can cast any spell you know at any time, assuming you haven’t yet used up your allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level. Your selection of spells is limited. At 4th level, you know two 1st-level spells of your choice. You gain more spells as you increase in level, as indicated on Table 1–2: Mystic Blade Spells Known. Unlike spells per day, the number of spells you know is not affected by your Charisma score. At 8th level and every 3 levels thereafter, you can choose to learn a new spell in place of one you already know. In effect, you lose the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. You may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that you gain new spells known for the level. This feature replaces spells. archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.mystic spellstrike (ex): At 4th level, choose either melee weapons or ranged weapons. If you choose melee weapons, then whenever you cast a spell with a range of “ touch ” gained from this archetype’s spell list, you can deliver the spell through any weapon you are wielding as part of a melee attack. Instead of the free melee touch attack normally allowed to deliver the spell, you can make one free attack with your weapon, at your highest base attack bonus, as part of casting this spell. If you choose ranged weapons, then whenever you cast a spell that calls for a ranged attack, you can deliver the spell through a ranged weapon you wield as part of a ranged attack. Instead of the free ranged attack normally allowed to deliver the spell, you can make one free ranged attack with a ranged weapon, at your highest base attack bonus, as part of casting this spell. The attack does not increase the spell’s range. If the spell can normally affect multiple targets, only a single missile, ray, or effect accompanies each attack; if the spell allows multiple attacks and the eldritch archer can make additional ranged attacks as part of a full-round action with spell combat, one additional ray, missile, or effect from the spell accompanies each subsequent ranged attack you make in the same round until all attacks allowed by the spell are made. Unused missiles, rays, or effects remaining at the end of your turn are wasted. If successful, your melee or ranged attack deals its normal damage as well as the effects of the spell. This attack uses the weapon’s critical threat range, but the spell effect only deals ×2 damage on a successful critical hit, while the weapon damage uses its own critical modifier. For the purposes of overcoming damage reduction, this spellstrike attack is considered to have an enhancement bonus equal to the spell being used. When making a spellstrike attack against a favored enemy, add your favored enemy bonus to any concentration checks that you are required to make. This feature replaces hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.improved armored casting (ex): At 8th level, you gain proficiency with medium armor and can arcane spells gained from this archetype while wearing medium armor without incurring a chance for arcane spell failure. Like any other arcane spellcaster, you still incur a chance of arcane spell failure while wearing heavy armor if the spell in question has a somatic component. This feature replaces swift tracker.
archetype-ranger-mystic-blade-ranger-arc.instinctual spell (su): At 11th level, you gain more flexibility with your spell list. Once per day, you can cast any 1st-level through 3rd-level spell on the magus spell list as if it were one of your spells known, expending a spell slot of the same spell level to cast the desired spell. Casting a spell with this ability always has a minimum casting time of 1 full round, regardless of the casting time of the spell. At 19th level, you can use this ability 3 times per day and can also use it to cast 4th-level magus spells. This feature replaces quarry and improved quarry.

archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.object reading (su): At 1st level, you learn how to read information from items you examine. Examining an item in this way requires you to spend 1 minute handling the item. If the item is a magic item, you learn its properties and command word as if you had successfully examined the item using detect magic and succeeded at a Spellcraft check. This ability does not reveal whether the item is cursed unless your ranger class level is equal to or greater than the caster level of the item. If the item has any historical significance, you learn one piece of information about its past (as determined by the GM). Finally, if the item was last used no longer than 1 day ago per ranger class level, you learn one piece of information about the last creature to use the item. This information might be a glimpse of the creature’s appearance, a brief vision of what it saw while using the item, or perhaps its emotional state when it last used the item. The GM determines what information is gained in this way. This functions like the psychometry occult skill unlock, but doesn’t require a skill check and can be used at will. If you have levels in the occultist class, they stack with your levels in ranger for the purposes of this ability. This feature replaces track and wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.iron will: You gain Iron Will as a bonus feat at 3rd level. This feature replaces endurance.
archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.phantom animal companion (ex): At 4th level, you call upon spirits of nature known as phantom animals to assist you in your journeys. A phantom animal functions like an animal companion except as noted in the descriptions below. You must choose your phantom animal from the list of animal companions normally available to you as a ranger, and your effective druid level and spiritualist level for your phantom animal companion statistics is equal to your ranger level –3. The phantom animal uses the statistics of an animal companion and follows the standard animal companion progression in regard to Hit Dice, base attack bonus, saving throws, skills, feats, natural armor bonus, Strength and Dexterity bonuses, and bonus tricks— but not its special abilities. A phantom animal instead gains the special abilities of a standard phantom standard phantom listed in the table on page 77 of Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Occult Adventures. A phantom animal is an outsider with the phantom subtype, and is considered a phantom for the purpose of all feats and abilities. It is capable of becoming harbored in your consciousness like a spiritualist ’s phantom, or becoming fully manifested. When fully manifested, your phantom animal shares your favored enemy and favored terrain bonuses. When your phantom animal is confined in your consciousness, you gain an insight bonus to Perception checks and to Survival checks made to track creatures equal to 1/2 your ranger level. This feature replaces hunter ’s bond and woodland stride.
archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.spellcasting: At 4th level, you gain spellcasting as a standard ranger, with the exception that your spells are cast as psychic spells instead of divine spells. (See Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Occult Adventures, p. 144.) Spells that would normally require verbal or somatic components instead require thought or emotion components, respectively, and only expensive material components are ever required. This feature alters spells.
archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.determination: Beginning at 9th level, if you make a Will saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, you instead avoid the effect entirely. This ability can only be used if you are wearing light armor, medium armor, or no armor. If you are helpless, you do not gain the benefit of this ability. This feature replaces evasion.
archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.animal senses (su): At 12th level, you share your phantom animal’s senses. If your phantom animal has any of the following abilities, you gain them whenever the phantom animal is harbored in your consciousness: blindsense, darkvision, low-light vision, and scent. This feature replaces camouflage.
archetype-ranger-psychic-ranger-ranger-a.see invisibility (sp): At 17th level, you gain see invisibility as a constant spell-like ability whenever the phantom animal is harbored in your consciousness. This feature replaces hide in plain sight.

archetype-ranger-reconnoiterer-ranger-ar.sneak attack (ex): At 2nd level, if you catch an opponent unable to defend itself effectively from your attack, you can strike a vital spot for extra damage. Your attack deals extra damage anytime your target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not), or when you flanks your target. This additional damage is 1d6 at 2nd level, and increases by 1d6 every 4 levels thereafter. Should you score a critical hit with a sneak attack, this additional damage is not multiplied. Ranged attacks can count as sneak attacks only if the target is within 30 feet. With a weapon that deals nonlethal damage (such as a sap, a whip, or an unarmed strike ), you can make a sneak attack that deals nonlethal damage instead of lethal damage. You cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal nonlethal damage in a sneak attack, not even with the usual –4 penalty. You must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot. You cannot use sneak attack while striking a creature that has concealment. This feature replaces combat style feats.
archetype-ranger-reconnoiterer-ranger-ar.reconnaissance (ex): At 3rd level, whenever you make a charge, your attack deals sneak attack damage as if the target were flat-footed. Foes with uncanny dodge are immune to this ability. This feature replaces endurance.
archetype-ranger-reconnoiterer-ranger-ar.skirmish (ex): At 7th level, whenever you move more than 10 feet in a round and make an attack action, the attack deals sneak attack damage as if the target was flat-footed. If you make more than one attack this turn, this ability only applies to the first attack. Foes with uncanny dodge are immune to this ability. This feature replaces woodland stride.

archetype-ranger-space-ranger-ranger-arc.technologically adept (ex): Handle Animal is not a class skill for you, but Knowledge (engineering) is. You are proficient with all firearms, but not with any kind of shields. Finally, you gain Technologist as a bonus feat at 1st level. This feature alters class skills and weapon and armor proficiency, and replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-space-ranger-ranger-arc.drone (ex): At 4th level, you gain a drone companion. This is a loyal construct that you build and maintain, and which accompanies you on you adventures. Your drone shares your favored enemy and favored terrain bonuses. This ability functions like the mechanic’s drone ability (which is part of the Artificial Intelligence class feature), except that your effective mechanic level is equal to your ranger level –3. This feature replaces hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-space-ranger-ranger-arc.spellcasting: As a space ranger, you draw your spells from the mystic spell list instead of the usual ranger spell list. Only mystic spells up to 4th level are considered to be on your spell list, and all 0-level mystic spells are treated as 1st-level space ranger spells for the purposes of your spell list. You otherwise prepare and cast your spells exactly the same as a standard ranger, including the number of spells that you can prepare per day and the fact that you cast them as divine spells. This feature alters spells.
archetype-ranger-space-ranger-ranger-arc.quick repair (ex): At 7th level, you can use make whole once per day as a spell-like ability that takes a full-round action to use. You can use this ability one additional time per day at 10th level and every 3 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 5 times per day at 19th level. This feature replaces woodland stride.

archetype-ranger-taelcwyr-ranger-archety.researched enemy: The bonus you gain from the favored enemy class feature does not apply to Bluff or Sense Motive checks, but does apply to and Spellcraft checks. In addition, Knowledge (arcana) is a class skill for you. This feature alters class skills and favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-taelcwyr-ranger-archety.divine spells: Beginning at 4th level, you gain the ability to cast a small number of divine spells, which are drawn from the druid spell list, except that only druid spells up to 3rd level are considered to be on your spell list. You must choose and prepare your spells in advance. Like a druid, you can cast any summon nature’s ally spell spontaneously in place of a prepared spell of the same level or lower. Table 2–1: Divine Spells Per Day Ranger Level Spell Level 0 1st 2nd 3rd 1–3 — — — — 4 1 0 — — 5 2 1 — — 6 2 1 — — 7 3 1 0 — 8 3 1 1 — 9 3 2 1 — 10 3 2 1 0 11 3 2 1 1 12 3 2 2 1 13 3 3 2 1 14 3 3 2 1 15 3 3 2 2 16 3 3 3 2 17 3 3 3 2 18 3 3 3 2 19 3 3 3 3 20 3 3 3 3 To prepare or cast a divine spell, you must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against one of your divine spells is 10 + the spell level + your Wisdom modifier. Like other spellcasters, you can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Your base daily allotment of divine spells is given on Table 2–1: Divine Spells per Day, above. In addition, you receive bonus divine spells per day if you have a high Wisdom score. When Table 2–1 indicates that you get 0 spells per day of a given spell level, you gain only the bonus spells you would be entitled to based on your Wisdom score for that spell level. You must spend 1 hour per day in quiet meditation to regain your daily allotment of spells. You may prepare and cast any spell on your divine spell list, provided that you can cast spells of that level, but you must choose which spells to prepare during your daily meditation. Through 3rd level, you have no caster level. At 4th level and higher, your caster level is equal to your ranger level –3. This feature alters the ranger ’s spells.
archetype-ranger-taelcwyr-ranger-archety.arcane spells and cantrips: Beginning at 4th level, you can prepare a number of cantrips, or arcane 0-level spells, each day, as noted on Table 2–2: Arcane Spells per Day. (Cantrips are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.) At 7th level, you gain the ability to cast a small number of spells, except that only sorcerer / wizard spells up to 3rd level are considered to be on your spell list. Your cantrips and other arcane spells are drawn from the sorcerer / wizard spell list. To learn, prepare, or cast an arcane spell, you must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against one of your arcane spells is 10 + the spell level + your Intelligence modifier. Your base daily allotment of arcane spells is given on Table 2–2. In addition, you receive bonus arcane spells per day if you have a high Intelligence score. When Table 2–2 indicates that you get 0 spells per day of a given spell level, you gain only the bonus spells you would be entitled to based on your Intelligence score for that spell level. You may know any number of arcane spells. You must choose and prepare your spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying your spellbook. While studying, you decide which spells to prepare. This may be done while you meditate for your divine spells. You can cast your arcane ranger spells while wearing light or medium armor and using a shield without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. This feature replaces hunter’s bond. archetype-ranger-xenoseeker-ranger-arche.monster lore (ex): You add your Wisdom modifier on Knowledge skill checks in addition to your Intelligence modifier, when making skill checks to identify the abilities and weaknesses of creatures. This feature replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-xenoseeker-ranger-arche.selective enemy (ex): At 1st level, when you successfully identify a creature you can see with a Knowledge check, you can designate that creature your favored enemy as a swift action. For the next 24 hours, you gain a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks against your target and all creatures of the same species. Likewise, you get a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against your target and creatures of the same species as your target. You can use this ability once at 1st level. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, you gain one additional use per day of this ability, to a maximum of 5 times per day at 20th level. In addition, at each of these levels, your bonus against your favored enemy increases by 1, to a maximum of +6 at 20th level. This feature alters favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-xenoseeker-ranger-arche.selective terrain (ex): At 3rd level, whenever you spend at least 10 minutes in a given type of terrain, you can designate it as your favored terrain. For the next 24 hours, you gain a +1 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks when you are in this terrain. When traveling through your favored terrain, you normally leave no trail and cannot be tracked (though you may leave a trail if you so choose). You can use this ability once per day at 3rd level. At 8th level and every five levels thereafter, you can use this ability one additional time per day, to a maximum of 4 times per day at 18th level. In addition, your bonus increases by 1 at each of these levels, to a maximum of +4 at 18th level. If a specific terrain falls into more than one category of favored terrain, your bonuses do not stack; you simply use whichever bonus is higher. This feature alters favored terrain.

archetype-ranger-amazon-ranger-archetype.manslayer (ex): An amazon can (and must) choose «( Human ) Males» as her first favored enemy.
archetype-ranger-amazon-ranger-archetype.terrible charge (su): When mounted and wearing a dress of peacock feathers, the amazon can scare her opponents’ horses during a charge. This works as a scare spell, usable once per day (affects a minimum of 1 target). This ability replaces Wild Empathy.
archetype-ranger-amazon-ranger-archetype.distracting beauty (ex): When unarmored and unencumbered, the amazon adds her Charisma bonus (if any) to her AC and her CMD. These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks or when the amazon is flat-footed. She loses these bonuses when she is immobilized or helpless, when she wears any armor, when she carries a shield, or when she carries a medium or heavy load. This ability replaces Hunter’s Bond.

archetype-ranger-slaver-ranger-archetype.weapon and armor proficiencies: Add proficiency with bolas, lasso, mancatcher, net, and whip. Remove proficiency with martial two-handed melee weapons. This alters Weapon and Armor Proficiencies. Skills: Replace Handle Animal with Disguise, and Knowledge (Nature) with Knowledge (Local).
archetype-ranger-slaver-ranger-archetype.intimidating presence (ex): The slaver adds half his slaver level (minimum 1) to all Intimidate skill rolls. This ability replaces Wild Empathy.
archetype-ranger-slaver-ranger-archetype.whip mastery (ex): At 2nd level, the slaver deals lethal damage and can affect any AC with a normal whip. At 6th level, the slaver does not provoke attacks of opportunity when he uses a whip. At 10th level, the slaver threatens 5 feet with a whip. At 14th level, the slaver threatens 10 feet with a whip. At 18th level, the slaver threatens 15 feet with a whip. This ability replaces Combat Style Feats. At the end of the initiation rite, a sufficiently high-level cult leader has the option of casting a mark of justice spell upon you, to ensure your loyalty to the cult. This class feature replaces Oracle ’s Curse.
archetype-ranger-slaver-ranger-archetype.cult secret: As you advance in levels as a Cultist, you learn new secrets that grant you powers and abilities. At 1st level, 3rd level, and every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, and so on), you select a new secret from the list of cult secrets listed in the cult’s description. Unless otherwise noted, activating the power of a cult secret is a standard action. This replaces Revelation.
archetype-ranger-slaver-ranger-archetype.cult spells: At 2nd level, and every two levels thereafter, you learn an additional spell taught by your cult. These spells are in addition to the number of spells given on the Spells Known table. They cannot be exchanged for different spells at higher levels. This feature is similar to the Bonus Spells feature of the Oracle’s Mystery.
archetype-ranger-slaver-ranger-archetype.cult hierarch (ex): At 20th level, you become the leader of your cult, with full control of the cult’s temples, treasures and relics, and you can command the lesser cult members as you desire. As a cult hierarch, the social circumstance bonuses you receive on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks increase to +8. If there is already a 20th-level Cultist in your cult, you must defeat him to gain your title and privileges. Likewise, you must be prepared to defend your position against those that rise in the ranks below you. This replaces Final Revelation.

archetype-ranger-wolf-heart.mutagen (su): At 1st level, a wolf heart discovers how to create a mutagen that he can imbibe in order to heighten his physical prowess at the cost of his personality. This functions as the alchemist ability of the same name, except the saving throw for a non- alchemist drinking the mutagen is 10 + 1/2 the wolf heart’s level + his Wisdom modifier. This replaces the favored enemy gained at 1st level.
archetype-ranger-wolf-heart.bomb (su): At 2nd level, a wolf heart learns how to create small explosives from easily obtained components. This functions as the alchemist bombs class feature, except the wolf heart an create and use a number of bombs each day equal to his ranger level + his Wisdom modifier. The wolf heart’s bombs deal 1d6 extra damage at 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 4d6 extra damage at 18th level. This replaces combat style.
archetype-ranger-wolf-heart.sigils (sp): At 3rd level, a wolf heart learns and can cast up to one 1st-level magus spell per day. At 8th, 13th, and 18th level, he learns and can cast up to one spell of the next highest level, as well as one additional spell of each level he already knows. For example, a 13th level wolf heart knows one 3rd-level magus spell, two 2nd-level spells, and three 1st-level spells. This replaces favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-wolf-heart.extracts: Wolf heart rangers don’t draw their spells from the ranger spell list. Instead, they gain extracts of the same level from the alchemist extract list. The wolf heart uses Wisdom instead of Intelligence to determine the saving throw DCs and other effects of his extracts. This modifies the ranger’s spells class feature.
archetype-ranger-wolf-heart.discovery (ex or su): At 5th level, and again at 10th, 15th, and 20th level, a wolf heart gains an alchemist discovery. In addition to the discoveries normally available to alchemists, the wolf heart can choose from the following. Instant Alchemy (Ex): If the wolf heart is at least 20th level and has swift alchemy, he can create any alchemical item as a full-round action if he succeeds at the Craft (alchemy) check and has the appropriate resources at hand to fund the creation. If he also has poison use, he can apply poison to a weapon as an immediate action. Persistent Mutagen (Su): If the wolf heart is at least 15th level, the effects of mutagens he drinks last for 1 hour per ranger level. Poison Use (Ex): The wolf heart is trained in the use of poison and cannot accidentally poison himself when applying poison to a weapon. Spell Combat (Ex): As the magus class feature. Spellstrike (Su): If the wolf heart has spell combat, he also gains the spellstrike magus class feature. Swift Alchemy (Ex): The wolf heart can create alchemical items in half the normal amount of time. If he has poison use, he can apply poison to a weapon as a move action. This replaces the favored enemies gained at the listed levels.

archetype-ranger-elemental-conduit-range.nature’s blessings (su): At 3rd level, an elemental conduit gains a pool of conductivity points equal to 1 + 1/2 his elemental conduit level, which he can use to power his supernatural elemental abilities. He selects one of the following warpriest blessings: air, earth, fire, water. This choice is permanent and cannot be changed. Using a standard action, an elemental conduit can spend one point from his conductivity pool to activate the minor ability of his chosen blessing. At 8th level, and every five levels thereafter, an elemental conduit selects another of the warpriest blessings from above. At 13th level, an elemental conduit can use his conductivity points to power major blessings, but doing so requires the expenditure of two conductivity points. An elemental conduit is free to use the points in his conductivity pool to power an ability from among any of his chosen blessings. This replaces favored terrain.

archetype-ranger-elemental-maverick-rang.frost and fire (sp): At 1st level, an elemental maverick can cast ray of frost and spark as spell-like abilities at will. For the purpose of this spell-like ability only, the elemental maverick’s caster level is equal to his extremist level. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-elemental-maverick-rang.combat style feat (ex): At 2nd level, an elemental maverick adds the magical combat style to his list of options from which to choose. If the elemental maverick selects magical combat, he can choose from the following list whenever he gains a combat style feat: Combat Casting, Improved Initiative, Spell Focus, and Spell Penetration. At 6th level, he adds Greater Spell Penetration, Rime Spell, and Spell Specialization to the list. At 10th level, he adds Burning Spell (fire only), Selective Spell, and Minor Spell Expertise to the list. This alters combat style.
archetype-ranger-elemental-maverick-rang.favored spells (ex): At 3rd level, an elemental maverick is considered to be constantly under the effects of endure elements. Furthermore, an elemental maverick adds all druid spells with the cold and fire descriptors to his spell list, and gains 1 extra spell per day for each level of spell he can cast. When preparing this extra spell, an elemental maverick must prepare a spell with either the cold or fire descriptor. Finally, an elemental maverick casts all spells with the cold or fire descriptor at +1 caster levels. This alters spells and replaces all iterations of favored terrain.
archetype-ranger-elemental-maverick-rang.bonded element (ex): At 4th level, an elemental maverick gains a third option from which to select for his hunter’s bond- he can select a bonded element. If he selects a bonded element, he must choose either cold or fire. (This choice is permanent and cannot be changed.) Whenever an elemental maverick deals damage from a weapon attack, he deals an additional +1d4 points of cold or fire damage (depending upon his selected element). This alters hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-elemental-maverick-rang.elemental resistance (ex): At 7th level, an elemental maverick selects either cold or fire and gains resistance 5 to that element. At 12th level, an elemental maverick again selects either cold or fire and gains resistance 10 to that element. At 17th level, an elemental maverick again selects either cold or fire and gains resistance 15 to that element. If the elemental maverick chooses the same element at multiple levels, the resistance stacks. For example, an elemental maverick that selects cold at all three levels would have cold resistance 30 by 17th level. This replaces woodland stride, camouflage, and hide in plain sight.

archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.class skills: A freerunner gains Acrobatics and Perform (tumble). This alters class skills.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.weapon and armor proficiency: A freerunner is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with one light or one handed exotic weapon of his choice. He is not proficient with any armor or shields. This alters weapon and armor proficiency.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.astute maneuverability (ex): When unarmored and unencumbered, a freerunner adds his Wisdom bonus (if any) to his AC and CMD. In addition, a freerunner gains a +1 bonus to AC and CMD at 4th level. This bonus increases by 1 for every four freerunner levels thereafter, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks or when the freerunner is flat-footed. He loses these bonuses when he is immobilized or helpless, when he wears any armor, when he carries a shield, or when he carries a medium or heavy load. (A multiclass freerunner with levels in monk treats his monk levels as freerunner levels for the purpose of determining when the +1 bonuses to AC/ CMD are gained.) A freerunner that takes levels in another class that adds the character’s Intelligence (or Charisma ) modifier to its AC while unarmored and unencumbered treats that class ability and astute maneuverability as one and the same for stacking purposes, and therefore must choose one or the other to add, but cannot add both. Furthermore, a freerunner can use his Wisdom modifier rather than his Dexterity modifier on his Acrobatics and Perform (tumble) skill check rolls. Once this choice is made, it is permanent and cannot be changed.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.fueled by adrenaline (ex): At 1st level, a freerunner gains a pool of adrenaline points, which provide him with short bursts of energy, allowing him to accomplish amazing feats. The number of points in a freerunner’s adrenaline pool is equal to 1/2 his freerunner level (minimum 1) + his Wisdom modifier. As long as a freerunner has at least 1 point in his adrenaline pool, he reduces the DC for any Acrobatics skill checks by 2 points, does not suffer any penalty to Acrobatics checks for obstructed or sloped conditions, and is always treated as having a running start when attempting an Acrobatics check to jump. By spending 1 point from his adrenaline pool as an immediate action when required to make a Reflex saving throw roll, a freerunner gains a +1 competence bonus to that roll. This bonus increases by +1 for every five freerunner levels, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. This, in conjunction with adrenaline powers, replaces favored enemy, quarry, and improved quarry.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.adrenaline powers (ex): Some adrenaline powers are constantly in effect, requiring no expenditure of points from the freerunner’s adrenaline pool, while others require the freerunner to expend 1 or more points to activate. Once an adrenaline power is selected, it cannot be changed. Some adrenaline powers require the freerunner to be of a specific level or higher before they can be chosen. A freerunner cannot select an adrenaline power more than once. A freerunner loses the use of his adrenaline powers if he wears any armor or carries a medium or heavy load. At 1st level, a freerunner can select 1 adrenaline power. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, the freerunner can select 1 additional adrenaline power. At 11th level, and again at 19th level, a freerunner can choose to either add +2 points to his adrenaline pool or select 1 additional adrenaline power. This, in conjunction with fueled by adrenaline, replaces favored enemy, quarry, and improved quarry.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.adrenaline surge (ex): A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to grant himself a sudden burst of speed. This increases the freerunner’s base land speed by 30 feet for 1 minute.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.constant motion (ex): When a freerunner with this power would normally be hit with a melee attack, he can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as an immediate action to gain a free Acrobatics check (DC = the attack roll that hit the freerunner) to deflect some or all of the blow. A freerunner suffers 1/2 damage (round down) on a successful Acrobatics check, and no damage if the Acrobatics check exceeds the DC by 5 or more. A freerunner must be at least 10th level before selecting this adrenaline power.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.effortless descent (ex): A freerunner with this power does not need to expend adrenaline points from his adrenaline pool to activate it; its effects are constantly active. Whenever the freerunner falls (intentionally or not), a successful DC 15 Acrobatics check allows him to ignore the first 30 feet fallen. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this distance increases by an additional 20 feet.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.expedited assault (ex): A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to increase his offensive capabilities; when taking the fullattack action, he gains 1 extra attack at his highest base attack bonus for 1 round. This extra attack stacks with the extra attack gained from the spell haste, but does not stack with extra attacks granted by the class ability flurry of blows. A freerunner must be at least 5th level before selecting this adrenaline power.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.perfect agility (ex): A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to gain a +5 competence bonus to all Acrobatics checks. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +5, to a maximum of +25 at 20th level. If a freerunner spends 2 points rather than 1 when activating this power, he gains additional benefits; he can move at full speed while making an Acrobatics check to move across a narrow surface without adding +5 to the DC of the check, and he can move through a threatened square to avoid provoking an attack of opportunity from an enemy without adding +10 to the DC. This effect lasts for 1 minute.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.quick-up (ex): A freerunner with this power does not need to expend adrenaline points from his adrenaline pool to activate it; its effects are constantly active, allowing a freerunner to use a swift action to stand from a prone position without provoking an attack of opportunity for standing while threatened by an enemy.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.ricocheting ascent (ex): A freerunner with this power does not need to expend adrenaline points from his adrenaline pool to activate it; its effects are constantly active, allowing a freerunner to walk on walls for brief distances. A freerunner can use a single move action to traverse a wall or other vertical surface if he begins and ends his movement on a horizontal surface. The height achieved on the wall is limited only by this movement restriction. If a freerunner does not end his move on a horizontal surface capable of supporting his weight, he falls. The wall is treated as a normal floor for the purposes of measuring movement. Passing from floor to wall costs no movement; a freerunner can change services freely. A freerunner can expend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a free action to gain the benefits of this power until the end of his current turn.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.unrestricted (ex): A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a free action to gain unrestricted movement; he is treated as though under the effects of freedom of movement for 10 minutes. A freerunner must be at least 10th level before selecting this adrenaline power.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.whirlwind assault (ex): A freerunner with this power can spend 2 points from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to gain the benefits of the feat Whirlwind Attack for 1 round. A freerunner must be at least 10th level before selecting this adrenaline power.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.motivation (ex): At 1st level, a freerunner selects 1 motivating force behind his love for running freely across a multitude of terrains. Each motivation comes with its own unique benefit. Once made, this selection is permanent, and cannot be changed.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.ducking the law (ex): You have either personally experienced time behind bars, or you have acted as a vigilante, taking the law into your own hands to free individuals you believed were wrongly incarcerated. You gain Disable Device as a class skill and can add 1/2 your freerunner level to Disable Device skill checks made to open locks.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.free-spirited (ex): You were born with an exuberance for fast-paced movement. You gain fast movement as the barbarian ability of the same name. At 8th level, your speed is increased by +20 feet instead of +10 feet.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.tricks of the trade (ex): You were either a street performer, a high-wire or trapeze artist with a traveling circus, or a professional athlete competing in local seasonal games. You can use Perform (tumble) checks in place of Acrobatics and Climb skill checks, and you gain a +2 competence bonus on Perform (tumble) skill checks. This replaces track and swift tracker.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.wilderness magic (sp): At 1st level, a freerunner selects 3 0-level spells (orisons) from the druid spell list. Once made, this selection is permanent, and cannot be changed. The freerunner can cast these spells as a spell-like ability, in any combination, a number of times per day equal to his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). At 4th level, a freerunner can use his wilderness magic spell-like ability an unlimited number of times per day. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.combat style feat (ex): A freerunner adds a new category of combat styles to the options he can select from called skirmisher. If a freerunner selects skirmisher as his combat style, he can choose from the following list whenever he gains a combat style feat: Acrobatic Steps, Dodge, Fleet, and Nimble Moves. At 6th level, he adds Landing Roll, Mobility, and Spring Attack to the list. At 10th level, he adds Acrobatic SpellcasterUI and Disorienting Maneuver to the list. This ability functions as combat style feat in all other ways. This alters combat style feat.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.run: At 3rd level, a freerunner gains the bonus feat Run. This replaces endurance.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.topographical bond (ex): At 4th level, a freerunner can select an animal companion following the standard rules for a ranger’s hunter’s bond, or he can elect to bond with his favored terrains. If he selects the latter, a freerunner gains a +2 insight bonus to his AC in all of his favored terrains. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1. This alters hunter’s bond.
archetype-ranger-freerunner-ranger-arche.perpetual motion (ex): At 20th level, a freerunner can select 1 of his adrenaline powers that requires the expenditure of adrenaline points to activate. The freerunner can activate this power without expending adrenaline points a number of times per day equal to 3 + the freerunner’s Wisdom modifier. Additionally, a freerunner can take an additional move action in the current round a number of times per day equal to his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). This replaces master hunter.

archetype-ranger-herbal-savant-ranger-ar.skilled botanist (ex): At 1st level, an herbal savant must select plant as his favored enemy. Furthermore, an herbal savant gains a +2 competence bonus on Fortitude saving throws made against all plant poisons, and is always treated as though he has a number of skill ranks equal to his herbal savant level in Knowledge (nature) when making a skill check regarding plants and plant creatures. Finally, an herbal savant gains woodland stride at 1st level rather than 7th level. This alters favored enemy and woodland stride, and replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-herbal-savant-ranger-ar.botanical medic (su): An herbal savant combines the botanical gifts of nature with his own magical essence to create curative tonics to restore his health during the course of the day. Only the herbal savant can gain the curative benefit of his tonics. At 2nd level, an herbal savant can create a number of curative tonics equal to 1 + his Wisdom modifier. At 6th level, and every four levels thereafter, an herbal savant can create one extra tonic. An herbal savant’s tonic cures a number of hit points equal to 1/2 his herbal savant level + 1d6 points of damage. For every three levels beyond 2nd, the damage the tonic cures increases by +1d6, to a maximum of +7d6 at 20th level. Each morning, after 8 hours of rest, an herbal savant must spend 10 minutes creating his curative tonics. A tonic, once created, remains potent for 1 day before becoming inert, so an herbal savant must prepare his curative tonics every day. Imbibing a curative tonic is treated in the same manner as drinking a potion with regards to the action type required and whether it provokes an attack of opportunity. This replaces all combat style feats, quarry, and improved quarry.
archetype-ranger-herbal-savant-ranger-ar.green-bond (ex and sp): At 4th level, an herbal savant gains the plant domain or any of the plant subdomains of his choice. He can even select two subdomains as long as when the two subdomains are combined, they replace different domain powers. For example, an herbal savant could select both the decay and growth subdomains because the decay subdomain replaces the bramble armor power and the growth subdomain replaces the wooden fist power. In addition to gaining the domain powers at the specified levels, the herbal savant adds the domain spells to his ranger spell list as soon as he is capable of casting spells of the appropriate level. (He never gets the spells of 5th level and above.) Finally, the herbal savant adds the following spells to his ranger spell list: goodberry at 4th level, plant shape l at 7th level, plant shape ll at 10th level, and plant shape lll at 13th level. This replaces hunter’s bond.

archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.undeterred: A shackle-breaker allows no distraction to interfere with the mission to topple tyranny. At 1st level, a shackle-breaker gains a +2 bonus on Will saving throws against mindaffecting effects. This replaces wild empathy.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.liberation pool: A shackle-breaker cannot rest while individuals suffer under the yoke of oppression. At 2nd level, a shackle-breaker gains a reserve of magical energy in the form of a liberation pool, which he can use to achieve the goal of freedom for all. This liberation pool refreshes each day, after a restful night’s sleep, and is equal to 1/2 the shackle-breaker’s level + his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). By expending one or more points, a shackle-breaker can activate any of the following abilities. This replaces all combat style feats.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.alleviate malady (ex and sp): By expending 1 point from his liberation pool as a standard action, a shacklebreaker can touch a creature to cure 2d8 points of non-lethal damage. A shackle-breaker can touch a target and expend 2 points to cure the dazzled, shaken, or sickened condition. At 6th level, a shackle-breaker can spend the specified number of points as a standard action to cast the listed spells as spell-like abilities with a caster level equal to his shackle-breaker level: remove fear (2 points), remove paralysis (2 points), restoration, lesser (2 points), remove curse (5 points).
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.beacon of hope (su): By expending 1 point from his liberation pool as an immediate action, a shackle-breaker can grant himself or an ally within 30 feet a morale bonus equal to 1/2 his shackle-breaker level (minimum 1) on a failed skill check, saving throw, or combat maneuver roll. If adding this bonus to the failed roll would meet the DC, the attempt is considered successful instead. A creature cannot benefit from this ability more than once per day.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.fear not (ex): When making a Will save against a fear effect, a shackle-breaker can expend 1 point from his liberation pool as an immediate action to gain a +2 morale bonus on saving throw rolls against fear for 1 minute. Furthermore, any ally that witnesses the shackle-breaker make a successful save, gains a +2 morale bonus on Will saves against fear as well (until the 1 minute duration expires).
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.invigorate the downtrodden (sp): By expending 2 points from his liberation pool as a swift action, a shacklebreaker can grant himself and all allies within 30 feet +2d8 temporary hit points. The number of temporary hit points granted increases by +2d8 at 10th and 18th level. A creature cannot benefit from this ability more than once a day.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.bind oppressor (sp): At 14th level, by expending 5 points from his liberation pool as a standard action, a shackle-breaker can cast leashed shackles as a spell-like ability with a caster level equal to his shackle-breaker level.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.unhindered (su): By expending 1 point from his liberation pool as a free action, a shackle-breaker can act as though under the influence of freedom of movement until the start of his next turn. By expending 2 points from his liberation pool as a standard action, a shackle-breaker can touch a creature to grant it the effects of freedom of movement for 1 round.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.weapon against oppression (sp): By expending 1 point from his liberation pool as a free action, a shacklebreaker can grant a weapon he is wielding the ability to ignore the DR of evil creatures that have DR 5 or lower, as long as the damage reduction is not DR /epic. The shacklebreaker also gains a +2 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls made against evil creatures, and a +1 insight bonus to his AC against attacks made by evil creatures. At 10th level, the amount of damage reduction this ability can bypass increases to 10, the bonus on attack and damage rolls increases to +4, and the AC bonus increases to +2. At 18th level, the shackle-breaker can add either the bane or the keen special weapon ability to his weapon against oppression. Once activated, this ability remains in effect for a number of rounds equal to the shackle-breaker’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). A weapon against oppression only functions in the hands of the shackle-breaker that created it.
archetype-ranger-shackle-breaker-ranger-.battlemate’s bond (ex): At 7th level, a shackle-breaker grants all allies within 30 feet of himself a +1 competence bonus on Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks anytime he is in one of his favored terrains. This replaces woodland stride.

archetype-sorcerer-aberrant-lord-sorcere.strange bloodline: An aberrant lord must have the aberrant or shapechanger bloodline.
archetype-sorcerer-aberrant-lord-sorcere.aberrant heritage: At 1st level, an aberrant lord chooses an alien heritage (see In The Company of Aberrations by Rite Publishing). Whenever he would gain a bloodline power, he may instead take an alien heritage power. At 1st level, the 1st-level power can be chosen; at 3rd level, the 3rd-level power; at 9th level, the 7th-level power; at 15th level, the 11th-level power; and at 20th level, the 17th-level power. This modifies the sorcerer’s bloodline powers.

archetype-sorcerer-elementalist-sorcerer.elemental spell (ex): An elementalist sorcerer gains Elemental Spell as a bonus feat at 1st level. She gains it again at 7th and 13th level, each time applying it to a different element among those she selected with her scion of many elements ability. This replaces eschew materials and the 7th- and 13th-level bloodline feats.
archetype-sorcerer-elementalist-sorcerer.scion of many elements: At 1st level, an elementalist sorcerer chooses two elements instead of one. Every time she uses her bloodline arcana, bloodline powers, and bloodline spells, she chooses which element she uses them with. At 10th level, she can select a third element to use her bloodline abilities with.

archetype-sorcerer-polar-sovereign-sorce.bloodline: A polar sovereign must have the boreal bloodline (or one of its wildblooded variants).
archetype-sorcerer-polar-sovereign-sorce.frozen spells: The polar sovereign replaces some of her bloodline spells with the following: frostbite (3rd), winter’s grasp (5th), cold ice strike (13th), summon monster VII ( ice elementals only) (15th), mass icy prison (19th).
archetype-sorcerer-polar-sovereign-sorce.diminished spellcasting: A polar sovereign casts one fewer spell of each level than normal. If this reduces the number to 0, she can cast spells of that level only if her Charisma score allows bonus spells of that level. This alters the sorcerer’s spellcasting.
archetype-sorcerer-polar-sovereign-sorce.ice magic (ex): At 1st level, whenever the polar sovereign casts a spell that deals energy damage, she changes the type of damage to cold. This also changes the spell’s descriptor to cold. All spells with the cold descriptor are considered to be in the polar sovereign’s sorcerer spell list (but not in her known spell list). This replaces bloodline arcana.
archetype-sorcerer-polar-sovereign-sorce.winter mastery: At 13th level, whenever she could gain a bloodline feat, a polar sovereign can instead choose to gain access to one of the following witch hexes: hoarfrost, ice tomb, or numbing chillRoWPG.

archetype-sorcerer-nanotech-infuser-sorc.artificer’s touch (sp): You can cast mending at will, using your sorcerer level as the caster level to repair damaged objects. In addition, you can cause damage to objects and construct creatures by striking them with a melee touch attack. Objects and constructs take 1d6 points of damage +1 for every two sorcerer levels you possess. This attack bypasses an amount of damage reduction and hardness equal to your sorcerer level. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. This replaces the bloodline power gained at 1st level.
archetype-sorcerer-nanotech-infuser-sorc.nanite adaptation (ex): At 7th level, the nanites infused into your body replace a portions of your vital organ and body systems. You have minor visible circuitry or mechanical elements, which can be hidden with a DC 15 Disguise check. You take only half damage from bleed or blood drain attacks (minimum 1) and automatically stabilize at negative hit points. You also gain a +2 bonus on saves against disease, poison, and mind-affecting effects. However, your personality becomes somewhat mechanical and inhuman, causing you to take a -2 penalty on Charisma checks and Charisma -based skill checks made when interacting with living creatures. If you take at least 5 points of electricity damage in a round, the benefits (but not drawbacks) of your nanite adaptation are suppressed until the end of your next turn. This replaces the bloodline feat and bloodline spell gained at 7th level.
archetype-sorcerer-nanotech-infuser-sorc.nanovirus (su): At 13th level, as a full-round action you can infect a living creature with a nanite virus derived from corrupted nanites in your own system. You must touch the target and expend two uses of your artificer’s touch, dealing 1d4 points of Wisdom damage and 1d2 points of Constitution damage ( Fortitude half). The save DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier. A target whose Wisdom damage equals or exceeds its Wisdom score becomes helpless for 1 hour and then rises as a nanite zombie. In this state, it is equivalent to either a standard or fast zombie (your choice), with construct traits replacing undead traits. It is neither living nor undead and is immune to both positive and negative energy; however, as a construct it can be healed with your artificer’s touch. The nanite zombie is remains under your control for a number of days equal to your sorcerer level, at which point its lifeless husk collapses into a heap of carrion and corroded cybernetic circuitry. You can control a maximum number of HD of nanite zombies equal to twice your sorcerer level. If creating a new nanite zombie would exceed this limit, the new nanite zombie is created and the oldest nanite zombie (s) in excess of your HD limit become uncontrolled and are immediately hostile to all living creatures. This replaces the bloodline feat and bloodline spell gained at 13th level.
archetype-sorcerer-nanotech-infuser-sorc.nanite apotheosis (su): At 19th level, the nanites infused into your body replace a most of your vital organs and body systems. Your partially mechanical nature is obvious to anyone unless you successfully hide it with a DC 25 Disguise check. You are immune to bleed and blood drain effects, disease, and poison, and gain a +4 bonus on saves against death effects and mind-affecting effects. Your personality becomes even more mechanical and distant, increasing the penalty on Charisma checks and Charisma -based skill checks when interacting with living creatures to -5. Your circuitry is more stable, however, and the benefits of your nanite apotheosis are suppressed only if you take at least 30 points of electricity damage in a round. This replaces the bloodline feat and bloodline spell gained at 19th level.

archetype-sorcerer-familiar.bonded spellcaster (ex): The Dreamlands cat selects an allied shaman, sorcerer, witch, wizard, or other spellcaster who can accept a familiar and who agrees to take on the Dreamlands cat as her familiar. Once this choice is made, the Dreamlands cat becomes a familiar sorcerer. That bonded spellcaster cannot take feats or options to improve her familiar beyond the normal baseline abilities her class grants to familiars. Typically, a Dreamlands cat selects another player character spellcaster to bond with in the same adventuring party. With the GM’s permission, a Dreamlands cat familiar sorcerer can gain an NPC bonded spellcaster as a cohort with the Leadership feat. Alternatively, the GM might permit a Dreamlands cat sorcerer of at least 5th level to gain the Improved Familiar feat, but only to obtain a NPC bonded spellcaster of his sorcerer level – 3. The bonded spellcaster enjoys the normal benefits gained by having a cat familiar except as described below. A familiar sorcerer gains his own Hit Dice, hit points, attacks, saving throws, and skills as normal for a sorcerer (he does not use the rules for determining these values for a familiar ). A familiar sorcerer’s Intelligence is determined normally and is not dependent upon or modified by his bonded spellcaster’s class level. The familiar sorcerer gains the following abilities in place of those of a typical familiar. Unlike most class features, these are gained as soon as either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is a high enough level. Share Spells: At 1st level, the familiar sorcerer and his bonded spellcaster may share spells with each other in the same manner as a familiar and its master.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.empathic link (su): The familiar sorcerer and his bonded spellcaster gain this ability normally. Deliver Touch Spells: If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 3rd level, the familiar sorcerer can deliver touch spells for the bonded spellcaster.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.evasion (ex): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 3rd level, the familiar sorcerer gains evasion as the rogue ability.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.natural armor (ex): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 5th level, the familiar spellcaster’s natural armor improves by 1. It improves by another +1 at 13th level and 19th level.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.speak with master (ex): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 5th level, they gain this ability normally.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.speak with animals of its kind (ex): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 7th level, the familiar sorcerer can communicate with all cat-like creatures, including monsters that have feline features (including creatures as diverse as dire lions, lamias, and rakshasas ) regardless of language barriers.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.improved evasion (ex): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 9th level, the familiar sorcerer gains improved evasion.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.spell resistance (ex): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 11th level, the familiar sorcerer gains spell resistance equal to the higher-level character’s level + 5.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.scrying (sp): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 13th level, the bonded spellcaster may scry on her familiar (as if casting the scrying spell) once per day, and the familiar sorcerer may do the same on his bonded spellcaster once per day.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.linked minds (su): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 15th level, they can communicate telepathically via their empathic bond. If one fails a Will saving throw and the other is within range of their empathic link, the other can make a Will save against the effect. On a success, the other’s saving throw succeeds. Each can use this ability to protect the other once per day.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.synergistic intellect (sp): If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is at least 17th level, the familiar sorcerer gains a +2 inherent bonus to Intelligence.
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.magical conduit: If either the familiar sorcerer or the bonded spellcaster is 20th level, each can use the other as the point of origin to determine range for any spell. Each can teleport to the other’s space once per day as a standard action across any distance, even across planar boundaries. If the familiar sorcerer’s bonded spellcaster is a shaman or witch, the familiar sorcerer still functions as a bonded shaman’s (or witch’s ) source of spells, but cannot access any spells himself to cast them with the exception of shaman spirit magic spells. If the bonded spellcaster is a shaman, the familiar sorcerer adds all of the bonded shaman’s spirit magic spells to the sorcerer spell list and to his own spells known as soon as both the familiar sorcerer and the bonded shaman are high enough level to cast the spirit magic spell. If the bonded spellcaster is slain, the familiar sorcerer loses all benefits of this archetype (and does not gain the normal bloodline benefits) until his bonded spellcaster is restored to life or he finds a new spellcaster to bond with. This ability replaces bloodline (including the bloodline skill, arcana, powers, spells, and feats the sorcerer would normally gain as the result of having a bloodline ).
archetype-sorcerer-familiar.symbiotic spellcasting (su): As long as the familiar sorcerer and the bonded spellcaster are adjacent or sharing the same space, the familiar sorcerer can take advantage of minute, reflexive motions in his bonded spellcaster to satisfy the requirements of somatic spell components. If the bonded spellcaster carries material components or focus components on her person, the familiar sorcerer can use those components as well. Material components are consumed as the familiar sorcerer casts his spell. In order to use a focus component, the bonded spellcaster must be carrying that focus component in a hand. This ability replaces Eschew Materials.

archetype-sorcerer-rage-mage-sorcerer-ar.spell rage (su): Beginning with 1st level, a rage mage lets the rage boiling in their blood to burst forth. They can spell rage for a number of rounds per day equal to 4 + their Charisma modifier. At each level after 1st, they can spell rage for an additional 2 rounds per day. Temporary increases to Charisma, such as that gained from eagle’s splendor, do not increase the total number of rounds that a rage mage can spell rage per day. A rage mage can enter a spell rage as a free action. The total number of rounds of spell rage per day is renewed after regaining spells. When in a spell rage, a rage mage gains a +2 bonus to the DCs and attack rolls of their spells for any evocation, conjuration, necromancy, or transmutation spell. Additionally, they gain a +2 bonus to caster level for dispel attempts and to bypass spell resistance as well. However, while in the spell rage, the roiling magic energy makes them more susceptible to the spells of others, they take a -2 penalty to AC and saves against spells and spell-like abilities and they take a -2 penalty to concentration checks. The penalty to saving throws does not extend to enchantment, compulsion, charm, or fear effects. While in the spell rage, a rage mage cannot use any Charisma – or Intelligence -based skill, except for Intimidate. A rage mage can end their spell rage as a free action and is fatigued for 1 minute after the spell rage ends. A rage mage cannot enter a new spell rage while fatigued or exhausted, but otherwise can enter a spell rage multiple times per day. If the rage mage falls unconscious, their spell rage immediately ends.
archetype-sorcerer-rage-mage-sorcerer-ar.spell rage power (su): At 6th level, a rage mage adds 1/2 their sorcerer class level to damage dealt with spells while in their spell rage. This bonus only applies once to a spell, not once per missile or ray, and cannot be split between multiple missiles or rays. This bonus damage is not increased by Empower Spell or similar effects.
archetype-sorcerer-rage-mage-sorcerer-ar.greater spell rage (su): At 11th level, a rage mage increases the bonus to DCs, attack rolls and caster level checks to +3 while in their spell rage.
archetype-sorcerer-rage-mage-sorcerer-ar.tireless spell rage (su): At 17th level, a rage mage is no longer fatigued at the end of their spell rage.
archetype-sorcerer-rage-mage-sorcerer-ar.mighty spell rage (su): At 20th level, a rage mage increases the bonus to DCs, attack rolls and caster level checks to +4 while in their spell rage.

archetype-sorcerer-seal-bound-sorcerer-s.bind spirit: A seal-bound sorcerer may seal pacts with otherworldly entities known as spirits. In order to summon a spirit, the seal-bound sorcerer must learn the spirit’s ceremony, constellation, personality, and seal by completing its four Knowledge Tasks; see Researching the Spirit for more information on this process. A soul-bound sorcerer begins play having completed all four Knowledge Tasks for one 1st-level spirit of her choice that belongs to her chosen constellation (see tunneled lore below). Each day, a seal-bound sorcerer may bind one spirit to her soul using pact magic; see Performing a Pact Ritual. This spirit’s level may not exceed the seal-bound sorcerer’s maximum spirit level, which is limited to 1st-level spirits at 1st level. At 4th level and every three sorcerer levels thereafter, the seal-bound sorcerer maximum spirit level increases by 1, to a maximum of 6th-level spirits at 16th level. A seal-bound sorcerer’s binder level is equal to her level. The DC to resist a seal-bound sorcerer’s supernatural powers is equal to 10 + 1/2 the seal-bound sorcerer’s binder level + the seal-bound sorcerer’s Charisma modifier. This ability replaces the sorcerer’s bloodline spells.
archetype-sorcerer-seal-bound-sorcerer-s.diminished spellcasting: A seal-bound sorcerer has one fewer spell known at each level (including cantrips) than is presented on Table: Sorcerer Spells Known.
archetype-sorcerer-seal-bound-sorcerer-s.tunneled lore: At 1st level, a seal-bound sorcerer chooses one constellation. She may only seal pacts with starless spirits and spirits belonging to her chosen constellation. All other constellations are barred to her.

archetype-sorcerer-bloodline-transmogrif.bloodline arcana (su): The bloodline transmogrifist gains the ability to transmogrify his armor as detailed above. Bloodline Powers: In place of any of the bloodline powers granted by his bloodline, the bloodline transmogrifist can gain and use one natural attack, spell-like ability, or activated supernatural ability possessed by the creature his summon monster spell would otherwise summon. If the ability learned in this way duplicates a spell, that spell cannot be one the bloodline transmogrifist couldn’t learn to cast (due to being a higher level, or on another spell list).

archetype-sorcerer-scion-of-civility-sor.civilized studies: A scion of civility may choose Knowledge (engineering), Knowledge (history), or the class skill specified for her bloodline. This alters the bloodline class skill.
archetype-sorcerer-scion-of-civility-sor.peacemaker spells: A scion of civility must take the following bonus spells at the specified levels in place of the bonus spells dictated by her bloodline: serenity (13th level) and euphoric tranquility (17th level). This alters the bloodline bonus spells.
archetype-sorcerer-scion-of-civility-sor.sweeten the pot: A scion of civility adds Skill Focus ( Diplomacy ) and Voice of the Sibyl to her list of bloodline bonus feats. This alters bloodline bonus feats.
archetype-sorcerer-scion-of-civility-sor.master mediator (ex): At 1st level, a scion of civility adds half her class level (minimum 1) to Profession (diplomat) skill checks. Additionally, a scion of civility can use her bonus in Profession (diplomat) in place of her bonus in Diplomacy and Knowledge (local). When substituting in this way, a scion of civility uses her total Profession (diplomat) skill bonus, including class skill bonus and master mediator bonus, in place of the Diplomacy and Knowledge (local) bonuses, regardless of whether or not she has ranks in either Diplomacy or Knowledge (local) or if they are class skills. This replaces bloodline arcana.
archetype-sorcerer-scion-of-civility-sor.law rules (ex): At 3rd level, a scion of civility gains the rule of law bloodline power.
archetype-sorcerer-scion-of-civility-sor.rule of law (ex): At 3rd level, you gain DR1/ chaotic. At 9th level, your damage reduction increases to DR2/ chaotic. This replaces the 3rd level bloodline power.

archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.weapon and armor proficiencies: Gadget guardians add proficiency with bolas, boomerangs, hand crossbows, and shuriken to the list of cavalier weapon proficiencies.
archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.expert glide (ex): At 1st level, a gadget guardian gains and masters the use of a gyro-glider. The gadget guardian can move 10 feet laterally for every 20 feet he falls using the gyro-glider. In addition, while wearing a gyro-glider, the gadget guardian reduces the DC of Acrobatics skill checks for a long jump by 10. This ability replaces the cavalier’s mount ability at 1st level.
archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.zip-line mod (ex): At 3rd level, a gadget guardian gains a grapnel gauntlet and learns how to modify it to increase its usefulness. The grapnel gauntlet’s range increases to 40 feet. As a swift action the gadget guardian can retract a fired cable, using it to pull him up, or to drag or lift a Medium load. The cable retracts at the end of the round. A retracted cable may be reused, but the grapnel gauntlet still requires a swift action to recock it. This ability replaces the cavalier’s charge ability at 3rd level.
archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.razor boomerang mod (ex): At 4th level, a gadget guardian learns to create miniature missiles that are part-boomerang, part- shuriken. A razor boomerang counts as a shuriken for the purposes of determining proficiencies and damage (see the Equipment chapter of the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook). The gadget guardian gains Weapon Focus ( shuriken ) and Weapon Specialization ( shuriken ) as bonus feats. A gadget guardian can choose to do either piercing or slashing damage with these weapons. If slashing damage is chosen, and the gadget guardian has a Dex of 15 or greater, the razor boomerang returns to him at the end of the round. If piercing damage is chosen, the target take 1 point of bleed damage from a successful hit. This ability replaces the cavalier’s expert trainer ability at 4th level.
archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.fearsome mask (ex): At 5th level, a gadget guardian creates a disguise with which to frighten their foes. While wearing this disguise, the gadget guardian gains a +20 equipment bonus on Bluff skill checks made to keep their identity a secret. In addition, the gadget guardian gains an equipment bonus equal to 1/2 their cavalier level on Intimidate checks made to demoralize an opponent. If the gadget guardian succeeds in demoralizing a target, the duration the target is shaken is doubled. The target does not need to see the gadget guardian if the gadget guardian is standing in an area of dim light or darkness, as long as the target can hear the gadget guardian’s verbal threats. If the target’s Hit Dice is less than half of your total Hit Dice, the target is frightened instead of shaken. This ability replaces the cavalier’s banner ability at 5th level.
archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.improvise (ex): At 11th level, the gadget guardian becomes adept at creating useful, improvised items to aid in any situation. A gadget guardian may use an appropriate Craft skill check to aid another if the gadget guardian has access to at least 100 gp worth of resources, the appropriate tools, and an uninterrupted hour to prepare the item. After the check is made the item becomes unusable, but is returned to the gadget guardian’s resources at no cost. The gadget guardian can reduce the time required to improvise an item by taking a –2 penalty for every 10 minutes quicker the gadget guardian wishes to be, up to a maximum of –10 for a total time of 10 minutes. The gadget guardian gains Throw Anything as a bonus feat, or Improvised Weapon Mastery if the gadget guardian already has that feat. The gadget guardian does not need to meet the prerequisites for these feats. This ability replaces the cavalier’s mighty charge ability at 11th level.
archetype-cavalier-gadget-guardian-caval.adaptive countermeasures (ex): At 14th level, gadget guardians build protective countermeasures into their arsenal of gadgets. As a standard action, the gadget guardian gains an additional saving throw against any one spell or effect that is targeting them. This save is made at the original DC, but the gadget guardian gains a +4 equipment bonus on this save. Spells and effects that do not allow saving throws are unaffected by this ability. The gadget guardian can use this ability once per day. This ability replaces the cavalier’s greater banner ability at 14th level.
