archetype-legendary-samurai-ancestral-in.greater spirit surge (su): At 10th level, an ancestral inheritor can spend 2 spirit as a move action to grant their spiritual guardian the effect of a evolution surge. This ability replaces greater banner.

archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.weapon proficiencies: A gunblade duelist is proficient with all simple and melee weapons, as well as the sword pistol cane. This ability alters the legendary samurai’s weapon proficiencies.
archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.signature weapon: At 1st level, a gunblade duelist gains a sword pistol cane. While it is in their possession, the gunblade duelist adds their class level to the Perception check required to notice that a sword cane pistol is anything other than a normal cane.
archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.bullet control (ex): Whenever a gunblade duelist sheathes a sword pistol cane, as long as they have at least 1 spirit, they can reload the weapon as a free action. This ability alters sheathe control.
archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.gun technique: A gunblade duelist cannot learn cut techniques. In addition, a gunblade duelist gains access to the following iaijutsu technique:
archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.bullet slash (ex): Whenever the legendary samurai makes an iaijutsu strike while wielding a pistol sword cane, they can choose to also fire a bullet from that weapon as a free action, targeting any creature within the first range increment of their weapon. This attack does not provoke attacks of opportunity. This ability alters iaijutsu technique.
archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.perfect craftsmanship (ex): At 2nd level, while wielding a sword pistol cane, its range is increased by 10 feet. At 5th level and every three levels afterwards, its range increases by an additional 10 feet. At 6th level, while wielding a sword pistol cane, its misfire rate is reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 0). This ability replaces resolve and greater resolve.
archetype-legendary-samurai-gunblade-due.gun fusion (ex): At 10th level, whenever a gunblade duelist makes an iaijutsu strike, they can apply the bullet slash iaijutsu technique in addition to another slash technique. In addition, the gunblade duelist can choose to have the effect of any iaijutsu slash apply to the target of the sword cane pistol’s ranged attack instead of the melee attack. This ability replaces iaijutsu master.

archetype-legendary-samurai-master-strik.weapon and armor proficiencies: A master striker is proficient simple and martial weapons as well as unarmed strikes. A master striker is also proficient in light armor. This alters a legendary samurai’s normal weapon and armor proficiencies.
archetype-legendary-samurai-master-strik.iron fist (ex): At 1st level, a master striker gains the unarmed damage of a monk of their class level. This ability replaces sheathe control.
archetype-legendary-samurai-master-strik.ac bonus (ex): When wearing light armor or no armor, not carrying a shield, and unencumbered, the master striker adds their Charisma bonus (if any) to their AC and her CMD; this bonus cannot exceed their class level. (A 1st level master striker with 16 Charisma still gains only a +1 bonus to their armor class from this class feature.) This AC bonus does not stack with any class features which share the same name as it. This bonus to AC applies even against touch attacks or when the master striker is flat-footed. They lose these bonuses when they are immobilized or helpless, when they wear medium or heavy armor, uses a shield, or when they carry a medium or heavy load.
archetype-legendary-samurai-master-strik.martial arts technique (ex): A master striker can use an unarmed strike in place of a one-handed melee slashing weapon to perform iaijutsu techniques and they do not require their weapon to be sheathed at the start of the attack. This ability alters iaijutsu strike.
archetype-legendary-samurai-master-strik.bare knuckle (ex): At 4th level, a master striker treats the critical range of their unarmed strikes as though it was 19-20. This ability replaces sheathe block.

archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.weapon proficiencies: An oni warrior is proficient simple and martial weapons as well as all two-handed melee bludgeoning weapons. This ability alters the legendary samurai’s weapon proficiencies.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.rage (ex): At 1st level, an oni warrior gains the rage class feature as though they were a barbarian of their class level. In addition, they gain a rage power of their choice, being treated as a barbarian of their level of the purpose of which rage powers they can select and for purpose of selecting the Extra Rage Power feat. This ability replaces challenge and sheathe control.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.smashing technique (ex): An oni warrior can use a melee bludgeoning weapon in place of a one-handed melee slashing weapon to perform iaijutsu techniques and they do not require their melee weapon to be sheathed at the start of the attack. This ability alters iaijutsu strike.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.smashing iaijutsu (ex): An oni warrior cannot learn cut iaijutsu techniques. This ability alters iaijutsu technique.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.critical smash (ex): At 4th level, an oni warrior can treat the critical range of any melee bludgeoning weapon they wield as though it was 19-20; doing so reduces its critical multiplier to x2. This ability replaces sheathe block.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.oni transformation (su): At 6th level, whenever an oni warrior is raging, they gain a gore attack as a primary natural weapon which deal 1d8 piercing damage. Whenever an oni warrior makes an iaijutsu strike while raging, they can make a gore attack with a -2 penalty as a free action against a target of their choice, dealing their full strength modifier rather than 1/2. At 11th level, the critical threat range of this gore attack increases to 18-20, and while raging, an oni warrior selects an energy type, gaining resistance to that element equal to their class level. At 16th level, an oni warrior can make two gore attacks which both deal their full strength modifier, although doing so requires a swift action instead of a free action. This ability replaces advanced blade.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.greater rage (ex): At 10th level, an oni warrior gains the greater rage class feature. This ability replaces iaijutsu master.
archetype-legendary-samurai-oni-warrior-.mighty rage (ex): At 20th level, an oni warrior gains the mighty rage class feature. This ability replaces last stand.

archetype-legendary-samurai-ronin-legend.no challenge: A ronin cannot issue a challenge, despite having the challenge ability. However they can exchange it for any ability which would require them to replace challenge. For example, a ronin could select the weapon training alternative class feature or the oni warrior archetype.
archetype-legendary-samurai-ronin-legend.tainted renown (ex): A ronin is treated as though they were both in their social and vigilante identity for the purposes of the renown vigilante talent. This ability alters samurai’s renown.
archetype-legendary-samurai-ronin-legend.honorless tactics (ex): At 2nd level, a ronin gains the Improved Dirty Trick feat, even if they would not meet the prerequisites. At 6th level, they also receive the Greater Dirty Trick feat, even if they would not meet the prerequisites. If the ronin already possesses one of these feats, they can instead select another combat feat. This ability replaces the determined ability of the resolve class feature.
archetype-legendary-samurai-ronin-legend.roguish guile (ex): A ronin can select a rogue talent in place of a social talent. At 10th level, they can also select advanced rogue talents. This ability alters warrior’s grace.
archetype-legendary-samurai-ronin-legend.uncanny dodge (ex): At 4th level, a ronin gains the uncanny dodge class feature. This ability replaces banner.
archetype-legendary-samurai-ronin-legend.improved uncanny dodge (ex): At 10th level, a ronin gains the improved uncanny dodge class feature. This ability replaces greater banner.

archetype-legendary-samurai-samurai-sphe.weapon and armor proficiencies: The samurai spherelord is proficient with all simple weapons and light armor. In addition, if this is this character’s first level in any class, they may select a martial tradition of their choice. This modifies proficiencies.
archetype-legendary-samurai-samurai-sphe.spellcasting: The samurai spherelord may combine spheres and talents to create magical effects. The samurai spherelord is considered a Low-Caster and uses Charisma as their casting ability modifier. ( Note: All casters gain 2 bonus talents and may select a casting tradition the first time they gain the casting class feature.) This replaces challenge, iaijutsu techniques, and kiai arts.
archetype-legendary-samurai-samurai-sphe.spell pool: The samurai spherelord gains a small reservoir of energy they can call on to create truly wondrous effects, called a spell pool. This pool contains a number of spell points equal to their level + their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). This pool replenishes once per day after roughly 8 hours of rest.
archetype-legendary-samurai-samurai-sphe.blended training (ex): A samurai spherelord gains a combat or magic talent every time they gain a level. The samurai spherelord uses their casting ability modifier as their practitioner modifier.

archetype-legendary-samurai-soul-blade-l.spirit weapon (su): At 1st level, a soul blade receives a mundane weapon of their choice, this weapon is treated as broken to all who would use it except the soul blade. While wielding the weapon, its appearance changes to that of a perfectly crafted version of itself, being treated as masterwork by the soul blade. In addition, this spirit weapon houses the soul of the soul blade’s ancestors. A spirit weapon is an intelligent weapon and has the following traits: Intelligence: This is the intelligence score of the spirit weapon. It starts at 9 and increases by 1 for every two levels of the legendary samurai (at 3rd level, 5th level, and so on). Wisdom and Charisma: As the legendary samurai increases in level, so do the Wisdom and Charisma of the spirit weapon. These abilities start at 6 and increase by 1 for every two levels of legendary samurai. Ego: A spirit weapon starts with an ego of 3, and that ego increases as the spiritual weapon becomes more powerful, as per Table 2-1: Spirit Weapon Progression below. In cases where a wielder and the spirit weapon come into conflict, like any intelligent item, a spirit weapon can attempt to exert its dominance (see Intelligent Items). Due to its flexible and powerful nature, a spirit weapon has a nonstandard ego progression. Languages and Skills: A spirit weapon starts with Common as a language. As the spirit weapon increases in Intelligence, it manifests knowledge of languages and arcane lore. Upon reaching an Intelligence of 12, it gains a bonus language of the GM’s choice, and gains 1 rank in Knowledge (arcana). Each time the sword gains a bonus to Intelligence, it gains another language and another rank in Knowledge (arcana). Senses: A spirit weapon is aware of everything around it like a creature that can see and hear. It can be blinded and deafened as if it were a creature. It uses the saving throws of its legendary samurai, even if the legendary samurai is not currently wielding the spirit weapon. This ability replaces challenge and advanced blade. TABLE 2-1: SOUL BLADE PROGRESSION SOUL BLADE CLASS Level ENHANCEMENT BONUS INT WIS/ CHA EGO SPECIAL 1st–2nd +0 9 6 3 Alertness, spiritual weapon strike, telepathy, unbreakable 3rd-4th +1 10 7 5 Spirit store, weapon bond 5th–6th +2 12 8 8 Kiai resonance 7th–8th +2 13 9 10 – 9th–10th +3 14 10 12 Teleport weapon 11th–12th +3 15 11 14 Greater spirit store 13th–14th +4 16 12 16 Spirit drinker 15th–16th +4 17 13 18 – 17th–18th +5 18 14 22 – 19th–20th +5 19 15 24 Bonded mastery
archetype-legendary-samurai-soul-blade-l.soul blade ability descriptions: A spiritual weapon has special abilities (or imparts abilities to its wielder) depending on the wielder’s legendary samurai level. The abilities are cumulative. A spiritual weapon normally refuses to use any of its abilities when wielded by anyone other than its legendary samurai, and acts as a masterwork weapon of its type. Alertness (Ex) While a soul blade is wielding their spiritual weapon, they gain the Alertness feat. Spiritual Weapon Strike (Sp) As a free action, the soul blade can spend 1 spirit, gaining a +1 on attack and damage rolls with their spirit weapon for 1 minute. For every four levels beyond 1st, this bonus increases by +1 (to a maximum of +5 at 17th level). Telepathy (Su) While a soul blade is wielding or carrying their spiritual weapon, they can communicate telepathically with it in a language that the legendary samurai and the spiritual weapon share. Unbreakable (Ex) A spiritual weapon is unable to have the broken status or be destroyed as long as the soul blade is alive. Spirit Store (Su) At 3rd level, a soul blade can imbue their spiritual weapon with 1 spirit as a free action. If they do so, that spirit remains, even if the soul blade is out of combat (this spirit still counts against the maximum spirit a soul blade can possess). While storing this spirit, the soul blade gains the listed enhancement bonus on Table 2-1: Soul Blade progression, and the soul blade can spend this spirit as though they possessed it. The spiritual weapon can hold this spirit for 24 hours before it harmlessly dissipates, and a spiritual weapon can only store 1 spirit at a time. Weapon Bond (Ex) At 3rd level, a spiritual weapon can be enhanced as though its owner possessed the Craft Magical Arms and Armor feat, treating its owner as though they possess whatever spells would be required to enhance it. In addition, a spiritual weapon does not need to have a +1 enhancement bonus to be granted a melee or ranged weapon special ability, but it cannot have a modified bonus ( enhancement bonus plus special ability bonus equivalents) higher than +5. Kiai Resonance (Su) At 5th level, whenever the soul blade spends 1 or more spirit on a kiai art, the next attack made with the spiritual weapon receives a bonus to damage equal to the soul blade’s Charisma modifier. This attack must be made within 1 minute or this bonus is lost. Teleport Weapon (Sp) A soul blade of 9th level or higher can call their spiritual weapon from as far as 1 mile away as a standard action, causing it to instantaneously teleport to their hand. Greater Spirit Store (Ex) At 11th level, a spiritual weapon can store up to 2 spirit. Spirit Drinker (Su) At 13th level, whenever a spiritual weapon confirms a critical hit while in the heat of combat, it gains 1 spirit; if it is already storing 1 spirit, this new spirit replaces the old spirit. Confirming a critical hit on a helpless or unaware creature or on a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the soul blade’s character level does not allow them to gain spirit. Bonded Mastery (Su) At 19th level, if a soul blade is in possession of their spiritual weapon at the start of combat, Form of the Spirit (Sp) At 20th level, a soul blade can spend 2 spirit as a standard action. If they do, they can summon the spirit of their weapon, treating this as summon monster IX. This ability replaces last stand.

archetype-legendary-samurai-steed-lord-l.mount (ex): At 1st level, a steed lord gains a mount as per the cavalier class feature. This ability replaces the unstoppable ability of the resolve class feature.
archetype-legendary-samurai-steed-lord-l.noble steed (ex): At 3rd level, a steed lord’s mount gains a +1 morale bonus to attack rolls made with its natural attacks. At 5th level and every four levels afterwards, this bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. This ability replaces the duty’s call, kiai art.
archetype-legendary-samurai-steed-lord-l.measured gait (ex): At 7th level, as long as the steed lord’s mount is being ridden by the steed lord, it can ignore difficult terrain while charging. At 10th level, the steed lord’s mount no longer needs to be charging to ignore difficult terrain. This ability replaces the duty’s call, charm kiai art.
archetype-legendary-samurai-steed-lord-l.iron steed (ex): At 11th level, as long as a steed lord is riding their mount, their mount gains DR 5/-. This damage reduction stacks with similar damage reduction. This ability replaces the duty’s call, compulsion kiai art.
archetype-legendary-samurai-steed-lord-l.rider’s bond (ex): At 15th level, as long as the steed lord’s mount is above 0 hit points and the steed lord is within 60 feet of it, the steed lord and their mount gain the benefits of the Diehard and Deathless Initiate feats, regardless of if they qualify for them. This ability replaces the duty’s call, possession kiai art.
archetype-legendary-samurai-steed-lord-l.powerful steed (ex): At 19th level, while riding their mount, a steed lord’s steed is treated as one size larger for the purpose of how much damage its natural attacks deal. This does not stack with any other virtual size increases, such as the impact weapon enhancement This ability replaces the duty’s call, mind kiai art.

archetype-legendary-samurai-yojimbo-lege.bonded challenge: Whenever a yojimbo issues a challenge, they can select an ally within 60 feet of themselves, known as their bonded ally. If they do, their bonded ally gains a dodge bonus to their armor class against attacks made by the challenged creature equal to the yojimbo’s Charisma modifier. The yojimbo only deals damage equal to 1/2 their level to the challenged creature. This ability alters challenge.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yojimbo-lege.bonded resolve: A yojimbo can spend spirit to use their resolve and greater resolve class feature on their bonded ally. This ability alters resolve and greater resolve.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yojimbo-lege.guardian’s toughness (ex): At 4th level, whenever a yojimbo issues a bonded challenge, they gain temporary hit points equal to their class level + their Charisma modifier. Whenever an attack made against their bonded ally misses, these temporary hit points are refreshed; but they cannot be refreshed more than once per round. At 9th level, as long as a yojimbo has a bonded challenge in effect, they gain DR / adamantine equal to 1/2 their class level. This ability replaces banner and greater banner.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yojimbo-lege.sentinel’s imposition (ex): At 5th level, whenever an attack would be made against the yojimbo’s bonded ally, if the yojimbo is adjacent to their boned ally, they can spend an immediate action to switch places with their bonded ally, becoming the new target of the attack. If this attack deals damage to them, they gain 2 spirit from their warrior’s guard ability. This ability replaces dragon defense.

archetype-legendary-samurai-yumi-sniper-.weapon proficiencies: A yumi sniper is proficient simple and martial weapons as well as all ranged weapons. This ability alters the legendary samurai’s weapon proficiencies.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yumi-sniper-.ranged acumen (ex): At 1st level, a yumi sniper gains Precise Shot as a bonus feat even if they do not meet the prerequisites and is treated as though they had the Point-Blank Shot feat for the purpose of meeting the prerequisites of feats. This ability replaces sheathe control.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yumi-sniper-.archer’s technique (ex): A yumi sniper can use a ranged weapon in place of a one-handed melee slashing weapon to perform iaijutsu techniques and they do not require their ranged weapon to be sheathed at the start of the attack. This ability alters iaijutsu strike.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yumi-sniper-.archer iaijutsu (ex): A yumi sniper cannot learn cut iaijutsu techniques. This ability alters iaijutsu technique.
archetype-legendary-samurai-yumi-sniper-.split shot (ex): At 10th level, a yumi sniper gains the Rapid Shot feat. If they already possess it, they instead gain a combat feat of their choice. In addition, the yumi can use this feat with an iaijutsu strike, being able to apply any slash technique to both attacks. This ability replaces iaijutsu master.

archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.weapon and armor proficiencies: A shinobi illusionist is not proficient with any armor or shields. Armor sometimes interferes with a shinobi illusionist’s gestures, which can cause her spells with somatic components to fail. This alters the ninja’s armor proficiencies. Class Skills: A shinobi illusionist gains Knowledge (arcana) and Spellcraft as class skills, but not Intimidate and Knowledge (local). This alters the ninja’s skills.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.spellcasting: A shinobi illusionist casts arcane spells from the shinobi illusionist’s spell list, using the magus ’ class spells per day table. The shinobi illusionist’s spell list includes all spells from the illusion school and all spells with the shadow descriptor from every class’ spell list. A shinobi illusionist must choose and prepare her spells ahead of time. She learns, prepares, and casts spells exactly as a wizard does, including adding new spells to her spellbook and gaining two additional spells known (of any level she can cast) each time she gains a ninja level with this archetype.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.magic ki pool (su): A shinobi illusionist cannot spend ki points to perform additional attacks or to increase her speed. Instead, a shinobi illusionist can spend 1 point of ki to add +1 to the DC of the next spell she casts on her turn. In addition, she can spend 1 point of ki to gain a +4 insight bonus on Spellcraft checks for 1 round. This modifies ki pool.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.poison training: A shinobi illusionist doesn’t gain poison use at 1st level. She can take poison use instead of a ninja trick.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.illusion master (su): At 3rd level, the DC to track a shinobi illusionist using the Survival skill increases by +1. In addition, a shinobi illusionist gains a +1 bonus on all saving throws against illusion and shadow spells and effects. Every three levels thereafter, these bonuses increase by 1. This replaces no trace.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.ninja tricks: At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the shinobi illusionist gains a ninja trick. This modifies the normal ninja trick progression.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.spell recall (su): At 4th level, with a swift action the shinobi illusionist can recall any single shinobi illusionist spell that he has already prepared and cast that day by expending a number of points from her ki pool equal to the spell’s level (minimum 1). The spell is prepared again, just as if it had not been cast. This replaces uncanny dodge. A 4th-level shinobi illusionist can select uncanny dodge as a ninja trick.
archetype-ninja-shinobi-illusionist-ninj.improved spell recall (su): At 11th level, whenever the shinobi illusionist recalls a spell with spell recall, she expends a number of points from her ki pool equal to 1/2 the spell’s level (minimum 1). Furthermore, instead of recalling a used spell, as a swift action the shinobi illusionist can prepare a spell of the same level that she has in her spellbook. She does so by expending a number of points from her arcane pool equal to the spell’s level (minimum 1). The shinobi illusionist cannot apply metamagic feats to a spell prepared in this way. The shinobi illusionist does not need to reference her spellbook to prepare a spell in this way. This replaces improved uncanny dodge. A 12th-level shinobi illusionist can select improved uncanny dodge as a ninja master trick.

archetype-ninja-ninja-of-the-five-elemen.elemental mystery: A ninja of the five elements chooses one of the following oracle mysteries: Elemental, Flame, Metal, Stone, Waves, or Wood. At 1st level, ninjas of the five elements can cast the first spell listed as a spell-like ability once per day. At 4th level, they gain the next spell listed, castable once per day as a spell-like ability. Every two levels thereafter, ninjas of the five elements gain the next spell on the list, which they can also cast once per day as a spell-like ability. Furthermore, at 4th and 8th level, a ninja of the five elements selects one revelation from their chosen mystery. The ninja treats their ninja of the five elements level as their oracle level for this revelation. For the purpose of qualifying for feats, this ability counts as both the mystery and the revelation class features. This replaces poison use, uncanny dodge, and improved uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-ninja-of-the-five-elemen.elemental healing (su): At 1st level, a ninja of the five elements can draw energy from the elemental building blocks of the planet to heal themselves and allies. To initiate an elemental healing, a ninja of the five elements must use a standard action and select a number of targets (this can include themselves) equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), all of whom must be within 30 feet of the ninja. The elemental healing cures 1d6 points of damage plus 1d6 points of damage for every two ninja of the five elements levels beyond 1st. A ninja of the five elements can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). This replaces all iterations of sneak attack.
archetype-ninja-ninja-of-the-five-elemen.elemental wisdom: Ninjas of the five elements use their Wisdom score (not Charisma ) to determine the number of points in their ki pool. They also substitute Wisdom for Charisma when a ninja trick, rogue talent, or revelation refers to Charisma or Intelligence. This alters ki pool.
archetype-ninja-ninja-of-the-five-elemen.medicinal touch (ex): At 2nd level, a ninja of the five elements can never select a ninja trick that interacts with sneak attack or poison. Instead, the ninja adds the following options to their list of ninja tricks to choose from: Restore Balance: A ninja of the five elements with this trick can expend 1 ki point and touch a creature as a standard action. The touched creature is cured of the fatigued, sickened, nauseated, blinded, deafened, and staggered conditions or has two points of ability damage restored (as lesser restoration ). A ninja of the five elements can restore balance on themself as an immediate action as soon as they acquire the condition, essentially negating the condition before it can take effect.
archetype-ninja-ninja-of-the-five-elemen.enlightened steps (ex): At 3rd level, a ninja of the five elements gains the light steps class feature earlier than a standard ninja. At 6th level, the ninja’s use of this ability expands. First, a ninja of the five elements can now use light steps either as a full-round action or as a move action. If the ninja of the five elements uses it as a move action, they can move up to their current land speed (which may be enhanced by spending a ki point). Second, a ninja of the five elements can now defy gravity, traversing any surface, including walls, trees, and ceilings (as long as they end their movement on a surface that can support them). During their movement, the ninja of the five elements can change surfaces freely from floor to ceiling to wall, etc. This replaces no trace and alters light steps, but counts as light steps for the purposes of qualifying for feats and ninja tricks.
archetype-ninja-ninja-of-the-five-elemen.ki master (su): At 20th level, a ninja of the five elements gains a bonus revelation from their elemental mystery. Additionally, once per day, a ninja of the five elements can expend 1 ki point when using elemental healing to automatically heal the maximum amount possible without the need to roll. Finally, when expending a ki point to gain an extra attack at their highest base attack bonus, a ninja of the five elements gains two extra attacks instead of one. This replaces hidden master.

archetype-ninja-clan-leader-ninja-archet.deshi (ex): At 1st level, a clan leader gains a special cohort called their deshi. The deshi begins as a 1st level warrior except they also have a 1d6 sneak attack. The deshi does not level up until the clan leader’s 3rd level. At 3rd level, the deshi may swap out their warrior level for a level in ninja. The deshi cannot multi-class until the clan leader’s 7th level. A clan leader also starts gaining followers as if they have the Leadership feat. However, all of their followers must be warriors or ninjas. At 7th level, this transforms into full Leadership as a bonus feat. This includes allowing for more diverse followers. However, their deshi must have levels in ninja equal to at least half of their total levels. This ability replaces all instances of sneak attack.

archetype-ninja-masked-assassin-ninja-ar.ghost step (su): Beginning at 1st level, as a swift action, a masked assassin can become invisible per the spell invisibility for 1 round. This can be done for a number of rounds equal to the masked assassin’s class level per day. This can be ended early as a free action. Additionally, the masked assassin can maintain the invisibility as free action if it was active in the previous round. At 4th level, a masked assassin can become invisible for a number of minutes equal to their class level instead of a number of rounds. At 10th level, a masked assassin may choose to gain the benefit of greater invisibility for a number of rounds equal to their class level instead of the normal invisibility for minutes. At 14th level, a masked assassin instead become ethereal for 1 round per class level instead of invisible. At 20th level, a masked assassin can gain the benefit of greater invisibility for a number of minutes equal to their class level or invisibility for a number of hours equal to their class level. This ability replaces poison use, and the ninja tricks gained at 4th, 10th, 14th, and 20th levels.
archetype-ninja-masked-assassin-ninja-ar.terrifier (ex): Beginning at 1st level, a masked assassin adds 1/2 their class level (minimum 1) to Intimidate checks. This ability replace all instances of no trace.
archetype-ninja-masked-assassin-ninja-ar.terrifying strike (ex): At 4th level, if a masked assassin makes a successful sneak attack, the target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the masked assassin’s class level + their Charisma modifier). On a failure, the masked assassin looks like something out of the target’s nightmares. The target is frightened for 1d4 rounds then shaken for 1 round per class level thereafter. On a successful saving throw, the target is shaken for 1d4 rounds. This is a mindaffecting, emotion, and fear effect. Beginning at 12th level, the fear becomes deadly. If the target fails their Will saving throw, then they must then make a Fortitude save against the same DC, on a failure the target dies of fear as if affected by the phantasmal killer spell. If the target has Hit Dice greater than the masked assassin’s class level, they are immune to the instant death part of this ability and are instead treated as succeeding on their Fortitude save. If the creature dies of fear from this ability, all creatures within 30 feet of the creature who see the attack (not including the initial target, the masked assassin, and their allies) must make Will saves (DC equal to the damage done to the victim + the masked assassin’s Charisma modifier). On a failed save, they are frightened for 1d4 rounds and shaken for 1 round per class level thereafter; on a successful save, they are shaken for 1d4 rounds. At 16th level, if the target fails their Will saving throw, they are panicked for 1d4 rounds then frightened for 1 round per class level thereafter. This ability is usable once per day at 4th level, and one additional time at 10th and 16th levels. This ability replaces uncanny dodge, the ninja trick gained at 12th and 16th levels.
archetype-ninja-masked-assassin-ninja-ar.ghostly sight (su): At 8th level, a masked assassin has a constant see invisibility spell effect. This ability replaces improved uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-masked-assassin-ninja-ar.terrifying cleave (ex): Beginning at 16th level, if a masked assassin reduces a target below 0 hit points with a terrifying strike, whether by the normal damage or the instant death effect, they may make an attack at their highest base attack bonus on another creature within reach. If the target is also subject to a sneak attack, they are also subject to the terrifying strike ability without needing to expend another use. This ability replaces the ninja trick gained at 16th level.
archetype-ninja-masked-assassin-ninja-ar.death in the dark (ex): At 20th level, if a target is killed by the instant death effect of their terrifying strike or reduced under 0 hit points by a sneak attack, a masked assassin regains a number rounds or other duration units of their ghost step ability equal to the Hit Dice of the target, up to their maximum number of rounds per day. This ability replaces hidden master.

archetype-ninja-ninja-guide-ninja-archet.coordination (ex): At 2nd level, a ninja guide gains a +20 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to see or hear their allies and Sense Motive to interpret signs or codes from them. At 10th level, they constantly benefit from the status spell for all allies within 100 feet. This ability replaces the ninja trick gained at 2nd level.
archetype-ninja-ninja-guide-ninja-archet.skill teamwork (ex): At 4th level, a ninja guide grants some competence in skills to their, non-self, allies. All allies within 30 feet gain a +2 competence bonus on Acrobatics, Climb, Escape Artist, Perception, and Stealth. If a ninja guide has 10 ranks in any of the listed skills, the bonus provided increases to +4 for those skills. This ability replaces uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-ninja-guide-ninja-archet.teamwork tracelessness (ex): At 4th level, a ninja guide can provide their no trace bonuses to all allies within 30 feet. This ability replaces the ninja trick gained at 4th level.
archetype-ninja-ninja-guide-ninja-archet.flanking teamwork (ex): At 8th level, when a ninja guide flanks a target, they and all allies who threaten the same target gain a +1 circumstance bonus on their attack rolls against the target. This is in addition to the normal flanking bonuses. This ability replaces improved uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-ninja-guide-ninja-archet.team sneak attack (ex): At 8th level, a ninja guide grants 1/2 of their sneak attack dice to any allies who are flanking the same creature. This cannot increase the ally’s sneak attack dice above the ninja guide’s own. This ability replaces the ninja trick gained at 8th level.
archetype-ninja-ninja-guide-ninja-archet.break away (ex): At 10th level, a ninja guide gains a +4 dodge bonus to AC on any turn in which they do nothing but move. This can be granted to an ally within 30 feet as a swift action for 1 round. This ability replaces the ninja trick gained at 10th level.

archetype-ninja-shadow-warrior-ninja-arc.shadow sneak (ex): A shadow-warrior can make sneak attacks against creatures benefiting from concealment, including total concealment, if the target and the shadow-warrior both have concealment from the same source, such as both being in a dark room. This ability alters sneak attack.
archetype-ninja-shadow-warrior-ninja-arc.shadow-strider (ex): Shadow-warriors gain a bonus to Acrobatics and Climb checks equal to 1/2 their class level. This ability replaces poison use.
archetype-ninja-shadow-warrior-ninja-arc.shadowed footsteps (su): Beginning at 2nd level, a shadow-warrior can make an Acrobatics check to pass through a space occupied by another creature as long as there is an area of shadow adjacent to that creature (whether its own shadow or one cast by a nearby object or creature). The DC for this check is the creature’s CMD. On a success, the shadow-warrior gains 20% concealment against any attack of opportunity incurred as they are briefly wrapped in shadow. This ability replaces no trace and its improvements.
archetype-ninja-shadow-warrior-ninja-arc.shadow dance (su): Beginning at 4th level, a shadowwarrior can travel between shadows as easily as doorways. As a standard action, the shadow-warrior may teleport from one touched shadow (at least half the size of the shadow-warrior) to another shadow within 30 feet plus an additional 5 feet for every two class levels. This ability replaces uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-shadow-warrior-ninja-arc.shadow stabbing (ex): Beginning at 8th level, whenever a shadow-warrior appears adjacent to a creature when using their shadow dance ability, they may make a melee attack against that creature as a swift action. If that attack hits it is considered to meet the requirements for a sneak attack. This ability replaces improved uncanny dodge.

archetype-ninja-unfettered-ninja-ninja-a.unfettered defense (ex): At 1st level, a unfettered ninja gains the AC bonus of a monk of their ninja level. This ability replaces the proficiency with light armor and poison use.

archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.class skills: A clandestine manipulator adds Knowledge (arcana) and Spellcraft to her list of class skills. This alters class skills.
archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.blade in the back (ex): At 1st level, a clandestine manipulator learns to take advantage of unprepared foes, striking them in a vital spot for extra damage. A clandestine manipulator can use this ability when her target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not), or when the clandestine manipulator flanks her target. A clandestine manipulator must declare that she is using this ability before making her attack roll (thus, a failed attack roll ruins the attempt). If a blade in the back attack is successful, the target suffers precision damage equal to +1d6. This damage increases by +1d6 for every 3 levels beyond 1st, to a maximum of +7d6 at 19th level. A clandestine manipulator can attempt a blade in the back attack 3 times per day, plus one additional time per day for every five clandestine manipulator levels, and no more than once per round. This replaces poison use.
archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.manipulative magic: At 1st level, a clandestine manipulator gains the ability to cast arcane spells. A clandestine manipulator’s spell list contains all the spells of the enchantment school from the bard and sorcerer / wizard spell lists up to 6th level, excluding all else. A clandestine manipulator uses the bard spell tables to determine her base daily spell allotment and her spells known, and like a bard, she can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, a clandestine manipulator must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a clandestine manipulator’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the clandestine manipulator’s Charisma modifier. A clandestine manipulator must spend 1 hour conducting mental exercises after getting 8 hours of sleep to prepare her mind to cast spells for the day. This replaces sneak attack and all of its iterations.
archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.ninja tricks: A clandestine manipulator cannot benefit from ninja tricks that enhance or interact with sneak attack unless she has the sneak attack class feature from another class. This alters ninja tricks.
archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.power of persuasion (ex): At 3rd level, a clandestine manipulator can use her bonus in the Profession (con artist) skill in place of her bonus in another skill. When substituting in this way, the clandestine manipulator uses her total Profession skill bonus, including class skill bonus, in place of the substituted skill’s bonus, whether or not she has ranks in that skill. The skills that a clandestine manipulator can use Profession (con artist) to substitute for are: Bluff, Diplomacy, Disguise, Intimidate, Linguistics, and Sense Motive. At 3rd level, a clandestine manipulator chooses two skills from this list for which she can use Profession (con artist) in place of. This choice is permanent and cannot be changed. At 6th level, a clandestine manipulator gains a +1 competence bonus to her Profession (con artist) skill checks. This bonus increases by +1 at 9th level, and every three levels thereafter, to a maximum of +5 at 18th level. This replaces no trace and all of its improvements.
archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.aura of despair (su): At 8th level, a clandestine manipulator gains the wizard’s enchantment school power aura of despair. This aura is activated as a free action. This replaces improved uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-clandestine-manipulator-.sap reserves (su): At 20th level, whenever a clandestine manipulator successfully uses her blade in the back ability, she can sacrifice additional damage dice to apply a penalty to one ability score of the target equal to the number of dice sacrificed for 1 minute. This penalty does not stack with itself and cannot reduce an ability score below 1. This replaces the portion of hidden master that pertains to sneak attack; all other aspects of hidden master remain unchanged.

archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.class skills: A dreamer gains Knowledge (arcana), Knowledge (planes), and Spellcraft, but does not gain Intimidate, Knowledge (nobility), and Perform. This alters class skills.
archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.rejuvenating sleep (ex): A dreamer’s sleep is especially beneficial. At 1st level, a dreamer requires half the amount of sleep that a creature of their kind normally does. Furthermore, beginning in the first encounter after a dreamer has slept, she gains a circumstance bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks equal to half the number of hours she spent sleeping (maximum +4). This bonus lasts for 1 minute per dreamer level or until the encounter is over, whichever comes first. This replaces poison use.
archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.illusive magic: At 1st level, a dreamer gains the ability to cast arcane spells. A dreamer’s spell list contains all the spells of the divination and illusion schools from the sorcerer / wizard’s spell list, excluding all else. A dreamer uses the bard spell tables to determine her base daily spell allotment and her spells known, and like a bard, she can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, a dreamer must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a dreamer’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the dreamer’s Charisma modifier. A dreamer must spend 1 hour daydreaming after getting (the equivalent of) 8 hours of restful sleep to prepare her mind to cast spells for the day. This replaces sneak attack and all of its iterations.
archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.illusion spotter (ex): At 3rd level, a dreamer gains a +2 bonus on saving throws made to see through illusions. At 6th level, whenever a dreamer comes within 10 feet of an illusion, she receives an immediate Will save to notice the illusion for what it really is. This check should be made secretly by the GM. At 12th level, once per day, as a free action, a dreamer can function as though under the effects of true seeing for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). This replaces no trace and all of its improvements.
archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.bed time (su): At 4th level, as a move action, a dreamer can emit a 10-footradius burst centered on herself that causes creatures to become drowsy, moving and reacting sluggishly. Creatures within the burst must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the dreamer’s level + her Charisma modifier) or suffer a -2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, Perception checks, and Reflex and Will saving throws for a number of rounds equal to the dreamer’s Charisma modifier (minimum 1). A successful save reduces the duration to 1 round. At 8th level, this burst extends to 15 feet, and the dreamer can exclude a number of creatures equal to her Charisma modifier from its effects. A dreamer can use this ability once per day, and one additional time at 8th level. This replaces uncanny dodge and improved uncanny dodge.
archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.waking nightmare (sp): A dreamer can cloud the minds of her foes with nightmarish visions. At 6th level, as a standard action, a dreamer can select a target within 60 feet of herself to become frightened for a number of rounds equal to 1 + her CH modifier. On a successful Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the dreamer’s level + her Charisma modifier), the target is shaken instead. At 12th level, the target becomes panicked instead of frightened on a failed save. A dreamer can use this ability once per day, and one additional time per day at 12th level. This replaces light steps.
archetype-ninja-dreamer-ninja-archetype.just a dream (su): At 20th level, once per day, as an immediate action, when a dreamer would be reduced to zero or fewer hit points from a melee attack, she can expend 1 ki point to momentarily shift her body to the dream dimension, avoiding the attack altogether. The dreamer instantly reappears in an unoccupied square of her choosing within 15 feet of her attacker. This replaces the portion of hidden master that pertains to sneak attack; hidden master is otherwise not altered.

archetype-arcanist-urban-arcanist-arcani.find the way (su): At 3rd level, while in an urban environment, the urban arcanist can draw upon her arcane might to find a specific place within the urban environment. By spending 1 point from her arcane reservoir, the urban arcanist can instantly discern the shortest route to any location she can name within the urban environment. She can name a specific location, such as an individual’s residence, or a general location, such as a bakery. If she names a specific location, she learns the most direct route to that location; if she names a generic destination, she learns the route to the nearest such place. This ability replaces the arcanist exploit gained at 3rd level.
archetype-arcanist-urban-arcanist-arcani.urban energies (su): At 7th level, while in an urban environment, the urban arcanist can call upon her connection to a city to unleash more powerful spells. The urban arcanist can expend 1 point from her arcane reservoir; if she does, she treats the caster level of all spells she casts in the next 1 minute as 1 higher than it actually is. If she spends this point from her urban reservoir, her caster level is increased by 2, instead. This ability replaces the arcanist exploit gained at 7th level.
archetype-arcanist-urban-arcanist-arcani.urban tracking (su): At 11th level, the urban arcanist can attempt to locate and follow the movements of an individual within an urban environment. By spending 2 points from her arcane reservoir, the urban arcanist can name a single individual. If that individual is within the same urban environment as the urban arcanist, he must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the urban arcanist’s level + the urban arcanist’s Charisma modifier), or the urban arcanist learns his location and can view him as though with the spell scrying. This effect lasts so long as the target remains within the same urban environment as the urban arcanist, for up to 10 minutes per level. She can suppress or resume this ability as a swift action. This ability replaces the exploit gained at 11th level.
archetype-arcanist-urban-arcanist-arcani.animate buildings (ex): At 19th level, the urban arcanist can use her magic to command the very city to fight for her. By spending 4 or more points from her arcane reservoir, she can animate a number of buildings equal to her Charisma modifier. For each building animated in this way, she must expend an additional 4 points from her arcane reservoir. Buildings animated in this way become Colossal animated objects with an additional number of construction points equal to the arcanist’s Charisma modifier for 1 minute. The animated buildings obey the urban arcanist’s spoken commands. The buildings are allowed a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the urban arcanist’s level + the urban arcanist’s Charisma modifier) to avoid being animated. Buildings with people in them make this save with the highest saving throw bonus among occupants. This ability replaces the arcanist exploit gained at 19th level.

archetype-arcanist-occult-exploiter-arca.arcane reservoir: Each day, when preparing spells, the occult exploiter’s arcane reservoir fills with raw magical energy, gaining a number of points equal to 3 + 1/4 her arcanist level. Otherwise, this ability functions as a standard arcanist’s arcane reservoir. This ability alters the arcane reservoir class feature.
archetype-arcanist-occult-exploiter-arca.bind spirit: An occult exploiter may seal pacts with otherworldly entities known as spirits. In order to summon a spirit, the occult exploiter must learn the spirit’s ceremony, constellation, personality, and seal by completing its four Knowledge Tasks; see Researching the Spirit. An occult exploiter begins play having completed all four Knowledge Tasks for one 1stlevel spirit of her choice that belongs to her chosen constellation (see tunneled lore below). Each day, an occult exploiter may bind one spirit to her soul using pact magic. This spirit’s level may not exceed the occult exploiter’s maximum spirit level, which is limited to 1st-level spirits at 1st level. At 4th level and every three arcanist levels thereafter, the occult exploiter’s maximum spirit level increases by 1, to a maximum of 6th-level spirits at 16th level. An occult exploiter’s binder level is equal to her level. The DC to resist an occult exploiter’s supernatural powers is equal to 10 + 1/2 the occult exploiter’s binder level + the occult exploiter’s Charisma modifier. This ability replaces the arcanist’s 1st-level exploit.
archetype-arcanist-occult-exploiter-arca.diminished spellcasting: An occult exploiter can prepare one fewer spell at each spell level (including cantrips) than is usual for an arcanist (minimum 0), as presented on Table: Arcanist Spells Prepared.
archetype-arcanist-occult-exploiter-arca.tunneled lore: At 1st level, an occult exploiter chooses one constellation. She may only seal pacts with starless spirits and spirits belonging to her chosen constellation. All other constellations are barred to her.
archetype-arcanist-occult-exploiter-arca.binder secret: Beginning at 3rd level, an occult exploiter may select a binder secret in place of an exploit. The occult exploiter’s level stacks with any pactmaker levels she possesses for the purpose of meeting the prerequisites for binder secrets. This replaces the arcanist exploit the occult exploiter gives up for this binder secret.

archetype-arcanist-divinist-arcanist-arc.divine spellcasting: A divinist is a divine spellcaster and uses the cleric / oracle spell list instead of the wizard / sorcerer spell list. The divinist uses her Wisdom score, rather than her Intelligence score, to determine which levels of spells she can cast, her spells’ save DC, and how many spells she can cast per day. However, she has not automatically access to every spell in her list, as a legendary cleric. Rather, she must learn spells and transcribe them into her prayer book. She can’t prepare any spell not recorded in her prayer book, except for read magic (which all arcanists can prepare from memory). A divinist begins play with a prayer book containing all 0-level cleric / oracle spells plus three 1st-level spells of her choice. The divinist also selects a number of additional 1st-level spells equal to her Wisdom modifier to add to the prayer book. At each new level, she gains two new spells of any spell level or 5 levels that she can cast (based on her new arcanist level) for her prayer book. At any time, a divinist can also add spells found in scrolls, divine spellbooks, or other divinists’ prayer books to her own (see Divine Magical Writings).This ability alters the spells and spellbooks class features. Orisons: A divinist can prepare a number of orisons, or 0-level divine spells, each day as per the arcanist’s spells prepared table. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume spell slots. As with her other spells, these spells are not expended when cast. Exploits: A divinist has no access to the following exploits: arcane discovery, bloodline development, familiar, school understanding. A divinist gains access to the following arcanist exploits:
archetype-arcanist-divinist-arcanist-arc.divine tampering (ex): Sometimes the deities feel disturbed by someone borrowing their power without permission. The divinist chooses one oracle curse, using her character level as his effective oracle level when determining the effects of this curse. If an oracle curse would add spells to the oracle’s list of spells known, the divinist instead adds those spells to her spell list as well as to her prayer book. Domain Meditation: The divinist can select one deity with an alignment within one step of her own, and one cleric domain that deity grants (druidic domains included). The divinist gains one domain power as though she were a 1st-level cleric, using her Charisma modifier in place of her Wisdom modifier for this power. The power must be one gained at 1st level and is limited in its use per day to 3 + the divinist’s Charisma modifier. As a swift action, the divinist can expend 1 point from her arcane reservoir to bolster her meditation, allowing her to treat her arcanist level as her cleric level for the purpose of using this power for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). During this time, she also gains use of any other abilities gained at 1st level for her selected domain (except for domain-granted familiars). She does not gain any other abilities when using this exploit in this way, such as those gained at 8th level. If the divinist already has access to domains (or gains it later), taking this exploit instead allows her arcanist levels to stack with the levels of the class that granted them when determining the powers and abilities of her domains. Mysteric Initiation: The divinist selects one oracle mystery upon taking this exploit. The divinist gains one revelation from that mystery as though she were a 1st-level oracle. As a swift action, the divinist can expend 1 point from her arcane reservoir to bolster her latent connection to divine forces, allowing her to treat her level as her oracle level for the purpose of using this ability, which lasts for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). She does not gain any other abilities when using this exploit in this way, such as an oracle’s curse. If the arcanist already has access to revelations (or gains it later), taking this exploit instead allows her arcanist levels to stack with the levels of the class that granted her access to revelations when determining the powers and abilities of her revelations.
archetype-arcanist-divinist-arcanist-arc.personalized channel (su): The divinist selects one feat that alters the channel energy ability to gain as a bonus feat. She can channel energy as a 1st-level cleric only to use the selected feat. As a swift action, the divinist can expend 1 point from her arcane reservoir to treat her level as her cleric level for the purpose of using this ability for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). The divinist can take other feats to add to this ability, such as Improved Channeling, but not feats that alter this ability, such as Alignment Channel.
archetype-arcanist-divinist-arcanist-arc.spirit animal (ex): A divinist with this exploit can acquire a spirit animal as the shaman class feature, using her class level as her shaman level to determine any of the statistics and abilities of the spirit animal. The divinist must select one shaman spirit upon taking this exploit; her spirit animal gains the ability of that spirit. If the divinist receives a spirit animal or familiar from another class, her levels stack with the levels from that class when determining the spirit animal’s statistics and abilities.
archetype-arcanist-divinist-arcanist-arc.spiritual contract (ex): The divinist can strike a temporary pact with spirits. She gains the Spirit Talker feat as a bonus feat and can use the granted hex as a shaman or witch of her same level, even if she has no access to hexes from other sources. She must meet the level prerequisites of the feat.

archetype-arcanist-magical-tinkerer-arca.trade tradition: If this is this character’s first level in any class, the magical tinkerer may select a trade tradition of her choice, and have an adroit trade rank (regardless of her skill ranks per level). This replaces the arcanist’s normal class skills.
archetype-arcanist-magical-tinkerer-arca.magengineer: At 1st level, the magical tinkerer gains the Spellhacking sphere as a bonus sphere. She can use Spellcraft instead of Use Magic Device as the associated skill for the Spellhacking sphere. The magical tinkerer can expend 1 point from her arcane reservoir to gain a +1 bonus on a skill check to hack magic or to create a mishap. She can expend no more than 1 point from her reservoir on a given skill check in this way. This replaces the arcanist exploit gained at 1st level.
archetype-arcanist-magical-tinkerer-arca.gimmicks: Whenever the magical tinkerer would gain an arcanist exploit, she may instead choose to gain a single skill talent. A magical tinkerer may not exchange an exploit if he possesses an archetype that would alter or replace the exploit gained at that level.

archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.umbral sorcery (su): At 1st level, you can expend 1 point from your arcane reservoir to add the darkness descriptor to a spell you prepare that affects an area. The effect created by that spell does not shed light, further all other sources of illumination within its area are reduced by one step for a number of rounds equal to the spell’s level. Multiple spells cast with this ability that affect the same area increase the duration of this decreased illumination within overlapping areas of effect but do not further decrease illumination. You cannot use this ability when casting a spell with the light descriptor. This replaces the arcanist exploit gained at 1st level.
archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.darkvision (ex): You gain darkvision 30 feet; if you already have darkvision, the range of your darkvision increases by 30 feet. You may select this exploit more than once. The effects stack.
archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.dark scholar (ex): You may add any one of the following spells to your list of spells known, plus one additional spell every 2 levels thereafter: 1st -dancing darkness, shadowtrap; 2nd -dark whispers, darkness, darkvision, shadow anchor; 3rd -darkvision (communal), shadow mind; 4th -darkvision (greater), deeper darkness, masochistic shadow, shadow barbs, shadow projection, shadow step, shadowy haven; 5th -darkvault, vampiric shadow shield; 6th -shadow walk; 7th -hungry darkness. In addition, you can prepare one additional spell per day of each level you can cast, provided the additional spells you prepare have the darkness descriptor. This can include spells you have prepared using umbral sorcery.
archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.shadow fade (su): Creatures you summon (including with shadow conjuration ) may fade into shadow as a move action, gaining total concealment (or concealment, against foes with darkvision ). When using this ability, they may attempt Stealth checks to hide even if being directly observed. They may not use this ability in areas of bright light.
archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.summon shadow (sp): You can expend 1 point from your arcane reservoir to summon a shadow to serve you for a number of minutes equal to your arcanist level. This shadow is treated as a monster summoned with a summon monster spell. If you use this ability when you already have a summoned shadow present, the previous shadow vanishes when the new shadow appears. If you are at least 15th level, you can expend 3 points from your arcane reservoir to summon 1 greater shadow rather than a shadow. If you are at least 19th level, you can expend 5 points from your arcane reservoir to summon a nightwing rather than a shadow.
archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.shadow ascendant (su): You gain a +2 bonus on caster level checks and increase save DCs by 2 when you cast spells you cast with the darkness or shadow descriptor. Spells with the light descriptor cannot be used to counter or negate such spells and do not suppress their darkness in overlapping areas of effect unless their caster level exceeds yours.
archetype-arcanist-penumbral-arcanist-ar.impenetrable shadow (su): At 20th level, darkvision, low-light vision, divinations (including true seeing ), and spells with the light descriptor (including searing light ) cannot detect, penetrate, or function within the area of any darkness or shadow spell of equal or higher level that you cast, unless their caster level is higher than yours. A mythic spell can function normally if the caster’s mythic tier is higher than yours. This replaces magical supremacy.

archetype-brawler-madcap-brawler-archety.madcap training (ex): At 1st level, you gain a vigilante talent of your choice, using your brawler level as your effective vigilante level. For the purposes of using these talents, you are always considered to be in your vigilante identity. You gain another vigilante talent at 3rd level and every four levels thereafter. This feature replaces martial flexibility.
archetype-brawler-madcap-brawler-archety.martial flexibility (ex): At 6th level, you can use a move action to gain the benefit of a combat feat you don’t possess. This effect lasts for 1 minute. You must meet the chosen feat’s prerequisites. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 1/2 your brawler level. You can use this ability again before the duration expires in order to replace your previously chosen combat feat with another choice. If a combat feat has a daily use limitation (such as Stunning Fist ), any uses of that combat feat while using this ability count toward that feat’s daily limit. At higher levels, when you gain multiple feats through this ability, you can use those feats to meet the prerequisites of other feats you gain with this ability. Doing so means you cannot replace a feat currently fulfilling another’s prerequisite without also replacing those feats that require it. Each individual feat selected counts toward your daily uses of this ability. At 10th level, you can use this ability to gain the benefit of two combat feats at the same time. You can select one feat as a swift action or two feats as a move action. At 14th level, you can use this ability to gain the benefit of three combat feats at the same time. You can select one feat as a free action, two feats as a swift action, or three feats as a move action. At 17th level, you can use this ability to gain the benefit of one combat feat as an immediate action or three combat feats as a swift action. At 20th level, you can use this ability to gain the benefit of any number of combat feats as a swift action. Each feat selected counts toward your daily uses of this ability, and can be used as a prerequisite for any of the other feats. This feature replaces maneuver training and knockout.

archetype-brawler-mage-masher-brawler-ar.dispelling strike (su): A mage masher’s unarmed strikes are able to break not only her opponent’s bones, but also their spells. Whenever a mage masher makes an unarmed strike, she may choose to make it a dispelling strike. She must declare that she is using this ability before the attack is made, and if the attack misses, the use is wasted. If the attack hits, the target suffers damage as normal, and the mage masher may attempt to dispel a single spell effect that the target is currently affected by. The mage masher can specify which spell effect to target, if she is aware of them. Otherwise, the attempt affects the spell with the highest spell level. If two or more effects are tied for spell level, determine randomly between them. The mage masher makes a dispel check (1d20 + the mage masher’s class level vs. DC 11 + the spell’s caster level ). If the check is successful, the spell effect is dispelled, as though with dispel magic. At 6th level, the mage masher can select a second spell effect to dispel each time she uses this ability. She makes only a single dispel check and compares the result to the DC for each of the two spell effects. At 10th level, the mage masher gains a +4 bonus on all dispel checks made with this ability. At 12th level, the mage masher can select a third spell effect to dispel each time she uses this ability. The mage masher can use this ability a number of times each day equal to 3 + 1/2 her class level. At 20th level, she can use this ability at will, and all unarmed strikes that she makes are automatically affected by this ability, unless she chooses not to use it. This ability replaces the martial flexibility class feature.
archetype-brawler-mage-masher-brawler-ar.shattering strike (su): Beginning at 16th level, the mage masher gains the ability to deliver a special shattering strike, which temporarily destroys magical protections the target may be benefitting from. As a standard action, the mage masher makes a single melee attack with her unarmed strike at her full base attack bonus. If the attack hits, the target loses any deflection bonus to AC he may possess for one minute. Additionally, if the target is currently benefitting from an armor, natural armor, profane, sacred, or shield bonus to AC that is the result of a spell, spell-like ability, supernatural ability, or magic item, he loses the benefit of that bonus for one minute as well. This does not apply to the armor bonus granted by a suit of magic armor, or the shield bonus granted by a magic shield, but does apply to other magic items that grant such bonuses, such as a pair of bracers of armor. This ability replaces the awesome blow class feature.
archetype-brawler-mage-masher-brawler-ar.improved shattering strike (su): At 20th level, whenever a mage masher successfully uses her shattering strike class feature, the target suffers an amount of additional damage equal to 2d6 per point of AC bonus suppressed by the ability (to a maximum of 10d6 additional damage, for 5 points of armor, deflection, natural armor, profane, sacred, or shield bonus to AC negated by the attack). This ability replaces the improved awesome blow class feature.

archetype-brawler-knife-fighter.showmanship: At 1st level, the knife-fighter gains Perform (Cha) as a class skill, but loses Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int).
archetype-brawler-knife-fighter.knife mastery (ex): At 1st level, the knife-fighter gains the benefits of the close weapon mastery ability, but only with daggers and punching daggers. When wielding a dagger or punching dagger, she uses the brawler’s standard unarmed strike damage instead of the base damage for that weapon (for example, a 5th-level Medium knife-fighter wielding a punching dagger deals 1d8 points of damage instead of the weapon’s normal 1d4). When attacking with unarmed strikes (and not a dagger), the knife-fighter uses the damage of a brawler four levels lower (i.e., to a minimum of 1st level, so a 4th-level Medium knife-fighter deals only 1d6 damage rather than 1d8 with her unarmed strikes). This ability modifies unarmed strike and close weapon mastery.
archetype-brawler-knife-fighter.pierce armor (ex): Starting at 4th level, once per day the knife-fighter can make a lightning-fast strike with a dagger or punching dagger, carefully aimed in such a way as to slide through a vulnerable part of her enemy’s armor or defenses. She must announce this intent before making her attack roll. As a standard action, the knife-fighter makes a melee touch attack against a target. If this attack hits, the target suffers 1d4 bleed damage in addition to the attack’s normal damage. At 10th level, the knife-fighter may use this ability twice per day; at 16th level, she may use it three times per day. This ability replaces knockout.
archetype-brawler-knife-fighter.brawler’s strike (ex): Starting at 5th level, the knife-fighter’s brawler’s strike feature applies to daggers and punching daggers, but not to her unarmed strikes.
archetype-brawler-knife-fighter.a thousand little cuts (ex): At 16th level, the knife-fighter can unleash a flurry of quick jabs with her daggers that literally cover her enemy in gaping wounds. When using the brawler’s flurry ability, every successful hit she scores with a dagger or punching dagger causes a cumulative 1d4 bleed damage. This ability replaces awesome blow.
archetype-brawler-knife-fighter.bloodletting (ex): At 20th level, the knife-fighter can explode into a tornado of flashing daggers. As a full-round action, she may use a dagger or punching dagger to make one melee attack at her highest attack bonus against each enemy within 10 feet. Each successful hit during this action also causes 1d4 bleed damage. This ability replaces improved awesome blow.

archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.breathbound (ex): A breath savant must have the draconic breath weapon racial trait as well as a bite attack to take this archetype.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.breath’s fury (su): At 1st level, a breath savant gains the Enigmatic Origin feat regardless of her character level. The damage die of the breath savant’s breath weapon increases as shown on Table 2-1: Breath Weapon Damage; dealing the amount of damage listed at each given level (eg; a 4th level breath savant’s breath weapon would deal 2d8 + her Constitution modifier damage, and a 20th level breath savant’s breath weapon would deal 12d10 + her Constitution modifier damage). The breath savant’s breath weapon cannot benefit from the Powerful Breath Weapon feat. Whenever a feat would reduce the damage die of the breath savant’s breath weapon, it uses this table to determine the reduced damage die until it reduced to 1d6, afterwards using the method listed in the breath feats section. This ability replaces unarmed strike.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.mutable breath (su): In addition to being able to gain a combat feat, a breath savant may decide to change the type of damage her breath weapon deals. Doing so is treated as gaining a single combat feat for the purposes of this ability, making the change permanent until they again change her breath weapon ’s damage type. A breath savant also treats all feats with the [breath] tag as combat feats for the purposes of which feats she can select with this ability and with her bonus combat feats. This ability alters martial flexibility and bonus combat feats.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.melee breath (su): At 2nd level, a breath savant gains the Unbound Breath Weapon and Combat Breath Weapon feats, even if she does not meet the prerequisites for them. At 6th level, whenever the breath savant uses an attack action, she may make an additional melee attack with a -3 penalty. At 12th level, she may make a second additional melee attack with a -6 penalty. At 18th level, she may make a third additional melee attack with a -9 penalty. These attacks must be made with a natural weapon. This ability replaces brawler’s flurry.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.consistent breath (ex): At 4th level, a breath savant gains the Flowing Breath feat. If she already possesses this feat, she may instead select a breath feat for which she qualifies. This ability replaces maneuver training.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.dragon scales (ex): At 4th level, a breath savant gains a +1 natural armor bonus. This natural armor bonus increases by 1 at 9th, 13th, and 18th levels. This ability replaces AC bonus.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.torrent breath (ex): At 4th level, once per day a breath savant may decide to make her breath weapon a torrent breath weapon. Doing this causes all damage from her breath weapon to be maximized and all associated saving throws gain a +2 to their DCs. At 9th level and every five levels thereafter, the breath savant may use this ability 1 additional time per day. This ability replaces knockout.
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.fang strike (ex): At 5th level, a breath savant’s natural attacks are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. At 9th level, her natural attacks also treated as cold iron and silver for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. At 12th level, she chooses one alignment component: chaotic, evil, good, or lawful; her natural attacks also counts as this alignment for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. (This alignment component cannot be the opposite of the breath savant’s actual alignment, such as a good breath savant choosing evil strikes.) At 17th level, her natural attacks are also treated as an adamantine weapon for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction and bypassing hardness. This ability alters brawler’s strike. Table 5: Breath Weapon Damage (Breath Savant) Level Breath Weapon Damage 1-3 1d6 4-7 1d8 8-11 1d10 12-15 2d6 16-19 2d8 20 2d10
archetype-brawler-breath-savant-brawler-.razor fang (ex): At 5th level, a savant’s damage with their bite attack increases. When attacking with her bite attack, she uses the base damage for her breath weapon instead of the base damage for her bite attack (for example, a 5th-level breath savant attacking with their bite attack deals 1d8 damage rather than 1d6). If her bite attack would normally deal more damage than this amount, its damage is unchanged. This ability does not affect any other aspect of her bite attack. This ability replaces close weapon mastery.

archetype-brawler-the-deckfighter.defender’s flurry (ex): At 2nd level, the deckfighter can perform a defender’s flurry. This ability works like brawler’s flurry except that a deckfighter can use defender’s flurry only with any combination of one-handed improvised melee weapons or one-handed light melee weapons with which she is proficient. She can also use a cutlass in one hand along with the other allowable weapons. A deckfighter can substitute any attack during a flurry with a dirty trick or disarm maneuver. This ability changes brawler’s flurry. Watchstander’s Vigilance: At 2nd level, the deckfighter gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to notice another ship’s attempt to pursue or board. She also gains a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative when an enemy crew boards the deckfighter’s ship. This ability replaces the bonus combat feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-brawler-the-deckfighter.into the drink (ex): At 4th level, a deckfighter gains a +2 circumstance bonus on bull rush combat maneuvers when aboard a ship. If she does not have the Improved Bull Rush feat, her bull rush attempts still provoke attacks of opportunity. If a foe is adjacent to the edge of a ship, the deckfighter does not consider a ship’s rail or any solid object up to four feet high as a wall or obstacle when determining whether she can perform a bull rush against that foe. Deckfighters often use this ability to push boarders into the sea. Her bonus to bull rush maneuvers increases to +4 at 10th level and +6 at 16th level. This ability replaces knockout.
archetype-brawler-the-deckfighter.improvised strike (ex): At 5th level, the deckfighter’s familiarity with improvised weapons allows her to use them against supernatural defenses. This ability works like, and otherwise replaces, brawler’s strike, except it applies to improvised weapons rather than unarmed strikes.
archetype-brawler-the-deckfighter.lucky tankard (ex): At 5th level, the deckfighter chooses a favorite improvised weapon. This must be a single, specific item she owns. This item can be temporarily enhanced with alchemical items or spell effects like weapon blanch or magic weapon as if it were an actual weapon. It can’t be permanently made into a magic weapon. While this only works for the deckfighter who owns the item (it acts like an ordinary object for anyone else), the effect’s duration continues normally even if the deckfighter drops or stows the item. However, if she uses her improvised weapon master ability to change her item’s damage type to qualify for a spell like keen edge, the effect is dismissed as soon as she stops spending swift actions to change the damage type. If she loses her lucky item permanently, she can choose a new one 24 hours later. This ability replaces close weapon Mastery.
archetype-brawler-the-deckfighter.deck the swabs (ex): At 16th level, the deckfighter gains the brawler’s awesome blow ability, except it applies only when she is wielding an improvised weapon or boarding pike. Her bonus from her into the drink ability also applies to her awesome blow combat maneuvers. At 20th level, she can use awesome blow against a creature of any size, but she may not attempt to confirm critical hits. This ability modifies awesome blow and improved awesome blow.

archetype-brawler-occult-bruiser-brawler.bind spirit: An occult bruiser may seal pacts with otherworldly entities known as spirits. In order to summon a spirit, the occult bruiser must learn the spirit’s ceremony, constellation, personality, and seal by completing its four Knowledge Tasks. An occult bruiser begins play having completed all four Knowledge Tasks for one 1st-level spirit of her choice. Each day, an occult bruiser may bind one spirit to her soul using pact magic; see Performing a Pact Ritual in Chapter 3. This spirit’s level may not exceed the occult bruiser’s maximum spirit level, which is limited to 1st-level spirits at 1st level. At 4th level and every three brawler levels thereafter, the occult bruiser’s maximum spirit level increases by 1, to a maximum of 6th-level spirits at 16th level. An occult bruiser’s binder level is equal to her level. The DC to resist an occult bruiser’s supernatural powers is equal to 10 + 1/2 the occult bruiser’s binder level + the occult bruiser’s Charisma modifier. This ability replaces martial training.
archetype-brawler-occult-bruiser-brawler.occult flexibility (su): An occult bruiser can take a move action to gain one minor granted ability belonging to a spirit whose Knowledge Tasks she has completed and that she isn’t currently bound to. While doing so, she is forced to show the physical sign and personality influence of any spirits whose granted abilities she gains while using this ability. This effect lasts 1 minute, but any penalties accrued from disobeying a personality influence imparted onto the binder using this ability remains for 24 hours, as usual for such penalties. The occult bruiser may use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + 1/2 her brawler level (minimum 1). The occult bruiser can use this ability again before the duration expires in order to replace the previous granted ability with another choice. If a granted ability has a daily use limitation, any uses of that granted ability while using this ability count towards that granted ability’s daily limit. At 6th level, an occult bruiser can tap into greater occult power when she uses occult flexibility.
