archetype-witchwarper-armiger-archetype.armiger prowesses: The following armiger prowesses complement the adaptive pilot but may be selected by all armigers unless otherwise specified.
archetype-witchwarper-armiger-archetype.mech aficionado: The armiger gains one of the following feats as a bonus feat: Biomech Pilot*, Boon Mech*, Extra Mech Enhancement*, Mech Piloting*, Midshipman’s Training*, Psicrystal Affinity, Psi-Core Upgrade*, Remote Legion*, Remote Piloting*, Skill Focus, Technologist*, Vehicle Expert*, or Wild Talent. The armiger must meet prerequisites for these feats as normal. This prowess may be taken any number of times, each time selecting another feat.
archetype-witchwarper-armiger-archetype.pilot’s change (ex): Whenever the armiger draws a customized weapon, she may immediately slot that weapon into her mech. If her mech has the transformation enhancement, she may transform the mech as part of the action to draw a customized weapon.

archetype-slayer-ebon-blade-slayer-arche.weapon and armor proficiencies: The ebon blade can cast ninja spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, an ebon blade wearing medium armor, heavy armor, or a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. A multiclass ebon slayer still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.
archetype-slayer-ebon-blade-slayer-arche.spell casting: The slayer casts arcane spells as a ninja, although they must use a spellbook in place of tattoos and cannot ignore spell components. Slayers use Intelligence to determine which spells they can cast and bonus spells received from a high casting ability score. This ability replaces the track class feature, the 6th and 12th level increases to sneak attack die, and the 4th, 10th, and 16th level slayer talents.

archetype-slayer-rustworn-hunter-slayer-.weapon and armor proficiencies: In addition to normal proficiencies, a rustworn hunter is proficient with heavy armor as well as all firearms and siege weapons. This replaces the slayer’s normal proficiencies.
archetype-slayer-rustworn-hunter-slayer-.delayed study: A rustworn hunter does not gain the studied target class feature until 5th level, and the bonus from studied target is always one less than it would be for normal slayers. This alters studied target.
archetype-slayer-rustworn-hunter-slayer-.armored blending (ex): At 6th level, a rustworn hunter has learned to adapt to stalking prey while heavily armored. He does not suffer any armor check penalties on Stealth checks. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 6th level.
archetype-slayer-rustworn-hunter-slayer-.wasteland sentinel (ex): At 12th level, a rustworn hunter can use their armor to insulate themselves from environmental threats. While wearing heavy armor, the rustworn hunter gains fire, cold, and acid resistance equal to his rustworn hunter level. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 12th level.

archetype-slayer-sicarius-slayer-archety.spellcasting: Starting at 4th level, a sicarius is able to cast a limited number of spells. The sicarius is a spontaneous caster, using the bloodrager’s spells per day and spells known. He draws his spells from the inquisitor spell list, and Wisdom is his casting stat. This replaces the slayer talents gained at 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.
archetype-slayer-sicarius-slayer-archety.relentless (ex): At 13th level, the sicarius can travel for an extended period of time without rest. The sicarius (and his mount, if he has one) can walk 16 hours in a day of travel without it being considered a forced march, but at the end of that day, he must attempt a DC 15 Fortitude saving throw. If he fails, he can travel for 8 hours the following day, and he (as well as his mount, if he has one) is fatigued for the following 24 hours. If he succeeds at the saving throw, he can use this ability again the following day. The DC of the Fortitude saving throw increases by 2 for every additional day the sicarius has been traveling for more than 8 hours. The sicarius does not need to attempt a separate saving throw for his mount. After the sicarius rests for 24 hours, the saving throw DC resets to 15. This replaces slayer’s advance. The sicarius can still get slayer’s advance by selecting it as an advanced slayer talent.
archetype-slayer-sicarius-slayer-archety.slayer talents: A sicarius has access to the following new slayer talents:
archetype-slayer-sicarius-slayer-archety.lesser inquisition: The sicarius gains the 1st-level power of one inquisition granted from his deity or philosophy.
archetype-slayer-sicarius-slayer-archety.vampiric focus (su): The sicarius gains one vampiric focus of his choice from the vampire hunter base class. A sicarius has access to the following new advanced talents: Greater Inquisition: The sicarius gains the higher-level power granted by the inquisition he selected with the lesser inquisition talent. The sicarius must be at least 8th level and have the lesser inquisition talent in order to select this one.
archetype-slayer-sicarius-slayer-archety.improved vampiric focus (su): The sicarius gains a second vampiric focus from the vampire hunter base class. The sicarius must have the vampiric focus talent in order to select this one.

archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.infiltration specialist (ex): A shadow commando adds 1/2 his level (minimum 1) to Stealth checks made while he is being observed. This ability replaces the track class feature.
archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.stealth coordination (ex): At 2nd level, a shadow commando is able to direct his allies to follow his lead while attempting to go unseen. Allies within 30 feet of the shadow commando gain the benefit of the shadow commando’s infiltration specialist class feature. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 2nd level.
archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.nonlethal takedown (ex): At 3rd level, a shadow commando can strike unseen in order to cripple or take down his foes. If the shadow commando attacks the target of his studied combat while unobserved by that target, he may choose to have the attack deal nonlethal damage. If he does, the target must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the shadow commando’s level + the shadow commando’s Intelligence modifier) or be staggered for 1d6 rounds. At 6th level, the shadow commando may choose to have the target become dazed for 1d6 rounds, instead. At 9th level, the shadow commando may choose to have the target become stunned for 1d4 rounds, instead. At 12th level, the shadow commando may choose to have the target become paralyzed for 1 round, instead. At 15th level, the shadow commando may choose to have the target fall unconscious until awakened, instead. At 18th level, the shadow commando may choose to have the target suffer an additional amount of nonlethal damage equal to her maximum hit points, instead. Additionally, the shadow commando never suffers a penalty to attack rolls for choosing to deal nonlethal damage. At 5th level, the shadow commando can attempt a nonlethal takedown against the target of his studied combat if the target is denied her Dexterity bonus to AC. He may only make one such attack against that creature each day. At 10th level, and every 5 levels thereafter, he may make an additional nonlethal take down against each target of his studied combat. This ability replaces the sneak attack class feature.
archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.stealthy armor (ex): At 10th level, a shadow commando has mastered the art of altering armor to be less cumbersome for stealth. By spending 1 hour and 100 gp per point of armor check penalty a suit of armor possesses, a shadow commando can modify a suit of armor to be stealthier, eliminating its armor check penalty to Stealth checks. The armor’s armor check penalty still applies normally for all other skills. The armor loses this benefit if it ever gains the broken condition. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 10th level.
archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.fast stealth (ex): At 11th level, a shadow commando suffers no penalty for moving at full speed while using the Stealth skill, and suffers only 1/2 the normal penalty for using Stealth while running (this effect is cumulative with other effects that reduce the penalty of Stealth for running, and is applied after any other effects, rounding down). This ability replaces the swift tracker class feature.
archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.quarry (ex): At 14th level, a shadow commando gains the quarry ability as normal; however, if his quarry is knocked unconscious or otherwise eliminated from an encounter, he may select a new quarry after a period of 1 minute has passed. At 17th level, he can immediately designate a new quarry if his quarry is knocked unconscious or otherwise taken out of an encounter. This ability modifies the quarry class feature.
archetype-slayer-shadow-commando-slayer-.shadow striker (ex): At 20th level, a shadow commando can dispatch his foes with the greatest of ease, rendering them unconscious and helpless before his fury. Any attack a shadow commando makes against the target of his studied combat is considered a nonlethal takedown, even if the target is aware of him. This ability replaces the master slayer class feature.

archetype-slayer-bow-master-slayer-arche.close archery (ex): At 2nd level, a bow master is ready to fight in tight quarters and can make a ranged attack in melee with a bow without provoking attacks of opportunity against a studied target. At 6th level, the bow master gains Snap Shot as a bonus feat, usable with any bow they are wielding. At 10th level this becomes Improved Snap Shot. The bow master need not meet the prerequisites of either bonus feat. This ability replaces slayer talents gained at 2nd, 6th and 10th levels.
archetype-slayer-bow-master-slayer-arche.archer’s sneak attack (ex or su): Beginning with 3rd level, bow master’s sneak attack deals damage in d8s rather than d6s when using a bow. Sneak attacks with all other weapons use d4s instead. This ability alters sneak attack.
archetype-slayer-bow-master-slayer-arche.deadly arrow (ex): A bow master can take a full round action to make a ranged attack against a studied target within 120 ft that they can see. At the end of this action the bow master makes an attack at their highest base attack bonus. If this attack hits it deals damage normally. Then subtract 5 from the attack roll and compare to the target’s AC, if the new total would hit the attack deals damage again. Repeat this process until subtracting 5 from the total would result in a miss. Each instance of damage caused by this attack deals additional damage for feats, special abilities, and other bonuses which are not additional dice and can each apply on-hit effects such as poison. Only the first attack can apply precision damage or is multiplied on a critical hit. This ability replaces stalker.
archetype-slayer-bow-master-slayer-arche.master of the bow (ex): At 20th level the bow master cannot be disarmed of a bow they are carrying and it cannot be sundered. In addition they treat all bows as though they had a critical threat range of 19-20, this stacks with Improved Critical or the keen magic weapon property. Whenever the bow master confirms a critical hit against a studied target, they increase the critical multiplier of the attack by 1. This ability replaces master slayer.

archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.quickdraw (ex): At 2nd level, the dagger master gains Quickdraw as a bonus feat. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 2nd level.
archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.dagger sneak attack (ex): Beginning with 3rd level, a dagger master’s sneak attacks use d8s rather than d6s when using daggers. With all other weapons, a dagger master’s sneak attack uses d4s. This ability modifies sneak attack.
archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.stabbing critical (ex): At 4th level, a dagger master can place strikes where they cause the most damage despite their chosen weapon’s small size. Once per round, when a dagger master confirms a critical hit with a dagger they may also treat the critical hit as a sneak attack even if it would not otherwise qualify. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 4th level.
archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.paired blades (ex): At 6th level, the dagger master becomes one with the blades they carry. They gain the Two-Weapon Fighting and Two Weapon Defense feats while wielding two daggers. If the dagger master already possesses the Two-Weapon Fighting feat or Two Weapon Defense feat they may choose a different feat which has Two-Weapon Fighting as a prerequisite for which they qualify. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 6th level.
archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.palm throw (ex): Beginning at 7th level, whenever they make a thrown attack roll with a dagger they may throw two daggers instead. Each dagger must target the same creature and precision damage may only be applied to one of the daggers, though each dagger may critically hit as normal. This ability replaces stalker.
archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.greater paired blades (ex): At 12th level, the dagger master deepens the bond with their signature weapon. They gain the Improved Two-Weapon Fighting feat and when wielding two daggers each blade uses a d8 for its damage die rather than a d4. This increase in damage die applies to any dagger thrown by the dagger master as well. If the dagger master already possesses the Improved Two-Weapon Fighting feat they may choose a different feat which has Two-Weapon Fighting as a prerequisite for which they qualify. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 12th level.
archetype-slayer-dagger-master-slayer-ar.master of blades (su): At 18th level, all daggers become truly deadly weapons in the hands of the dagger master. The dagger master gains the Greater Two-Weapon Fighting feat without meeting its prerequisites. In addition, whenever the dagger master is wielding two daggers they become +3 weapons, unless the weapon already has a better enhancement bonus and gain the keen and ghost touch weapon qualities. Thrown daggers maintain these abilities until the end of the dagger master’s turn. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 18th level.

archetype-slayer-fleet-foot-slayer-arche.skirmish (ex): Beginning with 1st level, the fleet-foot gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC, Reflex Saves and CMD as long as they move at least 10 ft on their turn. This bonus lasts until the start of their next turn and increases by an additional +1 at 4th level and every 4 class levels thereafter to a maximum of +6 at 20th level. At 3rd level, once per day as a swift action after moving 10 ft on their turn, they treat any attacks made before the beginning of their next turn as satisfying the conditions for sneak attack. They gain an additional use of this sneak attack at 5th, 10th, and 15th levels. This ability replaces studied target and all the extra studied targets.
archetype-slayer-fleet-foot-slayer-arche.fleet-foot master (ex): At 20th level, they can use their skirmish ability an unlimited number of times per day. Additionally, they gain two additional uses of slayer’s advance. This ability replaces master slayer.

archetype-slayer-ghostly-assassin-slayer.ghost step (su): Beginning at 1st level, as a swift action the ghostly assassin can become invisible per the spell invisibility for 1 round. This can be done for a number of rounds equal to the ghostly assassin’s class level per day. This can be ended early as a free action. Additionally, the ghostly killer can maintain the invisibility as free action if it was active in the previous round. At 5th level, the ghostly assassin can become invisible for a number of minutes equal to their class level instead of a number of rounds. At 10th level, the ghostly assassin may choose to gain the benefit of greater invisibility for a number of rounds equal to their class level instead of the normal invisibility for minutes. At 15th level, the ghostly assassin instead become ethereal for 1 round per class level instead of invisible. At 20th level, the ghostly assassin can gain the benefit of greater invisibility for a number of minutes equal to their class level or invisibility for a number of hours equal to their class level. This ability replaces all iterations of studied target.
archetype-slayer-ghostly-assassin-slayer.terrifier (ex): Beginning at 1st level, the ghostly assassin adds 1/2 their class level (minimum 1) to Intimidate checks. This ability replaces track.
archetype-slayer-ghostly-assassin-slayer.terrifying strike (ex): At 4th level, if the ghostly assassin makes a successful sneak attack, the target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the ghostly assassin’s class level + their Charisma modifier). On a failure, the ghostly assassin looks like something out of the target’s nightmares. The target is frightened for 1d4 rounds then shaken for 1 round per class level thereafter. On a successful saving throw the target is shaken for 1d4 rounds. This is a mind-affecting, emotion, fear effect. Beginning at 10th level, the fear becomes deadly. If the target fails their Will saving throw, then they must then make a Fortitude save against the same DC, on a failure the target dies of fear as if affected by the phantasmal killer spell. If the target has Hit Dice that exceeds the ghostly assassin’s class level, they are immune to the instant death part of the ability and are instead treated as succeeding on their Fortitude save. If the creature dies of fear from this ability, all creatures within 30 feet of the creature who see the attack, not including the initial target, the ghostly assassin, and the ghostly assassin’s allies, must make Will saves (DC equal to the damage done to the victim + the ghostly killer’s Charisma modifier). On a failure they are frightened for 1d4 rounds and shaken for 1 round per class level thereafter, on a successful save, they are shaken for 1d4 rounds. At 16th level, if the target fails their Will saving throw, they are panicked for 1d4 rounds then frightened for 1 round per class level thereafter. This ability is usable once per day at 4th level, and one additional time at 10th and 16th levels. This ability replaces the slayer talents granted at 4th, 10th and 16th levels.
archetype-slayer-ghostly-assassin-slayer.ghostly sight (su): At 11th level, the ghostly assassin has a constant see invisibility spell effect. This ability replaces swift tracker and the 12th level slayer talent.
archetype-slayer-ghostly-assassin-slayer.terrifying cleave (ex): Beginning at 14th level, if the ghostly assassin reduces a target below 0 hit points with a terrifying strike, whether by the normal damage or the killing effect, they may make an attack at their highest base attack bonus on another creature within reach. If the target is also subject to a sneak attack, they are also subject to the terrifying strike ability without needing to expend another use. This ability replaces quarry and improved quarry.
archetype-slayer-ghostly-assassin-slayer.death in the dark (ex): At 20th level, if a target is killed by the frightening effect of their terrifying strike or reduced to less than 0 hit points by a sneak attack, the ghostly assassin regains a number rounds or other duration units of their ghost step ability equal to the Hit Dice of the target, up to their maximum number of rounds per day. This ability replaces master slayer.

archetype-slayer-spell-sever-slayer-arch.spell hunter (ex): If the spell sever deals damage to a creature that casts spells or has spell-like abilities, as an immediate action they can apply their studied target bonus against that target even if he didn’t sneak attack it. This ability replaces track.
archetype-slayer-spell-sever-slayer-arch.sense aura (sp): At 2nd level, the spell sever can use detect magic at will as a standard action. At 10th level, this becomes the spell arcane sight. These spells use the spell sever’s class level as their caster level. This replaces the slayer talent gained at 2nd level.
archetype-slayer-spell-sever-slayer-arch.disrupting presence (ex): At 7th level, the spell sever can make intonations and movements that distract a spellcaster’s spell components. They apply their studied target bonus as a penalty to all concentration checks made by their target. This ability replaces stalker.
archetype-slayer-spell-sever-slayer-arch.see through tricks (ex): At 11th level, the spell sever gains a bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting and illusions spells equal to 1/4 their spell sever class level. This ability replaces swift tracker.
archetype-slayer-spell-sever-slayer-arch.spell-thwart (su): At 13th level, the spell sever can shed a magical effect placed upon them once per day. This operates as the spell break enchantment using the spell sever’s class level for the caster level. At 17th level, The spell sever can use this ability twice per day. This ability replaces slayer ’s advance.

archetype-slayer-pactbane-slayer-slayer-.occult animosity (ex): At 2nd level, the slayer adds half his level on Knowledge skill checks when making skill checks to identify the abilities and weaknesses of occult creatures and creatures with a binder level. If he successfully identifies such an opponent, he can make that opponent his studied target as an immediate action. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 2nd level.
archetype-slayer-pactbane-slayer-slayer-.occult wards (ex): At 6th level, an occult slayer gains an insight bonus equal to his studied target bonus to his AC and on all saving throws that he makes against any granted abilities that his studied target uses against him. This ability replaces the slayer talent earned at 6th level.

archetype-slayer-pactsworn-assassin-slay.bind spirit: A pactsworn assassin may seal pacts with otherworldly entities known as spirits. In order to summon a spirit, the pactsworn assassin must learn the spirit’s ceremony, constellation, personality, and seal by completing its four Knowledge Tasks; see Researching the Spirit for more information on this process. A pactsworn assassin begins play having completed all four Knowledge Tasks for one 1st-level spirit of his choice that belongs to his chosen constellation (see tunneled lore below). Each day, a pactsworn assassin may bind one spirit to his soul using pact magic; see Performing a Pact Ritual. The spirit’s level may not exceed the pactsworn assassin’s maximum spirit level, which is limited to 1st-level spirits at 1st level. At 4th level and every three slayer levels thereafter, the pactsworn assassin’s maximum spirit level increases by 1, to a maximum of 6th-level spirits at 16th level. A pactsworn assassin possesses a binder level equal to his level. The DC to resist a pactsworn assassin’s supernatural powers is equal to 10 + 1/2 the pactsworn assassin’s level + the pactsworn assassin’s Charisma modifier. This ability replaces track, stalker, slayer’s advance 1/day, and the slayer’s 4th-level, 10th-level, and 16th-level slayer talents.
archetype-slayer-pactsworn-assassin-slay.studied target (ex): This ability functions as the slayer class ability of the same name, except a pactsworn assassin cannot maintain his studied target’s bonuses against more than one target at a time. Tunneled Lore: At 1st level, a pactsworn assassin chooses one constellation. He may only seal pacts with starless spirits and spirits belonging to his chosen constellation. All other constellations are barred to him.

archetype-slayer-libertys-champion-slaye.studied target (ex): A liberty’s champion does not gain a +1 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, or Survival skill checks against her studied target. Instead, she gains a +1 competence bonus to her armor class on attacks made against her by her studied target. This bonus increases at the same rate as her bonuses on attack and damage rolls against her studied target. In all other ways, studied target is unchanged. This alters studied target.
archetype-slayer-libertys-champion-slaye.conditioned (ex): Beginning at 1st level, a liberty’s champion ignores armor check penalties when wearing light armor. This replaces track.
archetype-slayer-libertys-champion-slaye.to the rescue (ex): A conditioned body and unwavering conviction allows a liberty’s champion to overcome challenges and stay focused on her objective. At 7th level, she may choose one of the following benefits: • Gain a +2 morale bonus on Will saving throw rolls. (This can be selected up to four times. Each time it is selected, the bonus increases by +2.) Gain a +10-foot morale bonus to base land speed. (This can be selected twice. Upon selecting it a second time, the bonus increases by +10 feet.) Treat Strength score as 2 points higher for the purpose of determining carrying capacity. (This can be selected twice. Upon selecting it a second time, the Strength score is treated as an additional 2 points higher.) A liberty’s champion can make another selection from this list again at 11th, 14th, and 19th level. This replaces stalker, swift tracker, quarry, and improved quarry.

archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.swift swim (ex): The mako is an exceptional swimmer, able to cross great distances of water quickly. As long as she has at least 1 point of panache remaining, she can move up to her full speed as a move action while swimming, or twice her speed as a full-round action, instead of the normal rate of movement when using the Swim skill. Additionally, whenever she moves while underwater, she may spend 1 point of panache. If she does, her movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity for that action. This ability replaces the derring-do deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.underwater action (ex): At 3rd level, the mako can effectively deliver deadly and precise strikes while underwater. As long as she has at least 1 point of panache remaining, a mako never suffers a penalty to attack or damage for being underwater, regardless of what type of weapon she is wielding, and even if she fails her Swim check. This ability replaces the menacing swordplay deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.drowning blow (ex): At 7th level, the mako is able to inflict a rapid strike to her opponents that makes it extremely difficult to hold their breath. By spending 1 point of panache, the mako can make a single melee attack with a light or one-handed piercing weapon against a creature that is holding its breath underwater. If the attack is successful, the target suffers damage as normal and the number of rounds that the target can continue to hold its breath before being forced to make checks to avoid drowning is decreased to 0. If the creature is already making checks to avoid drowning, the DC of all such checks increases by +4 until the creature stops holding its breath. This ability replaces the targeted strike deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.underwater acrobatics (ex): At 11th level, the mako is able to perform amazing feats of dodging and weaving while underwater. As long as she has at least 1 point of panache remaining, the mako adds 1/2 her swashbuckler level to all Swim checks, and can take 5-foot steps while underwater. Additionally, whenever the mako is attacked underwater, she my expend 1 point of panache to gain a circumstance bonus against that attack equal to 1/3 the number of ranks she has in Swim. She must declare she is using this ability before she knows the result of the attack roll. This ability replaces the evasive deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.mako strike (ex): The mako can swim through the water in a brutal charge, delivering death with her weapon. At 15th level, as long as she has at least 1 point of panache, she can use the charge action while underwater. When she does, she gains a +4 bonus to attack rolls, rather than the normal +2, and if she hits, she may expend an additional point of panache in order to deal double damage with the charge attack. This ability replaces the dizzying defense deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.as the waves (ex): At 19th level, as long as she has at least 1 point of panache, the mako gains a swim speed equal to three times her land speed. Additionally, by spending 1 point of panache while underwater, the mako can act with such speed that she can make an additional move action each round, or alternatively make an additional attack at her highest base attack bonus whenever she makes a full-attack action. This effect lasts for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier. This ability replaces the stunning stab deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.breath reservoir (ex): A mako is a practiced free diver and is rarely caught short of breath. At 2nd level, she adds her Charisma score to her Constitution score for the purposes of determining how many rounds she can hold her breath. She can also perform actions other than moving while underwater without having to consume 2 rounds’ worth of held breath. This ability replaces the charmed life class feature.
archetype-swashbuckler-mako-swashbuckler.aquatic defense (ex): A mako is most at home in the water and knows how to use the ocean to defend herself from attack. Beginning at 3rd level, the mako suffers no armor check penalty on Swim checks. Additionally, while in at least 5 feet of water, she gains a +2 dodge bonus to AC. At 7th level, and every 4 levels thereafter, this bonus increases by a further +2 (to a maximum of +10 at 19th level). This ability replaces the nimble class feature.

archetype-swashbuckler-spear-dancer-swas.dancer’s finesse (ex): A spear dancer’s swashbuckler finesse class feature also applies to two handed piercing melee weapons in the polearm or spear weapon groups and all deeds the spear dancer possess may be used with such weapons. This ability modifies swashbuckler finesse.
archetype-swashbuckler-spear-dancer-swas.cloud leap (su): Beginning with 1st level, whenever a spear dancer uses their derring-do deed to modify an Acrobatics check to jump, they halve the DC and are always considered to have a running start. This ability modifies the derring-do deed.
archetype-swashbuckler-spear-dancer-swas.fast movement (ex): Starting at 3rd level, a spear dancer gains fast movement as a monk of their class level. This ability replaces all instances of charmed life.
archetype-swashbuckler-spear-dancer-swas.spear dancing (ex): At 4th level, a spear dancer can enter a state of ecstasy while in combat. While wielding a two handed piercing melee weapon from the spear or polearm weapon group and fighting defensively or benefiting from the Combat Expertise feat, the spear dancer can attack targets an additional 5 feet away. If the weapon has reach they may also attack adjacent targets. This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 4th level.
archetype-swashbuckler-spear-dancer-swas.spear dancer training (ex): At 5th level, a spear dancer gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with two-handed piercing melee weapons from the spear or polearm weapon group. Additionally, they gain the benefit of the Improved Critical feat while wielding such weapons. The bonus to attack and damage rolls increases by an additional +1 at 9th level and every 4 levels thereafter to a maximum of +4 at 17th level. This feature counts as weapon training for the purpose of feat prerequisites. This ability replaces all instances of swashbuckler weapon training.

archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.dilettante’s deeds: An esoteric dilettante doesn’t gain deeds like other swashbucklers. At 1st, 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 19th level, an esoteric dilettante selects one deed that is available to a swashbuckler of her level or lower. She gains the selected deed, but doesn’t gain any other deeds that she would normally be entitled to based upon her swashbuckler level. This ability alters the swashbuckler’s deeds.
archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.dilettante’s panache: Each day, an esoteric dilettante gains a number of panache points equal to her Charisma modifier. Unlike other swashbucklers, an esoteric dilettante gains panache only from scoring a critical hit or killing blow against a creature that qualifies as the favored enemy of one of her bound spirits. This ability alters the panache class feature.
archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.bind spirit: An esoteric dilettante may seal pacts with otherworldly entities known as spirits. In order to summon a spirit, the esoteric dilettante must learn the spirit’s ceremony, constellation, personality, and seal by completing its four Knowledge Tasks; see Researching the Spirit in Chapter 3 for more information on this process. An esoteric dilettante begins play having completed all four Knowledge Tasks for one 1st-level spirit of her choice. Each day, an esoteric dilettante may bind one spirit to her soul using pact magic; see Performing a Pact Ritual. The spirit’s level may not exceed the esoteric dilettante’s maximum spirit level, which is limited to 1st-level spirits at 1st level. At 4th level and every three swashbuckler levels thereafter, the esoteric dilettante’s maximum spirit level increases by 1, to a maximum of 6th-level spirits at 16th level. An esoteric dilettante possesses a binder level equal to her level. The DC to resist an esoteric dilettante’s supernatural powers is equal to 10 + 1/2 the esoteric dilettante’s level + the esoteric dilettante’s Charisma modifier.
archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.dilettante’s finesse (ex): At 1st level, an esoteric dilettante gains the benefits of Weapon Finesse feat with light or one-handed piercing melee weapons and with all melee touch attacks that she makes. Additionally, the esoteric dilettante treats all light or one-handed melee weapons that she gains from the granted abilities of a spirit that she is currently bound to as a one-handed piercing melee weapon for all swashbuckler class abilities that require such a weapon. This ability replaces swashbuckler’s finesse.
archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.bonus feats: An esoteric dilettante may select combat feats, grit feats, and pact feats as bonus feats. Alternatively, she may select one deed available to a swashbuckler of her level or lower that she does not possess and gain it in place of a bonus feat. This ability alters the swashbuckler’s bonus feats.
archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.dilettante weapon training (ex): At 5th level, an esoteric dilettante gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with light or one-handed weapon piercing melee weapons and with any melee touch attacks that she makes. While wielding such a weapon, she gains the benefit of the Improved Critical feat. These attack and damage bonuses increase by 1 for every 4 levels beyond 5th (to a maximum of +4 at 17th level). This ability alters swashbuckler weapon training.
archetype-swashbuckler-esoteric-dilettan.dilettante weapon mastery (ex): At 20th level, when an esoteric threatens a critical hit with a light or one-handed piercing melee weapon or a melee touch attack, that critical is automatically confirmed. Furthermore, the critical modifiers of such weapons increase by 1 (x2 becomes x3, and so on). This ability alters swashbuckler weapon mastery.

archetype-swashbuckler-buccaneer-swashbu.bardic performance (su): At 1st level, a buccaneer gains one 1st-level bardic performance of his choice. On the first round he performs each day, the buccaneer must spend 1 panache point. Once he does so, he can perform as a bard of his level -2 (minimum 1st) for up to a number of rounds equal to his Charisma modifier and may cease or resume performing without using additional panache. At 3rd level, and every 4 levels thereafter, the buccaneer can perform for up to 4 additional rounds and gains an additional bardic performance of his choice for his effective bard level. This replaces the deeds opportune parry and riposte, menacing swordplay, targeted strike, bleeding wound, perfect thrust, and deadly stab.
archetype-swashbuckler-buccaneer-swashbu.device expertise (ex): At 4th level, a buccaneer gains Skill Focus (use magic device) as a bonus feat. At 12th level, he gains the skill unlock powers for that skill as appropriate for his number of ranks in that skill. This replaces the bonus feats gained at the listed levels.
archetype-swashbuckler-buccaneer-swashbu.fighter training (ex): Beginning at 4th level, a buccaneer’s swashbuckler levels are considered fighter levels for the purpose of meeting combat feat prerequisites.
archetype-swashbuckler-buccaneer-swashbu.versatile performance (ex): At 8th level, and again at 16th level, a buccaneer gains the versatile performance bard class feature. This replaces the bonus feats gained at the listed levels.

archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.untamed (ex): Totem monks do not have to be lawful but they are prohibited from having an evil alignment. Any totem monk whose alignment becomes evil loses all benefits granted by their totem until they no longer have an evil component to their alignment. Additionally, the totem monk adds Knowledge (Nature) and Survival to their list of class skills, and they gain 2 extra skill points per level which must be applied to these skills. This alters alignment and class skills.
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.nature’s vessel (sp): At 1st level, a totem monk learns four druid cantrips of their choice and can cast them at will as spell-like abilities. This replaces the 1st level bonus feat.
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.spirit totem (su): At 2nd level, a totem monk forges a permanent bond with a formless entity, called a spirit totem, that merges with the totem monk. The spirit totem occupies the same space as the monk, is invisible, and is completely indistinguishable from the monk. It can’t be killed or affected as a separate entity. The only evidence of a totem monk’s bond to their spirit totem is a mark on their skin akin to a birthmark that vaguely resembles their totem animal spirit. When a totem monk dies, the spirit totem returns to the Astral Plane, and the totem monk loses all benefits conferred by their spirit totem until they merge with a new one. A raised or reincarnated totem monk can merge with a new spirit totem 24 hours after returning to life. The new totem must come from the same totem category as the original, though it can be a different creature. For example, if a totem monk originally had the prowler totem with a cougar spirit, they must select the prowler totem again but could choose a tiger instead. A spirit totem alerts a totem monk to the presence of danger and helps the totem monk to survive in the wilderness. The totem monk gains a +1 insight bonus on Perception checks and an insight bonus on Initiative rolls equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Listed below are the spirit totems a totem monk can merge with. In addition to choosing the broad spirit totem category, the totem monk must indicate what specific creature their totem is. (If there is a question as to which category a player’s chosen creature belongs to, the GM has final jurisdiction.) This replaces the 2nd level bonus feat. Table: Spirit Totems Spirit Totem Examples Fleetfoot All hoofed animals and flightless birds (horses, zebras, donkeys, mules, pigs, boars, cows, giraffes, camels, antelopes, sheep, deer, hippos, goats, emus, ostriches, etc. Howler Canines ( dogs, foxes, hyenas, wolves Mimic Primates (apes, lemurs, monkeys, simians, tarsiers, gorillas, baboons, chimpanzees Padfoot Mammals that don’t fit in any other category listed ( rats, mice, squirrels, porcupines, rabbits, moles, raccoons, kangaroos, wombats, opossums, etc. Prowler Felines (house cats, cheetahs, cougars, tigers, lions, jaguars, lynxes, panthers, etc. Powerhouse Bears and elephants ( elephants, grizzlies, black bears, polar bears, etc. Scaled Survivor Reptiles ( alligators, crocodiles, lizards, snakes, turtles, tortoises Wave-rider Water-living mammals, fish, crustaceans, cephalopods, and flightless web-footed birds ( whales, porpoises, dolphins, beavers, salmon, haddock, sharks, crabs, lobsters, octopuses, squid, penguins etc. Webfoot Amphibians ( frogs, toads, newts, salamanders Wind-rider Bats and birds that can fly ( owls, eagles, ravens, flamingos, bats, cardinals, robins, hummingbirds, etc.
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.trappings (ex): At 4th level, a totem monk’s skin changes based upon the influence of their spirit totem. This change grants the totem monk an enhancement bonus to their existing natural armor class (similar to barkskin ) rather than the untyped bonus to AC that a standard unchained monk receives. This enhancement bonus is only applied to the totem monk’s natural AC, not their CMD. Examples of the physical change might be a layer of feathers if their spirit totem is a bird, scales if their spirit totem is a fish or reptile, a thick pelt of fur if their spirit totem is a bear, or especially thick hide if their spirit totem is a hippopotamus. This enhancement bonus to the totem monk’s natural armor class is +1 at 4th level. The bonus increases by 1 for every four totem monk levels thereafter (up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level). This enhancement bonus stacks with the totem monk’s natural armor bonus, but not with other enhancement bonuses to natural armor; if a totem monk gains an enhancement to their natural armor bonus from another source (like barkskin ), they use the better of the two bonuses instead. This alters the monk’s AC bonus.
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.bonus feat: At 6th level, and every level an unchained monk gains a bonus feat thereafter, the totem monk chooses their bonus feats according to their spirit totem. A totem monk doesn’t need to meet the prerequisites for these feats. Every totem has access to Alertness, Improved Initiative, Improved Natural Armor (can only take once), Keen Scent, and Skill Focus ( Perception ). The table below lists the additional feat options available for each totem. This alters bonus feats. Table: Spirit Totems Spirit Totem Bonus Feat Fleetfoot Fleet, Ride-By Attack, Run Howler Improved Trip, Lightning Reflexes, Step Up Mimic Sure Grasp, Throw Anything, Tree Leaper Padfoot Agile Maneuvers, Dodge, Weapon Finesse Powerhouse Endurance, Iron Will, Toughness Prowler Cat’s Fall, Skill Focus ( Acrobatics ), Skill Focus ( Stealth )
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.scaled survivor: Improved Lightning Reflexes, Intimidating Prowess, Ironhide
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.wave-rider: Defensive Combat Training, Deep Diver, Skill Focus ( Swim ) Webfoot Athletic, Diehard, Swamper Wind-rider Deflect Arrows, Eagle -Eyed, Mobility
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.nature whisperer (sp): At 13th level, a totem monk can cast speak with animals as a spell-like ability a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and they can cast speak with plants and stone tell as spell-like abilities once each per day. This replaces tongue of the sun and moon.
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.totemic aspect (ex): At 17th level, a totem monk takes on qualities of their spirit totem, gaining the benefits listed below for their totem. This replaces timeless body. Spirit Totem Totemic Aspect Fleetfoot When you take the charge action, you do not incur a penalty to your Armor Class. Howler Whenever you confirm a critical hit against an opponent that is no more than one Size category larger than you, you can attempt to trip the target as a free action, but no more than once per round. For the purposes of this trip attempt only, you are treated as though you have the Improved Trip and Greater Trip feats. Mimic You gain a climb speed equal to your land speed (including your fast movement bonus) and you gain double the normal racial bonus to Climb checks for having a climb speed (+16 instead of +8). Padfoot Once per round, on the first attack of opportunity you would normally provoke due to your movement, you instead do not provoke the attack. Powerhouse You gain a +1 on damage rolls when you use your flurry of blows class feature. Prowler You are not penalized for making jumps without a running head start and your Dexterity score increases by +2.
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.wave-rider and webfoot: You gain resistance to cold 20, are always considered to be under the influence of freedom of movement while in water that is at least knee deep, and can hold your breath for a number of rounds equal to ten times your Constitution score (two times the Constitution score is normal).
archetype-monk-unchained-totem-monk-unch.wind-rider (su): You are constantly under the effects of feather fall, and the insight bonus you gain to Perception checks from your spirit totem class feature increases to +5.

archetype-monk-unchained-eternal-flower-.class skills: The eternal flower monk gains Diplomacy and Heal as class skills and does not gain Intimidate as a class skill.
archetype-monk-unchained-eternal-flower-.ring the temple bell (su): At 2nd level, the eternal flower monk can restore a creature to its right mind with a resounding strike. She can use this attack once per day, and additional times per day by expending uses of stunning fist. She must announce her intent before making her attack roll. If she strikes successfully, the attack deals no damage. Instead, it removes the dazed and shaken conditions. At 5th level and higher it removes additional effects. At 5th level it removes the cowering and frightened conditions. At 8th level it removes the fascinated and panicked conditions. At 11th level it removes the confused, paralyzed, and stunned conditions. At 14th level it makes a targeted dispel against enchantment spells and abilities affecting the creature, using the monk’s level as her caster level. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level and the 16th level monk ki power.
archetype-monk-unchained-eternal-flower-.tongue of the flowing river (ex): At 4th level, the eternal flower monk gains a +2 bonus to Diplomacy skill checks and may influence anyone who can hear her. She may choose to be heard regardless of ambient noise and silence effects when making these checks. This ability replaces still mind.
archetype-monk-unchained-eternal-flower-.ki pool (su): The eternal flower monk channels her deity’s power, rather than her own energies. She uses her Charisma modifier in place of her Wisdom modifier to determine the size of her ki pool. At 10th level, ki strike allows her unarmed attacks to be treated as chaotic weapons, if she is chaotic aligned, and good weapons, if she is good aligned, for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. This ability modifies ki pool and replaces ki strike (lawful). The eternal flower monk gains all other ki pool abilities as normal.
archetype-monk-unchained-eternal-flower-.sworn to the eternal flower (su): At 14th level, an eternal flower monk is immune to charm and compulsion spells and abilities, as long as she has a ki point available in her ki pool. This ability replaces the monk’s 14th level ki power.
archetype-monk-unchained-eternal-flower-.true freedom (ex): At 20th level, the eternal flower monk is immune to spells and effects that restrict movement, including binding, entangle, grappling, imprisonment, maze, paralysis, petrification, pinning, sleep, slow, stunning, temporal stasis, and web, and can travel freely through any spell or effect that blocks movement. She still suffers any damage or other effects for doing so. Finally, the monk gains the ability to enter a state of perfect calm. During this time, the monk can take no actions, but she does regain ki at the rate of 1 point per 10 minutes spent at calm. She cannot use this ability to gain an amount of ki in excess of his maximum. This ability replaces perfect self.

archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.elemental fist (su): At 1st level, a monk of the creation elements gains Elemental Fist as a bonus feat, even if she does not meet the feat’s prerequisites. She can only deal additional energy damage of the type matching her primary element. If her primary element is not air, earth, fire, or water, the monk deals additional bludgeoning damage with Elemental Fist. This ability replaces stunning fist. Ki Powers: A monk of the creation elements must select the following ki powers: elemental fury (6th level, stacks with Elemental Fist ), whirlwind attack (8th level), elemental burst (18th level). In addition, any ki power duplicating the effects of a spell of the elemental school matching the monk ’s chosen element is available 2 levels in advance to him; for example, cloak of winds can be selected at 4th level by a monk of air. The monk also gains access to the following ki powers:
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.elemental defense (sp): A monk with this power the kineticist ’s elemental defense tied to her primary element for 1 minute. Using this ability is a move action that consumes 1 point from the monk ’s ki pool.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.elemental kinesis (sp): A monk with this power gains an utility wild talent tied to her primary element (or an universal utility talent) as if he were a kineticist of her monk level. She can expend 2 ki points instead of 1 point of burn in order to use this talent. This power can be selected more than once, gaining a new utility talent each time.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.fast movement (ex): A golden streak monk gains the fast movement ability at 1st level, and the stunning fist ability at 3rd level. Ki Powers: A monk of the golden streak must select the following ki powers: sudden speed (4th level), bladed dash (6th level), abundant step (8th level), ki hurricane (10th level), greater bladed dash (12th level). He also gains access to the following ki powers:
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.kasoku (ex): When using the sudden speed and ki hurricane powers, a monk with this power can spend more ki points to further increase his speed. He adds another 10 feet to his base land speed for each additional ki point he spends. A monk must be at least 12th level and possess the sudden speed and ki hurricane powers before selecting this ki power.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.improvised weapon (ex): At 1st level, an indiscriminate fighting monk gains Catch Off-Guard as a bonus feat. This replaces the 1st-level bonus feat.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.improbable jutsu (ex): At 6th level, an indiscriminate fighting monk gains the martial flexibility class feature as a brawler of his level -5. He can use this power to gain combat feats or ki feats. This ability replaces the 6th and 18th-level bonus feats and the 12th and 16th-level ki powers.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.perfect improvisation (ex): At 20th level, an indiscriminate fighting monk can gain the benefit of any number of combat feats as a swift action. Each feat selected counts toward his daily uses of the martial flexibility ability. This replaces perfect self (the monk can still gain perfect self as his 20th-level ki power). Ki Powers: A monk of indiscriminate fighting must select the following ki power: Improvised Weapon Mastery (12th level). He also gains access to the following ki power:
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.tactical escape (ex): As a full-round action, a monk with this power can expend 1 ki point to move up to his speed away from a foe without provoking attacks of opportunity, while he thinks about the best way to attack or defend himself. In the round following the end of his tactical escape, he gains a +1 bonus on his attack rolls and CMB for each round spent running. A monk must be at least 8th level before selecting this ki power.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.flurry of a thousands blows (ex): A monk of the northern star adds one additional attack to his flurry of blows at 3rd and 15th level, in addition to the other attacks normally gained. This replaces fast movement and timeless body.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.ninja tricks: A monk of the northern star can select the following ninja tricks in place of ki powers, using his monk level as his ninja level for the purpose of gaining and using them. If a ninja trick improves a ninja ’s sneak attack, it applies to the monk’s flurry of blows instead.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.master tricks: see the unseen, unbound steps, vested power. Ki Powers: A monk of the northern star must select the following ki powers: Psychic Sensitivity (4th level), explode head (12th level). He also gains access to the following ki power:
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.delayed damage (su): Whenever a monk with this power would deliver damage to an opponent, he can spend 1 ki point from his pool to delay the damage’s onset by 1 round.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-way.chosen virtue (ex): At 1st level, a monk of the southern star must select one alignment. As long as he maintains the selected alignment, he receives a +2 morale bonus to one saving throw of his choice. Blessing: At 8th level, a monk of the southern star selects one warpriest minor blessing suited to his ideals and alignment. He can use the minor power of that blessing as a warpriest of the same level. At 16th level, the monk gains his blessing’s major power too. This replaces the 8th and 16th-level ki powers. Perfect Ideal: At 20th level, when a monk of the southern star gains the perfect self ability, his damage reduction applies to an alignment of his choice ( chaotic, evil, good, or lawful ) that is opposite to her own. This modifies perfect self. Ki Powers: A monk of the southern star must select the following ki power: one touch (12th level). He also gains access to the following ki powers:

archetype-monk-unchained-death-shroud-mo.death knell (sp): At 1st level, a death shroud monk draws the life out of dying creatures to empower themselves. They can cast death knell as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level. The DC for this spell-like ability is 10 + 1/2 the death shroud monk’s class level + their Wisdom modifier. This ability is usable once per day plus one per 3 class levels they have. At 8th level, they can use this as a swift action once per day on a creature they reduce to below 0 hit points with an unarmed attack or their death touch attack (see below). This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-unchained-death-shroud-mo.poison use (ex): At 2nd level, a death shroud monk is trained in the use of poison and never risks poisoning themselves when applying poison to a weapon. This ability replaces the bonus feat at 2nd level.
archetype-monk-unchained-death-shroud-mo.death’s shroud (ex): At 3rd level, a death shroud monk gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against death effects and a +2 bonus to Intimidate checks. This ability replaces still mind. The unchained monk gains this ability at 4th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-death-shroud-mo.death touch (su): At 6th level, a death shroud monk can replace one of their attacks made during a full attack or as a standard to deliver a death- empowered attack. The attack is a melee touch attack that deals 1d8 negative energy damage per 3 class levels the death shroud monk possesses. This does not heal undead. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels.

archetype-monk-unchained-divine-ascetic-.domain (su): At 1st level, a divine ascetic gains a domain available to their deity or faith. They gain the abilities from the domain at the levels a cleric would gain them. The spells from the domain are added to the divine ascetic’s spell list as noted below.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-ascetic-.spell casting: At 4th level, a divine ascetic gains the ability to cast spells. They use the same spells per day as a paladin, though they may prepare any spell from the cleric spell list and the list provided by their domain. They use their Wisdom modifier for their spellcasting ability modifier. This ability replaces all instances of slow fall, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels, and quivering palm for the monk. For the unchained monk, this ability replaces the ki power gained at 4th, 10th, and 16th levels, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels and the style strike gained at 17th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-ascetic-.divine strike (su): At 4th level, a divine ascetic can deliver melee touch spells as part of a full attack action. At 8th level, they are also able to deliver ranged touch attacks as melee touch attacks during the full attack action.

archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.sense the soul (sp): At 1st level, a divine dragon monk can cast detect evil and detect magic at will as spell-like abilities using their class level as the caster level. This ability replaces the bonus feat granted at 1st level.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.smite evil (su): At 1st level, a divine dragon monk gains smite evil as a paladin of their class level. This ability replaces flurry of blows.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.touch of the fire dragon (su): At 1st level, a divine dragon monk can cause their unarmed strikes to burst into flame. As a swift action, they can deal an additional 1d4 fire damage per 2 class levels on their next unarmed strike. A divine dragon monk can use this ability a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.scales of the metal dragon (ex): At 2nd level, a divine dragon monk has divinely inspired resilience. Anytime they succeed on a spell effect that would impose a partial or half effect on a Fortitude or Will save, they instead are unaffected. This ability replaces evasion and improved evasion.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.resilience of the earth dragon (ex): At 5th level, a divine dragon monk is immune to stunning and sleep and effects that impose slow. This ability replaces purity of body.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.purity of the water dragon (su): At 11th level, a divine dragon monk, regains 1 hit point per hour. Additionally, they can make a Fortitude save once per hour to recover ability score damage as if resting for 24 hours. The DC for the Fortitude save is 10 plus the ability score to be healed minus the total damage to the ability score. This ability replaces diamond body for the monk. The unchained monk gains this ability at 12th level and it replaces the ki power gained at that level.
archetype-monk-unchained-divine-dragon-m.blending of the wood dragon (sp): At 15th level, a divine dragon monk can cast greater invisibility a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. The caster level for this effect is their class level. This ability replaces quivering palm for the monk or all style strikes for the unchained monk.

archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.temper the ephemeral (su): A grounded spirit understands the impact of magic on the world but also knows that magic is just another force of nature no different than the wind and can be overcome like any other. A grounded spirit uses Intelligence in place of Wisdom to determine the effectiveness of all unchained monk abilities that normally rely on Wisdom.
archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.spellhardened (su): The bonus a grounded spirit gains to AC beyond their Intelligence modifier, gained at 4th level and every four levels thereafter, also applies on saves against spells and spell-like abilities. This ability modifies the monk’s AC bonus.
archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.redirect the energy (su): At 4th level, the grounded spirit has learned to make enemy power their own. Whenever a grounded spirit successfully saves against an enemy spell or spell-like ability they gain a ki point. This does not allow the grounded spirit to have more than their normal maximum number of ki points. This ability replaces still mind.
archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.bonus feats: Add the following feats to the list of bonus feats available at the listed level. This ability modifies bonus feats. 2nd – Disruptive 6th – Spellbreaker 10th – Shatterspell, Sunder Blessing 14th -Teleport Tactition
archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.stifle the flow (su): At 9th level, the grounded spirit can extend mastery of their own energy to the energies of others. Whenever an opponent fails their saving throw against the grounded spirit’s stunning fist, for one minute or until the next time that opponent casts a spell or uses a spell-like ability that opponent must succeed at a concentration check with a DC of 20 + twice the level of the spell being cast or the spell-like ability being used. Failure means the spell or spell-like ability fails and is expended with no effect. This ability replaces improved evasion.
archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.sever spirit (su): At 15th level, the grounded spirit has learned to block another’s ties to whatever source powers their magic. As a full round action a grounded spirit can send forth a wave of their own energy at a target within 30 ft. as a ranged touch attack or as a melee touch attack. If successful the target takes damage as though from the grounded spirit’s unarmed strike and must make a Fortitude save (DC of 10 + 1/2 the grounded spirit’s level + the grounded spirit’s Intelligence modifier) or lose the ability to cast spells or activate spell-like abilities. The target makes a new save each day when they would normally regain their spells or recharge spell-like abilities. This condition can be removed by a break enchantment spell or more powerful magic. Treat the caster level as equal to the grounded spirit’s class level to determine the strength of the effect for the purposes of such spells. This ability replaces the ability to use style strike twice per round.
archetype-monk-unchained-grounded-spirit.ki expertise: The grounded spirit may select the following expertise in place of a ki power, if the expertise requires spending a charge of stolen magic the grounded spirit may substitute 2 ki points and if the expertise refers to spelljack level it uses grounded spirit level instead: Drain item, familiar, guided blade, improved familiar, pilfered potency.

archetype-monk-unchained-healer-monk-unc.lay on hands (su): At 3rd level, a healer monk gains lay on hands as a paladin of their class level. Instead of uses per day, they expend a ki point to use this ability and they use their Wisdom modifier in place of their Charisma modifier. This ability replaces still mind, purity of body, wholeness of body and diamond body for the monk. For the unchained monk, they instead gain this ability at 4th level, replacing still mind, purity of body, and the ki powers at 8th and 12th levels.
archetype-monk-unchained-healer-monk-unc.mercies (su): When gaining a bonus feat from their monk levels, a healer monk may instead choose to gain a mercy available to the paladin. This ability modifies bonus feats but does not prevent another archetype from replacing those bonus feats.

archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.weapon and armor proficiencies: At 1st level, an iron-skinned monk gains proficiency with the gauntlet, spiked gauntlet, cestus, and armor spikes. Additionally, the iron-skinned monk gains proficiency in light armor. This alters the unchained monk’s weapon and armor proficiencies.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.iron skinned style (ex): An iron-skinned monk uses their unarmed damage progression instead of the normal damage for cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and armor spikes and they may make their flurry of blows or stunning fist attacks with these weapons. All abilities of the unchained monk function while they are wearing light or no armor but still not while they are carrying a medium or heavy load. This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 1st level and an iron-skinned striker does not add their Wisdom bonus to their AC, though they still gain an improved AC bonus at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter even while wearing light armor.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.ki like iron (su): When the iron-skinned monk gains a ki pool (at 3rd level for the unchained monk) they gain a new use for that ability. When making a combat maneuver check the iron skinned monk may expend a point of ki to avoid an attack of opportunity from their target and adds their Wisdom bonus (minimum 1) to the combat maneuver check. Beginning at 7th level, cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and armor spikes carried by the iron-skinned monk also benefits from ki strike. This ability modifies ki strike.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.ever vigilant (ex): At 5th level, all squares the iron-skinned monk threatens with a melee weapon or unarmed strike, are considered difficult terrain for enemies. This ability applies even to jumping, flying, and incorporeal foes, as well as swarms, so long as the iron-skinned monk wields a melee weapon or unarmed strike capable of affecting them. The iron-skinned monk must be aware of the enemy to affect them. The iron-skinned monk also provides cover but not total cover to adjacent allies if their square lies between the ally and the origin of the attack or effect that includes the ally as a target. This ability replaces purity of body.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.bulwark (ex): At 10th level, the iron-skinned monk has learned to defend against some kinds of magic. If they are wearing gauntlets or cestus they may expend a point of ki and deflect a ray effect that targets them as an immediate action causing it to harmlessly dissipate. If the iron-skinned monk expends an additional point of ki they make a Reflex save against that ray using whatever the save DC vs the effect would normally be, even if it does not allow one. If they succeed they may redirect the ray to a target of their choice. The target must be within range of the spell as though the ironskinned monk was the point of origin. This redirection uses the same attack roll result by the original caster. This ability replaces improved evasion.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.steel reserves (ex): Beginning at 10th level, the ironskinned monk gains 2 bonus temporary ki at the beginning of each combat. This ki is used first before their normal pool of ki and if this bonus ki remains at the end of combat, it is lost. This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 10th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.steel skinned master (ex/su): Beginning at 16th level for the unchained monk, the iron-skinned monk treats cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets and armor spikes as though they were one size larger for the purpose of their unarmed damage progression. Furthermore they may spend a ki point to emulate the effects of stoneskin on themselves as a standard action using their character level as the caster level, while under the effects of this stoneskin effect they are also not subject to critical hits or precision damage. This ability replaces the ki power gained at 16th level for the unchained monk.
archetype-monk-unchained-iron-skinned-un.unyielding iron: Beginning at 19th level, while the iron-skinned monk still has at least one point of ki in their pool they cannot be moved from their square by the force of another creature, spell, spell-like, or supernatural ability, or by other means. Natural forces such as gravity still affect the iron-skinned monk, though a tidal wave, gust of wind, or other such phenomenon may not as long as the iron-skinned monk is standing on a surface which can support their weight. This ability replaces flawless mind for the unchained monk.

archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.planar combatant (ex): At 1st level, a monk of many worlds gains Bluff and Knowledge (planes) as class skills, but they lose Knowledge (history), Knowledge (religion), and Ride as class skills.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.phasing strike (su): At 1st level, a monk of many worlds can make an attack that phases through planes and through their opponent’s defenses. As a swift action, the monk of many worlds can make a feint attempt with a bonus to the attempt equal to 1/2 their class level. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to their class level. At 6th level, the strike is always considered to have the ghost touch property when this ability is used. At 12th level, all of a monk of many worlds’ unarmed attacks have the ghost touch property. This ability replaces stunning fist.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.dimension slip (su): Beginning with 3rd level, a monk of many worlds can shift 5 feet into any unoccupied space as an immediate or swift action. If this shift would put them beyond the range of an attack or area of effect, they are unaffected but the attack is still made, if applicable. This ability is usable once per day plus 1 per 3 levels after 3rd. This ability replaces fast movement.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.dimensional charge (su): Starting with 4th level, a monk of many worlds can slip between dimensions while making a charge. This allows them to triple their speed on a full-round charge attack. At 12th level, a monk of many worlds does not suffer the AC penalty from charging and may turn any number of times while charging. This ability replaces all instances of slow fall for the monk and the ki powers gained at 4th and 12th levels for the unchained monk.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.far strike (su): At 6th level, a monk of many worlds can open a small gate with an attack. They may make a single attack as a full-round action to attack a creature within 30 feet. At 12th level, this increases to 60 feet. This attack can be modified by Vital Strike or its improvements. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 6th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.dimensional jump (sp): At 10th level, a monk of many worlds can cast dimension door as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces the bonus feat at 10th level, and diamond body for the monk, or the 10th-level ki power for the unchained monk.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-many-wo.multi-dimensional strike (su): At 15th level, a monk of many worlds can make their attacks through a dimensional portal they create and use their full attack or flurry of blows to attack any creature within 30 feet. The attacks can target multiple creatures or the same creature at their discretion. These attacks automatically gain the free feint attempt from the phasing strike ability. This ability is usable a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces quivering palm for the monk, or all instances of style strike for the unchained monk.

archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.hidden step (ex): The monk of the darkened hand learns techniques to hide among the shadows. Beginning at 2nd level, they gain a bonus to their Stealth checks equal to 1/2 their class level while in areas of dim light or darkness. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.uncanny dodge (ex): Starting at 3rd level, the monk of the darkened hand cannot be caught flat-footed, even if the attacker is invisible. They still lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A monk of the darkened hand with this ability can still lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against them. If the monk of the darkened hand already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge instead. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 3rd level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.shadow split (sp): Beginning at 4th level, as a standard action a monk of the darkened hand can spend a point of ki to split off a part of their own shadow to cast silent image as a spell like ability. The DC for this spell-like ability is 10 + 1/2 the monk of the darkened hand’s class level + their Wisdom modifier and they use class level for the caster-level-dependent variables. This ability replaces slow fall at 4th level for the monk or the ki power at 4th level for the unchained monk.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.hide in plain sight (su): At 6th level, a monk of the darkened hand can use the Stealth skill even while being observed as long as they are in an area of dim light or darker. They need not have cover to do so. This ability replaces fast movement gained at 6th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.shadow calling (sp): At 8th level, a monk of the darkened hand’s connection to the plane of shadow allows them to create creatures and effects out of the power of that plane. They can expend 2 ki points to cast shadow conjuration as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level and their Wisdom bonus to determine the DC. At 14th level, this becomes greater shadow conjuration. This ability replaces the slow fall gained at 8th and 14th levels and the ki powers granted at 8th and 14th levels.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.shadow step (su): At 9th level, a monk of the darkened hand can expend a point of ki to travel between shadows as if using the spell dimension door. However, unlike that spell, the teleportation must begin and end in an area of dim light or darker. A monk of the darkened hand can travel up to 5 feet per class level per point of ki spent in this manner. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 9th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.defensive roll (ex): At 10th level, the monk of the darkened hand can expend 3 ki points to attempt to avoid a lethal blow. This functions as the rogue’s advanced talent of the same name. This ability replaces the ki power gained at 10th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.improved uncanny dodge (ex): At 12th level, a monk of the darkened hand can no longer be flanked. This defense denies a rogue the ability to sneak attack the monk of the darkened hand by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than the target has monk levels. If a character already has uncanny dodge from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank the character. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 12th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.shadow blast (sp): At 14th level, the monk of the darkened hand learned to harness the power of the shadow plane to deal devastating effects against their enemies. They can spend 2 ki points to cast shadow evocation as a spell like ability, using their class level as their caster level and their Wisdom modifier for the DC. At 18th level, this increases to greater shadow evocation. This ability replaces the ki power gained at 14th level and fast movement gained at 18th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.slippery mind (ex): At 15th level, a monk of the darkened hand becomes yet more resilient to enchantment spells. This functions as the rogue’s advanced talent of the same name. This ability replaces the fast movement gained at 15th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-monk-of-the-dar.shadow self (su): At 20th level, the monk of the darkened hand gains DR 10/- and a +2 luck bonus on all saving throws while in an area of dim light or darker. Additionally, all abilities use one fewer ki points when in an area of dim light or darker. This ability replaces perfect self.

archetype-monk-unchained-mystic-fist-unc.energetic fist (su): At 2nd level, a mystic fist can empower their strikes as a swift action to deal 1d6 energy damage. Doing so expends one of their daily uses of stunning fist. The energy damage is chosen between acid, cold, electricity, or fire, chosen when the ability is used. If the attack misses, the use of the ability is lost. At 8th level, the attack also deals an extra 1d10 of the energy damage on a critical hit, increased by the multiplier like a burst weapon. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
archetype-monk-unchained-mystic-fist-unc.spell casting: At 4th level, a mystic fist gains the ability to cast spells. They use the same spells per day and spells known as a bloodrager, though they may choose any spell available to a sorcerer or wizard when learning spells. They use their Wisdom modifier for their spellcasting ability modifier. This ability replaces all instances of slow fall, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels, and quivering palm for the monk. This ability replaces the ki powers gained at 4th, 10th, and 16th levels, the bonus feats at 6th and 14th levels and the style strike gained at 17th level.
archetype-monk-unchained-mystic-fist-unc.mystic strike (su): At 4th level, a mystic fist can deliver melee touch spells as part of a full attack action. At 8th level, they are also able to deliver ranged touch spell attacks as melee touch attacks during the full attack action.

archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.tattoo (su or sp): Beginning with 1st level, a tattooed monk gains a magical tattoo that empowers them. The tattoo choices are detailed below. They gain another tattoo at 2nd level and every 4 levels thereafter. These tattoos replace the monk’s bonus feats. Activating a tattoo is a swift action unless otherwise stated or if it is constant. The caster level, if applicable, for these tattoos is equal to the tattooed monk’s class level.
archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.bamboo or bear (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to his Constitution score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.bat or orchid (su): A character with this tattoo gains the power of good fortune, usable once per day. This ability allows the tattooed monk to reroll one d20 roll that they have just made. The character must take the result of the reroll, even if it’s worse than the original roll. The character must declare the reroll before the result of the original roll has been determined.
archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.black star or centipede (sp): Once per week, a character with this tattoo can cast shadow walk as a spell-like ability using their class level as the caster level. This ability allows the tattooed monk to cross great distances, but they must end their journey on the material plane. A tattooed monk must be at least 10th level to gain this tattoo.
archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.bull or oni (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Strength score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.cat or fire (su): Once per day per tattoo they possess, a character with this tattoo can add the number of tattoos they possess as an enhancement bonus to their Dexterity score for 1 round per class level.
archetype-monk-unchained-tattooed-monk-u.chameleon or kitsune (sp): A character with this tattoo can use an alter self effect once per day per tattoo they possess. This benefit lasts for 1 hour per class level.
