For example, at 6th level, he gains a 3rd-level spell slot and the invocation he places there can be 1st, 2nd, or 3rd-level. This ability replaces commune with dragon spirit, shared adaptation, and draconic wings.

archetype-dulra-brown-friar-dulra-archet.alignment: non-evil; a brown friar must choose a deity at 1st level and her alignment must be within one step of her deity’s, along either the law/chaos axis or the good/evil axis. This replaces the normal dúlra alignment restrictions.
archetype-dulra-brown-friar-dulra-archet.class skills: A brown friar adds Knowledge (religion) to her list of class skills and removes Intimidate. This modifies the dúlra class skills.
archetype-dulra-brown-friar-dulra-archet.spells: The brown friar loses access to all spells of the polymorph subschool; the illusion school; and that create, control or emulate the powers of undead. She gains access to all cleric and druid spells with the light descriptor; of the enchantment school; the healing subschool; non-evil spells of the abjuration school; and spells that qualify for the Peacemaker feat. This modifies spellcasting.
archetype-dulra-brown-friar-dulra-archet.holy patron: Brown friars mostly revere the same aspects of nature as other dúlra, but do so in a more worshipful way. This sometimes yields the same results as other dúlra, while other times, it rewards the brown friar differently. The Father: The father is the brown friar’s name for the Unicorn. Brown friars who revere the Father may receive the Unicorn’s benefits, or ( BoMT 2 ) create an aura out to 5 ft. The friar and her allies in the aura gain a bless effect that increases by +1 and extends out to 30 feet at 4th level. As a standard action, the brown friar can end her aura’s effect until the next time she regains spells. If she does, she gains a shield of faith effect that lasts for 1 minute per dúlra level. ( BoMT 2 ) The Moon Goddess: At 1st level, a brown friar with this holy patron gains a supernatural sanctuary effect she can activate on her turn as a standard action once per day plus one additional time per day for every 3 dúlra levels she possesses beyond 1st, to a maximum of 7 times per day at 19th level. Beginning at 4th-level, she can expend two uses of this ability to apply it to an ally she can see. The Mother: At 1st level, a brown friar with this holy patron gains the lame or tongues oracle curse and applies the arcane bond wizard class feature to her holy symbol (see below). Beginning at 4th level, the brown friar also applies the divine bond paladin class feature to her weapon. The Preacher: The Preacher is what the brown friar calls the satyr. Those who revere the Preacher may receive the Satyr’s blessings, or ( BoMT 2 ) inspire rage in her allies. This functions as the raging song of the same name, except it doesn’t improve beyond 4th level and the friar can use it a number of rounds per day equal to 3 + her Wisdom modifier. The Saint: Brown friars of the Saint can choose two domains granted by their deity to have access to. They add the domain spells to their spell list, but do not gain additional domain spell slots with which to cast them. Alternatively, they can choose only one domain and gain the domain spell slots as well. The Wilds: The Beast is known to brown friars as the Wilds, and it grants them the animal domain as it does other dúlra. ( BoMT 2 ) Instead of gaining an animal companion at 4th level, these brown friars sometimes receive a mask of the skinwalker from their circle that they rarely go without. The mask only functions for the friar to whom it was gifted and is otherwise worthless. The Wise: Brown friars treat the Hag is more of a wise crone from whom they gain the same benefits as the dúlra who revere her. ( BoMT 2 ) They will sometimes give up their 8th and 12th-level hexes for a mask of the changeling. The mask only functions for the friar to whom it was gifted and is otherwise worthless.

archetype-generational-hero-nights-champ.class skills: A night’s champion adds Knowledge (religion) and Knowledge (planes) to his list of class skills and removes Handle Animal and Ride. This alters the generational hero’s class skills.
archetype-generational-hero-nights-champ.weapon and armor proficiency: Night’s champions are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, all whips, and light armor. They are not proficient with shields. This alters the generational hero’s weapon and armor proficiencies.
archetype-generational-hero-nights-champ.smite evil (su): At 2nd level, a night’s champion gains smite evil 1/day, as the paladin class feature. He gains additional uses of this ability at 5th level and every 3 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 7/day at 20th level. This replaces bomb.
archetype-generational-hero-nights-champ.whip mastery (ex): At 2nd level, a night’s champion gains Whip Mastery as a bonus feat and is considered to meet its prerequisites when gaining other feats that require Whip Mastery. When using a scorpion whip, he treats it as a one-handed weapon for the purpose of feats and abilities that affect weapon type. This replaces Combat Expertise.
archetype-generational-hero-nights-champ.generational bond: A night’s champion always chooses a weapon as his bond. This alters generational bond.

archetype-monster-trainer-monster-auror-.monster training: A monster auror begins play with one monster he has been given by another trainer, such as a monster researcher. This monster is considered the auror’s primary monster. At 2nd level, and every level thereafter, the auror can allow his primary monster to grow, if able, or choose a new primary monster from the common monsters to which he has access (different areas have different common monsters, as detailed in Chapter 4). He can also trade his primary monster with another trainer, provided the monster he receives has a CR equal to or lower than his monster trainer level. Finally, a monster auror can still accept willing creatures into his essence and call upon them in the same way any trainer could, but these monsters do not change the trainer’s spells known (see below). This alters monster training and replaces capture monster.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-auror-.spellcasting: Each monster auror begins play with the ability to tap into his own essence to cast spells. He gains spells known as a sorcerer of his level, and the spells he can learn are drawn from his primary monster’s trainer spell list. If he chooses to change his primary monster upon gaining a level, the auror can decide to learn new spells from either the original monster or his new primary monster.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-auror-.starting characters above 1st level: A monster’s value to its trainer is equal to its CR squared x 500 gp. When starting a monster trainer above 1st level, use this guideline to effectively “purchase” monsters you have captured up to this point in your adventures. This does not mean you can buy monsters at any time or sell monsters you’ve captured in game; it only reflects their value as an aid when building a new character, and you should still work with your GM to determine how you acquired the monsters you do start with. Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even-numbered monster trainer level after that (6th, 8th, and so on), an auror can choose to learn a new spell in place of one he already knows. In effect, the auror loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. An auror may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that he gains new spells known for the level. This alters the monster trainer’s spellcasting ability.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-auror-.alter essence (sp): At 1st level, a monster auror learns how to alter his essence to mimic the monsters with whom he interacts. Once per day, after witnessing a monster cast a spell or use one of its spell-like, supernatural, or extraordinary abilities, the auror can use a standard action within 1 minute to add that ability to his list of spells known until the next time he regains spells. At 3rd level, and every 4 levels thereafter, the auror can use alter essence one additional time per day. The effective spell level of an ability gained with alter essence is equal to a spell of the same name, or half the CR of the monster using it (minimum 1) if no such spell exists. If the equivalent spell exists at different levels, the auror uses the highest level at which it could be gained. Abilities with limited uses (1/day, every 1d4 rounds, etc…) are similarly limited for the auror, in addition to requiring a spell slot. Any ability learned with alter essence counts as a spell when used by the auror and uses the auror’s Charisma modifier in place of another (a breath weapon typically uses Constitution, for example). Abilities gained more than once do not stack. Constant abilities last a number of hours equal to the auror’s monster trainer level before they must be cast again. Abilities with no spell equivalent are mimicked exactly as they were used, except that any save DCs are replaced by the auror’s spell save DC for the level used to cast them. Alter essence replaces eschew materials, talented trainer, swap monster, and the trainer perk gained at 19th level.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-auror-.echoes of magic (sp): At 3rd level, a monster auror learns how to pattern a small number of abilities he has learned with alter essence so that he can recall them after resting. When he uses alter essence, the auror can now choose to learn or pattern an ability he would gain. He can pattern up to a maximum number of abilities equal to his Charisma modifier + 1/2 his level (minimum 1). Once a monster auror has patterned his maximum number of abilities, he cannot pattern more unless he gives up one of those he has already. Each morning, when the auror regains his spells, he can expend uses of alter essence to relearn an ability he has patterned, adding it to his list of spells known for the day. This replaces spell familiarity and channel monster.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-auror-.trainer perks: The following perks complement the auror: Beloved monster, downtime ally, evasion, stalwart, tactics training, tough command, and uncanny dodge.

archetype-monster-trainer-monster-gamble.stack the deck (su): At 1st level, before attempting an attack, saving throw, or skill check, a monster gambler can take up to a –5 penalty to that roll as a free action and grant it as a circumstance bonus to her active monster’s next attempt to perform the same action against the same target or effect. She can also use an immediate action to direct her active monster to do the same for her. This replaces eschew materials.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-gamble.take the advantage (ex): The gambler gains no bonus on attacks and damage rolls against her favored enemies. Instead, she gains sneak attack, as the rogue feature. The gambler’s sneak attack damage is 1d6 at 2nd level and increases by 1d6 every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 5d6 at 18th level. The gambler’s active monster can also use sneak attack, and its effective rogue level is equal to the gambler’s monster trainer level when overcoming uncanny dodge or similar abilities. At 13th level, the gambler’s sneak attack can even damage targets normally immune to precision damage. This ability alters favored enemy and replaces spell familiarity and channel monster.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-gamble.play the odds (ex): At 9th level, a gambler can spend 1 use of talented trainer as a free action to reroll a single d20 before learning the outcome, but must keep the second result. She can also spend that use as an immediate action and direct her monster to do the same. This ability replaces great trainer.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-gamble.trainer perks: The following trainer perks complement the gambler archetype: Appraise monster, evasion, fast movement, inspiring trainer, side-by-side, skilled trainer, stalwart, and uncanny dodge.

archetype-monster-trainer-monster-perfor.spells per day: A performer gains spells per day as a bard of her monster trainer level, which means she cannot cast 7th-level or higher trainer spells, even if a monster would grant them to her. This alters the monster trainer’s spells.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-perfor.bardic performance: Every monster performer begins play with the inspire courage bardic performance, as the bard class feature. Her effective bard level is equal to her monster trainer level. The performer shares her ranks in Perform with her active monster, if it could reasonably use that Perform skill (a monster that cannot speak a language cannot give a speech, for example). If the performer is unable to maintain her performance, she can still direct her active monster to do so through their telepathic connection. At 2nd level, and every even level thereafter, the performer gains another performance of her choice. The performance must be one that could be gained by a bard of the performer’s level. At 20th level, if the performer chooses deadly performance, it counts as a master perk. This ability replaces eschew materials, favored enemy, and spell familiarity.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-perfor.tandem training (ex): At 4th level, a monster performer who chooses the tactics training perk at least once shares her teamwork feats with her active monster. This ability alters the tactics training perk.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-perfor.versatile performance (ex): At 9th level, a performer can choose one type of Perform skill. She can use her bonus in that skill in place of her bonus in associated skills. When substituting in this way, the performer uses her total Perform skill bonus, including class skill bonus, in place of its associated skill’s bonus, whether or not she has ranks in that skill or if it is a class skill. The types of Perform and their associated skills are: Act ( Bluff, Disguise ), Comedy ( Bluff, Intimidate ), Dance ( Acrobatics, Fly ), Keyboard Instruments ( Diplomacy, Intimidate ), Oratory ( Diplomacy, Sense Motive ), Percussion ( Handle Animal, Intimidate ), Sing ( Bluff, Sense Motive ), String ( Bluff, Diplomacy ), and Wind ( Diplomacy, Handle Animal ). This ability replaces great trainer.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-perfor.trainer perks: The following trainer perks complement the performer archetype: Beloved monster, extraordinary channeler, improved channel monster, inspiring trainer, skilled trainer, supernatural channeler, and tactics training.

archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.hit dice and base attack: A monster researcher’s monster trainer Hit Die is a d6, and her base attack bonus is equal to one-half her monster trainer level. This alters the monster trainer’s Hit Dice and base attack.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.armor proficiencies: The researcher is not proficient with any armor and suffers arcane spell failure in all armor types. This alters the monster trainer’s proficiencies.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.researcher’s knowledge (ex): A monster researcher adds half her monster trainer level (minimum 1) to all monster lore Knowledge skill checks and may make all Knowledge skill checks related to monsters untrained.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.researcher’s journal: A researcher uses her Intelligence as her spellcasting ability modifier, rather than Charisma. Every researcher begins play with a journal in which she keeps a collection of spells granted by her captured monsters for easy use. This functions as a wizard ’s spellbook, except as noted here.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.learning spells: The spells a researcher adds to her journal for free are drawn from those granted by the monsters she has captured. At 1st level, this includes up to 10 common cantrips and a number of 1stlevel spells equal to 3 + the researcher’s Intelligence modifier. The researcher need not add all of these spells immediately, choosing instead to add them from new monsters as she captures them. She adds additional spells to her journal as a wizard of her monster trainer level. Preparing and Casting Spells: Each morning, a monster researcher can designate one or more of her monster trainer spell slots in which to prepare spells from her journal. Once a spell is prepared in one of these slots, it cannot be used to cast a spell granted by the researcher’s active monster until the next time she would prepare spells. The researcher can cast spells prepared in this way with or without an active monster. When she casts a spell prepared with her journal, the researcher cannot cast it through her active monster unless that monster could grant her the spell normally. Researching Spells: A monster researcher cannot research new monster trainer spells without having regular access to one or more monsters that can grant them to a trainer. This ability alters the monster trainer’s spellcasting ability and replaces spell familiarity and channel monster.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.bonus feat: At 13th level, a monster researcher gains one bonus feat from the following list: Extra Perk, Improved Familiar, or any item creation or metamagic feat. If she has the monster summoning trainer perk, she adds Augment Summoning to her list of available bonus feats as well.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-resear.trainer perks: In addition, the following trainer perks complement the researcher archetype: Appraise monster, extended calling, extraordinary channeler, familiar bond, monster summoning, skilled trainer, and supernatural channeler.

archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.hit dice and base attack: d10. The scout’s base attack bonus is equal to her level.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.weapon and armor proficiency: The scout is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, with all types of armor and with shields (except tower shields). She suffers no arcane spell failure for casting spells while wearing armor or using a shield.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.spells per day: The scout’s spells per day are more limited than other trainers. Refer to the table presented here when determining the scout’s spells per day. Scouts also do not receive a monster’s cantrips like other trainers do.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.monster companion: The scout gains Monster Companion as a bonus feat at 1st level.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.detection (su): As a standard action, a scout can detect monsters. This ability functions as detect animals or plants, but with any creature that shares a type with a monster she has captured.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.faction: Each monster scout must choose to be either a reeve or a sentinel. This choice can’t be changed later. Reeve (Su): At 2nd level, and every 3 levels thereafter, a reeve gains the smite monster trainer perk. If she chooses the improved favored enemy perk, the reeve treats monsters of the chosen type the same as a paladin would treat an undead. Sentinel (Ex): At 1st level, a sentinel gains favored enemy, as the ranger feature. She gains additional favored enemies at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter. If she chooses the improved favored enemy perk, the sentinel gains a favored terrain of her choice instead. This ability replaces the trainer’s normal favored enemy and modifies the improved favored enemy perk.
archetype-monster-trainer-monster-scout.trainer perks: A monster scout can’t choose smite monster as a trainer perk. The following trainer perks complement the scout archetype: Animal companion, armored companion, natural armor, run with me, side-by-side, tough companion, and warrior companion.

archetype-necromancer-pale.curse (ex): At 1st level, a pale has already died at least once and been returned to life. He gains one of the following oracle’s curses, as the oracle class feature. Accursed, clouded vision, haunted, hellbound, lich, possessed, shadowbound, or wasting. This replaces charnel touch and spectral hand.
archetype-necromancer-pale.dominion: A pale does not receive dominion slots with which to cast his dominion spells, but he can prepare those spells to be cast up to once per day each.
archetype-necromancer-pale.mystery: Every pale begins play with a mystery that was revealed to him upon his original death. This functions as the oracle class feature, except the pale does not gain mystery spells.
archetype-necromancer-pale.revelation: The mystery revealed to the pale grants him insight and knowledge beyond that of other mortals. At 1st level, he gains one revelation from his mystery. He gains additional revelations at 3rd level, and every 4 levels thereafter. This replaces cruelty and improved iron will. archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.base attack bonus: A sanguine outlaw’s base attack bonus is equal to 3/4 his level, as a bard. This alters the necromancer’s base attack.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.weapon and armor proficiency: A sanguine outlaw is proficient with all simple weapons and all firearms, as well as light armor, but not shields. This modifies the necromancer’s proficiencies.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.spells: Sanguine outlaws gain spells per day, and spells known, as a bard of the same level. This alters the necromancer’s normal spellcasting progression.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.charnel touch (su): The sanguine outlaw does not gain charnel touch until 4th level. This alters the level at which the necromancer gains charnel touch.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.dominion of the gun (ex): At 1st level, a sanguine outlaw gains grit and gunsmith, as the gunslinger abilities. This ability replaces the necromancer’s dominion powers. He still gains his dominion spells and spell slots for the spell levels he can cast.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.deadeye (ex): At 1st level, the sanguine outlaw can resolve an attack against touch AC instead of normal AC when firing beyond his firearm’s first range increment. Performing this deed costs 1 grit point per range increment beyond the first. The outlaw still takes the –2 penalty on attack rolls for each range increment beyond the first when he performs this deed.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.deeds: Starting at 3rd level, a sanguine outlaw can spend grit points to accomplish additional deeds. When determining if he can use a deed, his effective gunslinger level is equal to his sanguine outlaw level -2. At 20th level, he gains the deeds normally granted to a 19th-level gunslinger.
archetype-necromancer-sanguine-outlaw.charnel shot: Starting at 4th level, as long as he is wielding a firearm and has at least 1 grit point, the sanguine outlaw’s charnel touch shares his firearm’s range increment. This replaces spectral hand. The Book of Many Things, © 2018-2021,Samurai Sheepdog; author Kevin Glusing.

archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.charnel touch (su): Necrotechs increase their charnel touch base damage to 2d8 at 12th level. They do not increase it to 3d8. This alters the progression of charnel touch.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.technomancer training (ex): A necrotech adds Disable Device ( Int ), Knowledge (engineering) ( Int ), and Linguistics ( Int ) to his list of class skills and removes Appraise, Knowledge (dungeoneering), and Sleight of Hand. At 1st level, necrotechs gain proficiency with all firearms, and they gain Technologist as a bonus feat. At 5th level, he also gains Skill Focus (knowledge [engineering]) as a bonus feat. This alters the necromancer’s class skills and proficiencies.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.recondition (su): At 2nd level, a necrotech can keep a single piece of still-functioning timeworn technology in good working order. Reconditioning a timeworn technological item takes 8 hours, after which the item no longer has a chance of glitching when used by the necrotech and can be recharged normally by the necrotech but no one else. Keeping a reconditioned item working requires 1 hour of maintenance each day (this can overlap with other preparations, if any), or the item reverts to a normal piece of timeworn technology and must be reconditioned again. At 4th level and every 3 levels thereafter, a necrotech can keep an additional item in good working order, without increasing his daily maintenance time.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.efficient construction (ex): At 3rd level, a necrotech using a technological crafting lab reduces the necessary energy expenditure of the facility by 25%. At 10th level, this energy reduction increases to 50%. This ability replaces cruelty.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.spell battery (su): At 3rd level as a swift action, a necrotech can expend an unused spell slot to power a technological device he touches. Each spell level expended in this way grants the device 1 charge. Any charges unused at the end of the round are lost, and any charges used by the device that round that aren’t provided by the necrotech must come from the device’s own power reserves. He can use this ability to power timeworn technology. He can’t power devices that don’t use charges.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.technical expertise (ex): Starting at 4th level, a necrotech adds his class level to Craft, Disable Device, Knowledge (engineering), and Linguistics checks regarding technology. This replaces spectral hand.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.command robot (sp): At 5th level, a necrotech can issue a command to a robot within 30 feet as a standard action once per day. The command must be in a language the robot can understand. Robots can resist this ability by succeeding at a Will saving throw. DC of 10 + 1/2 the necrotech’s class level + his Charisma At 8th level, the necrotech can use this ability twice per day, and at 10th level he can use it three times per day. This ability otherwise functions as suggestion, save that it is not mind-affecting and can only affect constructs with the robot subtype.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.graft technology (ex): Also at 5th level, undead created by a necrotech can each be outfitted with one of the following technological upgrades. The necrotech chooses which option to apply when he creates an undead. Recognition Display: Grant the undead lifesense, which allows it to detect the presence of living creatures within 60 feet. Robot Legs: Increase the undead’s movement speed by +10 feet. Shield Plating: Increase the undead’s natural armor bonus by +2. Targeting Sensor: Grant the undead a +1 enhancement bonus on attacks and damage. If the necromancer has a weapon in his possession with a higher enhancement bonus, he can grant that bonus to exactly one of the undead.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.recycle technology (ex): At 4th level, a necrotech can dismantle existing technological items and construct new ones from the parts, though such creations are prone to malfunctioning. He trades in each item for an amount of crafting potential based on a fraction of its crafting cost (not price), as described below. He can use this potential and his technological crafting feats to make a new item. For example, a necrotech could use a broken laser pistol in place of 500 gp for crafting technological items (10% of the laser pistol ‘s crafting cost of 5,000 gp). He then follows the normal rules for crafting a technological item (see page 16), except that he must pay at least 50% of the crafting cost using recycled technology. If he pays 100% of the cost in this fashion, he crafts the item at double the normal speed. In the process of cannibalizing the old items, the new items are destroyed and any excess gold value is lost. The item he creates is considered timeworn technology, even if new items were broken down to build it. Recycle technology cannot be used to build constructs, cybertech, pharmaceuticals, or technology that uses nanites. Technology Status Crafting Potential Fully functioning 100% of crafting cost Reconditioned 75% of crafting cost Timeworn technology 50% of crafting cost Broken or nonfunctional 10% of crating cost
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.applied learning (ex): At 9th level, when a necrotech succeeds at a saving throw against a technological effect that has reduced effects on a successful save, he instead avoids the effect entirely. A helpless or flat-footed necrotech does not benefit from this ability.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.technic spell mastery (ex): At 9th level, a necrotech selects one of the following spells: antitech field, destroy robot, detect radiation, discharge, greater discharge, greater remove radioactivity, infuse robot, irradiate, magic circle against technology, memory of function, rebuke technology, recharge, remove radioactivity, protection from technology, or technomancy. If the spell chosen isn’t one that’s normally on his necromancer spell list, he adds it to his class spell list at the level a wizard casts the spell. The spell chosen must be of a spell level he would otherwise be able to cast. If he prepares spells, he can prepare this spell one additional time in excess of the normal maximum number of spells he can prepare. If he casts spells spontaneously, he adds the spell to his spells known, and can cast this spell once per day without using a daily spell slot. At 5th level, he picks another spell from the list above, and at 8th level, he picks a 3rd spell from the list above.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.unified energy (su): At 11th level, a necrotech can draw power from a technological device in his possession to cast a spell he knows without expending a spell slot. He consumes 2 charges from the device for each spell level of the spell being cast. In the process of casting the spell, he can apply any of his metamagic feats, using a number of charges appropriate to the increase in spell level, but he cannot exceed the highest effective level of spell he is able to cast. The necrotech can use this ability multiple times per day, but never in excess of a number of charges equal to his necromancer level.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.fortification (ex): A necrotech doesn’t gain light fortification until 13th level. He still gains moderate fortification at 17th level, and heavy fortification at 20th level. This alters the progression of fortification.
archetype-necromancer-necrotech-necroman.field improvisation (ex): At 10th level, a necrotech can recycle technology with astounding speed. Each hour of crafting when using his recycle technology ability is equivalent to 8 hours of uninterrupted crafting. He can perform up to 8 hours of such amazingly efficient work per day. Any item the necrotech completes is treated as reconditioned for the remainder of that day, even if he has no remaining slots. It can also be added permanently to his group of reconditioned items if he has an available slot or stops maintaining one of his current reconditioned items.

archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.armor proficiency: Blood knights are proficient with all types of armor (light, medium, and heavy), but not with shields. This alters the veritus champion’s armor and shield proficiencies.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.runeforging (ex): Blood knights pay their blood debt with runes specially crafted during their morning ritual. At 1st level, when a blood knight fills his blood debt each morning, he can immediately dedicate 12 of those points to a single two-handed melee weapon or split between two light or one-handed melee weapons he wields. This functions as sheathed in blood, except the bonuses last until the next time the knight fills his blood debt. As he gains levels, a blood knight can dedicate more of his blood debt to his weapons with runeforging, in the same way a veritus champion improves his weapon through sheathed in blood. Beginning at 12th level, a blood knight can take 5 minutes to change the enhancement bonuses and weapon properties applied to his weapons using this ability, so long as the resulting total is the same. This time can be spent in conjunction with scourge of volwryn (see below). This alters blood debt and sheathed in blood.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.bone shield (su): As long as a blood knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, he gains a shield bonus to his AC equal to half his Constitution bonus (minimum 1) plus the highest enhancement bonus among weapons he wields.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.grip of death (su): At 2nd level, a blood knight gains Improved Drag as a bonus feat. As long as he has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, a blood knight can attempt to drag an enemy toward him from up to 30 feet away. The knight doesn’t move when dragging a creature in this way. At 7th level, the knight gains Greater Drag as a bonus feat. This replaces Endurance and Die Hard.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.scourge of volwryn: At 3rd level, a blood knight can take 5 minutes to tap into the soul of Volwryn from across any planar boundary to transform his power over undeath into something else. When he does, the blood knight becomes his choice of a frost knight or plague knight. He gains those abilities in place of bone shield, boil blood, fetid decay, grasp of death, and dancing weapon.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.boiling blood (sp): At 6th level, a blood knight can convert 12 points of his blood debt as a standard action to cast boiling blood as a spell-like ability. This replaces waves of blood.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.fetid decay (su): At 9th level, as long as a blood knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, he can target any creature with boiling blood (even if it doesn’t have blood), and the damage dealt counts as both negative energy and fire (it affects creatures resistant or immune to fire damage normally). At 13th level, the knight can target one creature per three levels, no two of which may be more than 50 ft. apart. At 17th level, the knight can use fetid decay a number of times per day equal to his Constitution modifier (minimum 1) without converting blood debt to do so. This replaces blood burst at the listed levels.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.grasp of death (su): At 11th level, a blood knight can convert points of his blood debt and use a standard action to drag each creature within 30 feet of a creature he can see toward that creature. He makes one drag attempt and applies it to each target. Using this ability costs 6 points of blood debt per creature successfully dragged in this way. This replaces Survivor.
archetype-veritus-champion-blood-knight.dancing weapon (su): At 15th level, a blood knight can convert 4 points of his blood debt as a standard action and release one of the weapons to which he has dedicated points of blood debt to fight for him. This functions as the dancing weapon property, except that it doesn’t count against the total enhancements the knight’s weapon can possess. As part of the same action, the knight can convert up to 6 points instead and release both of the weapons he wields. He can do this once per day at 15th level, twice per day at 18th level, and at will at 20th level. This replaces blood possession.

archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.armor proficiency: Frost knights are proficient with all types of armor (light, medium, and heavy), but not with shields. This alters the veritus champion’s armor and shield proficiencies.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.runeforging (ex): Frost knights pay their blood debt with runes specially crafted during their morning ritual. At 1st level, when a frost knight fills his blood debt each morning, he can immediately dedicate 12 of those points to a single two-handed melee weapon or split between two light or one-handed melee weapons he wields. This functions as sheathed in blood, except the bonuses last until the next time the knight fills his blood debt. As he gains levels, a frost knight can dedicate more of his blood debt to his weapons with runeforging, in the same way a veritus champion improves his weapon through sheathed in blood. Beginning at 12th level, a frost knight can take 5 minutes to change the enhancement bonuses and weapon properties applied to his weapons using this ability, so long as the resulting total is the same. This time can be spent in conjunction with scourge of volwryn (see below). This alters blood debt and sheathed in blood.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.frost blade (su): As long as a frost knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, they automatically gain the frost weapon property. If he converts points of his blood debt to add that property to a weapon, it gains icy burst instead.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.grip of death (su): At 2nd level, a frost knight gains Improved Drag as a bonus feat. As long as he has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, a frost knight can attempt to drag an enemy toward him from up to 30 feet away. The knight doesn’t move when dragging a creature in this way. At 7th level, the knight gains Greater Drag as a bonus feat. This replaces Endurance and Die Hard.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.scourge of volwryn: At 3rd level, a frost knight can take 5 minutes to tap into the soul of Volwryn from across any planar boundary to transform his power over undeath into something else. When he does, the frost knight becomes his choice of a blood knight or plague knight. He gains those abilities in place of frost blade, cone of cold, frost pillar, ice chains, and aura of the remorseless.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.cone of cold (sp): At 6th level, a frost knight can convert 12 points of his blood debt as a standard action to cast cone of cold as a spell-like ability. This replaces waves of blood.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.frost pillar (su): At 9th level, as long as a frost knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, he can cast flame strike as a full-round action. When cast this way, the spell’s damage is half cold damage and half negative energy. The knight can use this ability a number of times per day equal to his Constitution modifier. At 13th level, the knight can ignore his allies within the area of the spell. At 17th level, the knight can cast the spell as a standard action instead. This replaces blood burst at the listed levels.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.ice chains (su): At 11th level, a blood knight can convert 6 points of his blood debt as a standard action to cast entangle. Creatures that fail their saving throw must succeed at a Fortitude save at the same DC or be slowed for the duration and up to 1 round afterward. This replaces Survivor.
archetype-veritus-champion-frost-knight.aura of the remorseless (su): At 15th level, as long as a frost knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, enemies within 30 feet of him at the start of each of his turns take cold damage equal to the knight’s Constitution modifier and reduce their movement speed by half. The knight can suppress or reactivate this ability as a free action on his turn. At 18th level, this affects enemies within 50 feet of the knight. At 20th level, those enemies also take damage equal to the highest enhancement bonus among weapons the knight wields, and the damage counts as both cold and negative energy. This replaces blood possession.

archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.armor proficiency: Plague knights are proficient with all types of armor (light, medium, and heavy), but not with shields. This alters the veritus champion’s armor and shield proficiencies.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.runeforging (ex): Plague knights pay their blood debt with runes specially crafted during their morning ritual. At 1st level, when a plague knight fills his blood debt each morning, he can immediately dedicate 12 of those points to a single two-handed melee weapon or split between two light or one-handed melee weapons he wields. This functions as sheathed in blood, except the bonuses last until the next time the knight fills his blood debt. As he gains levels, a plague knight can dedicate more of his blood debt to his weapons with runeforging, in the same way a veritus champion improves his weapon through sheathed in blood. Beginning at 12th level, a plague knight can take 5 minutes to change the enhancement bonuses and weapon properties applied to his weapons using this ability, so long as the resulting total is the same. This time can be spent in conjunction with scourge of volwryn (see below). This alters blood debt and sheathed in blood.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.undead companion (ex): As long as a plague knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, he gains an undead companion. This functions as the necromancer class feature, except the knight’s effective druid level is equal to half his veritus champion level (minimum 1st).
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.grip of death (su): At 2nd level, a plague knight gains Improved Drag as a bonus feat. As long as he has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, a plague knight can attempt to drag an enemy toward him from up to 30 feet away. The knight doesn’t move when dragging a creature in this way. At 7th level, the knight gains Greater Drag as a bonus feat. This replaces Endurance and Die Hard.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.scourge of volwryn: At 3rd level, a plague knight can take 5 minutes to tap into the soul of Volwryn from across any planar boundary to transform his power over undeath into something else. When he does, the plague knight becomes his choice of a blood knight or frost knight. He gains those abilities in place of undead companion, festering strike, fetid decay, plaguebringer, and army of undead.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.sickening strikes: At 6th level, a plague knight can convert 12 points of his blood debt as a standard action to cast sickening strikes as a spell-like ability. Creatures normally immune to disease can be affected by the knight’s sickening strike, but do gain a +2 bonus to save against it. This replaces waves of blood.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.fetid decay (su): At 9th level, as long as a plague knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, he can cast boiling blood, targeting any creature (even if it doesn’t have blood), and the damage dealt counts as both negative energy and fire (it affects creatures resistant or immune to fire damage normally). At 13th level, the knight can target one creature per three levels, no two of which may be more than 50 ft. apart. At 17th level, the knight can use fetid decay a number of times per day equal to his Constitution modifier (minimum 1) without converting blood debt to do so. This replaces blood burst at the listed levels.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.plaguebringer (su): At 11th level, when a plague knight hits a creature already affected by his sickening strikes with an attack, each enemy within 10 feet of that creature must also save against the effect. Each creature that fails its save (including the original target) takes damage equal to the knight’s Constitution modifier. This replaces Survivor.
archetype-veritus-champion-plague-knight.army of the undead: At 15th level, as long as a plague knight has at least 12 points of his blood debt dedicated to his weapons, he can convert 60 points of his blood debt to cast summon nature’s ally V, but only to create 1d4+1 creatures. Those creatures gain undead traits, a +7 bonus to AC, attacks, and saves, and a +3 bonus to damage. These bonuses also apply to the knight’s undead companion. At 18th level, the knight can cast summon nature’s ally VI instead, and his bonuses increase to +9 and +4. At 20th level, the knight can cast summon nature’s ally VII instead, and his bonuses increase to +10 and +5. This replaces blood possession.

archetype-malefactor-curse-eater.devour curse (su): As part of a full-round action when you successfully use the Cursebreaker ability, you gain temporary hit points equal to the caster level of the broken curse.
archetype-malefactor-curse-eater.cursed resilience (ex): When you successfully use the Cursebreaker ability you gain spell resistance equal to the caster level of the curse. This ability lasts for a number of rounds equal to your Con bonus.
archetype-malefactor-curse-eater.transfer curse (su): Instead of devouring a curse, as a standard action you can instead spit it forth to a new target within 30 feet. The new target is allowed a saving throw at the original curse DC to avoid the effects.

archetype-malefactor-doom-herald.guileful polyglot (ex): As per the feat, the Doom Herald gains 2 additional languages, or 4 additional languages if he has at least one rank in Linguistics.
archetype-malefactor-doom-herald.divine will (ex): The Doom Herald’s conviction is greater than most, and he shrugs off mental attacks with ease. You gain a +2 divine bonus to all saves made against mind-affecting abilities. This ability replaces luck of the damned.
archetype-malefactor-doom-herald.utterance of damnation (ex): The Doom Herald speaks of doom and the target becomes hopeless and more susceptible to curses. As a standard action, the Doom Herald speaks words of conviction and all enemies within 60’ who are capable of hearing (and comprehending) the Herald’s speech must make Will saves equal to 10 plus half the Doom Herald’s level plus Charisma modifier or be forced to roll twice for all saving throws related to curses or hexes, taking the worse result. This ability replaces aura of misfortune.

archetype-malefactor-kismet.karmic blessing (ex): Choose any ally within 30’, as an immediate action you may grant them a luck bonus equal to your Charisma modifier for a single roll. You may use this ability a number of times per day equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1.) This ability replaces aura of misfortune and harrowing strike.

archetype-malefactor-moirae.verum fatis (ex): The Moirae speak prophetic words and their visions become truth. As a full round action, the Moirae may speak of an action by a target. The ally is then fated to succeed at this task. When the ally targeted attempts this single action (skill check, attack roll, etc.) as defined by the Moirae, they are treated as if they “took 20” on the roll, regardless of whether or not they would normally be allowed to do so. Using this ability on an attack roll does not produce a critical hit. The Moirae can perform this ability a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). This ability only functions on a target once per 24 hours. This ability replaces aura of misfortune and luck of the damned.

archetype-malefactor-reaver.heavy armor proficiency (ex): Reavers are fully capable of donning heavy armor and going face to face with the toughest of opponents.
archetype-malefactor-reaver.cursed blade (ex): Whenever the Reaver uses a melee weapon against a cursed opponent, they gain +1d6 points of bonus damage. Each time a Reaver can choose an additional malediction, he can instead elect to add an additional +1d6 of damage to his Cursed Blade attacks. This ability replaces luck of the damned.

archetype-everyman-gaming-unchained-ninj.expanded finesse training (ex): At 1st level, a yoru no kuroura selects one one-handed melee weapon that she is proficient with and cannot normally be used with Weapon Finesse (like a katana). She gains the benefits of Weapon Finesse with the selected melee weapon and, beginning at 3rd level, she can select this weapon with her finesse training class feature. This replaces poison use.
archetype-everyman-gaming-unchained-ninj.flamboyant ki (ex): At 2nd level, every time a yoru no kuroura would gain a ninja trick, she may select a swashbuckler ’s deed instead. This must be a deed that a swashbuckler of her ninja level could use. The yoru no kuroura can spend points from her ki pool as panache points to use these deeds. She can’t spend points from her ki pool to use deeds from other classes or those gained by feats, nor can she regain points to his ki pool as a swashbuckler would regain panache points.
archetype-everyman-gaming-unchained-ninj.ninja tricks: A yoru no kuroura gains access to the following new ninja trick:
archetype-everyman-gaming-unchained-ninj.slide through shadows (su): A ninja who selects this trick can spend 1 ki point to disappear into an area of dim light or darkness and emerge from another area of dim light or darkness she can see within 10 feet per ninja level.

archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.totem transformation (lesser, su): You gain any of the following abilities possessed by the animal you select as your animal spirit: bite (1d6 for a Medium character), 2 claws (1d4 for a Medium character), darkvision, improved land movement speed (up to a +20-foot enhancement bonus to the character’s base land movement speed), low-light vision, scent, and swim (up to 30 feet).
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.pack leader (intermediate, su): When you summon animals that match your animal spirit, they gain a +2 bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.wildstrike (greater, su): You can allow your animal spirit to gain 1 point of influence over you as a swift action to allow an animal or plant within 30 feet that can see or hear you to immediately take an additional standard action.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.wild heart (supreme, ex/sp): You gain a +4 bonus on saves against enchantment and mind-affecting effects, and immunity to effects that affect only humanoids. Once per day, you can cast summon nature’s ally IX as a standard action. Bloodline Arcana: Your mind-affecting spells can affect plants of hit dice equal to or less than your caster level as a sorcerer. Your spells still follow restrictions based on type or language-dependence, except that mind-affecting spells that can affect animals affect plants as well. Bloodline Powers: You have always felt a special bond to plants, particularly forests and trees. As your power increases, so does the call of the green.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.fey blood (ex): You are considered to have the fey bloodline for purposes of effects and archetypes. If an archetype replaces an element of the fey bloodline you do not have, you give up the ability from the corresponding level instead.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.green binding (sp): At 1st level, you can entangle a creature in vines for 1 round as a melee touch attack. The vines are not considered anchored. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.woodland stride (su): At 3rd level, you can move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at your normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect you.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.lignification (ex): At 9th level, your flesh becomes as hard and resilient as wood, though your appearance does not change. You gain a natural armor bonus of +2. This bonus increases to +3 at 13th level, and +4 at 17th level.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.fey magic (su): At 15th level, you may reroll any caster level check made to overcome spell resistance. You must decide to use this ability before the results are revealed by the GM. You must take the second result, even if it is worse. You can use this ability at will.
archetype-mesmerist-animal-mesmerist-spi.soul of the forest (su): At 20th level, you become one with the forest. You gain DR 10/ cold iron. Creatures of the plant type do not attack you unless compelled to do so through magic. Once per hour, you can cast transport via plants as a spell-like ability using your sorcerer level as your caster level.

archetype-mesmerist-astrologer-mesmerist.nightwatcher (ex): You gain a bonus on Perception checks in dim light or darkness. In addition, you gain a +2 bonus on Knowledge (arcana), Knowledge (geography), Knowledge (nature), and Survival checks outdoors at night equal to 1/2 your mesmerist level. This replaces consummate liar.
archetype-mesmerist-astrologer-mesmerist.guiding star (su): At 4th level, you can determine your precise location whenever you can see the open sky at night. When the night sky is visible to you, you may also add your Charisma modifier to your Wisdom modifier on all Wisdom -based checks. In addition, once per night while outdoors, you can cast one spell as if it were modified by the Empower Spell, Extend Spell, Silent Spell, or Still Spell feat without increasing the spell’s casting time or level. This replaces the mesmerist trick gained at 4th level.
archetype-mesmerist-astrologer-mesmerist.student of the stars (ex): At 8th level, you can use an astrolabe, telescope, or technological device created to observe the stars or track their movements in place of any focus component costing 1,000 gp or less. In addition, your copious astronomical observations and notes allow you to gain insight into the past, present, or future if you spend 10 minutes in contemplation, as if you had cast commune with a caster level equal to your mesmerist level. This effect is not magical. This replaces the mesmerist trick gained at 8th level.
archetype-mesmerist-astrologer-mesmerist.the stars are right (sp): At 12th level, you expend one of your mesmerist tricks to foretell a willing creature’s future by spending 1 minute in contemplation of the stars and conversation with them, granting them the benefit of a moment of prescience. You can use this ability even if the stars are not visible by consulting your notes and an astrolabe instead, but the creature gains only one-half the normal bonus from the spell. You cannot use this ability on yourself. This is a language-dependent ability, and a creature receiving the effect cannot benefit from it again for one week. This replaces the mesmerist trick gained at 12th level.
archetype-mesmerist-astrologer-mesmerist.satellite (su): At 16th level, you can expend one of your mesmerist tricks to create a Medium-sized force construct that resembles a small planet, moon, or star, orbiting around your body. The satellite sheds bright light within 10 feet and dim light 10 feet beyond that, and it otherwise functions as a forceful hand (though it is size Small, rather than Large). If you use this ability outdoors at night, the satellite gains additional temporary hit points equal to your mesmerist level and can be used as a clenched fist. You may create or dismiss the satellite as a standard action, but you must expend an additional mesmerist trick each time it is created, and the total duration per day cannot exceed 1 round per level. Any damage dealt to the satellite remains if it is dismissed and then recreated; if reduced to 0 hp it is destroyed and cannot be recreated for 24 hours. This replaces the mesmerist trick gained at 16th level.
archetype-mesmerist-astrologer-mesmerist.stargate (sp): At 20th level, you may cast interplanetary teleport once per day, expending one of your mesmerist tricks for each passenger you wish to take with you. You and all companions gain the benefits of life bubble for 24 hours upon arriving at your destination. This replaces the mesmerist trick gained at 20th level.

archetype-mesmerist-contract-mesmerist-t.phistophilus whip style (ex): A contract mesmerist can wield whips with deadly efficiency, dealing lethal damage regardless of the armor bonus of their target. At level 3, she deals 1 point of bleed damage whenever she confirms a critical hit with her whip. This bleed damage increases by +1 at levels 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18. This replaces painful stare.
archetype-mesmerist-contract-mesmerist-t.scribe scroll: At 2nd level, a contract mesmerist gains Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat. This replaces towering ego.
archetype-mesmerist-contract-mesmerist-t.contracted ally (su): At 3rd level, a contract mesmerist can select up to one willing ally to be her contracted ally. She can implant mesmerist tricks in this ally as a swift action and activate the trick at double the normal range. A contract mesmerist can select an additional contracted ally at levels 6, 10, and 14. This replaces touch treatment.

archetype-mesmerist-nereid-mesmerist-spi.fey blood (ex): You are considered to have the fey bloodline for purposes of effects and archetypes. If an archetype replaces an element of the fey bloodline you do not have, you give up the ability from the corresponding level instead.
archetype-mesmerist-nereid-mesmerist-spi.drench (sp): Starting at 1st level, you can make a melee touch attack as a standard action that drenches a creature in chill water. This deals 1d6 points of nonlethal cold damage of your energy type + 1 for every two sorcerer levels you possess. In addition, it extinguishes non-magical flames of Medium size or smaller. At 11th level, you extinguish non-magical flames of Large size or smaller, and can dispel magic flames as dispel magic. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier.
archetype-mesmerist-nereid-mesmerist-spi.touched by the waters (ex): At 3rd level, you gain a swim speed equal to your land speed and can hold your breath for a number of rounds equal to four times your Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating.
archetype-mesmerist-nereid-mesmerist-spi.fleeting glance (sp): At 9th level, you can turn invisible for a number of rounds per day equal to your sorcerer level. This ability functions as greater invisibility. These rounds need not be consecutive.
archetype-mesmerist-nereid-mesmerist-spi.fey magic (su): At 15th level, you may reroll any caster level check made to overcome spell resistance. You must decide to use this ability before the results are revealed by the GM. You must take the second result, even if it is worse. You can use this ability at will.
archetype-mesmerist-nereid-mesmerist-spi.soul of the water (su): At 20th level, you become one with the forest. You gain DR 10/ cold iron. Creatures with the animal type and aquatic subtype do not attack you unless compelled to do so through magic. You can breathe water and have a swim speed of 60 feet or your land speed, whichever is greater. For purposes of acting underwater, you are considered to have freedom of movement, though you do not gain the other benefits of that effect.

archetype-mesmerist-norn-mesmerist-spiri.fey blood (ex): You are considered to have the fey bloodline for purposes of effects and archetypes. If an archetype replaces an element of the fey bloodline you do not have, you give up the ability from the corresponding level instead.
archetype-mesmerist-norn-mesmerist-spiri.pluck the threads (sp): Starting at 1st level, as a standard action you can manipulate the fortune of a creature within 30 feet. You can choose to either give the creature a +2 luck bonus on its next saving throw and yourself a -2 penalty on your next, or to give the creature a -2 penalty and yourself a +2 bonus. At 11th level, the bonus or penalty you grant increases to 4. your bonus or penalty remains 2. Saving throws that carry no risk (including harmless effects) do not invoke the bonus or penalty. This effect fades after 24 hours, and you can affect any given creature once in a 24 period. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier.
archetype-mesmerist-norn-mesmerist-spiri.shift fate (su): Starting at 3rd level, as an immediate action you can force any one target within 120 feet to reroll a saving throw—this ability must be used immediately after the saving throw is rolled, and the target must abide by the results of this second roll. You can use this ability once per day. At 7th level and every four levels thereafter, you can use this ability an additional time per day, to a maximum of five times per day at 19th level.
archetype-mesmerist-norn-mesmerist-spiri.heart of winter (su): Starting at 9th level, your blood chills in your veins. You gain cold and fire resistance 10. At 17th level, these resistances improve to 20.
archetype-mesmerist-norn-mesmerist-spiri.fey magic (su): At 15th level, you may reroll any caster level check made to overcome spell resistance. You must decide to use this ability before the results are revealed by the GM. You must take the second result, even if it is worse. You can use this ability at will.
archetype-mesmerist-norn-mesmerist-spiri.fated soul (su): At 20th level, you perfect your control of fate. You gain DR 10/ cold iron and immunity to cold. Once per day you can manifest and attempt to cut short the thread binding a creature’s fate. You must be wielding a weapon or natural weapon capable of dealing slashing damage, and the target must be within 120 feet and your line of sight. The target immediately takes 20d6 of damage. It can reduce this damage by half if it succeeds at a Fortitude DC with a save equal to 20 plus your Charisma modifier. If the target dies from this damage, it can only be restored to life via miracle, wish, or divine intervention. This is a death effect.

archetype-mesmerist-nymph-mesmerist-spir.fey blood (ex): You are considered to have the fey bloodline for purposes of effects and archetypes. If an archetype replaces an element of the fey bloodline you do not have, you give up the ability from the corresponding level instead.
archetype-mesmerist-nymph-mesmerist-spir.nymph’s grace (sp): At 1st level, as a swift action you can add a bonus equal to 1/2 your sorcerer level to your saving throws and as a deflection bonus to your AC for 1 round. The minimum bonus is +1, but otherwise cannot exceed your Charisma modifier.
archetype-mesmerist-nymph-mesmerist-spir.dazzling aura (su): At 3rd level, your presence dazzles anyone within 30 feet looking directly at you (as a gaze attack, except you cannot direct it). You can suppress or resume this ability as a free action.
archetype-mesmerist-nymph-mesmerist-spir.unearthly presence (su): At 9th level, you gain a +2 inherent bonus to your Charisma. This bonus increases to +4 at 13th level and +6 at 17th level.
archetype-mesmerist-nymph-mesmerist-spir.fey magic (su): At 15th level, you may reroll any caster level check made to overcome spell resistance. You must decide to use this ability before the results are revealed by the GM. You must take the second result, even if it is worse. You can use this ability at will.
archetype-mesmerist-nymph-mesmerist-spir.soul of the nymph (su): At 20th level, your soul becomes one with the world of the fey. You gain immunity to poison and DR 10/ cold iron. Creatures of the animal type do not attack you unless compelled to do so through magic. As a standard action, you can blind those beholding your dazzling aura ( Fortitude DC = 10 + 1/2 your sorcerer level plus your Charisma modifier negates) for 1 round.

archetype-mesmerist-satyr-mesmerist-spir.fey blood (ex): You are considered to have the fey bloodline for purposes of effects and archetypes. If an archetype replaces an element of the fey bloodline you do not have, you give up the ability from the corresponding level instead.
archetype-mesmerist-satyr-mesmerist-spir.laughing touch (sp): At 1st level, you can cause a creature to burst out laughing for 1 round as a melee touch attack. A laughing creature can only take a move action but can defend itself normally. Once a creature has been affected by laughing touch, it is immune to its effects for 24 hours. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. This is a mind-affecting effect.
archetype-mesmerist-satyr-mesmerist-spir.woodland stride (su): At 3rd level, you can move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at your normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect you.
archetype-mesmerist-satyr-mesmerist-spir.beguiling melody (su): At 9th level, you can substitute the playing of a wind instrument for the verbal and somatic components of a spell of the enchantment school. Performing in this manner increases the spell’s DC by +1. By making a Perform (wind instruments) check with a DC equal to 15 plus twice the spell’s level, you can apply the Bouncing Spell. Disruptive Spell, Enlarge Spell, Extend Spell, or Widen Spell metamagic feat to the spell, without altering its casting time or spell level, whether or not you have the metamagic feat in question. If you fail this check, the save DC of your spell is reduced by -4.
archetype-mesmerist-satyr-mesmerist-spir.fey magic (su): At 15th level, you may reroll any caster level check made to overcome spell resistance. You must decide to use this ability before the results are revealed by the GM. You must take the second result, even if it is worse. You can use this ability at will.
archetype-mesmerist-satyr-mesmerist-spir.soul of the faun (su): At 20th level, your body transforms, giving you the ram’s horns and goat’s legs of a satyr. You gain DR 5/ cold iron, a natural armor bonus of +5, and your land speed increases by 10 feet. The natural armor bonus does not stack with any existing natural armor bonus, though your speed bonus stacks with other speed bonuses. You gain a horn attack that deals 1d6 points of damage (1d4 if you are Small). this attack deals bludgeoning damage.

archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.weapon and armor proficiencies: Champion mesmerists are proficient with simple weapons, as well as light armor and bucklers. In addition, if this is this character’s first level in any class, they may select a martial tradition of their choice. This alters proficiencies.
archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.spellcasting: The champion mesmerist may combine spheres and talents to create magical effects. The champion mesmerist is considered a Mid-Caster and uses Charisma as his casting ability modifier. (Note: All casters gain 2 bonus talents and may select a casting tradition the first time they gain the casting class feature.) This replaces the spells class feature.
archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.spell pool: The champion mesmerist gains a small reservoir of energy he can call on to create truly wondrous effects, called a spell pool. This pool contains a number of spell points equal to his level + his casting ability modifier (minimum 1). This pool replenishes once per day after roughly 8 hours of rest.
archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.blended training: A champion mesmerist gains 3 talents every 4 levels; the same as he gains caster levels. Whenever he gains a talent he may choose to gain either a magic talent or a combat talent. Champion mesmerists use their casting ability modifier as their practitioner modifier. Mental Power: At 1st level, the champion mesmerist gains the Mind sphere as a bonus magic talent. This replaces knacks.
archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.mass charmer: At 5th level, the champion mesmerist gains the Group Charm talent of the Mind sphere as a bonus magic talent and increases the number of creatures he may affect when using it by his casting ability modifier. This replaces mental potency.
archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.rule minds: The champion mesmerist ’s rule minds ability may be triggered off an any Mind sphere charm that allows a saving throw. This alters rule minds.
archetype-mesmerist-champion-mesmerist-m.greater training: The champion mesmerist may choose to lose consummate liar and glib lie to instead gain a combat or magic talent at every class level. He may not take this option if possessing an archetype that would alter or replace consummate liar and glib lie.

archetype-psychic-dream-disciple-psychic.spells: A dream disciple adds all spells with “ dream ” or “ dreams ” in their name to her psychic spells list (but not to her known spell list). This replaces the phrenic amplification gained at 1st level.
archetype-psychic-dream-disciple-psychic.lucid dreamer (ex): At 3rd level, a dream disciple gains Lucid Dreamer as a bonus feat. She needs not to meet the feat’s prerequisites. This replaces the 3rd-level phrenic amplification.
archetype-psychic-dream-disciple-psychic.truth in dreams (su): At 5th level, once per day a dream disciple can enter an oneiric trance to learn the answer to an important question. For every 10 minutes of uninterrupted sleep, the dream disciple automatically succeeds at one Knowledge check rolled in the 24 hours after she awakes. At 12th level, this ability can instead function as legend lore, except that the dream disciple must spend the whole casting time sleeping, and the informations gained are always clear and accurate as if she had the person or thing she is investigating about at hand. This replaces the 5th-level discipline power.
archetype-psychic-dream-disciple-psychic.bewitching dreams (su): At 11th level, a dream disciple can choose to gain the Nightmares or Speak in Dreams witch hexes in place of a phrenic amplification.
archetype-psychic-dream-disciple-psychic.oneiric protection (sp): At 20th level, a dream disciple is affected by dream shield as a constant spell-like ability. This modifies and otherwise functions as remade self.

archetype-psychic-esoteric-starseeker-ps.written in the stars: An esoteric starseeker can spend 1 hour each night in quiet contemplation of the stars to attune herself to a constellation of the Cosmic Caravan, gaining knowledge of new spells from it. She gains one bonus constellation spell slot for each spell level she can cast, and she can prepare a spell associated with her attuned constellation into that slot. At 11th level, she can attune herself to two constellations, choosing between the spells offered by both constellations when she prepares her constellation spells. Whenever she attunes herself to a constellation, the esoteric starseeker must also weaken her connection to one school of magic of her choice, increasing the casting time for all spells of that school to a full-round action or an additional full-round action, as though she were using a metamagic feat. She can change her attuned constellations and her weakened school each day when she prepares her constellation spells. The Cosmic Caravan and their associated spells are as follows. The Thrush: comprehend languages (1st), magic mouth (2nd), tiny hut (3rd), dream (4th), remote viewing (5th), battlemind link (6th), phase door (7th), discern location (8th), wish (9th). The Lantern Bearer: liberating command (1st), glitterdust (2nd), guiding star (3rd), wandering star motes (4th), true seeing (5th), sonic form (6th), prismatic spray (7th), sunburst (8th), meteor swarm (9th). The Newlyweds: charm person (1st), enthrall (2nd), synesthesia (3rd), break enchantment (4th), reincarnate (5th), joyful rapture (6th), mass synesthesia (7th), bilocation (8th), overwhelming presence (9th). The Bridge: endure elements (1st), resist energy (2nd), daylight (3rd), fire shield (4th), wall of force (5th), contagious flame (6th), reverse gravity (7th), create demiplane (8th), world wave (9th). The Daughter: bless (1st), hypnotic pattern (2nd), heroism (3rd), freedom of movement (4th), hostile juxtaposition (5th), cloak of dreams (6th), greater hostile juxtaposition (7th), irresistible dance (8th), freedom (9th). The Rider: anticipate peril (1st), acute senses (2nd), ablative barrier (3rd), dimensional anchor (4th), echolocation (5th), blade barrier (6th), grasping hand (7th), frightful aspect (8th), ride the lightning (9th). The Patriarch: command (1st), spiritual weapon (2nd), dispel magic (3rd), telekinetic charge (4th), contact other plane (5th), find the path (6th), mage’s sword (7th), brilliant inspiration (8th), gate (9th). The Wagon: expeditious retreat (1st), twisted space (2nd), haste (3rd), mirror transport (4th), teleport (5th), fluid form (6th), walk through space (7th), etherealness (8th), time stop (9th). The Pack: calm animals (1st), animal aspect (2nd), rage (3rd), greater animal aspect (4th), summon monster V (5th), mass bear’s endurance (6th), summon monster (7th), animal shapes (8th), shapechange (9th). The Mother: identify (1st), aid (2nd), invisibility purge (3rd), stoneskin (4th), spell resistance (5th), contingency (6th), mind blank (7th), refuge (8th), wall of suppression (9th). The Stargazer: know the enemy (1st), augury (2nd), arcane sight (3rd), locate creature (4th), feeblemind (5th), geas/quest (6th), arcane sight (greater) (7th), moment of prescience (8th), dream voyage (9th). The Stranger: disguise self (1st), invisibility (2nd), displacement (3rd), riding possession (4th), prying eyes (5th), veil (6th), project image (7th), maze (8th), divide mind (9th). The Follower: forced quiet (1st), darkness (2nd), vision of hell (3rd), enervation (4th), waves of fatigue (5th), shadow walk (6th), simulacrum (7th), destruction (8th), energy drain (9th). This replaces the bonus spells normally granted by the psychic’s discipline and the phrenic amplifications gained at 1st and 11th levels. Major Amplifications: An esoteric starseeker gains this ability at 15th level.

archetype-psychic-wildepath-psychic-arch.primal spells: A wildepath adds one 1st-level spell from the druid spell list to the psychic spell list and her spells known. Each time a wildepath gains the ability to cast a new level of spell, she can add one spell of that level from the druid spell list to both the psychic spell list and her spells known. She casts these spells as psychic spells, and once the spells are selected these choices cannot be changed. This replaces discipline spells.
archetype-psychic-wildepath-psychic-arch.nature’s command (ex): The wildepath’s mind-affecting spells can affect even plant creatures. When she casts a mind-affecting spell, the wildepath can spend 2 points from her phrenic pool to overcome a plant creature’s immunity to mind-affecting effects for the purposes of that spell. This ability functions even on mindless plant creatures, but it has no effect on creatures that aren’t plants. At 11th level, when the wildepath casts a mind-affecting or language-dependent spell, the psychic can spend 2 points from her phrenic pool to cause the spell to affect creatures of the plant and animal types as if they were humanoids that understood her language. This replaces the phrenic amplifications gained at 1st and 11th levels.
archetype-psychic-wildepath-psychic-arch.know the land (sp): At 9th level, the wildepath can cast commune with nature as a spell-like ability once per day, using her psychic level as her caster level. She can also expend any unused spell slot of 5th level or higher to cast commune with nature. This replaces telepathic bond.
archetype-psychic-wildepath-psychic-arch.wild mind (su): At 17th level, when the wildepath gains the telepathy ability, she can also mentally communicate with any animal or plant creature as if it had a language. This alters telepathy.

archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.grim phantom (su): The spirit linked to a grim apostle functions in all respects as a regular spiritualist’s phantom, but each day when the grim apostle regains her daily spell slots, she can choose which Horseman focus is dominant within the grim phantom. When the grim phantom is banished to the Ethereal Plane, the grim apostle takes an amount of damage equal to 1d4 × the grim phantom’s number of Hit Dice. This ability modifies the phantom ability and replaces the phantom’s emotional focus.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.hardened soul (su): At 1st level, while a grim phantom is confined in the grim apostle’s consciousness, the grim apostle gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against death effects and effects that would remove or subsume the grim apostle’s soul (such as possession or trap the soul ). At 6th level and every 6 levels thereafter, this bonus increases by 2 (to a maximum of +10 at 18th level). This ability replaces shared consciousness and fused consciousness.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.marked for death (su): When manifested in ectoplasmic form, the grim phantom gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls against a creature the grim apostle has hit with a melee or ranged attack since its last turn (the phantom’s “marked target”). Additionally, such an attack by the grim phantom deals an additional 1d6 points of negative energy damage. At 5th level and every 5 spiritualist levels thereafter, the negative energy damage increases by 1d6.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.fatal aura (su): At 7th level, the grim phantom can create a 10-foot-radius aura as a swift action that makes healing more difficult. The DC of Heal checks to provide first aid and treat deadly wounds within the aura is increased by 5. Any creature within the aura that casts a conjuration ( healing ) spell, or casts another spell or uses an ability that restores hit points, must succeed at a Will saving throw or lose the spell or use of the ability. Ending the aura is a free action.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.no escape (su): At 12th level, the grim phantom gains the benefits of the Following Step, Step Up, and Step Up and Strike feats but only against its marked target.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.killing word (sp): At 17th level, the grim phantom can cast power word kill once per day as a spell-like ability.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.ravenous bite (ex): The grim phantom’s natural attacks take the form of bites that deal piercing damage as a creature one size category larger than its current size. It also gains Power Attack as a bonus feat.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.aura of starvation (su): At 7th level, the grim phantom can create a 10-foot-radius aura of starvation as a swift action. Enemies within the aura take a –2 penalty on attack and damage rolls. Ending the aura is a free action.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.wail of the hungry (sp): At 12th level, the grim phantom can cast waves of fatigue once per day as a spell-like ability.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.distended gullet (su): At 17th level, as a swift action, the grim phantom in ectoplasmic form gains the swallow whole ability (4d8 negative energy damage, AC 17, one-tenth the phantom’s total hit points ) for a number of rounds equal to its Charisma modifier. This ability can affect creatures no more than two size categories larger than the phantom. Each creature the grim phantom swallows is shunted into an extradimensional space that can hold any number of creatures. When the duration of this ability ends, any creatures still within the extradimensional space appear adjacent to the grim phantom. The grim phantom is exhausted for 1 hour after using this ability and can’t use it again during that time.
archetype-spiritualist-grim-apostle-spir.weakening strike (su): A creature hit by the grim phantom’s slam attack must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw or take a –2 penalty on ability checks, attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks for 1d4 rounds.
